```go
    switch args[0] { case truth: r = falsity; case falsity: r = truth; ... }
} ... if yes && len(args) == 2 && args[0] == args[1] { r, e = m.MkTrue() }
```
F2, F3, F4 and F5 below are further differences in the same engine.

**Impact.** Every `dom-simplify` goal that contains `(not true)`, `(not false)`, `(not (not true))` or a reflexive equality prints differently. In `diff_tactic_ib_1021` the Go turns `(not true)` into `false`. Goal update then marks the goal inconsistent, and g3 prints `false` where z3 prints the whole goal.

**Reproduction.** All 5 fuzz scripts. Minimized (`$S/work/FUZZ_B/t/m1.smt2`, `m2`, `m3`):
```
(assert (not (not true)))
(apply dom-simplify)
```
z3: `(goal (not (not true)) ...)`. g3: `(goal true ...)`. The same holds for `(not false)` (g3 `true`) and `(not true)` (g3 `false`).

**Fix.** Delete the Go-only engine (`dom_simplify_context.go`, and everything in `dom_simplify_rewrite.go` except `domOp`). Add `dom_simplify_subst.go`, a faithful `expr_substitution_simplifier` built on `ast.ASTExprSubstitution` + `ast.ASTScopedExprSubstitution`:
- `AssertExpression`: push, then `update_substitution` on `t`, on `tt` when `t` is `(not tt)`, or on `mk_not(t)`; always return true.
- `updateSubstitution`: if ground and `=`/`iff`, ref lhs/rhs into the trail and insert by `is_gt`. If neither side is greater, fall through. Then insert `n1→false` for `(not n1)`, otherwise `n→true`.
- `Rewrite` = `ScopedExprSubstitutionFindValue`.
- `Pop`, `ScopeLevel`, `TranslateDom`.

Make `NewDomSimplifyTactic` install it, so `Apply` always calls `applyDomSimplifier` (and `Translate` always uses `TranslateDom`). The verified code is in `$S/work/FUZZ_B/fix/dom_simplify_subst.go` and `dom_simplify_tactic.go`.

**Regression test.**
- `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/dom_simplify_no_not_folding.smt2`:
```
(declare-const p Bool)
(push)
(assert (not (not true)))
(assert (not false))
(assert p)
(apply dom-simplify)
(pop)
(assert (not true))
(apply dom-simplify)
```
  Expected (`scriptResults`): `"(goals\n(goal\n  (not (not true))\n  (not false)\n  p\n  :precision precise :depth 1)\n)\n(goals\n(goal\n  (not true)\n  :precision precise :depth 1)\n)\n"`.
- Rewrite `TestDomSimplifyDefaultCallbackSubstitutesBooleanIff` (`tactic/core/dom_simplify_source_fidelity_test.go`), which uses `domContext`/`assertContext`. It should use `newExprSubstitutionSimplifier`, `AssertExpression(iff,false)`, then `Rewrite` on a ref to `dom-b`; expect `dom-a`, scope level 1. This version was verified in the private copy.
- Check with `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`.

<a id="fuzz-b-f2"></a>
#### FUZZ_B-F2: Go substitution scope lets a later binding override an earlier one; C++ keeps the first

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/dom_simplify_context.go:25-30,17-24` (`domContext.insert`/`find`)
- C++: `src/ast/expr_substitution.h:66-71` (`scoped_expr_substitution::insert`)

**C++ behavior.** `if (!m_subst.contains(s)) { m_subst.insert(...); m_trail.push_back(s); }`. The first binding stays in force until it is popped.

**Go behavior.** Each scope is its own map, and `find` searches from the innermost scope outwards, so the newest binding wins.

**Impact.** Different substitution results whenever the same key is asserted twice in nested scopes.

**Reproduction.** `vec/dom_simplify_first_binding_wins.smt2`:
```
(declare-const a Int)(declare-const b Int)(declare-const x Int)(declare-const y Int)(declare-const z Int)
(declare-fun f (Int) Int)
(assert (= x a))
(assert (= y (ite (= x b) (f x) z)))
(apply dom-simplify)
```
z3 prints `(= y (ite (= x b) (f a) z))`; g3 prints `(f b)`.

**Fix.** Same as F1: use `ScopedExprSubstitutionInsert`, which already has the `contains` check.

**Regression test.** Add that vector. Expected: `"(goals\n(goal\n  (= x a)\n  (= y (ite (= x b) (f a) z))\n  :precision precise :depth 1)\n)\n"`.

<a id="fuzz-b-f3"></a>
#### FUZZ_B-F3: an equality with no orientable side is not recorded as `eq → true`

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/dom_simplify_context.go:85-102` (`assertContext`)
- C++: `src/tactic/core/dom_simplify_tactic.cpp:495-520` (`update_substitution`)

**C++ behavior.** If neither `is_gt(lhs,rhs)` nor `is_gt(rhs,lhs)` holds (for example `(= x x)`), it traces "incompatible" and falls through to `insert(n, true)`.

**Go behavior.** Returns `nil` after the two `greater` checks, so nothing is inserted. The Go also tests `IsGround` on each side separately, rather than once on `n`.

**Reproduction.** `vec/dom_simplify_reflexive_equality_key.smt2`:
```
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-fun h (Bool) Bool)
(assert (= x x))
(assert (h (= x x)))
(apply dom-simplify)
```
z3 prints `(h true)`; g3 prints `(h (= x x))`.

**Fix.** Same as F1 (`updateSubstitution` in the fix falls through).

**Regression test.** That vector. Expected: `"(goals\n(goal\n  (= x x)\n  (h true)\n  :precision precise :depth 1)\n)\n"`.

<a id="fuzz-b-f4"></a>
#### FUZZ_B-F4: simplify_ite returns the wrong result: branch checks in the wrong order, rewritten condition dropped, is_false tested after assert_expr

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/dom_simplify_rewrite.go:254-260` (`simplifyITE`); `pkg/tactic/core/dom_simplify_plugin.go:434-441,493-499` (`domITE`)
- C++: `src/tactic/core/dom_simplify_tactic.cpp:213-247`

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
else if (m.is_false(new_c) || !assert_expr(new_c, false)) r = simplify_arg(e);
...
if (c == new_c && t == new_t && e == new_e) r = ite;
else if (new_t == new_e) r = new_t;
else r = m.mk_ite(new_c, new_t, new_e);
```

**Go behavior.** There are three differences:
- Both paths check `yes == no` before the "unchanged" test. As a result `(ite p x x)` becomes `x`, while the C++ keeps `ite`.
- The default path's "unchanged" test, `yes == thenBranch && no == elseBranch`, ignores a rewritten condition. It returns the old `ite` even when the condition `q` was rewritten to `p`.
- `domITE` calls `AssertExpression(nc,false)` before testing `nc == false`, so it pushes a scope the C++ never pushes. That matters for `propagate-bv-bounds-new`.

**Reproduction.** `vec/dom_simplify_ite_result.smt2`:
```
(declare-const p Bool)(declare-const q Bool)(declare-const x Int)(declare-const y Int)
(declare-fun h (Int) Bool)
(push)
(assert (=> p (h (ite p x x))))
(apply dom-simplify)
(apply propagate-bv-bounds-new)
(pop)
(push)
(assert (ite p q q))
(apply dom-simplify)
(pop)
(assert (= q p))
(assert (h (ite q x y)))
(apply dom-simplify)
```
z3 prints `(=> p (h (ite p x x)))` (twice), then `(ite p q q)`, then `(h (ite p x y))`. g3 prints `(h x)` (twice), then `q`, then `(h (ite q x y))`.

**Fix.** In `domITE`, test `IsTrue`/`IsFalse(nc)` before `AssertExpression`, and order the result checks as in the C++. The default `simplifyITE` is deleted by F1.

**Regression test.** That vector, with the z3 output above. The unit test `TestDomSimplifyITEEqualBranches` (`dom_simplify_ite_test.go`) currently asserts the non-C++ result `b`. Change it to expect the unchanged `ite` handle. Verified: with the fix it fails as written, and z3 prints `(ite a b b)`.

<a id="fuzz-b-f5"></a>
#### FUZZ_B-F5: the rebuilt and/or uses `MkAndArgs`/`MkOrArgs` instead of `mk_and`/`mk_or`, so a unary `and` is not unwrapped

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/dom_simplify_rewrite.go:171-175` (`simplifyAndOr`)
- C++: `src/tactic/core/dom_simplify_tactic.cpp:349`, `src/ast/ast_util.h:112,122`

**C++ behavior.** `r = is_and ? mk_and(args) : mk_or(args)`. `mk_and` of a single argument returns that argument. `domAndOr` in `dom_simplify_plugin.go` already uses `domMkAndArgs`.

**Reproduction.** `vec/dom_simplify_unary_and.smt2`:
```
(declare-const p Bool)
(assert (not (and p)))
(apply dom-simplify)
```
z3 prints `(not p)`; g3 prints `(not (and p))`.

**Fix.** Covered by F1, since the only remaining path is `domAndOr`.

**Regression test.** That vector. Expected: `"(goals\n(goal\n  (not p)\n  :precision precise :depth 1)\n)\n"`.

<a id="fuzz-b-f6"></a>
#### FUZZ_B-F6: simplify_rec skips the root's self-edge in the dominator tree (z3 behavior here is unsound)

- Severity: high (the observable difference); see the note on z3 soundness
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/dom_simplify_plugin.go:264-270`, `dom_simplify_rewrite.go:50-56` (`if child != h`); `dom_simplify_dominators.go:43-45`
- C++: `src/tactic/core/dom_simplify_tactic.cpp:286-288` (`for (expr * child : tree(e)) simplify_rec(child);`), `:89,127-131`

**C++ behavior.** `m_doms.insert(root, root)`, so `extract_tree` adds the edge root→root. When the root is a single goal formula (not an `and`/`or`/`ite`), `simplify_rec(root)` recurses into `root` itself. It does this repeatedly, under whatever scopes are already asserted, until `m_max_depth` (1024). The inner results are cached and reused. (`display` skips the self edge; `simplify_rec` does not.)

**Go behavior.** `if child != h` skips the self edge.

**Impact.** The outputs differ. In the C++ the inner pass rewrites the root using facts derived from the root itself, which is circular reasoning. This is a real z3 soundness bug: z3 turns a satisfiable goal into `(= true false)`.

**Reproduction.** `vec/z3_bug_dom_simplify_root_resimplify.smt2`:
```
(declare-const p0 Bool)
(declare-const p1 Bool)
(assert (= true (ite p1 p0 p1)))
(check-sat)
(check-sat-using (then dom-simplify smt))
(apply dom-simplify)
```
z3 prints `sat`, `unsat`, then `(goal (= true false) ...)`. That is wrong: p1=p0=true satisfies the assertion. g3 prints `sat`, `sat`, `(goal (= true (ite p1 p0 false)) ...)`.

A sound example where the outputs still differ: `vec/dom_simplify_root_resimplify_sound.smt2`:
```
(declare-const p1 Bool)
(declare-const p3 Bool)
(assert (= (and (or true p3 p3)) p1))
(apply dom-simplify)
```
z3 prints `(= (or true p3 false) p1)`; g3 prints `(= (and (or true p3 p3)) p1)`.

**Fix.** Drop the `child != h` filter in `domRec` (the fix does this). This reproduces z3 exactly, including the unsound result above.

Owner decision needed. If unsoundness is not acceptable, keep the filter for the root only, add `z3_bug_dom_simplify_root_resimplify` to `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/z3_bug_exclusions.txt`, and accept the output differences on sound cases like the vector above.

**Regression test.**
- `dom_simplify_root_resimplify_sound.smt2`, expected `"(goals\n(goal\n  (= (or true p3 false) p1)\n  :precision precise :depth 1)\n)\n"`.
- `z3_bug_dom_simplify_root_resimplify.smt2`: either the z3 output (faithful port) or an exclusion-list entry.

<a id="fuzz-b-f7"></a>
#### FUZZ_B-F7: dominator-tree child order is post-order in Go; the C++ uses m_doms obj_map (hash) order

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/dom_simplify_dominators.go:40-53` (`compile`)
- C++: `src/tactic/core/dom_simplify_tactic.cpp:127-131` (`extract_tree`)

**C++ behavior.** `for (auto const& kv : m_doms) add_edge(m_tree, kv.m_value, kv.m_key);` walks the obj_map table. That order depends on AST hashes and is deterministic (it is not pointer-based, so the recorded manifest deviation, "pointer/hash iteration ... undefined", is incorrect).

**Go behavior.** It appends the root first and then the nodes in post-order.

**Impact.** Children are simplified in a different order, so the cached results and scopes differ.

**Reproduction.** `vec/dom_simplify_tree_hash_order.smt2`:
```
(declare-const p2 Bool)(declare-const p3 Bool)
(assert p3)
(assert (= (and (not true) p2) (not p3)))
(assert (= true false))
(apply dom-simplify)
```
z3 prints `(= (and (not true) p2) (not false))`. g3 with F1-F6 fixed but post-order kept prints `(= (and (not false) p2) (not false))`.

**Fix.** Store `m_doms` in an `ast.ObjMap` (`NewObjMap`; `Insert`/`Find`/`Contains`; `Reset` keeps the table capacity, as `reset()` does). Build `tree` by iterating `doms.Entries()`. Remove the manifest deviation. Done in `fix/dom_simplify_dominators.go`.

**Regression test.** That vector, with the z3 output above.

<a id="fuzz-b-f8"></a>
#### FUZZ_B-F8: compute_post_order visits the first argument first; C++ pushes all unmarked arguments, so the last argument is numbered first

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/dom_simplify_dominators.go:57-116` (`computePostOrder`)
- C++: `src/tactic/core/dom_simplify_tactic.cpp:30-67`

**C++ behavior.** The loop pushes every unmarked argument onto `todo`, then pops from the back, so the last argument is processed first. `m_post2expr` order (and therefore `intersect` and `compute_dominators`) follows that.

**Go behavior.** It pushes one argument at a time, left to right.

**Reproduction.** `vec/dom_simplify_post_order.smt2`:
```
(declare-const p0 Bool)(declare-const p1 Bool)
(assert (=> (and p1 (not p0)) (not p0)))
(assert p0)
(apply dom-simplify)
```
z3 prints `(=> (and p1 (not p0)) (not true))`. g3 prints `(=> (and p1 false) false)`, and with only F1-F6 fixed it prints `(=> (and p1 (not true)) (not true))`.

**Fix.** Rewrite `computePostOrder` exactly like the C++ loop. See `fix/dom_simplify_dominators.go`.

**Regression test.** That vector, with the z3 output above. Also add a unit test in `dom_simplify_dominators_test.go`: `compile(MkOr(a,b))` gives `post == [b, a, root]` (use `newDomFixture`).

<a id="fuzz-b-f9"></a>
#### FUZZ_B-F9: expr_ref lifetimes not mirrored, so AST ids and the trace log differ even when stdout matches

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/dom_simplify_plugin.go:157-216` (`pinDom`, `clearDomPins`, `cacheDom`); `dom_simplify_tactic.go:154`
- C++: `dom_simplify_tactic.cpp` (the `expr_ref`s `r`, `new_c`/`new_t`/`new_e`, `args`; `m_trail`, `m_args`; `cleanup()` run by the `clean()` wrapper)

**C++ behavior.** Temporaries die at the end of their scope. For example, `init()`'s `fml = mk_and(args)` dies when `init` returns, and `m_trail` keeps only the cached results.

**Go behavior.** Every handle it touches is pinned until the end of the pass (or of `Apply`). Freed ids are therefore not recycled at the same points: `[mk-app] #28 and ...` in z3 versus `#26 and ...` three times in g3.

**Reproduction.** `t/tr1.smt2`:
```
(declare-const p Bool)(declare-const q Bool)(declare-fun h (Bool) Bool)
(assert p)(assert (h p))(assert q)
(apply dom-simplify)
```
Run with `trace=true`. Stdout is identical, but the logs differ at line 42.

**Fix.** Replace pins with `ast.ASTRef` ownership that mirrors each `expr_ref`. Run `cleanup()` (the `m_trail`/`m_args`/`m_dominators` reset, plus the `m_root` ref) after `Apply`. Release `init`'s `args` and `fml` on return. See `fix/dom_simplify_plugin.go`.

After this change the trace logs are byte-identical on all 24 cases checked and on ~16,000 random scripts.

**Regression test.** Add `t/tr1.smt2` as a vector to the trace-golden set (`pkg/cmd/g3/trace_golden_test.go`, `TestTraceGolden`).

<a id="fuzz-c-f1"></a>
#### FUZZ_C-F1: bvarray2uf rewriter is a hand-written memo walk, not rewriter_tpl; it skips the built-in simplification and misnames fresh functions

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/bv/bvarray2uf_rewriter.go:49` (`bvArrayRewriter.rewrite`), `pkg/tactic/bv/bvarray2uf_array.go:8` (`reduce`), `pkg/tactic/bv/bvarray2uf_sorts.go:72-127` (`functionFor`), `pkg/tactic/bv/bvarray2uf_tactic.go:105` (`Apply`)
- C++: `src/tactic/bv/bvarray2uf_rewriter.h:75` (`bvarray2uf_rewriter : rewriter_tpl<bvarray2uf_rewriter_cfg>`), `src/tactic/bv/bvarray2uf_rewriter.cpp:105-376` (`mk_uf_for_array`, `reduce_app`)

**C++ behavior.** `bvarray2uf_rewriter` is a `rewriter_tpl`. The template constant-folds `ite` with a true or false condition while it walks, and it runs `reduce_app` on every application (BR_FAILED leaves the node as `mk_app` rebuilt it). It caches results, honours `BR_REWRITE1` (for `distinct` on arrays it expands to pairwise `not (= ..)` and rewrites that again), and runs `pre_visit`/`reduce_var`/`reduce_quantifier`. `mk_uf_for_array` calls `m_manager.mk_fresh_func_decl("f_t", "", 1, &domain, range)`. Its suffix `""` is a non-null symbol, so the name is `f_t!!N`. `m_arrays_fs` is an `obj_map`. The term-ite case looks up `f_a` but inserts under `e`. Every `reduce_app` case builds its arguments in GCC right-to-left order, e.g. `mk_eq(mk_app(f_t,x), mk_app(f_s,x))` builds `f_s(x)` first.

**Go behavior.** `rewrite` is a private recursive walk that only calls `reduce`. Nothing is folded, so `(not (ite true false p1))` stays as written. `distinct` is expanded and then rewritten directly, which goes through `extensionalEquality` and yields `(not (forall ...))` instead of z3's `(not (= (_ as-array f_t!!0) (_ as-array f_t!!1)))`. Each `rewrite` call starts a fresh memo map, so a shared subterm in two assertions is reduced twice and the store axioms are duplicated (see b3 below). `functionFor` passes `usymbol.Symbol{}` (null) as the suffix, which produces `f_t!N`. The construction order differs throughout: `forall`/var before `as-array`, and left-to-right arguments.

**Impact.** Every `bvarray2uf` user (`apply bvarray2uf`, `(then bvarray2uf smt)`, and the QF_ABV/QF_AUFBV pipelines that use it) prints different goals, models and fresh names, gets different AST ids, and in some cases a different goal (duplicated axioms, `forall` under `not`).

**Reproduction.** These are the minimized scripts in `$S/work/FUZZ_C/t/`:
```
(declare-const p1 Bool)
(assert (not (ite true false p1)))
(apply bvarray2uf)
```
z3 prints `(not false)`; g3 prints `(not (ite true false p1))`.
```
(declare-const a (Array (_ BitVec 3) (_ BitVec 3)))
(declare-const b (Array (_ BitVec 3) (_ BitVec 3)))
(declare-const v (_ BitVec 3))
(assert (= (store a v v) b))
(assert (= (store a v v) a))
(apply bvarray2uf)
```
z3 prints four formulas using `f_t!!0..2`. g3 prints six formulas using `f_t!0..2`, because the store axioms are added twice. The `distinct` case (`(assert (distinct a b))`) gives z3 `(not (= (_ as-array f_t!!0) (_ as-array f_t!!1)))` and g3 `(not (forall ((x ..)) (= (f_t!0 x) (f_t!1 x))))`.

**Fix.** Verified: the stdout of all of b1-b12, ab_1125, ai_1222, ib_1222, ir_1222, is_1166 and s_1116 is identical to z3, the AST traces are identical, and 600 random scripts show no difference.
1. Make `bvArrayRewriter` embed `rewriter.DefaultConfiguration`. Own a `*rewriter.Traversal`, built with `NewProofTraversal` when `m.ProofsEnabled()` and `NewTraversal` otherwise (the `rewriter_tpl(m, m.proofs_enabled(), cfg)` constructor), plus `out`/`proof` refs. `rewrite(h)` returns `(value, proof)` from `Rewrite`/`RewriteWithProof`.
2. Port `reduce_app` as `ReduceApp(f, args, out, proof)` case by case. For `eq`/`distinct`, test `is_bv_array(f->get_domain()[0])` and use `m.AreEqual`. For `distinct`, return `MkDistinctExpanded` with `rewriter.Rewrite1`. In the term-ite case, look up `f_a = mk_app(f,args)` and register under `e = mk_ite(c, f_t(x), f_f(x))`. In the uninterpreted (null-family) case, return the rebuilt `t` with BR_DONE when an argument is an array. Map, store and const each get their own case. Build every argument in GCC right-to-left order. Pin the locals in a per-call scratch slice that is released on return.
3. Port `PreVisit` (push quantifier decl sorts onto `bindings`), `ReduceVar` (exception when `idx < len(bindings)`) and `ReduceQuantifier` (NOT_IMPLEMENTED: keep the tactic exception).
4. Write `mkUFForArray`: `as-array` returns its function; otherwise look it up in an `ast.ObjMap` (`m_arrays_fs`). A fresh entry uses `MkFreshFuncDecl(intern("f_t"), intern(""), …)`, and the trace message is emitted before the `emc`/`fmc` insert. `close()` releases the map entries in table order.
5. In `Apply`: create `tactic_report` before `fail_if_unsat_core_generation` (C++ order; the `-v:10` output differs otherwise), call `traversal.Reset()` before the loop (`m_rw.reset()`), and pass the rewriter's proof to `g.Update` with no extra modus ponens, because `m_produce_proofs` is never set in the C++. `Cleanup` builds the fresh rewriter first and then closes the old one (`std::swap`, `dealloc`).

**Regression test.** Extend `pkg/tactic/bv/bvarray2uf_tactic_test.go` with `TestBVArray2UFFoldsIteAndNamesFreshFunctions`, using the fixture in `bvarray2uf_test_support_test.go`. Rewrite `(not (ite true false p))` and expect `(not false)`. Rewrite `(= (store a v v) b)` and expect a fresh decl named `f_t!!0`. Rewrite `distinct a b` and expect `not (= as-array as-array)`. Vectors: `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/bvarray2uf_ite_fold.smt2` (b1 above, expected `(goals\n(goal\n  (not false)\n  :precision precise :depth 1)\n)`), `bvarray2uf_shared_store.smt2` (b3) and `bvarray2uf_distinct.smt2`, with z3's outputs in `scriptResults`. Check them with `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`. The existing unit tests that call `rewriter.rewrite` and read `rewriter.arrays[...]` need updating for the new signature and the ObjMap.

<a id="fuzz-c-f2"></a>
#### FUZZ_C-F2: pb-preprocess replaces the C++ m_ge-index bookkeeping and accumulating subsumption vectors with "fixed" logic (documented deviation, observable)

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/pb_preprocess_simplify.go:7-11,281-289` (`simplify`, classify loop), `:404-422` (subsumption), `pkg/tactic/core/pb_preprocess_terms.go` (`parse`), `pkg/tactic/core/pb_preprocess_tactic.go:95-103` (`Apply`)
- C++: `src/tactic/core/pb_preprocess_tactic.cpp:180-182` (`classify_vars(i, …)`), `:233-257` (subsumption), `:593-627` (`to_ge`), `:145-164` (`operator()`)

**C++ behavior.** `classify_vars(i, to_app(g->form(m_ge[i])))` records `i`, the position inside `m_ge`. Elimination, resolution and subsumption then use those numbers as goal indices. In the subsumption pass, `args2/coeffs2` are declared once per `m_ge[i]`, and `to_ge` only appends, so successive candidates accumulate. `to_ge` relies only on `SASSERT(pure_args)` (compiled out). The tactic has no `tactic_report`, and it throws `"pb-preprocess does not support proofs"`.

**Go behavior.** The file header says: "Deliberate deviations from 4.7.1, both of which can make the source unsound: classify_vars records the index into m_ge but later code reads it as a goal index, so g3 records the goal index (m_ge[i]); and the subsumption pass never resets args2/coeffs2 between candidates, so g3 rebuilds them for each candidate." `parse` also returns nil on impure arguments. `Apply` creates a `tactic_report` (an extra `-v:10` line) and fails with `fail_if_proof_generation`'s message `"… does not support proof production"`.

**Impact.** Any goal that mixes PB-fragment formulas and other formulas comes out with different contents. In the fuzz case, `p0` is dropped by g3 and kept by z3. Models differ, and `-v`/proof-mode messages differ. I checked whether the C++ behavior is unsound against plain `check-sat` truth. Over 500 random `(then pb-preprocess smt)` scripts, z3 gave the wrong answer 4 times and the current g3 2 times, and both were wrong on the same 2. So the deviation removes some unsound z3 answers, but g3 is unsound on others too. Every other script differs from z3 only in output. One random script (`$S/work/FUZZ_C/gen/pb2/pb_1213.smt2`) segfaults the native z3. This is a real candidate for `z3_bug_exclusions.txt`, but the deviation is not recorded there and has no test vectors.

**Reproduction.** Fuzz script `diff_tactic_ab_1004.smt2`, minimized:
```
(declare-const p0 Bool)
(declare-const v0 (_ BitVec 16))
(declare-const v1 (_ BitVec 16))
(assert (= (bvnot v0) v1))
(assert p0)
(apply pb-preprocess)
```
z3 keeps `(= (bvnot v0) v1)` and `p0`; g3 keeps only `(= (bvnot v0) v1)`. (`m_ge=[1]`, so z3 records goal index 0 for `p0`, and the replacement rewrites formula 0, which does not contain `p0`.)

**Fix.** Verified on ab_1004 and pb1-pb5: stdout and trace identical. Over 1500 random scripts there are 0 differences, against 377 with the current g3. This is a project decision: either mirror the C++ or keep the repair and record it.
To mirror: call `t.classifyVars(r, uint32(i), f)` with the m_ge position. In subsumption, keep one accumulating `pbPreprocessConstraint` per `gi` and append each parsed candidate's terms (bound = latest). Drop the `pureLiteral` checks inside `parse` (they are SASSERTs). In `replace`, stop after `g.Update` once `g.Inconsistent()` is true, because the C++ then reads past the shrunk goal; the result is unobservable and Go would otherwise fail with "arena: vector index or length out of bounds". In `Apply`, remove `NewTacticReport` and throw `tactic.NewTacticException("pb-preprocess does not support proofs")`.
If the repair is kept instead, add the deviating vectors to `z3_bug_exclusions.txt` with a TODO.md entry, and still fix the report line and the message.

**Regression test.** Vector `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/pb_preprocess_mixed_goal.smt2` (the script above), expected `(goals\n(goal\n  (= (bvnot v0) v1)\n  p0\n  :precision precise :depth 1)\n)`. Add `pb_preprocess_proofs_message.smt2` (`(set-option :produce-proofs true)(declare-const p0 Bool)(assert p0)(apply pb-preprocess)`), expected `(error "tactic failed: pb-preprocess does not support proofs")`. Unit test: extend `pb_preprocess_resolve_test.go` using the helpers in `pb_preprocess_test_support_test.go`.

<a id="fuzz-c-f3"></a>
#### FUZZ_C-F3: purify-arith mod handling, fresh-variable order, apply-def argument order, and filter order differ from C++

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/arith/qfnra_purify_tactic.go:165-186` (`ReduceApp`, mod case), `:292` (`newEntryWithFresh`), `pkg/tactic/arith/qfnra_purify_integer_division.go:34-43` (`processIntegerDivision`), `pkg/tactic/arith/qfnra_purify_forward_trig.go:143` (`publishModel`)
- C++: `src/tactic/arith/purify_arith_tactic.cpp:309-368` (`process_idiv`, `process_mod`), `:243-250` (`mk_def_proof`), `:767-778` (filter)

**C++ behavior.** `process_mod` calls `process_idiv(f, …)` with the mod decl. `div_app` is therefore `(mod x y)`: k1 is cached under the mod term and then overwritten by k2. The quotient term is never cached, so a later `(div x y)` creates a fresh k2/k3 pair. `k2 = mk_fresh_int_var()` is created before `mod_app`. `mk_apply_def(k, def, pr1)` yields `(~ k def)`. The filter model converter inserts the values of `m_app2fresh` (an obj_map) in table order, so k1, which was overwritten, is not filtered.

**Go behavior.** For mod, the Go builds `(div x y)` as the definition ("The source passes the modulus declaration as that definition, producing an invalid premise …"), caches both div and mod, and reuses them. It builds `mod` before the fresh k2. `MkProofApplyDef(term, fresh, …)` swaps the arguments. The filter covers every fresh declaration in creation order.

**Impact.** For `purify-arith` (and `(then purify-arith …)`) with `mod`/`rem`: different goals (`(= k!1 k!0)` vs z3's `(= k!1 k!2)` plus a second constraint block), different filter lists, a model that keeps or drops `k!N` (the fuzz divergence), different proof terms (`(~ (div x y) k!00)` vs `(~ k!00 (div x y))`), and different AST ids.

**Reproduction.** `diff_tactic_i_1054.smt2`; minimized:
```
(declare-const x0 Int)
(assert (< (rem x0 0) (+ 7 100 x0)))
(check-sat-using (then purify-arith smt))
(get-model)
```
z3's model contains `(define-fun k!2 () Int 0)`; g3's does not. Also:
`(declare-const x Int)(declare-const y Int)(assert (= (mod x y) (div x y)))(apply purify-arith :print-model-converter true)`: z3 prints 13 formulas and `(filter-model-converter k!2 k!3)`; g3 prints 7 formulas and `(filter-model-converter k!0 k!1)`.

**Fix.** Verified: i_1054 and p1-p9 stdout identical; traces identical for p1, p3, p9, i_1054; 600 random scripts show 0 stdout differences against 41 before.
(a) In `ReduceApp`, remove the `definition := MkFamilyApp(IDiv…)` block and call `i.newEntry(term)` for mod too. `processIntegerDivision` then creates the remainder entry for the same mod term, which overwrites `i.cache[term]` as the C++ does.
(b) In `processIntegerDivision`, create `k2 := MkFreshConstNullable(nil, sort(x))` before building `mod`, and use `newEntryWithFresh(mod, k2, true)`.
(c) `MkProofApplyDef(fresh, term, definition)`.
(d) Keep an `ast.ObjMap` `app2fresh` (term → entry index), updated by `InsertNum` in `newEntryWithFresh`, and in `publishModel` filter the decls of `app2fresh.Entries()` in table order instead of `freshDecls`. The root-object (`root_object_purify_publish.go`) and quantifier paths use the same `freshDecls` list and should get the same treatment.

**Regression test.** Vectors `purify_arith_mod_div_shared.smt2` (the mod/div script above) and `purify_arith_rem_model.smt2` (i_1054 minimized), with z3's outputs. A proof vector `purify_arith_div_proof.smt2` (`produce-proofs`, `(> (div x y) 5)`, `(< (div x y) 3)`, `(check-sat-using (then purify-arith smt))`, `(get-proof)`) covers (c). Unit test in `qfnra_purify_integer_division_test.go`: after rewriting `(mod x y)` the cache maps it to the second fresh constant, and `(div x y)` is not cached.

<a id="fuzz-c-f4"></a>
#### FUZZ_C-F4: qe MBP extract_bools turns the release-compiled SASSERT into an error ("AST source precondition")

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/qe/projection_literals.go:105` and `:166` (`extractNestedBooleans`)
- C++: `src/qe/qe_mbp.cpp:233-257` (`mbp::impl::extract_bools`)

**C++ behavior.**
```
expr_ref val = eval(e);
SASSERT(m.is_true(val) || m.is_false(val));
if (!m_bool_visited.is_marked(e)) fmls.push_back(m.is_true(val) ? e : mk_not(m, e));
...
expr_ref val = eval(tmp);
SASSERT(m.is_true(val) || m.is_false(val));
fmls.push_back(m.is_true(val) ? tmp : mk_not(m, tmp));
```
In the release build the SASSERT does nothing, and any value other than true takes `mk_not`. The value can be non-Boolean-literal when it involves `div0`/`mod0`/`/0` under a partial model, e.g. `(<= (div x0 0) (ite p0 2 3))`. `val`, `tmp` and `sub` are locals of `extract_bools`.

**Go behavior.** `if !m.IsTrue(v) && !m.IsFalse(v) { return found, ast.ErrASTDomain }` at both sites. In addition, the replacer and the evaluated values are held by the call-wide `c` (released only when `extract_literals` returns), and in `qsat_tactic.go` `fml` keeps the abstracted formula alive after `fml = ::mk_and(m_answer)`. Those two lifetime differences change AST id recycling (traces) but not stdout.

**Impact.** `qe2`, `qsat`/`qe_rec` and anything else using MBP fail with `(error "...: g3: AST source precondition")` on formulas where a Boolean atom contains `div`/`mod`/`/` by zero, where z3 answers `sat`/`unsat` or eliminates quantifiers.

**Reproduction.** `diff_tactic_ai_1186.smt2`; minimized:
```
(declare-const p0 Bool)
(declare-const x0 Int)
(assert (<= (div x0 0) (ite p0 2 x0)))
(check-sat-using (then qe2 smt))
```
z3 prints `sat`; g3 prints `(error "line 4 column 31: g3: AST source precondition")`. With `(apply qe2)`, z3 prints `(or (<= (div x0 0) (ite true 2 x0)) (not p0))`, `(or (<= (div x0 0) (ite false 2 x0)) p0)`. The same happens for `mod` and real `/` by 0.

**Fix.** Verified: q3, q5-q9 and ai_1186 have identical stdout and identical traces (27518 lines).
(1) At both sites, delete the check and test `if !m.IsTrue(v)` before negating, with a comment that the SASSERT is compiled out.
(2) Give `extract_bools` its own lifetimes: a local `rewriter.NewExprSafeReplace` closed by defer, each `eval` result held in a ref released at the end of its block, and `tmp` in a local ref released on return.
(3) In `pkg/qe/qsat_tactic.go:316`, after `h = MkAndArray(answers)`, do `t.manager.SetRef(fml, h)` (the C++ `fml = ::mk_and(m_answer)`).
A minimal version of fix (1) alone already makes stdout match; it is saved as `$S/work/FUZZ_C/projection_literals.minimal_fix.go.txt`.

**Regression test.** Vector `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/qe2_div_by_zero_atom.smt2` (above), expected `sat`. Vector `qe2_apply_div_by_zero.smt2` with the `(apply qe2)` form and z3's goal output. Unit test in `pkg/qe` (beside the existing projection tests): `extractLiterals` on `[(<= (div x 0) (ite p 2 3))]` with a model where `p=true` returns the two literals instead of `ErrASTDomain`.

<a id="fuzz-c-f5"></a>
#### FUZZ_C-F5: tactic Exec does not print the `(tactic-exception "...")` verbose line

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/tactic_base.go:438` (`Exec`)
- C++: `src/tactic/tactic.cpp:164-174` (`exec`)

**C++ behavior.** On `tactic_exception`, `IF_VERBOSE(TACTIC_VERBOSITY_LVL, verbose_stream() << "(tactic-exception \"" << escaped(ex.msg()) << "\")" << std::endl;)`, then `cleanup` and rethrow.
**Go behavior.** It cleans up and returns the error without printing.
**Impact.** With `-v:10`, every failing tactic (`fail`, `bvarray2uf` under unsat cores, pb-preprocess under proofs, …) is missing this line on stderr.
**Reproduction.** `(declare-const p Bool)(assert p)(apply fail)(check-sat-using fail)` with `-v:10`: z3 prints `(tactic-exception "fail tactic")` before each error or unknown; g3 prints nothing.
**Fix.** Verified with `-v:10` on that script and on `bvarray2uf` with `:produce-unsat-cores`. In `Exec`, when `errors.As(err, &tacticErr)` and `diagnostic.ProcessVerboseEnabled(tacticVerbosityLevel)`, write `(tactic-exception "` + the message with `"` escaped as `\"` + `")\n` to `diagnostic.BorrowProcessVerboseStream()`, flush, then clean up.
**Regression test.** `pkg/tactic/tactic_base_test.go`: `TestExecVerboseTacticException` sets `diagnostic.SetProcessVerbosityLevel(tacticVerbosityLevel)` (as `tactic_annotate_test.go` does), runs `Exec` on the fail tactic, and expects the line on the captured verbose stream.

<a id="fuzz-c-f6"></a>
#### FUZZ_C-F6: SMT2 parser releases a failed expression frame immediately; C++ keeps the stack until reset()

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed (trace only)
- Go: `pkg/parsers/smt2/expressions.go:215-218` (`expressionFrame`)
- C++: `src/parsers/smt2/smt2parser.cpp:3054-3075` (`operator()` catch path then `reset()`), `:2992-3012`

**C++ behavior.** A `parser_exception` unwinds without shrinking `m_expr_stack`. The command loop then calls `reset()`, which drops the whole stack front to back.
**Go behavior.** On error, `expressionFrame` does `p.exprs.shrink(start)` frame by frame (inner frames first). The same nodes are freed in a different order, so the AST ids recycled afterwards differ.
**Impact.** After any parse error in an expression (an unknown function, or `(_ map bvadd)` without a signature, which the fuzzer produces often), all later `[mk-app] #id`s in the trace differ from z3. That breaks trace comparison for every following command. stdout is unaffected.
**Reproduction.** `$S/work/FUZZ_C/t/pe2.smt2`:
```
(declare-const v0 (_ BitVec 3))
(declare-const v1 (_ BitVec 3))
(declare-fun f ((_ BitVec 3) (_ BitVec 3)) (_ BitVec 3))
(assert (= (f (bvnot v0) (bvadd v0 v1)) (f v1 (undefined_fn v0))))
(assert (= (bvmul v0 v1) (bvor v1 v0)))
```
With `trace=true`, line 43 is `[mk-app] #25 v1` in z3 and `#24 v1` in g3.
**Fix.** Verified: the trace becomes identical (pe2, bva_0021). In `expressionFrame`, return `resultErr` without shrinking. `clearCommand` already resets `p.exprs` front to back.
**Regression test.** A trace-identity vector `parse_error_expr_stack_ids.smt2` (above) in the trace-comparison suite; stdout is z3's two `(error ...)` lines.

<a id="fuzz-c-f7"></a>
#### FUZZ_C-F7: purify-arith division and zero-power constraints are built in left-to-right order

- Severity: low
- Confidence: confirmed (trace only)
- Go: `pkg/tactic/arith/qfnra_purify_tactic.go:359-437` (`processDivision`), `:510-545` (`processPower`, zero exponent)
- C++: `src/tactic/arith/purify_arith_tactic.cpp:297-305, 416-419`

**C++ behavior.** `OR(EQ(y, mk_real_zero()), EQ(u().mk_mul(y, k), x))` evaluates its arguments right to left (GCC): the mul and eq are built before `y = 0`, and each `mk_real_zero()` call is separate. The same applies to `OR(EQ(x,zero), EQ(k,one))`.
**Go behavior.** It builds `y = 0` first and reuses one `yZero` for the second constraint.
**Impact.** Only AST ids, visible in traces.
**Fix.** Verified: purify-arith random-sample trace identity rose from 119/150 to 141/150. Reorder as in the C++ (patch in `fixes.patch`).
**Regression test.** Covered by trace comparison of `purify_arith_mod_div_shared.smt2` plus a `/` vector.

<a id="fuzz-d-f1"></a>
#### FUZZ_D-F1: QF_NIA nlsat route calls the bare nlsat tactic instead of mk_qfnra_nlsat_tactic

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/smtlogics/qfnia_tactic.go:115` (`NewQFNIATacticWithOutput`)
- C++: `src/tactic/smtlogics/qfnia_tactic.cpp:96-108` (`mk_qfnia_nlsat_solver`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
return and_then(using_params(mk_simplify_tactic(m), simp_p),
                try_for(mk_qfnra_nlsat_tactic(m, simp_p), 3000),
                mk_fail_if_undecided_tactic());
```
`mk_qfnra_nlsat_tactic` is the full preprocessing pipeline. It runs simplify, purify-arith
(complete=false, which turns `div0` into an uninterpreted function), propagate-values, solve-eqs,
elim-uncnstr, elim-term-ite, solve-eqs, tseitin-cnf, and only then nlsat.

**Go behavior.**
```go
nlsatSolver := b.using(b.keep(nlsattactic.NewNLSATTactic(m, c, g, nlsatParams, config.ModelEvaluator)), nlsatParams)
```
The Go calls the raw `nlsat` tactic with no purification. A goal that contains `(div x x)` makes
nlsat spin until the 3 s `try_for` fires. The final SMT fallback then answers `unknown`
(incomplete theory arithmetic).

**Impact.** On any QF_NIA script that the bit-blasting and 2 s SMT routes cannot decide, the Go
answers `unknown` (after about 3 s) where z3 answers `sat`/`unsat` at once.

**Reproduction.** (`in1000a.smt2`)
```
(declare-const x0 Int)
(assert (= (+ 6 (div x0 x0)) (* 5 (- 10 x0 x0))))
(check-sat)
(get-model)
```
- z3: `sat`, `x0 = 0`.
- g3: `unknown`, reason "smt tactic failed ... (incomplete (theory arithmetic))".
- With the fix: identical to z3.

**Fix.** In `qfnia_tactic.go`, change the line to
`nlsatSolver := b.keep(NewQFNRANLSATTactic(m, nlsatParams, config))`, keep it wrapped in
`b.timed(..., 3000)`, and drop the `nlsattactic` import. `NewQFNRANLSATTactic` already reads
`factor=false` from the params, as the C++ does.

**Regression test.** Add `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/qfnia_nlsat_div_self.smt2` with the script above.
Expected output: `sat` followed by `(model \n  (define-fun x0 () Int\n    0)\n)`. Add it to the
`scriptResults` table in `pkg/cmd/g3/main_test.go`, and run the C++ cross-check with
`G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`.

<a id="fuzz-d-f4"></a>
#### FUZZ_D-F4: hoist_multiplication is not a port of poly_rewriter::hoist_multiplication / merge_muls

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/ast/rewriter/arith_polynomial.go:279-370` (`hoistCommonMultiplication`), call site `:618`
- C++: `src/ast/rewriter/poly_rewriter_def.h:903-972`, call sites `:626` and `:658`

**C++ behavior.** The C++ uses `TO_BUFFER` to flatten nested `+` and `*` (it replaces slot i with
`arg0` and appends the remaining arguments). Numerals are skipped. `merge_muls` swaps the common
factors to the front of both factor lists and builds `(* common... (+ rest1 rest2))`. Hoisting runs
on the finished sum built by `mk_add_app`. So `(+ (* 3 x x) (* 2 x))` becomes
`(* x (+ 2 (* 3 x)))`.

**Go behavior.** The Go uses only the top-level arguments of `*`, without the TO_BUFFER
flattening. Its merge matches factors differently: it keeps the left order, does not swap, and
only removes the first match from the right. It runs on `resultArgs` before `makeAdd`. The result is
that the Go leaves `(+ (* 3 x x) (* 2 x))` unhoisted, and differs on `(+ (* 3 x y) (* 2 x))`.

**Impact.** Under `hoist_mul=true` (the qfnia nla2bv route) the Go builds different terms, so the
nla2bv/bit-blast encoding differs and so does the model (in_1158).

**Reproduction.** (`hoist1.smt2`)
```
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(simplify (+ (* 3 (* x x)) (* 2 x)) :hoist_mul true)
(simplify (+ (* 3 x y) (* 2 x)) :hoist_mul true)
```
- z3: `(* x (+ 2 (* 3 x)))` and `(* x (+ 2 (* 3 y)))`.
- g3: `(+ (* 3 x x) (* 2 x))` and `(+ (* 3 x y) (* 2 x))`.

`diff_check_in_1158.smt2`:
- z3 model: `x0 = -18`. g3 model: `x0 = -30`.
- With F4+F5 fixed: same model, identical trace.

**Fix.** Replace `hoistCommonMultiplication` with a literal port of the C++, operating on one
`som` handle:
- `toBuffer(kind, e)`: the TO_BUFFER macro.
- `mergeMuls(x, y)`: swaps into position k, then `makeMul(m1[k:])` and `makeMul(m2[k:])`, `makeAdd` of the two, and `makeMul(m1[:k+1])`.
- `hoistCommonMultiplication(som)`: a `mulMap`, a `valid` slice, `adds[k] = 0`, then `makeAdd(adds)`.

In `rewriteAdd`, build `result := makeAdd(resultArgs)` first, then call
`hoistCommonMultiplication(result)` and return `RewriteFull` on change. The full working patch is in
`$S/work/FUZZ_D/patches/ast_rewriter_arith_polynomial.go.patch`.

**Regression test.**
- Add `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/hoist_mul.smt2` with `hoist1.smt2`. Its expected output is the z3 lines in `$S/work/FUZZ_D/.o.z3`; regenerate it with `build/z3`.
- Add `diff_check_in_1158.smt2` as a model vector with expected `x0 = (- 18)`, `p0 = false`.
- Add a unit test `TestHoistMultiplicationMatchesSource` in the `ast/rewriter` arith tests. It should run `(+ (* 3 x x) (* 2 x))` with `hoist_mul` set and expect `(* x (+ 2 (* 3 x)))`.

<a id="fuzz-d-f5"></a>
#### FUZZ_D-F5: bv2int mk_bv_mul keeps intermediate extensions alive (AST id order)

- Severity: high (changes the model in combination with F4)
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/arith/bv2int_rewriter.go:545-553` (`bv2IntCall.mulBV`)
- C++: `src/tactic/arith/bv2int_rewriter.cpp:371-410` (`bv2int_rewriter::mk_bv_mul`)

**C++ behavior.** `expr_ref s1(s), t1(t); align_sizes(s1,t1); s1 = mk_extend(...); t1 = mk_extend(...)`.
Each assignment releases the previous extension, and the locals die at return. The freed ids are
then reused by the next `mk_app`.

**Go behavior.** `s, t = c.align(s, t, signed)` followed by `c.extend(...)` keeps every intermediate
in the call's `refs` until the whole reduction ends. So a different id is recycled: for example
`zero_extend #54` gets #74 instead of #66. `addBV` already uses `newLocal`/`assignLocal` for exactly
this reason; `mulBV` does not.

**Impact.** Fresh AST ids differ, so hash-table and arith variable order differ, so search and model
can differ (in_1158, together with F4).

**Reproduction.** `diff_check_in_1158.smt2` with only F4 applied: the trace first differs at
`[mk-app] #66 zero_extend #54` (z3) vs `#74` (g3). With F5 applied: the trace is byte-identical.

**Fix.** Use the `addBV` pattern:
- `s1, t1 := c.newLocal(s), c.newLocal(t)`
- `defer c.releaseLocals(&t1, &s1)`
- `c.alignLocals(&s1, &t1, signed)`
- `c.assignLocal(&s1, c.extend(extra, c.localValue(s1), signed))`, and the same for t1
- then use `c.localValue(s1)` and `c.localValue(t1)` for the side conditions and `bvmul`.

**Regression test.** Use the `diff_check_in_1158.smt2` vector from F4. The full trace comparison
(`trace=true`) in `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference` catches this one.

<a id="fuzz-d-f6"></a>
#### FUZZ_D-F6: mk_mod_core `arg1 == arg2` builds (mod 0 0) before abs (construction order)

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed (trace)
- Go: `pkg/ast/rewriter/arith_rewriter.go:691-721` (`ArithRewriter.rewriteMod`)
- C++: `src/ast/rewriter/arith_rewriter.cpp:820-825` (`mk_mod_core`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
mk_abs_core(arg2, abs);
result = m().mk_ite(m().mk_eq(arg2, zero), m_util.mk_mod(zero, zero), abs);
```
The abs is built first. GCC then evaluates the `mk_ite` arguments right to left, so `mk_mod(0,0)` is
built before `mk_eq`.

**Go behavior.** The Go builds `undefined := mod(0,0)` before `rewriteAbs`. In
`diff_check_in_1000`, `#66..#69` come out in a different order.

**Impact.** AST ids are permuted, so later search order can differ. With F1 fixed, the output of
in_1000 did not change, but the trace did.

**Fix.** Move the `r.app(arithOpMod, zero, zero)` call to after the `rewriteAbs`/`RefGet` block, and
keep `MkEq` after it. With this change the trace matched up to the later id-recycling difference.

**Regression test.** Run `diff_check_in_1000.smt2` (or in1000a above) through the trace-comparing
C++ reference runner. The output-only vector is covered by F1.

<a id="fuzz-f-f1"></a>
#### FUZZ_F-F1: spacer `ExpandObligation` l_undef branch calls create_children on a fact rule (no uninterpreted tail)

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/muz/spacer/predicate_expand.go:208` (`PredicateTransformer.ExpandObligation`, `default:` case)
- C++: `src/muz/spacer/spacer_context.cpp:2993` (`context::expand_node`, `case l_undef`)

**C++ behavior.**
```
if (r && r->get_uninterpreted_tail_size() > 0) {
    ... has_new_child = create_children(n,*r,mev,reach_pred_used);
}
if (has_new_child) { return l_undef; }
n.bump_weakness(); return expand_node(n);
```

**Go behavior.**
```
if check.Rule != nil && check.Model != nil {
    reachPredUsed := make([]bool, len(check.ReachPredUsed))
    child, childErr := p.CreateDerivationChild(obligation, check.Rule, check.Model, ...)
    if childErr != nil { return ExpansionResult{}, childErr }
```
The tail-size guard is missing. Under weak abstraction (`arith.ignore_int`), the check of an initial-rule
obligation returns l_undef with the fact rule selected. `createDerivationChildWith` then finds no predecessors
and returns `ast.ErrASTDomain` (`predicate_derivation.go:52-53`), and the query aborts.

**Impact.** Any spacer query whose weak (w=0) check of a level-0 obligation comes back unknown on an initial rule.
g3 prints `(error "...: g3: AST source precondition")` where z3 answers. This is a wrong result (error instead of sat).

**Reproduction.** `diff_arith-spacer_177.smt2` is already minimal for this path; removing any rule changes the search.
```
(set-option :fixedpoint.engine spacer)
(declare-rel q0 (Int Int))
(declare-rel err ())
(declare-var x Int)
(declare-var y Int)
(declare-var x1 Int)
(declare-var y1 Int)
(rule (=> (and (= x 3) (= y 1)) (q0 x y)))
(rule (=> (and (q0 x y) (= x1 (- y 3)) (= y1 (- x 1))) (q0 x1 y1)))
(rule (=> (and (q0 x y) (= x1 (+ y y)) (= y1 (+ x x))) (q0 x1 y1)))
(rule (=> (and (q0 x y) (>= x y) (= x1 y) (= y1 2)) (q0 x1 y1)))
(rule (=> (and (q0 x y) (= y 9) (= x1 y) (= y1 (+ x 1))) (q0 x1 y1)))
(rule (=> (and (q0 x y) (= y 9)) err))
(query err :print-certificate true)
```
z3: `sat`. g3 (g3fix5): `(error "line 14 column 34: g3: AST source precondition")`.
The `G3_ERRSTACK=1` frame is `muz/spacer/predicate_derivation.go:53` <- `predicate_expand.go:210`.
z3 `-v:1` shows `create_child: q0 (0, 4) FAR 1 UNDEF` followed by `w(1) ... T`; that is the bump-weakness path.

**Fix (verified).** In the `default:` branch, compute `UninterpretedTailSize()` of `check.Rule` and require it to be > 0:
```go
uninterpretedTail := 0
if check.Rule != nil {
    if uninterpretedTail, err = check.Rule.UninterpretedTailSize(); err != nil { return ExpansionResult{}, err }
}
if check.Rule != nil && uninterpretedTail > 0 && check.Model != nil { ... }
```
With this change g3 prints `sat` and its output is byte-identical to z3.

**Regression test.** Add `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/spacer_undef_fact_rule.smt2` (the script above) with expected output
`sat` in the `scriptResults` table of `pkg/cmd/g3/main_test.go`. Check it against the C++ with
`G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`.

<a id="fuzz-f-f2"></a>
#### FUZZ_F-F2: spacer weak-abstraction parameter override is scoped to the solver check, not to all of `expand_node`

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed (trace)
- Go: `pkg/muz/spacer/predicate_reachability.go:154-163` (`CheckReachability` passes `WeakAbstraction`/`Weakness` to `PropSolver.CheckAssumptions`, which applies `scopedWeakAbstraction`, `prop_solver.go:441`)
- C++: `src/muz/spacer/spacer_context.cpp:2873-2876` (`context::expand_node` `flet`s on `m_arith_ignore_int` / `m_array_weak`)

**C++ behavior.** The `flet`s cover the whole of `expand_node`. That includes the lemma generalizers and `add_lemma`
in the l_false branch, `create_children`, and the recursive `expand_node` after `bump_weakness`.
`is_reachable` called from `context::is_reachable` (`spacer_context.cpp:2760`) is not covered and runs with the user's setting.

**Go behavior.** The override is pushed and popped around the single `CheckAssumptions` inside `CheckReachability`.
Generalizer and lemma-propagation solver calls therefore run with `arith.ignore_int=false`, where the C++ uses `true`.
`confirmConcreteReachability` (`search.go:54`), which also calls `CheckReachability`, gets the override, where the C++ does not.

**Impact.** Different SMT search in inductive generalization: different lemmas, rlimit and trace.
With F1 applied, `diff_arith-spacer_177.smt2` gives z3's answer, but the trace diverged at line 36459 and the rlimit
was 312876 against z3's 474193.

**Reproduction.** The spacer script above with `trace=true trace_file_name=...`. After the fix the first divergence moves
from line 36459 to line 106255 (of 3.70M lines). That remaining divergence is FUZZ_F-F6.

**Fix (verified for trace progress).** Apply `p.solver.scopedWeakAbstraction(p.solver.contexts[0], p.weakAbstraction, weakness)`
at the top of `ExpandObligation` and restore it in a defer. Use the weakness read on entry; the recursive call after
`BumpWeakness` installs its own scope, as the nested C++ `flet` does. Drop `WeakAbstraction`/`Weakness` from the
`CheckReachability` options so the confirm path runs unweakened.

**Regression test.** Extend `pkg/muz/spacer` tests (next to the existing `predicate_expand` tests). Expand a weakness-0
obligation whose l_false branch runs a generalizer, and assert that the backend's `arith.ignore_int` parameter reads
true inside the generalizer callback and false after return. The C++ trace comparison on the vector from F1 also covers it.

<a id="fuzz-f-f3"></a>
#### FUZZ_F-F3: pdr walks `p.rules` (rule order) where the C++ walks `m_tag2rule` (obj_map hash order)

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/muz/pdr/predicate_rules.go:19` (`selectRule`), `:804` (`makeAssumptions`), `:867` (`makeAssumptionRefs`), `:978` (`PropagationFormula`)
- C++: `src/muz/pdr/pdr_context.cpp:151` (`find_rule`), `:242` (`get_propagation_formula`), `:491` (`mk_assumptions`)

**C++ behavior.** All four iterate `obj_map<expr, rule const*> m_tag2rule`, whose order follows the tags' hashes.
`find_rule` returns the first rule whose tag is true in the model.

**Go behavior.** All four iterate `p.rules` in insertion order. Spacer already has the right emulation
(`muz/spacer/predicate_rules.go:972` `tagTableRules`, commit 67e9abb2e); pdr does not.

**Impact.** When a model makes more than one tag true, a different rule is selected, so the search takes a different path.
The child-property assumptions are also asserted in a different order, which changes the AST ids, the SMT search and
the `:print-certificate` trace. This is the cause of the `diff_arith-pdr_177.smt2` difference.

**Reproduction.** `diff_arith-pdr_177.smt2` (the rules of F1 with `fixedpoint.engine pdr`).
z3 prints `(= (:var 21) (+ (- 3) (:var 24))) (q0 4 (:var 24)) (= (:var 24) (- 4)) (q0 (- 2) 2)`.
g3 prints `(= (:var 21) (- 1)) (q0 4 2) (q0 1 2)`.
The first trace difference is `[mk-app] #480 => #156 #482` (z3) against `=> #150 #482` (g3): the tag order of `mk_assumptions`.

**Fix (verified together with F4 and F5).** Add `func (p *PredicateTransformer) tagTableRules() ([]*normalizedRule, error)`
to pdr, a copy of the spacer helper (an `ast.NewObjMap` filled with the tags in rule order, read back with `Entries()`).
Use its result instead of `p.rules` in `selectRule` (including its single-rule shortcut), `makeAssumptions`,
`makeAssumptionRefs` and `PropagationFormula`. `selectInitialRule` and `Premises` do not correspond to `m_tag2rule`
walks; check them against their C++ call sites.

**Regression test.** Add `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/pdr_tag_order_certificate.smt2` (`diff_arith-pdr_177.smt2`) with the
15-line z3 certificate as the expected output. Also add a unit test in `pkg/muz/pdr/predicate_rules_test.go`: build a
transformer with 3 or more tagged rules and assert that `tagTableRules` matches the order of `ast.ObjMap.Entries`.

<a id="fuzz-f-f4"></a>
#### FUZZ_F-F4: `qe.EqualityDER` drops the `m_subst_map` / `m_new_args` member lifetimes

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed (trace)
- Go: `pkg/qe/equality_der_conjunctions.go:298` (`createSubstitution`), `pkg/qe/equality_der_quantifier.go:38` (`applyQuantifierSubstitution`)
- C++: `src/qe/qe_lite.cpp:441-453` (`create_substitution`), `:475-479` (`apply_substitution`), members `:78-79`

**C++ behavior.** `m_subst_map` (`expr_ref_vector`) and `m_new_args` (`expr_ref_buffer`) are members of `eq::der`.
They keep the substituted terms and the kept conjuncts alive after `reduce_quantifier` returns, until the next call
resets them or the der is destroyed. In `create_substitution`, `cur` and `r` are locals that die each iteration.

**Go behavior.** The substitutions are held in per-call `c.refs` and released when the call finishes. `remaining`
is a plain slice. Terms therefore die earlier, ids are recycled, and later AST ids differ: z3 `[mk-app] #481 and #709`
against g3 `#301 and #709` in pdr qe-lite projection.

**Impact.** AST-id and trace divergence in every qe_lite user (pdr create_children, tab, rule inliner, duality).
The ids feed hash-table orders, so outputs can differ downstream.

**Reproduction.** `diff_arith-pdr_177.smt2` with F3 applied: the trace diverges at line 27246 (QE quantifier projection).
With this fix the divergence moves on to line 43775 (F5).

**Fix (verified for trace progress).** Add `substMap, newArgs []ast.ASTRef` fields to `EqualityDER`.
`createSubstitution` releases `substMap` front to back, then resizes it. Each binding is computed with scoped
`cur`/`r` refs and stored as a new ref in `substMap[inx]`. `applyQuantifierSubstitution` resets `newArgs` and then
`NewRef`s each kept argument. `Close` releases `newArgs` and then `substMap` after the rewriter (reverse member order).
The full patch is in `$S/work/FUZZ_F/pkg/qe/equality_der*.go`.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/qe` (next to the existing equality_der tests), run `ReduceQuantifier` on `(exists x. (and (= x t) (p x)))`.
Then assert that the substituted term `t'` keeps a nonzero ref count after the call (`m.GetRefCount`) and is released by `Close`.

<a id="fuzz-f-f5"></a>
#### FUZZ_F-F5: pdr `FarkasLearner.proofPostOrder` visits proof parents first-to-last; the C++ finishes the last parent first

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/muz/pdr/farkas_learner.go:311` (`proofPostOrder`)
- C++: `src/muz/pdr/pdr_farkas_learner.cpp:700-720` (`farkas_learner::get_lemmas` todo loop)

**C++ behavior.** It pushes the unvisited parents `0..n-1` onto `todo` and processes `todo.back()`, so the subtree of the
last parent is finished first. The lemmas are `INSERT`ed in that post-order.

**Go behavior.** The parents are pushed `n-1..0`, so parent 0 is finished first. The lemma list comes out in another order:
z3 `(>= q0_1_n 9) ; (not (>= q0_1_n 14)) ; (not (<= q0_0_n 8))` against g3 `(not (<= q0_0_n 8)) ; (>= q0_1_n 9) ; ...`.
The resulting cores and generalizations differ, and so does the search.

**Impact.** Together with F3 this is the pdr_177 certificate difference. Fixing F3 alone did not fix the output; adding F5 did.

**Reproduction.** `diff_arith-pdr_177.smt2`. With F3, F4 and F5 applied, the g3 certificate is byte-identical to z3.
The trace matches up to line 140886.

**Fix (verified).** In `proofPostOrder`, push the parents with `for i := uint32(0); i < count; i++`.

**Regression test.** Covered by the `pdr_tag_order_certificate.smt2` vector of F3. Also add a unit test in
`pkg/muz/pdr/farkas_learner_test.go`: a th-lemma with two B-pure Farkas parents, asserting the lemma order is last-parent-first.

<a id="fuzz-g-f1"></a>
#### FUZZ_G-F1: `concatTerm`/`assertFlattenedConcatLength` creates the leaf lengths before `str.len(concat)`

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/theory_str_terms.go:192-247` (`assertFlattenedConcatLength`, called from `concatTerm` :189)
- C++: `src/smt/theory_str.cpp:813-827` (`theory_str::mk_concat`)

**C++ behavior.**
```
expr_ref concat_length(mk_strlen(concatAst), m);
ptr_vector<expr> childrenVector; get_nodes_in_concat(concatAst, childrenVector);
for (auto el : childrenVector) items.push_back(mk_strlen(el));
expr_ref lenAssert(ctx.mk_eq_atom(concat_length, m_autil.mk_add(...)), m);
```
`str.len(concat)` is created first, then the length of each leaf.

**Go behavior.** The function walks the leaves and builds their `str.len` terms first, and only then calls `m.MkSequenceLength(expression)` (line 225).

**Impact.** Every fresh concatenation gets different AST ids, e.g. `#44 str.len (str.++ ...)` vs `#44 str.len ts1`. This is the first difference in the trace of `(str.contains s0 "abc")`. It changes later id-ordered choices.

**Reproduction.** Line 96 of the `trace=true` log of `m1.smt2` (below): z3 `[mk-app] #44 str.len #43`, g3 `[mk-app] #44 str.len #42`. Fixed together with F2; see F2 for the outputs.
