<a id="smtcore-02-f1"></a>
#### smtcore_02-F1: `NextCaseSplit` lets the queue's phase override the quantifier rule

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_case_split_queue.go:152-158` (`(*SMTActivityCaseSplitQueue).NextCaseSplit`)
- C++: `src/smt/smt_context.cpp:1836-1845` (`context::decide`)

**C++ behavior.** The quantifier test comes first and overrides any phase the
queue returned:
```cpp
if (is_quantifier(m_bool_var2expr[var])) {
    // Overriding any decision on how to assign the quantifier.
    phase = l_false;
}
if (phase != l_undef) { is_pos = phase == l_true; }
else { bool_var_data & d = m_bdata[var]; if (d.try_true_first()) ...
```

**Go behavior.** The queue's phase returns before the quantifier test:
```go
if preferred != lbool.Undef {
    return next, preferred, nil
}
data := &q.state.booleanData[next]
if data.IsQuantifier() {
    return next, lbool.False, nil
}
```
The relevancy queues (strategies 3, 4, 5) return `l_true` for a positive
AND/OR child (`relevantCandidate`), so a quantifier child is decided true.

**Impact.** Any run with `smt.case_split=3|4|5` (auto_config off, relevancy 2)
whose OR/AND has an unassigned quantifier child. C++ makes the quantifier
false (irrelevant); Go asserts it and starts instantiating.

**Reproduction.** `$S/work/smtcore_02/cs3_quant_vec.smt2`:
```
(set-option :auto_config false)
(set-option :smt.case_split 3)
(declare-fun f (Int) Int)
(declare-const p Bool)
(assert (or (forall ((x Int)) (> (f x) x)) p))
(check-sat)
(get-value (p))
```
z3: `sat` / `((p true))` at once (1 decision). g3: no answer in 20 s
(`timeout 20` kills it). With `trace=true`, z3 logs
`[assign] (not #42) decision axiom`, g3 logs `[assign] #42 decision axiom`
followed by `[instance]` lines. Same result with `:smt.case_split 4` and `5`.

**Fix.** In `NextCaseSplit`, move the quantifier test above the preferred-phase
return, keeping the rest of the order (`try_true_first`, then phase selection):
```go
data := &q.state.booleanData[next]
if data.IsQuantifier() {
    return next, lbool.False, nil
}
if preferred != lbool.Undef {
    return next, preferred, nil
}
if data.TryTrueFirst() { ... }
```
No other caller consumes the phase.

**Regression test.** Add `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/case_split_relevancy_quantifier_phase.smt2`
with the input above and `scriptResults` entry
`"sat\n((p true))\n"`; add two more vectors with `:smt.case_split 4` and `5`
(same expected text). `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run
TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3` checks them against C++. Unit level:
extend `smtcore/smt_case_split_queue_test.go` next to
`TestSMTRelevantCaseSplitQueueSelectsConnectiveChild` (it uses
`smtInternalizerFixture`, `smtRelevancyBool`, `NewSMTActivityCaseSplitQueue`,
`ConfigurePhases(SMTParamsState{CaseSplitStrategy: 3, RelevancyLvl: 2})`):
`TestSMTRelevantCaseSplitQueueQuantifierChildDecidedFalse` builds
`(or q b)` with `q` a quantifier, marks the OR true and relevant, and expects
`NextCaseSplit()` to return `(var(q), lbool.False)`.

<a id="smtcore-02-f2"></a>
#### smtcore_02-F2: congruence table matches flat-associative binary applications modulo commutativity

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_cg_table.go:74-81` (`(*smtCongruenceBucket).find`), `:318-332` (`FindApp`)
- C++: `src/smt/smt_cg_table.cpp:156-186` (`cg_table::mk_table_for`), `:138-146` (`cg_table::cg_eq::operator()`)

**C++ behavior.** The table kind is chosen from the declaration; a
flat-associative binary declaration gets the n-ary table, whose equality is
positional. Only non-flat commutative declarations get `comm_table`:
```cpp
case 2:
    if (d->is_flat_associative()) {
        // applications of declarations that are flat-assoc (e.g., +) may have many arguments.
        r = TAG(void*, alloc(table), NARY);
    }
    else if (d->is_commutative()) {
        r = TAG(void*, alloc(comm_table, cg_comm_hash(), cg_comm_eq(m_commutativity)), BINARY_COMM);
```

**Go behavior.** The swapped key is probed for every two-argument node whose
declaration is commutative, flat-associative or not:
```go
if node.commutative && len(node.arguments) == 2 && key[0] != key[1] {
    if candidate := b.small[[2]*SMTEnode{key[1], key[0]}]; candidate != nil {
        congruent, commuted, err := SMTEnodesCongruent(candidate, node)
```
(`node.commutative` is `len(args) == 2 && flags.Commutative`,
`smt_enode_core.go:129`.)

**Impact.** `(+ a b)`/`(* a b)`-style enodes with congruence enabled and
arguments kept: `theory_diff_logic`, `theory_utvpi` (`mk_enode(n, false,
false, true)`), i.e. `smt.arith.solver=1`/UTVPI. Go derives `(+ a b) = (+ d c)`
when `a~c, b~d`; C++ does not. The answer changes.

**Reproduction.** `$S/work/smtcore_02/cg_flat_assoc_comm.smt2`:
```
(set-option :auto_config false)
(set-option :smt.arith.solver 1)
(declare-sort U 0)
(declare-const u1 U)
(declare-const u2 U)
(declare-const w1 U)
(declare-const w2 U)
(declare-const q Bool)
(declare-const r Bool)
(declare-fun h (U) Int)
(declare-fun g (Int) Int)
(assert (or (= u1 w1) q))
(assert (or (= u1 w1) (not q)))
(assert (or (= u2 w2) r))
(assert (or (= u2 w2) (not r)))
(assert (not (= (g (+ (h u1) (h u2))) (g (+ (h w2) (h w1))))))
(check-sat)
```
z3: `unknown` (reason `(incomplete (theory difference-logic))`, 0 conflicts).
g3: `unsat` (6 conflicts). Control: with the last sum written
`(+ (h w1) (h w2))` both print `unsat` with identical statistics. The trace
logs first differ where g3 assigns the `(= (g ..) (g ..))` atom from the two
equalities.

**Fix.** Record flat-associativity per bucket and use positional matching for
it. In `ensureTable` read `GetFuncDeclFlags(node.declaration)` once and store
`flatAssociative` in `smtCongruenceBucket`; in `find` change the guard to
`if node.commutative && !b.flatAssociative && len(node.arguments) == 2 && key[0] != key[1]`.
The exact-key probe already reports `commuted == false`. `FindApp` goes
through the same `find`; it needs no separate change once the bucket carries
the flag. Leave `SMTEnodesCongruent` itself alone: it is the port of
`smt::congruent()`.

**Regression test.** Extend `smtcore/smt_cg_table_test.go`:
`TestSMTCongruenceTableFlatAssociativeBinaryIsPositional`, built like
`TestSMTCongruenceTableExactCommutativeInsertFindEraseReset` with
`smtCGTestDeclaration(t, manager, id, sort, ast.ASTFuncFlags{Commutative: true, FlatAssociative: true})`,
`smtEnodeConstant`, `smtCGTestApplication`: insert `ab`, then
`table.Insert(ba)` must return `ba` itself with `Commuted == false`, and
`table.Find(ba)` on a table holding only `ab` must return nil. Vector:
`pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/cg_table_flat_assoc_commutative.smt2` with the input
above, `scriptResults` value `"unknown\n"`; checked against C++ by
`G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`.

<a id="smtcore-02-f5"></a>
#### smtcore_02-F5: `occurrencePhase` counts packed binary clauses

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_case_split_queue.go:111-131` (`occurrencePhase`)
- C++: `src/smt/smt_context.cpp:1874-1877` (`context::decide`, `PS_OCCURRENCE`), `src/smt/smt_internalizer.cpp:1313-1320,1378-1379` (`mk_clause`)

**C++ behavior.** `is_pos = m_lit_occs[l.index()].size() > m_lit_occs[(~l).index()].size();`
`m_lit_occs` holds clause objects only: `add_lit_occs(cls)` is reached after
the `use_binary_clause_opt` branch has returned, so watch-only binary clauses
are never counted.

**Go behavior.**
```go
for i := range q.state.clauses {
	record := &q.state.clauses[i]
	literals := record.Literals
	if record.clause != nil { literals = record.clause.literals }
	for _, literal := range literals { ... positive++ / negative++ }
```
Records with `record.Binary` (no clause object) are counted too. The scan is
also O(all literals) per decision where C++ is O(1).

**Impact.** Every decision under `smt.phase_selection=6` on a variable that
occurs in a binary clause.

**Reproduction.** `$S/work/smtcore_02/ps6_vec.smt2`:
```
(set-option :auto_config false)
(set-option :smt.phase_selection 6)
(declare-fun P (Int) Bool)
(assert (or (P 1) (P 3) (P 4)))
(assert (or (not (P 1)) (P 5)))
(assert (or (not (P 1)) (P 6)))
(check-sat)
(get-value ((P 1) (P 3) (P 4) (P 5) (P 6)))
```
z3: `(P 1) false, (P 3) false, (P 4) true, (P 5) false, (P 6) false`.
g3: all five `true`. Log: z3 decides `(not #35)` (`(P 6)`, no counted
occurrence), g3 decides `#35`. Phase selections 0-5 are identical on both
binaries for the same kind of input.

**Fix.** Skip watch-only records: `if record.Binary || record.clause == nil { continue }`
at the top of the loop. Better, keep two counters per literal maintained at
the points where C++ touches `m_lit_occs` (clause creation and deletion,
`simplify_clause` literal removal, `reinit_clauses`), enabled only when
`PhaseSelection == 6`, and compare them here.

**Regression test.** Vector
`pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/phase_selection_occurrence_binary.smt2` with the
input above; `scriptResults` value
`"sat\n(((P 1) false)\n ((P 3) false)\n ((P 4) true)\n ((P 5) false)\n ((P 6) false))\n"`;
`G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`.
Unit: in `smtcore/smt_case_split_queue_test.go` near
`TestSMTActivityCaseSplitQueueHonorsConfiguredAndCachedPhases`, add a binary
clause `(or v w)` and a ternary clause containing `(not v)` and expect phase
`False` for `v` with `PhaseSelection: 6`.

<a id="smtcore-02-f7"></a>
#### smtcore_02-F7: `GetConsequences` rebuilds `m_var2val` for every call; C++ keeps the table and its capacity

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_consequences.go:479` (`(*SMTKernel).GetConsequences`)
- C++: `src/smt/smt_consequences.cpp:283,361-364` (`context::get_consequences`), `src/smt/smt_context.h:1427` (`m_var2val`), `src/util/hashtable.h:286-308` (`core_hashtable::reset`)

**C++ behavior.** `m_var2val` is a context member. `m_var2val.reset()` frees
the slots but keeps the capacity (halving it only when more than 3/4 of a
table larger than 16 was free). The chunk loop, `delete_unfixed` and
`extract_fixed_eqs` iterate the table in slot order, so a later call iterates
in the order given by the capacity an earlier call left behind.

**Go behavior.** `var2val: newSeqObjHashtable(m)` — a new table of the
initial capacity on every call.

**Impact.** Second and later `get-consequences` calls on one solver: the order
in which variables are tested, hence the order of the reported consequences
and the search, differs from C++. All consequences are still reported.

**Reproduction.** `python3 gen_conseq.py 24 8 > conseq_reuse_24_8.smt2`
(generator and file in `$S/work/smtcore_02/`; 24 variables `w_i` with
`(assert (or w_i (g w_i)))`, 8 variables `v_i` each forced by four ternary
clauses over `t_i,u_i`, then `(get-consequences (a) (w0 ... w23))` and
`(get-consequences (a) (v0 ... v7))`). Second answer:
z3 `v0 v2 v3 v4 v1 v5 v6 v7`, g3 `v0 v2 v4 v3 v1 v5 v6 v7`. With the first
`get-consequences` line removed both print the same order; the difference
also shows for first-call sizes 27, 48, 50, 60 and 70.

**Fix.** Make the table a field of the kernel (next to `lastSearch`), created
once, and at the top of `GetConsequences` call a new
`(*seqObjHashtable).reset()` that ports `core_hashtable::reset` exactly
(count free slots, mark the rest free, halve the capacity when
`capacity > 16 && overhead*4 > capacity*3`, zero size and deleted count).
Tombstones from `remove` must stay until that reset, as in C++.

**Regression test.** Vector
`pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/get_consequences_table_reuse.smt2` = the generated
109-line file; `scriptResults` value = z3's output (second list
`(=> true v0) (=> true v2) (=> true v3) (=> true v4) (=> true v1) (=> true v5)
(=> true v6) (=> true v7)`, one per line); the existing
`get_consequences.smt2` entry shows the format.
`G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`.

<a id="smtcore-02-f8"></a>
#### smtcore_02-F8: proof of an extended theory equality propagation states `(= lhs rhs)` instead of `mk_eq_atom(lhs, rhs)`

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_conflict_proof.go:799` (`objectProof`, case `*SMTExtTheoryEqualityPropagationJustification`)
- C++: `src/smt/smt_justification.cpp:370` (`ext_theory_eq_propagation_justification::mk_proof`)

**C++ behavior.** `expr * fact = ctx.mk_eq_atom(m_lhs->get_owner(), m_rhs->get_owner());`
(smaller id first; numerals right for arithmetic).

**Go behavior.** `fact, e := b.state.manager.MkEq(value.Left.owner, value.Right.owner)`.

**Impact.** `(get-proof)` text whenever the propagating theory passes the
pair with the larger id first (arithmetic fixed-variable equalities, seq,
datatype): the `th-lemma` conclusion is reversed and the `symm` step C++ adds
afterwards is missing. The proof stays valid.

**Reproduction.** `$S/work/smtcore_02/pfx_1.smt2`:
```
(set-option :produce-proofs true)
(set-logic QF_UFLIA)
(declare-fun f (Int) Int)
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(declare-const p Bool)
(assert (or (not p) (<= y 5)))
(assert (or (not p) (>= y 5)))
(assert (or (not p) (<= x 5)))
(assert (or (not p) (>= x 5)))
(assert (or (not p) (not (= (f x) (f y)))))
(assert (or p (<= y 6)))
(assert (or p (>= y 6)))
(assert (or p (<= x 6)))
(assert (or p (>= x 6)))
(assert (or p (not (= (f y) (f x)))))
(check-sat)
(get-proof)
```
z3: `((_ th-lemma arith eq-propagate 0 0 0 0) ... (= y x))` then
`(monotonicity (symm @x97 (= x y)) $x42)`. g3: `... (= x y))` then
`(monotonicity @x97 $x42)`. 26 differing lines.

**Fix.** Replace the `MkEq` call by `b.state.MkEqAtom(value.Left.owner, value.Right.owner)`.
`normalizeEqualityProof` already adds the symmetry step when the fact is
reversed with respect to the edge.

**Regression test.** Vector
`pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/proof_eq_propagate_atom_order.smt2` with the input
above and the z3 output as the `scriptResults` value
(`G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`).
Unit: in `smtcore/smt_conflict_proof_test.go` build a
`NewSMTExtTheoryEqualityPropagationJustification(..., left, right, nil)` with
`id(left.owner) > id(right.owner)` and assert the proof fact is
`(= right left)`.

<a id="smtcore-02-f9"></a>
#### smtcore_02-F9: `smt.case_split=6` uses the configured phase selection; the reference build always decides negative

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_case_split_queue.go:191-193` (`selectVariable`, strategy 6 returns `lbool.Undef`)
- C++: `src/smt/smt_case_split_queue.cpp:1165-1188` (`theory_aware_branching_queue::next_case_split`), `src/smt/smt_context.cpp:1808-1810`

**C++ behavior.** `decide` declares `lbool phase;` without a value and the
theory-aware queue returns without writing it:
```cpp
while (!m_queue.empty()) {
    next = m_queue.erase_min();
    if (m_context.get_assignment(next) == l_undef)
        return;
}
```
The value is indeterminate in the source. In the reference build it is never
`l_undef` and never `l_true`: all decisions are negative, for every
`smt.phase_selection`.

**Go behavior.** `variable, err := q.state.theoryAwareBranching.next(...)`;
`return variable, lbool.Undef, err`, so `NextCaseSplit` applies
`try_true_first` and the phase-selection switch.
`TestSMTTheoryAwareCaseSplitWithoutHintProducerUsesActivity` asserts this
(`PhaseSelection: 1` -> `lbool.True`).

**Impact.** Every run with `smt.case_split=6`: different decisions, models and
statistics from `build/z3`.

**Reproduction.** `$S/work/smtcore_02/cs6_phase.smt2`:
```
(set-option :auto_config false)
(set-option :smt.case_split 6)
(set-option :smt.phase_selection 1)
(set-option :produce-models true)
(declare-const a Bool)
(declare-const b Bool)
(declare-const c Bool)
(assert (or a b c))
(check-sat-using smt)
(get-value (a b c))
```
z3: `a true, b false, c false`; g3: `a false, b false, c true`. On a 200-clause
QF_UF input z3 with `smt.case_split=6` has the statistics of
`smt.case_split=0 smt.phase_selection=0` (281 decisions, all negative in the
log) whatever `phase_selection` is; g3 with `case_split=6` has the statistics
of its own `case_split=0`.

**Fix.** Owner decision, because the C++ is undefined behavior. To match the
reference binary: in `selectVariable` return `lbool.False` for strategy 6
when a variable was selected (the quantifier rule gives the same value), put
a comment next to it quoting the two C++ places, and change the existing unit
test's expectation. Otherwise record the deviation in the manifest and keep a
vector with a `.expected_cpp` file as `theory_aware_case_split_scopes` does.

**Regression test.** Vector
`pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/theory_aware_case_split_phase.smt2` with the input
above, `scriptResults` value `"sat\n((a true)\n (b false)\n (c false))\n"`;
update `TestSMTTheoryAwareCaseSplitWithoutHintProducerUsesActivity` in
`smtcore/smt_case_split_queue_test.go` to expect `lbool.False`.

#### smtcore_02-F10: `del_inactive_lemmas1` path sorts a copy; C++ sorts `m_lemmas` in place

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_clause_maintenance.go:142-165` (`garbageCollectLearnedClauses`, `config.Half`)
- C++: `src/smt/smt_context.cpp:2683-2734` (`context::del_inactive_lemmas1`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
std::stable_sort(m_lemmas.begin() + start_at, m_lemmas.begin() + end_at, clause_lt());
unsigned start_del_at = (start_at + end_at) / 2;
```
The old part of `m_lemmas` stays in activity order afterwards. The next
collection's stable sort starts from that order, so ties are broken by the
previous activity ranking.

**Go behavior.**
```go
candidates := append([]int(nil), learned[:oldEnd]...)
sort.SliceStable(candidates, func(i, j int) bool { ... left > right })
for _, index := range candidates[len(candidates)/2:] { ... remove ... }
```
`s.clauses` keeps creation order, so from the second collection on ties are
broken by creation order.

**Impact.** Configurations with `m_lemma_gc_half = true` (set by
`setup_QF_UFIDL` for dense problems, `smt_setup.cpp:422`): from the second GC
the deleted half can differ when activities tie at the cut, which is common
for low-activity lemmas.

**Reproduction.** not attempted: needs a dense QF_UFIDL/QF_IDL instance with
more than 10000 conflicts; the difference is plain from the two listings.

**Fix.** Keep the order. Either reorder the lemma records of `s.clauses`
in place (write the sorted records back into the same index positions
`learned[:oldEnd]`, updating any index held elsewhere), or keep a per-state
`lemmaOrder []*SMTClause` that mirrors `m_lemmas` (append on creation, remove
on deletion, sorted in place here) and derive `learned` from it in both GC
variants, in `simplifyClausesAtBase` and in `DisplayClauseSections`.

**Regression test.** `smtcore/smt_clause_maintenance_test.go`:
`TestSMTClauseMaintenanceHalfKeepsSortedOrder`, modelled on
`TestSMTClauseMaintenanceDeletesInactiveLemmasAndRepairsScopes`: config
`{Half: true, Recent: 0}`, lemmas L1..L4 with activities 1,2,2,1; first GC
(all pinned as reasons or marked non-deletable) leaves order L2,L3,L1,L4; set
all activities equal, run again and expect L1 and L4 deleted (C++ order), not
L3 and L4.

<a id="smtcore-03-f1"></a>
#### smtcore_03-F1: `Assert` has no port of `context::assert_distinct` (large `distinct`)

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_internalizer.go:1307` (`(*SMTInternalizerState).Assert`, default path at 1420-1433)
- C++: `src/smt/smt_internalizer.cpp:263-266` and `286-308` (`context::internalize_assertion`, `context::assert_distinct`)

**C++ behavior.** A top-level `distinct` with more than 32 arguments (proofs off) is not expanded. It is encoded with a fresh sort and a fresh unary function:
```cpp
if (num_args == 0 || num_args <= DISTINCT_SZ_THRESHOLD || m_manager.proofs_enabled()) {
    assert_default(n, pr); return;
}
sort * s = m_manager.get_sort(n->get_arg(0));
sort_ref u(m_manager.mk_fresh_sort("distinct-elems"), m_manager);
func_decl_ref f(m_manager.mk_fresh_func_decl("distinct-aux-f", "", 1, &s, u), m_manager);
for (unsigned i = 0; i < num_args; i++) {
    app_ref fapp(m_manager.mk_app(f, arg), m_manager);
    app_ref val(m_manager.mk_fresh_const("unique-value", u), m_manager);
    enode * e   = mk_enode(val, false, false, true);
    e->mark_as_interpreted();
    app_ref eq(m_manager.mk_eq(fapp, val), m_manager);
    assert_default(eq, nullptr);
    mark_as_relevant(eq.get());
}
```
The caller then runs `mark_as_relevant(n)`.

**Go behavior.** `Assert` only special-cases gates. A `distinct` falls to the default path, which goes through `internalizeDistinct` and `MkDistinctExpanded`, creating n(n-1)/2 disequalities:
```go
if err = s.Internalize(expression, true); err != nil {
    return err
}
literal, err := s.Literal(expression)
...
if err = s.assignRootLiteral(literal, proof); err != nil {
```
`ast_manager::mk_fresh_sort` has no Go counterpart either.

**Impact.** Any assertion `(distinct t1 ... tn)` with n > 32. The model differs from C++ (no `distinct-elems!0` universe, no `distinct-aux-f!!1`), statistics differ, and the cost is quadratic instead of linear.

**Reproduction.** `$S/work/smtcore_03/distinct33_model.smt2`: `(declare-sort U 0)`, constants `x0`..`x32` of sort `U`, `(assert (distinct x0 ... x32))`, `(check-sat)`, `(get-model)`.
- z3: 316 lines, starting `sat`, `(model`, `;; universe for distinct-elems!0:`, and containing `(define-fun distinct-aux-f!!1 ((x!0 U)) distinct-elems!0`; `-st` gives `:mk-bool-var 39`.
- g3: 142 lines, only `;; universe for U:`; `-st` gives `:mk-bool-var 536 :binary-propagations 529`.
- `distinct2000.smt2` (same shape, 2000 constants): z3 answers `sat` in 0.03 s; g3 does not finish in 20 s.

**Fix.**
1. Port `ast_manager::mk_fresh_sort` (`src/ast/ast.cpp:2239`) as `(*ASTManager).MkFreshSort(prefix string)` in `pkg/ast/ast_core_fresh_factories.go`: name `prefix!<fresh id>`, same counter as `MkFreshConst`/`MkFreshFuncDecl`.
2. In `smt_internalizer.go`, factor lines 1420-1433 into `assertDefault(n, proof)`.
3. Add `assertDistinct(n, proof)` following the C++ statement order above. Use `MkFreshSort("distinct-elems")` then `MkFreshFuncDecl("distinct-aux-f", "", {s}, u)`. Per argument: `MkApp(f, arg)`, `MkFreshConst("unique-value", u)`, `MkEnode(val, false, false, true)`, `node.MarkAsInterpreted()`, plain `manager.MkEq(fapp, val)` (not `MkEqAtom`), `assertDefault(eq, null)`, `markRelevant(eq)`.
4. In `Assert`, after the gate block and before the default path:
```go
if basic && op == ast.ASTOpDistinct {
    if err = s.assertDistinct(expression, proof); err != nil {
        return err
    }
    return s.markRelevant(expression)
}
```

**Regression test.** In `pkg/smtcore/smt_internalizer_test.go` add `TestSMTInternalizerAssertLargeDistinctUsesAuxFunction`. Build 33 constants with `smtUFConstants(t, m, "big-distinct-", 33)`, `m.MkDistinct(values)`, `_, _, state := smtInternalizerFixture(t, m, nil)`, `state.Assert(distinct, ast.ASTHandle{}, 0)`. Expect `state.BoolVar(distinct)` not found, `state.boolVar.count() == 33`, every one of those variables assigned true, and 33 interpreted enodes whose owners are named `unique-value!k`. Repeat with 32 constants and expect `state.BoolVar(distinct)` found and assigned true.
SMT-LIB vector `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/distinct_large_aux_function.smt2` = `distinct33_model.smt2`; the `scriptResults` entry is the C++ output verbatim (316 lines). `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3` checks it against the C++.

<a id="smtcore-03-f2"></a>
#### smtcore_03-F2: deep-expression top-sort treats any non-Boolean operator of kind 4 as a term `ite`

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_internalizer_order.go:104` (`(*SMTInternalizationOrder).visitChildren`)
- C++: `src/smt/smt_internalizer.cpp:139-144` (`context::ts_visit_children`)

**C++ behavior.** `m_manager.is_term_ite(n)` is `is_app_of(n, basic_family_id, OP_ITE) && !is_bool(n)`. Only a basic-family `ite` gets the (true, false, false) child contexts:
```cpp
if (m_manager.is_term_ite(n)) {
    ts_visit_child(to_app(n)->get_arg(0), true, tcolors, fcolors, todo, visited);
    ts_visit_child(to_app(n)->get_arg(1), false, tcolors, fcolors, todo, visited);
    ts_visit_child(to_app(n)->get_arg(2), false, tcolors, fcolors, todo, visited);
    return visited;
}
```

**Go behavior.** The family is not tested:
```go
operation, err := o.manager.GetDeclKind(item.Expression)
...
termITE := operation == ast.ASTOpIte && !boolean
...
if termITE {
    for index, gate := range []bool{true, false, false} {
        child, e := o.manager.GetArg(item.Expression, uint32(index))
```
`ast.ASTOpIte` is 4, and so is `bvadd` (`theoryBVOpAdd int32 = 4`), `OP_FPA_RM_TOWARD_ZERO` and `OP_ARRAY_DEFAULT`. A two-argument `bvadd` fails on `GetArg(.., 2)`. A three-argument `bvadd` pushes its first argument with gate context true, and `Internalize` then rejects a non-Boolean term in gate context.

**Impact.** Any assertion deeper than 1024 (`smtDeepExpressionThreshold`) that reaches the SMT core and contains a not-yet-internalized `bvadd` (or `RTZ`, or array `default`). `check-sat` returns an error instead of an answer.

**Reproduction.** `$S/work/smtcore_03/deep_bvadd_smt.smt2`: declare `f : (_ BitVec 8) -> (_ BitVec 8)` and `x y z`; let `t0 = x`, `t(k+1) = (f (bvadd t(k) y))`; `(assert (= t600 z))`; `(check-sat-using smt)`.
- z3: `sat`
- g3: `(error "line 6 column 20: smt kernel internalize assertions: g3: AST source precondition")`

With `(bvadd t y w)` (`deep_bvadd3_smt.smt2`) g3 reports `... pre-internalize deep expression: g3: AST source precondition`. Controls with `bvmul` and `bvxor` at the same depth, and with 400 levels of `bvadd`, give `sat` in both.

**Fix.** Line 104 becomes
```go
termITE := family == o.manager.BasicFamilyID() && operation == ast.ASTOpIte && !boolean
```
The same omission is at line 166-167 in `Sort` (`op != ast.ASTOpNot` without a family test). It is harmless today because theory-family items are skipped by `preInternalizeDeep`, but it should test `family == BasicFamilyID()` too, as `m_manager.is_not(curr)` does.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/smtcore/smt_internalizer_order_test.go` add `TestSMTInternalizationOrderTheoryOperatorIsNotTermITE`, built like `TestSMTInternalizationOrderTermITEContextsAndInternalizedCutoff`. Use `sort, _ := m.BitVectorSort(8)`, constants `x y z`, `add := m.MkFamilyApp(bvFamily, 4, nil, {x, y})`, `root := m.MkEq(add, z)`, `order.Sort(root)`. Expect no error and the items `x, y, add, z` in that order, all with `GateContext == false`.
SMT-LIB vector `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/deep_bvadd_topsort.smt2` = `deep_bvadd_smt.smt2`, `scriptResults` entry `"sat\n"`, checked with `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`.

<a id="smtcore-03-f3"></a>
#### smtcore_03-F3: `hasRelevantFalseEquality` counts Boolean `iff` atoms; C++ `is_diseq` never does

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_equality_atom_index.go:14` (`equalityAtomTerms`) and `:78` (`hasRelevantFalseEquality`)
- C++: `src/smt/smt_context.cpp:1164-1193` (`context::is_diseq`)

**C++ behavior.** `is_diseq` probes the congruence table with a dummy `(= n1 n2)` enode:
```cpp
app * eq = m_manager.mk_eq(n1->get_owner(), n2->get_owner());
...
enode * r = m_cg_table.find(m_is_diseq_tmp);
if (r) {
    literal l = enode2literal(r->get_root());
    return l == false_literal || (is_relevant(l) && get_assignment(l) == l_false);
}
return false;
```
For Boolean operands `mk_eq` builds an `iff`. `iff` is a gate, internalized with suppressed arguments (`smt_internalizer.cpp:569-572`), so it is never in the congruence table. `is_diseq` is therefore always false for Boolean terms.

**Go behavior.** The replacement index accepts both operators:
```go
op, basic, err := s.basicOperation(expression)
if err != nil || !basic || op != ast.ASTOpEq && op != ast.ASTOpIff {
    return ast.ASTHandle{}, ast.ASTHandle{}, false, err
}
```
The deviation is documented at the call site, `theory_array_extensionality.go:218-220`: "Boolean equality uses iff and need not create a disequality in the egraph's non-Boolean disequality table." It does change behavior.

**Impact.** Arrays with Boolean range. `theory_array_base::already_diseq` (`theory_array_base.cpp:280`) returns true in Go when a relevant `iff` over two selects is false, so the extensionality axiom C++ instantiates is skipped. Models and statistics differ.

**Reproduction.** `$S/work/smtcore_03/arr_bool1_m.smt2`:
```
(declare-const a (Array Int Bool))
(declare-const b (Array Int Bool))
(declare-const i Int)
(declare-const q2 Bool)
(declare-fun g (Bool) Int)
(assert (= (g (= (select a i) (select b i))) 0))
(assert (= (g true) 1))
(assert (or (= a b) q2))
(assert (or (not (= a b)) (not q2)))
(check-sat)
(get-model)
```
- z3: `k!0` is `(ite (= x!0 2) false (ite (= x!0 3) false false))` and `k!1` has the matching two entries; `-st` shows `:array-ext-ax 1 :mk-bool-var 16 :decisions 5`.
- g3: `k!0` is `(ite (= x!0 2) false false)`, `k!1` likewise; `-st` shows no `array-ext-ax`, `:mk-bool-var 13 :decisions 4`.

The same script with `(Array Int Int)` (`arr_int1.smt2`) gives identical statistics in both.

**Fix.** In `equalityAtomTerms` accept only `ast.ASTOpEq`. In `hasRelevantFalseEquality` return `false, nil` at once when `first.boolean` is set. Update the comment in `theory_array_extensionality.go:218-220`.

**Regression test.** SMT-LIB vector `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/array_bool_range_extensionality.smt2` = the input above. `scriptResults` entry is the C++ output:
```
sat
(model 
  (define-fun i () Int
    2)
  (define-fun b () (Array Int Bool)
    (_ as-array k!1))
  (define-fun a () (Array Int Bool)
    (_ as-array k!0))
  (define-fun q2 () Bool
    true)
  (define-fun k!0 ((x!0 Int)) Bool
    (ite (= x!0 2) false
    (ite (= x!0 3) false
      false)))
  (define-fun k!1 ((x!0 Int)) Bool
    (ite (= x!0 2) true
    (ite (= x!0 3) true
      true)))
  (define-fun g ((x!0 Bool)) Int
    (ite (= x!0 false) 0
    (ite (= x!0 true) 1
      0)))
)
```
Check with `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`.

<a id="smtcore-03-f4"></a>
#### smtcore_03-F4: dyn-ack triple instantiation fails with proofs enabled

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_dyn_ack_manager.go:32-53` (`newSMTDynamicAckJustification`), used at `:225` (`instantiateTriple`)
- C++: `src/smt/dyn_ack.cpp:32-40` and `406-436` (`dyn_ack_justification` constructor, `dyn_ack_manager::instantiate(app*, app*, app*)`)

**C++ behavior.** The triple instantiation reuses the pair justification. Its preconditions are `SASSERT`s only, so a release build accepts any two applications:
```cpp

    SASSERT(m_app1->get_num_args() == m_app2->get_num_args());
    SASSERT(m_app1->get_decl() == m_app2->get_decl());
    SASSERT(m_app1->get_num_args() > 0);
...

clause * cls = m_context.mk_clause(lits.size(), lits.c_ptr(), js, CLS_AUX_LEMMA, del_eh);
```

```go

if err != nil || firstDecl != secondDecl || firstCount == 0 || firstCount != secondCount {

}
```
In a triple, `n1` and `n2` are arbitrary equal terms (usually constants), so this always fails. `dynamicAckProof` (`smt_conflict_proof.go:842-923`) has the same checks (`count == 0`, `len(parents) == 0`).

```

(set-option :smt.dack.threshold 1)
(set-option :smt.dack.factor 1.0)
(declare-sort U 0)
(declare-fun f (U) U)
(declare-const c1 U) (declare-const c2 U)
(declare-const x1 U) (declare-const x2 U) (declare-const x3 U)
(declare-const p Bool)
(assert (or (= x1 c1) (= x1 c2)))
(assert (or (= x2 c1) (= x2 c2)))
(assert (or (= x3 c1) (= x3 c2)))
(assert (or (= x1 x2) p)) (assert (or (= x1 x3) p)) (assert (or (= x2 x3) p))
(assert (not (= (f x1) (f x2))))
(assert (not (= (f x1) (f x3))))
(assert (not (= (f x2) (f x3))))
(check-sat)
```
(the file has one command per line)
- z3: `unsat`
- g3: `(error "line 22 column 10: dynamic Ackermann propagation: g3: AST source precondition")`

**Fix.** In `newSMTDynamicAckJustification` keep only the nil-manager and null-handle checks. In `dynamicAckProof` follow `dyn_ack_justification::mk_proof` (`dyn_ack.cpp:73-102`) without the extra refusals: loop over `first`'s argument count, allow zero premises for `MkProofCongruence`, allow a one-literal lemma. Return an error only where C++ would read past `m_app2`'s arguments. Apply F5's `mk_eq_atom` change in the same function.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/smtcore/smt_dyn_ack_manager_test.go` extend `TestSMTDynamicAckManagerBuildsClauseProof` (or add `TestSMTDynamicAckTripleWithProofs`). With `manager.ToggleProofMode(ast.ASTProofEnabled)`, `config.Threshold = 1`, `config.Factor = 1`, `config.Equalities = true`, three constants from `smtUFConstants`, call `state.dynamicAck.schedule.usedEquality(v0, v1, v2, true)`, set `state.statistics.NumConflicts = 1`, and expect `state.dynamicAck.propagate()` to return nil with `NumDynAck == 1` and one three-literal clause.
SMT-LIB vector `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/dack_eq_triple_proofs.smt2` = the input above, `scriptResults` entry `"unsat\n"`, checked with `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`.

<a id="smtcore-03-f5"></a>
#### smtcore_03-F5: dyn-ack builds equality atoms with `MkEq` instead of `context::mk_eq_atom`

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_dyn_ack_manager.go:134-143` (`(*smtDynAckManager).equalityLiteral`); same in `pkg/smtcore/smt_conflict_proof.go:872-905` (`dynamicAckProof`)
- C++: `src/smt/dyn_ack.cpp:341-348` (`dyn_ack_manager::mk_eq`), `:60-71` and `:83-94` (`mk_hypothesis`, `mk_proof`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
literal dyn_ack_manager::mk_eq(expr * n1, expr * n2) {
    app * eq  = m_context.mk_eq_atom(n1, n2);
    m_context.internalize(eq, true);
    literal l = m_context.get_literal(eq);
```
`mk_eq_atom` orders the operands by AST id, or uses the theory's convention (`arith_util::mk_eq`). The proof uses the same atom and adds a symmetry step when the operands were swapped.

**Go behavior.**
```go
func (m *smtDynAckManager) equalityLiteral(first, second ast.ASTHandle) (SMTLiteral, error) {
    equality, err := m.state.manager.MkEq(first, second)
```
The operands are used in the order given. For a pair `(n1, n2)` only `id(n1) < id(n2)` is guaranteed; the argument pairs and the triple's representative can be in either order. `MkEqAtom` exists (`smt_mk_eq_atom.go:15`) and is not used here.

**Impact.** Default configuration (`smt.dack=1`). When argument ids are descending, Go creates `(= b a)` where C++ creates or reuses `(= a b)`. If that atom already exists, Go adds a second Boolean variable and the search diverges.

**Reproduction.**
`$S/work/smtcore_03/dack1.smt2` (same declarations as in F4, without the first two options):
```
(set-option :smt.dack.threshold 1)
(set-option :smt.dack.factor 1.0)
... declarations of U, f, c1, c2, x1, x2, x3, p ...
(assert (or (= x1 c1) (= x1 c2)))
(assert (or (= x2 c1) (= x2 c2)))
(assert (or (= x3 c1) (= x3 c2)))
(assert (or (= x1 x2) p))
(assert (or (= x1 x3) p))
(assert (or (= x2 x3) p))
(assert (not (= (f x3) (f x2))))
(assert (not (= (f x3) (f x1))))
(assert (not (= (f x2) (f x1))))
(check-sat)
```
- z3 `-st`: `:added-eqs 33 :conflicts 5 :decisions 4 :dyn-ack 3 :mk-bool-var 19`
- g3 `-st`: `:added-eqs 35 :conflicts 4 :decisions 3 :dyn-ack 3 :mk-bool-var 24 :mk-clause 2`

With the last three assertions written as `(f x1) (f x2)`, `(f x1) (f x3)`, `(f x2) (f x3)` (`dack2.smt2`) both print identical statistics. With `(set-option :produce-proofs true)` and `(get-proof)` the proofs are byte-identical for `dack2` and differ for `dack1`.
Default parameters: `php76p_desc.smt2` (7 pigeons, 6 holes, clauses `(or (= xi xj) pp)`, disequalities `(not (= (f xp) (f xq)))` emitted for p descending) gives z3 `:conflicts 1074 :dyn-ack 7 :mk-bool-var 91` and g3 `:conflicts 991 :dyn-ack 4 :mk-bool-var 113`. The ascending variant `php76p_asc.smt2` is identical in both.

**Fix.** In `equalityLiteral` call `m.state.MkEqAtom(first, second)`. In `dynamicAckProof` build each atom with `MkEqAtom` and port `mk_hypothesis`: hypothesis of the atom (or of its negation for the conclusion), wrapped in `MkProofSymmetry` when the atom's operands are not `(lhs, rhs)` in that order.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/smtcore/smt_dyn_ack_manager_test.go` add `TestSMTDynamicAckUsesCanonicalEqualityAtoms`. Take `values` from `smtUFConstants(t, manager, "dack-atom-", 2)`, create `app0 = f(values[1])` before `app1 = f(values[0])`, configure `Threshold = 1`, `Factor = 1`, call `schedule.conflictCongruence(app0, app1, dynAckRoot)`, set `NumConflicts = 1`, `propagate()`. Expect `state.BoolVar(MkEq(values[0], values[1]))` found and `state.BoolVar(MkEq(values[1], values[0]))` not found.
SMT-LIB vector `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/dack_eq_atom_order_proof.smt2` = `dack1.smt2` with `(set-option :produce-proofs true)` first and `(get-proof)` last; the `scriptResults` entry is the C++ output (59 lines), checked with `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`.

<a id="smtcore-03-f6"></a>
#### smtcore_03-F6: `used_cg_eh`/`used_eq_eh` events from the resolution loop reach dyn-ack one conflict late

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_dyn_ack_manager.go:260-280` (`recordConflictUses`); single call site `pkg/smtcore/smt_conflict_resolver.go:416` (outside this shard)
- C++: `src/smt/smt_conflict_resolution.cpp:127` and `:175` (`eq_justification2literals`, `eq2literals`)

**C++ behavior.** The hooks are called inline, every time a congruence or equality is expanded: once while `get_max_lvl` expands the conflict justification, and again in the main loop and in lemma minimization. All counts are in place when `m_dyn_ack_manager.propagate_eh()` runs after `resolve_conflict`.

**Go behavior.** The expander buffers the events in `congruenceUses`/`equalityUses`. They are flushed once per conflict, right after the max-level pass and before the main loop:
```go
conflictLevel, err := SMTBooleanJustificationMaxLevel(r.expander, consequent, conflict, levels)
...
if err = r.state.dynamicAck.recordConflictUses(r.expander); err != nil {
```
Everything recorded afterwards (`expandInSession` in the loop, minimization) stays buffered until the next conflict's flush. The last conflict's events are never delivered.

**Impact.** `smt.dack=2` and `smt.dack.eq=true` only (not the default `smt.dack=1`). Pairs reach the threshold one conflict later than in C++.

**Reproduction.** `$S/work/smtcore_03/dack_cr_lag.smt2`: the declarations of F4 without `p` and without the `(or (= xi xj) p)` clauses, with the options
```
(set-option :smt.dack 2)
(set-option :smt.dack.threshold 4)
(set-option :smt.dack.factor 1.0)
```
- z3 `-st`: `:added-eqs 29 :dyn-ack 2 :mk-bool-var 18 :mk-clause 1`
- g3 `-st`: `:added-eqs 27 :dyn-ack 1 :mk-bool-var 16`

In the variant that keeps `p` and the `(or (= xi xj) p)` clauses (`dack2_cr_t1.smt2` .. `dack2_cr_t4.smt2`), thresholds 1 and 3 give identical statistics and thresholds 2 and 4 differ (threshold 2: `:added-eqs 33` against `36`; threshold 4: `:dyn-ack 2` against `1`). That is the pattern a one-conflict lag predicts, since C++ counts a conflict-justification congruence twice per conflict.

**Fix.** Deliver the events when they happen. Give `SMTAntecedentExpander` the dyn-ack manager (or two callbacks) and call `usedCongruence` at `smt_conflict_antecedents.go:157` and `usedEquality` at `:237` instead of appending to the buffers. Then remove the buffers, `recordConflictUses` and `ResetUses`. If the buffers are kept, flush on every exit of `resolve` and after every other expansion (`smt_consequences.go:395`, unsat-core expansion).

**Regression test.** In `pkg/smtcore/smt_dyn_ack_manager_test.go` add `TestSMTDynamicAckConflictUsesAreCountedWithinTheConflict`. Configure `Strategy = uint32(dynAckConflictResolution)`, `Threshold = 2`, `Factor = 1`. Build a conflict whose justification contains one congruence `f(a) ~ f(b)` (the fixtures of `smt_equality_propagation_test.go`), run one `SMTConflictResolver.resolve`, and expect `len(resolver.expander.congruenceUses) == 0` and `state.dynamicAck.pairs.counts[dynAckPair{f(a), f(b)}] == 2`. No SMT-LIB vector: only statistics differ.

- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_dyn_ack_pairs.go:35` (`newDynAckPairState`), `pkg/smtcore/smt_dyn_ack_manager.go:109-115` (`updateConfig`), `pkg/smtcore/smt_dyn_ack_schedule.go:38` (`newDynAckSchedule`)

<a id="smtcore-03-f8"></a>
#### smtcore_03-F8: `propagate_eh` is skipped when the context is still inconsistent after `resolve_conflict`

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_search.go:467-481` (`(*SMTKernel).boundedSearch`, outside this shard; it drives `smt_dyn_ack_manager.go:238` `propagate`)
- C++: `src/smt/smt_context.cpp:3583-3613` (`context::bounded_search`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
if (!resolve_conflict())
    return l_false;
if (!inconsistent()) {
    ... resource, cancel, restart and max-conflict returns ...
}
if (m_num_conflicts_since_lemma_gc > m_lemma_gc_threshold && ...)
    del_inactive_lemmas();
m_dyn_ack_manager.propagate_eh();
```
`propagate_eh` is outside the `if (!inconsistent())` block. It runs after every resolved conflict that does not return.

**Go behavior.**
```go
if !k.internalizer.inconsistent {
    if restarts.due(k.internalizer.scopeLevel, baseLevel) {
        return lbool.Undef, true, nil
    }
    ...
    if err = k.internalizer.dynamicAck.propagate(); err != nil {
```
The comment above it says `if (!inconsistent()) { restart and conflict-limit checks; m_dyn_ack_manager.propagate_eh(); }`, which misreads the C++.

**Impact.** When the learned clause or `reinit_clauses` leaves a conflict, C++ still counts the propagation (dyn-ack GC schedule) and instantiates pending pairs; Go does both one conflict later.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: it needs a search where `resolve_conflict` returns with a conflict still set while dyn-ack candidates are pending.

**Fix.** Move the `dynamicAck.propagate()` call after the closing brace of the `if !k.internalizer.inconsistent` block, keeping the early returns inside it.

<a id="smtcore-03-f9"></a>
#### smtcore_03-F9: an auxiliary lemma with a true first watch and a false second watch is not put on the reinit stack

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_internalizer.go:370-377` (`addClauseKindWithJustificationAndDeleteHandler`)
- C++: `src/smt/smt_internalizer.cpp:1351-1366` (`context::mk_clause`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
if (get_assignment(cls->get_literal(0)) == l_false) {
    set_conflict(b_justification(cls));
    if (k == CLS_AUX_LEMMA && m_scope_lvl > m_base_lvl) { reinit = true; iscope_lvl = m_scope_lvl; }
}
else if (get_assignment(cls->get_literal(1)) == l_false) {
    assign(cls->get_literal(0), b_justification(cls));
    if (k == CLS_AUX_LEMMA && m_scope_lvl > m_base_lvl) { reinit = true; iscope_lvl = m_scope_lvl; }
}
if (reinit)
    mark_for_reinit(cls, iscope_lvl, save_atoms);
```
The second branch is taken whenever literal 0 is not false, so also when it is true.

**Go behavior.**
```go
if kind == SMTClauseAuxLemma && s.scopeLevel > s.baseLevel &&
    (firstValue == lbool.False || secondValue == lbool.False && firstValue == lbool.Undef) {
    clause.reinit = true
    s.markForReinit(clause, s.scopeLevel)
}
```
With literal 0 true and literal 1 false the clause is not registered at `m_scope_lvl`. It stays at its atoms' internalization level if `save_atoms` holds, and is otherwise not registered at all.

**Impact.** Theory and dyn-ack lemmas created above the base level with exactly one true literal and the rest false. C++ re-examines the clause at the next backjump (`reinit_clauses`, `smt_context.cpp:2202`): it re-selects the watches or propagates the first literal. Go keeps the old watches, so watch-list order and propagation timing can differ.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: it needs a lemma created in that exact assignment state at a level above its atoms' internalization level.

**Fix.** Change the condition to `(firstValue == lbool.False || secondValue == lbool.False)`. The assignment branch below it can keep its `firstValue == lbool.Undef` guard, since assigning a true literal is a no-op.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/smtcore/smt_internalizer_test.go` add `TestSMTInternalizerAuxLemmaTrueFalseWatchesIsReinitialized`. With `smtInternalizerFixture`, create Boolean variables `p q r` at the base level (`smtRelevancyBool`, `state.MkBoolVar`). Push three scopes; assign `q` and `r` false in scope 1 and `p` true in scope 2. In scope 3 call `state.addClauseKindWithJustificationAndDeleteHandler({p, q, r}, false, SMTClauseAuxLemma, ast.ASTHandle{}, nil, nil)`. Expect the new clause to have `InReinitStack() == true` and `reinitLevel == 3`.

<a id="smtcore-03-f10"></a>
#### smtcore_03-F10: implied equalities return different class identifiers and drop the result on `unknown`

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_implied_equalities.go:38-47` (`(*smtImpliedEqualityClasses).merge`), `:92-98` (`ImpliedEqualitiesWithStats`), `pkg/smtcore/smt_implied_equalities_values.go:9`, `pkg/smtcore/smt_implied_equalities_fallback.go:3`
- C++: `src/smt/smt_implied_equalities.cpp:74-111`, `147-241`, `323-368`; `src/util/union_find.h:120-134`

**C++ behavior.** Class ids are `m_uf.find(id)` of a size-based union-find; on a size tie the root is the second argument's root:
```cpp
if (m_size[r1] > m_size[r2])
    std::swap(r1, r2);
...
m_find[r1] = r2;
```
Sorts that are not value sorts (uninterpreted sorts among them) go through `get_implied_equalities_filter_basic`, which calls `m_uf.merge(terms[i].id, terms[j].id)` with `j > i`. The driver asserts `Relevant!(t)` for every non-array term, continues when the first check is `l_undef` (`if (is_sat != l_false)`), handles arrays through fresh-index selects, and leaves `produce_models` set to true.

**Go behavior.** The smaller index is always the root:
```go
if first > second {
    first, second = second, first
}
classes.parent[second] = first
```
and
```go
status, result = s.CheckSat(nil)
if result != nil || status != lbool.True {
    ...
    return status, nil, stats, result
}
```
There is no `Relevant!` assertion, arrays use the quadratic pair check, every non-array sort is bucketed by model value without the `is_value_sort` test, and `produce_models` is restored. The manifest records this as "Go always uses the source exact quadratic fallback ... It preserves implied-equality classes"; the partition is preserved, the identifiers are not.

**Impact.** `Z3_get_implied_equalities` (`pkg/api/api_solver.go:317`). For uninterpreted-sort terms `a b c d` with `a = b = c` and a Boolean `p`, C++ returns `[1, 1, 1, 3, 4]` and Go returns `[0, 0, 0, 3, 4]`. On `unknown` C++ fills the class ids and Go returns none. The number and order of solver checks also differ.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted with the binaries: the entry point is API-only. The C++ ids above follow from `filter_basic`: `merge(0,1)` makes 1 the root; `merge(0,2)` then has sizes 2 and 1 and keeps 1.

**Fix.** Port `get_implied_equalities_impl` step by step: a union-find with the `union_find.h` merge rule; `assert_relevant`; the `is_sat != l_false` test; `get_implied_equalities_model_based` with `is_value_sort`, `reduce_value`, the per-value representative lists and `filter_basic`; the array branch with fresh `index` constants. Leave `produce_models` true as C++ does.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/smtcore/smt_implied_equalities_test.go` tighten `TestSMTSolverImpliedEqualitiesPartitionsByProofAndSort`: it already builds `a b c d p` with `a = b`, `b = c`. Expect `classes` to equal `[]uint32{1, 1, 1, 3, 4}`. Add a case where the first check returns `Undef` and expect non-nil classes.

<a id="smtcore-03-f11"></a>
#### smtcore_03-F11: a pair queued twice makes `markInstantiated` fail where C++ instantiates again

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: medium
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_dyn_ack_pairs.go:131-141` (`(*dynAckPairState).markInstantiated`), reached from `smt_dyn_ack_manager.go:181`
- C++: `src/smt/dyn_ack.cpp:366-370` (`dyn_ack_manager::instantiate`) and `:254-275` (`gc`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
SASSERT(m_app_pair2num_occs.contains(n1, n2));
m_app_pair2num_occs.erase(n1, n2);
// pair n1,n2 is still in m_app_pairs
m_instantiated.insert(p);
```
In a release build a missing entry is a no-op. The `gc` comment says the invariant "is not true": a pair can be in `m_app_pairs` twice (instantiated, its clause deleted, counted again before the next `gc`). `gc` then pushes it to `m_to_instantiate` twice when both decayed counts reach the threshold, and the second `instantiate` just adds a duplicate clause.

**Go behavior.**
```go
if _, found := s.counts[key]; !found {
    return ast.ErrASTDomain
}
```
`gc` in Go reproduces the duplicate queue entry (it walks `s.apps` the same way), so the second instantiation returns an error and `check-sat` fails with `dynamic Ackermann propagation: ...`.

**Impact.** Long searches where a dyn-ack lemma is deleted by lemma GC and its pair is counted again to about 17 before the next dyn-ack GC while the instance budget is exhausted. Rare, but the outcome is an error instead of an answer.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: it needs lemma deletion, budget starvation and a dyn-ack GC in a specific order.

**Fix.** Make `markInstantiated` unconditional: `delete(s.counts, key); s.instantiated[key] = struct{}{}; return nil`. Do the same in `(*dynAckTripleState).markInstantiated` (`smt_dyn_ack_triples.go:120-130`).

**Regression test.** In `pkg/smtcore/smt_dyn_ack_pairs_test.go` add `TestDynAckPairMarkInstantiatedTwice`: after one `congruenceEvent` on a pair, call `markInstantiated(key)` twice and expect nil both times, with the key in `instantiated` and absent from `counts`.

<a id="smtcore-04-f1"></a>
#### smtcore_04-F1: `smtMAMCompiler.isSemiCompatibleCheck` fails the whole pattern insertion when the CHECK enode has no label hash

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_mam_compiler.go:573` (`(*smtMAMCompiler).isSemiCompatibleCheck`); error source `pkg/smtcore/smt_enode_trail.go:121` (`(*SMTEnode).LabelHash`)
- C++: `src/smt/mam.cpp:1377` (`compiler::is_semi_compatible(check*)`), `src/smt/smt_enode.h:386` (`enode::get_lbl_hash`)

**C++ behavior.** `get_lbl_hash()` has only a debug assertion; in the release build an enode whose hash is
still `-1` returns 255, which can never equal a pattern label hash (0..63), so the predicate is simply false and
the CHECK instruction is treated as incompatible:
```cpp
unsigned char get_lbl_hash() const {
    SASSERT(m_lbl_hash >= 0 && ...);
    return static_cast<unsigned char>(m_lbl_hash);
}
bool is_semi_compatible(check * instr) const {
    unsigned reg  = instr->m_reg;
    return m_registers[reg] != 0 && get_check_mark(reg) == NOT_CHECKED &&
        is_ground(m_registers[reg]) &&
        get_pat_lbl_hash(reg) == instr->m_enode->get_lbl_hash();
}
```
The comment at `mam.cpp:1549-1561` states that a CHECK enode without a label hash is a real case.

**Go behavior.** `LabelHash()` returns `ErrASTDomain` for an unset hash, and the compiler records it as a
compile failure, which aborts `insertAt` (`for c.err == nil`) and propagates out of `AddPattern`:
```go
h, err := instr.enode.LabelHash()
c.fail(err)
return c.getPatLblHash(instr.reg) == uint32(h)
```

**Impact.** A multi-pattern whose two patterns have the same head symbol, the same first ground argument, a
shared variable in swapped positions and a later ground argument that differs. While `update_filters` is still
processing the second pattern, the path tree inserts the first pattern into a code tree compiled a moment
earlier from the second one, whose later ground argument has not been hashed yet (`update_filters` hashes ground
arguments left to right). C++ continues; g3 fails the quantifier assignment and the check ends `unknown` with an
internal error text as the reason.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed.
```smt2
(set-option :auto_config false)
(set-option :smt.mbqi false)
(declare-sort S 0)
(declare-fun g (S S S S) S)
(declare-fun P (S S) Bool)
(declare-const a S)
(declare-const d0 S)
(declare-const d1 S)
(declare-const u S)
(declare-const v S)
(assert (forall ((x S) (y S)) (! (P x y) :pattern ((g x y a d0) (g y x a d1)))))
(assert (= (g u v a d0) (g v u a d1)))
(assert (not (P u v)))
(check-sat)
(get-info :reason-unknown)
```
`z3`: `unsat` / `(:reason-unknown "")`.
`g3`: `unknown` / `(:reason-unknown "smt search propagate: theory assignments: assign quantifier 1: g3: AST source precondition")`.
Control: adding `(declare-fun h (S S) S) (declare-fun Q (S) Bool) (assert (forall ((x S)) (! (Q x) :pattern ((h x d1)))))`
before the multi-pattern quantifier (so `d1` already has a label hash) makes g3 answer `unsat` too.

**Fix.** In `isSemiCompatibleCheck`, keep the C++ operand evaluation (the pattern side may set a hash) and
return false for an unhashed instruction enode instead of failing:
```go
r := c.register(instr.reg)
if r.IsNull() || c.getCheckMark(instr.reg) != mamNotChecked || !c.isGround(r) {
    return false
}
patHash := c.getPatLblHash(instr.reg) // may set_lbl_hash, as in C++
if !instr.enode.HasLabelHash() {
    return false // get_lbl_hash() == 255 never equals a pattern hash
}
h, err := instr.enode.LabelHash()
c.fail(err)
return patHash == uint32(h)
```
Both callers (`getCompatibilityMeasure`, `insertAt`) go through this one function. No other `LabelHash()` call
in the MAM is reachable with an unset hash (`getPatLblHash`, `updateFiltersPat`, `RelevantEh` all guard it).

**Regression test.** (1) Vector `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/mam_multipattern_unhashed_check.smt2` with the input
above minus the `get-info` line; `scriptResults` entry `"unsat\n"`;
`G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3` checks it against the C++.
(2) Unit test `TestSMTMAMSemiCompatibleCheckWithoutLabelHash` in `pkg/smtcore/smt_mam_test.go`, built like
`TestSMTMAMJoinsMultiPatternsAndRollsBackPatterns`: `smtMAMFixture(t)`, a 4-ary function over one sort,
constants from `smtEnodeConstant` registered with `state.context.RegisterEnode`, two `MkVar` variables, a
two-variable quantifier built like `smtMAMQuantifier` does (it only makes one bound variable, so call
`m.MkPattern`/`m.MkQuantifier` directly), `registry.Add(quantifier, 0)`, then
`astTestMust(t, mam.AddPattern(quantifier, pattern))`. Expected: nil error (today `ast.ErrASTDomain`).

<a id="smtcore-04-f2"></a>
#### smtcore_04-F2: no model after an `unknown` check (quantifier or theory incompleteness)

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_kernel.go:1483` (`(*SMTKernel).buildGeneratedModel`), together with code outside this shard: `pkg/smtcore/smt_solver.go:755`, `pkg/smtcore/smt_search.go:320`, `pkg/smtcore/smt_quantifier_manager.go:571` (`CheckModel`)
- C++: `src/smt/smt_context.cpp:3479` (`context::restart`), `:4274` (`mk_proto_model`), `:4306` (`get_model`); `src/smt/smt_context.h:204` (`scoped_mk_model`); `src/smt/smt_solver.cpp:183` (`get_model`)

**C++ behavior.** A proto model is built whenever the search ends without `l_false`, and `~scoped_mk_model`
turns whatever proto model exists into `m_model`; `smt_solver::get_model` returns it for any status:
```cpp
if (m_last_search_failure != OK) {
    if (status != l_false) mk_proto_model(status);   // THEORY, QUANTIFIERS, UNKNOWN
    return false;
}
if (status == l_true) {
    mk_proto_model(l_true);                          // before check_model, MBQI or not
    cmr = m_qmanager->check_model(m_proto_model.get(), ...);
    if (cmr == quantifier_manager::UNKNOWN) { m_last_search_failure = QUANTIFIERS; status = l_undef; return false; }
```
`mk_proto_model` only skips MEMOUT, CANCELED, TIMEOUT, NUM_CONFLICTS and RESOURCE_LIMIT.

**Go behavior.** Three gates drop the model. (a) `smt_solver.go:755` copies the kernel model into the result
only for `status == lbool.True`. (b) `smt_search.go:320` skips `buildGeneratedModel` for
`SMTFailureQuantifiers` ("check_model's proto model was already built"), but `CheckModel` builds no candidate at
all when MBQI is off, and when MBQI rejects a candidate it is retired. (c) `buildGeneratedModel` only knows
`manager.acceptedModel`; it releases the rejected candidate (`releaseRetiredProto`) instead of publishing it.

**Impact.** `(get-model)` and `(get-value ...)` after an `unknown` answer from the incremental solver. z3 prints
the candidate model; g3 prints an error.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed, three ways.
```smt2
(set-option :auto_config false)
(declare-const x Real)
(declare-const y Real)
(declare-const a Bool)
(assert (= (* x y) 2.0))
(assert (> x 1.0))
(assert (> (* y y) 3.0))
(check-sat-assuming (a))
(get-info :reason-unknown)
(get-model)
```
`z3`: `unknown`, `(:reason-unknown "(incomplete (theory arithmetic))")`, then
`(model (define-fun a () Bool true) (define-fun y () Real (/ 1.0 2.0)) (define-fun x () Real (/ 3.0 2.0)))`
(one definition per two lines). `g3`: same first two lines, then `(error "line 10 column 10: model is not available")`.
```smt2
(set-option :auto_config false)
(set-option :smt.mbqi false)
(declare-sort S 0)
(declare-fun f (S) S)
(declare-fun g (S) S)
(declare-const c S)
(push)
(assert (forall ((x S)) (= (f x) (g x))))
(assert (not (= (f c) c)))
(assert (not (= (g c) (f (f c)))))
(check-sat)
(get-model)
```
`z3`: `unknown` and a model with universe `S!val!0 S!val!2 S!val!1` and `c`, `f`, `g`.
`g3`: `unknown`, `(error "line 12 column 10: model is not available")`.
Third case (MBQI on, candidate rejected): `(set-option :auto_config false) (set-option :smt.mbqi.max_iterations 1)
(declare-fun f (Int) Int) (push) (assert (forall ((x Int) (y Int)) (=> (< x y) (< (f x) (f y))))) (assert (> (f 0) 5))
(check-sat) (get-model)`: z3 prints a model with `k!3`, `f!4`, `f`; g3 prints "model is not available".
`smt.max_conflicts` (NUM_CONFLICTS) agrees on both: no model.

**Fix.** The rule to restore is "the kernel has a model exactly when C++ `m_proto_model` is non-null at the end
of `search()`".
1. `smt_solver.go:755`: publish for every status, as `context::get_model` does:
   `if s.produceModels && !s.kernel.Inconsistent() { if md := s.kernel.GeneratedModel(); md != nil { result.SetModel(md) } }`.
   This should be enough for the THEORY case: `smt_search.go:320` already calls `buildGeneratedModel` there
   (read, not run).
2. `smt_quantifier_manager.go` `CheckModel`: when the MBQI branch returns `SMTQuantifierModelUnknown`, keep the
   rejected generator (a new field next to `acceptedModel`) instead of `retireCandidate`; C++ publishes that same
   proto model, so rebuilding one would give different values.
3. `smt_kernel.go` `buildGeneratedModel`: take `acceptedModel`, else the kept rejected generator, else
   `buildCandidateModelGenerator()` (the MBQI-off case; C++ `adjust_model` is a no-op there).
4. `smt_search.go:320`: drop `k.lastFailure != SMTFailureQuantifiers` from the condition.
5. `smt_solver.go:802` `PrepareCandidateModel` (the `candidate_models` path of the `smt` tactic) builds a model
   on demand, also for NUM_CONFLICTS, where C++ `m_ctx->get_model(md)` only reads `m_model`. After 1-4 it should
   read the kernel model and never build one.
A stale candidate left by an earlier `RESTART` round is also published by C++ when the search later ends with a
failure that does not rebuild; decide whether to mirror that.

**Regression test.** Vectors `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/unknown_model_theory.smt2`,
`unknown_model_quantifiers_no_mbqi.smt2`, `unknown_model_mbqi_rejected.smt2` with the three inputs above; the
`scriptResults` entries are the z3 outputs (generate them with `<repo>/build/z3 -in`), and
`G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3` checks them.
Unit test `TestSMTSolverPublishesModelAfterUnknown` in `pkg/smtcore/smt_solver_test.go`, set up like
`TestSMTSolverKernelFacadeAssertionsScopesAndResults`: after a `CheckSat` that returns `lbool.Undef` with an
incomplete-theory or incomplete-quantifier reason, `AcquireModel()` must be non-nil.

<a id="smtcore-04-f3"></a>
#### smtcore_04-F3: MAM cancellation and resource-limit calls are dropped (hooks declared, never assigned)

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_mam_interpreter.go:42-43, 363, 493` (`cancelled`, `resourcesExceeded`); `pkg/smtcore/smt_mam_impl.go:95, 597, 631, 646` (`newSMTMAMImpl`, `processPP`, `processPC`, `matchNewPatterns`)
- C++: `src/smt/mam.cpp:2515` (`ON_MATCH`), `:2683-2699` (backtrack), `:3667` (`process_pp`), `:3711` (`process_pc`), `:3733` (`match_new_patterns`); `src/smt/smt_context.cpp:132` (`get_cancel_flag`)

**C++ behavior.** `get_cancel_flag()` is `!m_manager.limit().inc()`: it counts one resource step and reports
cancellation. The MAM calls it once per YIELD, once per `plbls` element in `process_pp`/`process_pc`, once per
new pattern in `match_new_patterns`, and calls `resource_limits_exceeded()` (timer, cancel, memory) on every
102nd backtrack:
```cpp
if (m_context.get_cancel_flag()) { return; }      // ON_MATCH
if (since_last_check++ > 100) { since_last_check = 0; if (m_context.resource_limits_exceeded()) { ... return; } }
```

**Go behavior.** The interpreter has `cancelled func() bool` and `resourcesExceeded func() bool`, both guarded
by `!= nil`, and nothing in the package assigns them (`grep cancelled smtcore/*.go` shows only the declaration
and the two nil checks). `processPP`, `processPC` and `matchNewPatterns` have no cancel call at all.

**Impact.** `:rlimit-count` is lower than C++ by one per match and per pattern, so a resource limit trips at a
different point; and matching cannot be interrupted by a timeout, a cancel or the memory watermark until the
whole code tree has been enumerated.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed on the statistic. File A:
```smt2
(set-option :auto_config false)
(set-option :smt.mbqi false)
(declare-sort S 0)
(declare-fun f (S) S)
(declare-fun h (S) S)
(declare-fun P (S) Bool)
(declare-fun Q (S) Bool)
(declare-const a1 S)
(declare-const a2 S)
(declare-const a3 S)
(assert (forall ((x S)) (! (P x) :pattern ((f x)) :pattern ((h x)))))
(assert (Q (f a1)))
(assert (Q (h a1)))
(assert (Q (f a2)))
(assert (Q (h a2)))
(assert (Q (f a3)))
(assert (Q (h a3)))
(check-sat)
```
File B is A without `:pattern ((h x))`. Both give 3 instantiations; A has 3 extra duplicate matches and one
extra pattern. `-st` `:rlimit-count`: z3 A 484, B 444 (A-B = 40); g3 A 455, B 419 (A-B = 36). The missing 4 are
the 3 YIELDs and the one `match_new_patterns` call. With 10/40/100 constants the gap is 11/41/101.
The interruption half could not be shown end to end because g3 currently ignores `rlimit` and `-t` altogether
(see Needs verification).

**Fix.** In `newSMTMAMImpl`, after creating the interpreter:
```go
r.interp.cancelled = func() bool {
    canceled, err := state.manager.Canceled()
    if err != nil { r.interp.err = err; return true }
    return canceled
}
r.interp.resourcesExceeded = func() bool {
    if state.resourceLimitsExceeded == nil { return r.interp.cancelled() }
    exceeded, err := state.resourceLimitsExceeded()   // read lazily: the kernel installs it later
    if err != nil { r.interp.err = err; return true }
    return exceeded
}
```
Add the same `Canceled()` call at the top of each outer iteration of `processPP` and `processPC` (return `false`
from the `ForEach` callback to stop, as C++ `break`s) and at the top of each iteration of the first loop of
`matchNewPatterns` (`break`, then still run the second loop and the reset, as C++ does).

**Regression test.** `TestSMTMAMCountsResourceStepsAndHonorsCancel` in `pkg/smtcore/smt_mam_test.go`, modeled on
`TestSMTMAMMatchesUnaryAndRepeatedVariablesModuloEquality`: fixture `smtMAMFixture(t)`, one unary pattern,
three relevant applications (`smtQuickApplicationNode`, `smtMAMTestCongruence`), `mam.AddPattern`, then
`before := m.Limit.Count(); mam.Match()`; expect `m.Limit.Count()-before == 4` (1 pattern + 3 YIELDs) and 3 new
entries. Second half: `m.Limit.Cancel()` before `Match()`, expect 0 new entries, then `m.Limit.ResetCancel()`.
A `.smt2` vector is not suitable: the difference is only in statistics.

<a id="smtcore-04-f4"></a>
#### smtcore_04-F4: `SMTKernel.assertFormulaCore` omits the leading `get_cancel_flag()` of `context::assert_expr_core`

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_kernel.go:812` (`(*SMTKernel).assertFormulaCore`)
- C++: `src/smt/smt_context.cpp:2902` (`context::assert_expr_core`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
void context::assert_expr_core(expr * e, proof * pr) {
    if (get_cancel_flag()) return;
    pop_to_base_lvl();
    ...
```
One resource step per assertion, and a canceled context silently drops the assertion.

**Go behavior.** The function starts with `initContextEnodes()` and `popToBaseLevel()`; the comment at line 820
says "context::assert_expr_core starts with pop_to_base_lvl". There is no `Canceled()` call on the path
(`SMTSolver.AssertFormula` and the `smt` tactic call it directly).

**Impact.** `:rlimit-count` is one lower per assertion, and after a cancel/limit the Go kernel still pops to
base level, rewrites and stores the assertion.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed.
```smt2
(declare-const p1 Bool)
(declare-const p2 Bool)
(declare-const p3 Bool)
(push)
(assert p1)
(assert p2)
(assert p3)
(get-info :all-statistics)
```
`:rlimit-count`: z3 11, g3 6. Without the three asserts: z3 5, g3 3. So an assertion of a constant costs 2 in z3
(this call plus the rewriter entry at `rewriter_def.h:654`) and 1 in g3. With `(assert (or p q))` it is 3 vs 2.

**Fix.** Insert before `k.popToBaseLevel()`:
```go
if canceled, err := k.manager.Canceled(); canceled || err != nil {
    return err // C++ returns without asserting
}
```
`assertFormulaCore` has a single caller (`Assert`).

**Regression test.** `TestSMTKernelAssertCountsCancelCheck` in `pkg/smtcore/smt_kernel_test.go`, same setup as
`TestSMTKernelDisplayStatisticsResetAndCancellation` (`astTestManager`, `smtTestKernel(t, m)`,
`smtRelevancyBool`): record `m.Limit.Count()`, `kernel.Assert(a, ast.ASTHandle{})`, record again, and expect
the growth to be exactly one more than it is today (measure the rewriter's own steps for the constant once and
hard-code the sum). Then `m.Limit.Cancel()` with `t.Cleanup(m.Limit.ResetCancel)`: `kernel.Assert(b, ...)` must
return nil and `len(kernel.Assertions())` must not change.

<a id="smtcore-04-f5"></a>
#### smtcore_04-F5: delayed learned units are never dropped at base level, so `delay_units_threshold` counts the wrong set

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/smtcore/smt_learned_persistence.go:373` (`(*SMTInternalizerState).restoreLearnedUnits`); the count is read at `pkg/smtcore/smt_search.go:248` (`learnedBackjumpLevel`)
- C++: `src/smt/smt_context.cpp:2333` (`context::reassert_units`), `:3806-3812` (`delay_forced_restart`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
for (; i < sz; i++) { ... assign(l, b_justification::mk_axiom()); }
if (at_base_level()) {
    m_units_to_reassert.reset();
    m_units_to_reassert_sign.reset();
}
```
Every pop that lands on the base level (each restart when there are no assumptions, each non-delayed unit
backjump, `pop_to_base_lvl`) empties the vector, and the delay test is
`m_units_to_reassert.size() < m_fparams.m_delay_units_threshold`.

**Go behavior.** `restoreLearnedUnits` reinstalls a unit and sets `unit.installedLevel = level` but keeps it
in `s.learnedUnits`; entries leave only in `endSearchPersistence` (`installedLevel == ownerLevel`) or on a user
pop. `learnedBackjumpLevel` tests `len(k.internalizer.learnedUnits) >= DelayUnitsThreshold`, so it counts every
delayed unit of the current search, and units reinstalled at base by the `pop_to_base_lvl` after an
assumption search stay counted during the next search.

**Impact.** With `smt.delay_units=true` and quantifiers, g3 stops delaying after `threshold` units per search
where z3 starts counting again after each return to base level. The search path, conflicts and decisions
diverge (answers stay sound).

**Reproduction.** Confirmed. Eight blocks `(or y z p) (or y (not z) p) (or (not y) z p) (or (not y) (not z) p)`
over fresh `y_i z_i p_i`, plus `(assert (forall ((x S)) (! (P (f x)) :pattern ((f x)))))` and `(assert (P (f c)))`,
with `(set-option :auto_config false)`:

| options | z3 conflicts/decisions | g3 conflicts/decisions |
|---|---|---|
| none | 14 / 80 | 14 / 80 |
| `smt.delay_units=true` | 13 / 29 | 13 / 29 |
| `smt.delay_units=true smt.delay_units_threshold=1` | 12 / 47 | 10 / 45 |
| `smt.delay_units=true smt.delay_units_threshold=2` | 15 / 52 | 11 / 58 |

The script is `work/smtcore_04/du.smt2` (and `du2.smt2` with the options in `set-option` form) in the scratchpad.

**Fix.** At the end of `restoreLearnedUnits`, after the loop has succeeded:
```go
// reassert_units: if (at_base_level()) m_units_to_reassert.reset().
if level == s.baseLevel {
    return s.releaseLearnedUnits()
}
return nil
```
`PopScopes` has already lowered `s.baseLevel` when this runs, and it is only called on the preserve branch.
`TestSMTLearnedUnitSurvivesSearchBacktrackAndExpiresWithBase` asserts `state.learnedUnits[0].installedLevel == 1`
after a pop to base level; that line must become `len(state.learnedUnits) == 0`.

**Regression test.** Extend that test in `pkg/smtcore/smt_learned_persistence_test.go` (helpers
`smtInternalizerFixture`, `smtTestUserPush`, `smtRelevancyBool`): after the pop that lands on base level expect
the unit literal assigned `lbool.True` and `len(state.learnedUnits) == 0`. Add
`TestSMTLearnedUnitStaysListedAboveBase`: two `PushScope` calls after `beginSearchPersistence`, add the unit at
level 3, `PopScopes(1)`, expect one entry with `installedLevel == 2`. In `smt_delayed_unit_test.go`
(`TestSMTDelayedUnitBackjumpGuard` style) add a case: threshold 1, one unit captured, pop to base, then
`learnedBackjumpLevel` must return `ConflictLevel-1` again.

- Severity: low

**C++ behavior.** The fork diagnostic is inside `literal::display`, so every caller gets it:
```cpp
else if (trace_no_pp()) {
    if (sign()) out << "(not #" << bool_var2expr_map[var()]->get_id() << ")";
    else        out << "#" << bool_var2expr_map[var()]->get_id();

```

```go
if traceNoPP() {

}
```

the package variable `traceNoPPSet = true` (restore in `t.Cleanup`), display a negative literal over an
expression table as the existing tests in that file do, expect `"(not #<id>)"` with `<id>` from `m.GetASTID`.
