<a id="ast-rewriter-05-f1"></a>
#### ast_rewriter_05-F1: `RewriteApp` drops the single-argument `re.++` / `re.union` rule

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/ast/rewriter/seq_rewriter.go:192-199` (`SequenceRewriter.RewriteApp`)
- C++: `src/ast/rewriter/seq_rewriter.cpp:365-376` (`seq_rewriter::mk_app_core`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
case OP_RE_CONCAT:
    if (num_args == 1) { result = args[0]; return BR_DONE; }
    return mk_re_concat(args[0], args[1], result);
case OP_RE_UNION:
    if (num_args == 1) { result = args[0]; return BR_DONE; }
    return mk_re_union(args[0], args[1], result);
```

**Go behavior.**
```go
case 17:
    if len(values) == 2 { return r.RewriteRegexConcat(values[0], values[1], out) }
case 18:
    if len(values) == 2 { return r.RewriteRegexUnion(values[0], values[1], out) }
```
With one argument, both cases fall through to `RewriteFailed`. (The sequence `OP_SEQ_CONCAT` case 2 does handle a single argument.)

**Impact.** Any `(re.++ r)` or `(re.union r)` written with one argument stays wrapped. As a result, `str.in.re` over it is no longer reduced by `mk_str_in_regexp` (the automaton builder sees a 1-argument concat). `simplify` output differs, and the solver gets a different term.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed.
```smt2
(declare-const x String)
(simplify (re.++ (str.to.re "a")))
(simplify (re.union (str.to.re "a")))
(simplify (str.in.re x (re.++ (str.to.re "a"))))
(simplify (str.in.re x (re.union (str.to.re "a"))))
```
`g3`: `(re.++ (str.to.re "a"))`, `(re.union (str.to.re "a"))`, `(str.in.re x (re.++ (str.to.re "a")))`, `(str.in.re x (re.union (str.to.re "a")))`.
`z3`: `(str.to.re "a")`, `(str.to.re "a")`, `(= x "a")`, `(= x "a")`.

**Fix.** In `RewriteApp`, give cases 17 and 18 the same one-argument shortcut that case 2 has:
```go
case 17:
    if len(values) == 1 { return RewriteDone, r.manager.SetRef(out, values[0]) }
    if len(values) == 2 { return r.RewriteRegexConcat(values[0], values[1], out) }
case 18:
    if len(values) == 1 { return RewriteDone, r.manager.SetRef(out, values[0]) }
    if len(values) == 2 { return r.RewriteRegexUnion(values[0], values[1], out) }
```

**Regression test.** Extend `TestSequenceRewriterDeclarationDispatch` in `pkg/ast/rewriter/seq_rewriter_test.go`:
- Build `to_re("a")` with `m.MkSequenceToRegex(str)`.
- Get the `re.++` and `re.union` declarations from `m.MkRegexConcat` / `m.MkRegexUnion` via `m.GetDecl`.
- Call `rw.RewriteApp(decl, ast.SliceArguments([]ast.ASTHandle{toRe}), out)` for each.
- Expect `RewriteDone` with `out == toRe`.

SMT-LIB vector `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/regex_single_arg_concat_union.smt2` holds the four commands above. Its `scriptResults` entry is `"(str.to.re \"a\")\n(str.to.re \"a\")\n(= x \"a\")\n(= x \"a\")\n"`. Check it with `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`.

<a id="ast-rewriter-05-f2"></a>
#### ast_rewriter_05-F2: `RewriteAt` bounds the index with the flattened concat; `mk_seq_at` only bounds a single atom

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/ast/rewriter/seq_rewriter.go:573-600` (`SequenceRewriter.RewriteAt`)
- C++: `src/ast/rewriter/seq_rewriter.cpp:778-795` (`seq_rewriter::mk_seq_at`), `:1913-1932` (`min_length`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
unsigned len = 0;
bool bounded = min_length(1, &a, len);       // only a itself, not its concat leaves
if (bounded && r >= rational(len)) { result = mk_empty(sort(a)); return BR_DONE; }
```
`min_length` returns `bounded = false` for any element that is not a unit, empty or string literal, and that includes a concatenation. So for `a = (seq.++ ...)`, the C++ falls through to the unit walk. When every leaf is a unit and the index is past the end, the walk returns `BR_FAILED`.

**Go behavior.**
```go
leaves, err := r.manager.SequenceFlattenConcat(a)
for _, leaf := range leaves { ... knownLength += ...; or bounded = false }
if bounded && (!position.IsUint64() || position.Uint64() >= knownLength) {
    return r.assignEmptyLike(a, out)
}
```
The Go treats a concatenation of units and strings as bounded, and rewrites an out-of-range `seq.at` to empty.

**Impact.** `seq.at` / `str.at` over a concatenation of units and literals, with a numeral index past the end, is rewritten to the empty sequence. The C++ leaves it unchanged. The result is still sound, but `simplify` output and solver input differ from the reference.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed.
```smt2
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(simplify (seq.at (seq.++ (seq.unit x) (seq.unit y)) 5))
```
`g3`: `(as seq.empty Seq)`. `z3`: `(seq.at (seq.++ (seq.unit x) (seq.unit y)) 5)`.

**Fix.** Compute the bound on `a` alone, as `min_length(1, &a, len)` does:
- `a` is a unit: bound 1.
- `a` is empty: bound 0.
- `a` is a string literal: bound `len(text)`.
- Anything else, including a concatenation: unbounded.

Keep `SequenceFlattenConcat(a)` only for the unit walk that follows the `is_string` branch. The C++ runs that walk only when `r.is_unsigned()`, so guard it with `position.IsUint64() && position.Uint64() <= math.MaxUint32`.

**Regression test.** In `TestSequenceRewriterConstantLengthExtractAtAndIndex` (`pkg/ast/rewriter/seq_rewriter_test.go`):
- Build `u1 := m.MkSequenceUnit(num("1"))`, `u2 := m.MkSequenceUnit(num("2"))` and `c := m.MkSequenceConcat(u1, u2)`.
- Call `rw.RewriteAt(c, num("5"), out)`.
- Expect `RewriteFailed`.

SMT-LIB vector `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/seq_at_concat_out_of_range.smt2` holds the script above. Its `scriptResults` entry is `"(seq.at (seq.++ (seq.unit x) (seq.unit y)) 5)\n"`.

<a id="ast-rewriter-05-f3"></a>
#### ast_rewriter_05-F3: `th_rewriter` passes `rewriter.ignore_patterns_on_ground_qbody` to `elim_unused_vars`; the C++ passes an empty `params_ref`

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/ast/rewriter/th_rewriter.go:233` (`theoryRewriterConfiguration.ReduceQuantifier`), `:1126` (`readLocalParams`)
- C++: `src/ast/rewriter/th_rewriter.cpp:656` (`th_rewriter_cfg::reduce_quantifier`), `src/ast/rewriter/var_subst.cpp:42-46`

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
elim_unused_vars(m(), q1, params_ref(), result);
// unused_vars_eliminator: m_ignore_patterns_on_ground_qbody =
//     m_params.get_bool("ignore_patterns_on_ground_qbody", true);   // always true here
```
`th_rewriter_cfg` stores `m_ignore_patterns_on_ground_qbody` in `updt_local_params` but never reads it.

```go
eliminated, err := elimUnusedVars(m, updated, c.ignoreGroundPatterns)
...
if c.ignoreGroundPatterns, err = p.IgnorePatternsOnGroundQBody(); err != nil {
```

**Impact.** With `rewriter.ignore_patterns_on_ground_qbody=false` (global), or `:ignore_patterns_on_ground_qbody false` on `simplify`, the Go keeps a quantifier whose body is ground (with its patterns). (simplify (forall ((x Int)) (! (> (f a) 0) :pattern ((f x)))) :ignore_patterns_on_ground_qbody false)

**Fix.** In `ReduceQuantifier`, call `elimUnusedVars(m, updated, true)`, which is the `params_ref()` default. The `ignoreGroundPatterns` field can stay (the C++ keeps the dead member too), but it must not be passed on.

**Regression test.** Extend `TestTheoryRewriterQuantifierMergeAndUnusedProof` in `pkg/ast/rewriter/th_rewriter_test.go`, or add `TestTheoryRewriterGroundBodyIgnoresLocalParam` next to it:

- Rewrite `forall x. f(a) > 0` with pattern `f(x)`.
- Expect the bare body.

<a id="ast-rewriter-05-f4"></a>
#### ast_rewriter_05-F4: `NewStringRegexAutomaton` never compresses, but the theory_str complement automaton comes from `re2automaton::operator()`, which does

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/ast/rewriter/string_regex_automaton.go:39-86` (`NewStringRegexAutomaton`), used uncompressed at `pkg/smtcore/theory_str_regex_stage_intersection.go:97`
- C++: `src/ast/rewriter/seq_rewriter.cpp:207-215` (`re2automaton::operator()`), `src/smt/theory_str.cpp:10571`

**C++ behavior.** `eautomaton * aut_c = m_mk_aut(rc);` goes through `re2automaton::operator()`, which calls `r->compress()` before `mk_product(aut_inter, aut_c)` is called.

**Go behavior.** `NewStringRegexAutomaton` builds and materializes without `Compress`. The regex-stage caller compresses its own result (`theory_str_regex_stage.go:170`), but the complement built for the intersection is passed to `NewStringRegexAutomatonProduct` uncompressed. `NewSeqAutomaton` in the same file does compress.

**Impact.** The product accepts the same language, so emptiness agrees. However, the product pairs different moves, which changes:
- the number of `mk_and` / `is_sat` calls;
- the `mk_fresh_const("x")` draws and expression-solver checks they trigger;
- the structure that theory_str later inspects on the compressed `aut_inter` (`final_states().size() == 1`, `get_moves_from(init).empty()`).

This can shift fresh-name counters and theory_str decisions.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: reaching the complement branch needs a theory_str intersection with a falsely assigned membership. I found no small script that shows output-visible effects.

**Fix.** Make `NewStringRegexAutomaton` match `re2automaton::operator()`: call `a.graph.Compress()` after `materialize` and before `own`, as `NewSeqAutomaton` does. Then remove the now-redundant `graph.Compress()` at `theory_str_regex_stage.go:170`, or route both theory_str call sites through one constructor. Leave `NewStringRegexAutomatonProduct` uncompressed, because `mk_product` does not compress.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/ast/rewriter/seq_rewriter_automaton_test.go`, add `TestStringRegexAutomatonCompressedLikeRe2Automaton`:
- Build `(re.++ (re.* (str.to.re "a")) (str.to.re "b"))` with `NewStringRegexAutomaton`.
- Assert its graph equals `NewSeqAutomaton` on the same regex: same `NumStates()`, `Moves()` and `FinalStates()`.

<a id="ast-rewriter-05-f5"></a>
#### ast_rewriter_05-F5: AST construction order differs from GCC's right-to-left argument evaluation in several `seq_rewriter` rules

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/ast/rewriter/seq_rewriter.go:719-756` (`RewriteStringToInt`), `:984-1007` (`RewriteRegexComplement`), `:1570-1606` (`RewritePrefix` string-strip branches through `assignSequenceRelation`), `:1920` (`RewriteSuffix` final branch)
- C++: `src/ast/rewriter/seq_rewriter.cpp:1140` (`mk_str_stoi`), `:1393-1399` (`mk_re_complement`), `:899-900` and `:921-922` (`mk_seq_prefix`), `:1089-1090` (`mk_seq_suffix`)

**C++ behavior.** In each of these the reference build evaluates call arguments right to left:
- `mk_str_stoi`: `m().mk_ite(m_autil.mk_ge(b, m_autil.mk_int(0)), b, m_autil.mk_int(-1))` creates `-1`, then `0`, then `>=`.
- `mk_re_complement`: `mk_union(mk_complement(e1), mk_complement(e2))` creates `complement(e2)` first.
- `mk_seq_prefix` (both strip branches) and `mk_seq_suffix` (last branch): `mk_prefix/mk_suffix(mk_concat(..as..), mk_concat(..bs..))` creates the right concat first.

**Go behavior.**
- `RewriteStringToInt` makes `0`, then `-1`, then `>=`.
- `RewriteRegexComplement` makes the left complement first.
- `assignSequenceRelation` builds the left side before the right.

**Impact.** New AST nodes get ids in a different order. That can change id-ordered iteration and sorting later, and break trace identity. The terms themselves are identical. The project already records similar construction-order items (for example ast_rewriter_01-F8 and ast_rewriter_02-F3).

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: the difference is only in node ids, not in printed output.

**Fix.**
- `RewriteStringToInt`: build `minusOne` before `zero`.
- `RewriteRegexComplement`: build `rightComplement` before `leftComplement`.
- `assignSequenceRelation`: add a flag, or a variant used by the two `RewritePrefix` strip branches and the final `RewriteSuffix` branch, that builds `rightParts` before `leftParts`. Leave the `i > 0` prefix branch alone: there the C++ uses two separate statements, left first.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/ast/rewriter/seq_rewriter_test.go`, add `TestSequenceRewriterConstructionOrder`. For `RewriteStringToInt(itos(x))`, check `m.GetID(minusOne) < m.GetID(zero)`. For `RewriteRegexComplement(inter(r1, r2))` with fresh `r1`/`r2`, check that the id of `complement(r2)` is smaller than the id of `complement(r1)`.

<a id="ast-rewriter-05-f6"></a>
#### ast_rewriter_05-F6: 32-bit `is_unsigned` semantics are not followed in `RewriteIndex` and `RewriteRegexLoop`

- Severity: low
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/ast/rewriter/seq_rewriter.go:651-662` (`RewriteIndex`), `:1180-1193` (`RewriteRegexLoop`)
- C++: `src/ast/rewriter/seq_rewriter.cpp:829-833` (`mk_seq_index`), `:1444-1462` (`mk_re_loop`)

**C++ behavior.**
- `mk_seq_index` folds two literals only when `r.is_unsigned()`. Otherwise it returns `BR_FAILED`, unless `r` is negative.
- `mk_re_loop` accepts any `n.is_unsigned()` bound and stores it through `parameter(unsigned)`, which is an `int`.

**Go behavior.**
- `RewriteIndex` folds any non-negative offset, so offset 2^32 gives `-1`.
- `RewriteRegexLoop` refuses bounds above `MaxInt32`.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed.
```smt2
(simplify (str.indexof "abc" "b" 4294967296))
(simplify (re.loop (str.to.re "a") 2147483648))
```
`g3`: `(- 1)` and `(re.loop (str.to.re "a") 2147483648)`.
`z3`: `(str.indexof "abc" "b" 4294967296)` and `((_ re.loop -2147483648) (str.to.re "a"))`.

**Fix.**
- `RewriteIndex`: run the literal fold only when `position.IsUint64() && position.Uint64() <= math.MaxUint32`. Keep the negative-offset rule as the C++ orders it: literal fold first, then negative, then empty-needle.
- `RewriteRegexLoop`: accept bounds up to `MaxUint32` and pass `int32(uint32(v))` to `MkRegexLoop`, which reproduces the C++ int parameter.

The owner may prefer to exclude the loop case as a z3 bug instead. If so, record it in `z3_bug_exclusions.txt`.

**Regression test.** Add both lines to a vector `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/seq_unsigned_bounds.smt2`. Its expected output is the z3 output above, or only the indexof line if the loop case is excluded.

<a id="ast-rewriter-05-f7"></a>
#### ast_rewriter_05-F7: Go-only `elim_unused_vars` TRACE with no C++ counterpart

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/ast/rewriter/unused_vars_ufbv.go:45,52`, `unused_vars_trace_entry.go`, `unused_vars_trace_result.go`
- C++: `src/ast/rewriter/var_subst.cpp` (only the `var_subst_bug`, `var_subst` and `instantiate_bug` tags exist)

**C++ behavior.** `unused_vars_eliminator::operator()` and `elim_unused_vars` emit no trace. No `"elim_unused_vars"` tag exists anywhere under `src/`.

**Go behavior.** `elimUnusedVars` emits `elim_unused_vars` trace blocks. They claim `var_subst.cpp` lines 98 and 210, neither of which holds a TRACE.

**Impact.** With `trace=elim_unused_vars`, the Go writes output that z3 never writes. There is no effect otherwise.

**Fix.** Delete `traceUnusedVarsEntry` and `traceUnusedVarsResult`, their two call sites in `elimUnusedVars`, and the `unused_vars_trace*.go` files they use. If the tag must stay as a deliberate g3 diagnostic, document it as Go-only.

**Regression test.** None needed beyond removal. Optionally, add a test in `pkg/ast/rewriter` that runs `ElimUnusedVarsUFBV` with trace tag `elim_unused_vars` enabled and asserts the trace output is empty.

<a id="ast-rewriter-06-f1"></a>
#### ast_rewriter_06-F1: bit-blaster gate layer ignores global `rewriter.ite_extra_rules` / `local_ctx` (hard-coded bool_rewriter defaults)

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/ast/rewriter/bit_blaster/gates.go:24-44,68-70` (`NewConfig`, `newRewriterConfig`, `Config.simplify`); `pkg/ast/rewriter/bool_rewriter_public.go:121-125` (`SimplifyBooleanGateConfigured`)
- C++: `src/ast/rewriter/bit_blaster/bit_blaster_rewriter.cpp:69-79` (`blaster::blaster`), `src/ast/rewriter/bit_blaster/bit_blaster.cpp:124-128` (`bit_blaster::bit_blaster`), `src/ast/rewriter/bool_rewriter.cpp:23-32` (`bool_rewriter::updt_params`)

**C++ behavior.** Both bit-blasters own a `bool_rewriter` built with `bool_rewriter(m)`, which means `updt_params(params_ref())`. `bool_rewriter_params` falls back to the global `rewriter` module, so it reads `flat`, `elim_and`, `local_ctx`, `local_ctx_limit`, `blast_distinct`, `blast_distinct_threshold` and `ite_extra_rules` from gparams. Then `blaster` overrides only two of them:
```cpp
blaster(ast_manager & m): ..., m_rewriter(m), m_util(m) {
    m_rewriter.set_flat(false);
    m_rewriter.set_elim_and(true);
}
```
Every `mk_ite`, `mk_eq`, `mk_and` and `mk_or` of the circuit goes through that rewriter. That covers the multiplexer, shifts, udiv/urem, `mk_eq` and `mk_le`. The rewriter therefore applies the `ite_extra_rules` rewrites in `mk_ite_core` and `try_ite_value` when the user has set them globally. Its `m_local_ctx_cost` also accumulates across calls, because the instance is persistent.

**Go behavior.** Each gate builds a throwaway rewriter that carries only flat and elim_and:
```go
rw := boolRewriter{manager: m, flat: flat, elimAnd: elimAnd, localContextLimit: ^uint32(0)}
```
`newRewriterConfig` hard-codes `flat=false, elimAnd=true`. `smtcore/theory_bv.go:180-199` reads only `Flat()` and `EliminateAnd()` from the global rewriter params. `iteExtraRules`, `localContext` and `localContextLimit` always keep their defaults, and `localContextCost` is reset on every gate.

**Impact.** A user who sets `rewriter.ite_extra_rules=true` (or `rewriter.local_ctx=true`) gets a different bit-blasted formula from the `bit-blast` tactic. The tactic path is used by `apply`, `check-sat-using`, the sat preprocessing in `sat_solver/preprocess.go`, and muz `xform.bit_blast`. The SMT `theory_bv` blaster is affected the same way. The answers stay equisatisfiable, but the printed goals differ, and so do the clause sets and search.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed with the binaries. Input:
```smt2
(set-option :rewriter.ite_extra_rules true)
(declare-const x (_ BitVec 4))
(declare-const y (_ BitVec 4))
(declare-const z (_ BitVec 4))
(assert (= (bvashr x y) z))
(apply bit-blast)
```
z3 (`build/z3`):
```
(goals
(goal
  (let ((a!1 (not (ite (or k!6 k!7)
                       k!3
                       (ite k!5 (ite k!4 k!3 k!2) (ite k!4 k!1 k!0))))))
    (not (= a!1 k!8)))
  (let ((a!1 (= (not (ite (or k!6 k!7 k!5) k!3 (ite k!4 k!2 k!1))) k!9)))
    (not a!1))
  (let ((a!1 (= (not (ite (or k!6 k!7 k!5 k!4) k!3 k!2)) k!10)))
    (not a!1))
  (not (= (not k!3) k!11))
  :precision precise :depth 1)
)
```
g3 differs in goals 2 and 3:
```
  (let ((a!1 (not (ite (or k!6 k!7) k!3 (ite k!5 k!3 (ite k!4 k!2 k!1))))))
    (not (= a!1 k!9)))
  (let ((a!1 (not (ite (or k!6 k!7) k!3 (ite k!5 k!3 (ite k!4 k!3 k!2))))))
    (not (= a!1 k!10)))
```
Without the `set-option` line the two outputs are identical. In g3 the `(ite c1 t1 (ite c2 t1 t2)) ==> (ite (or c1 c2) t1 t2)` rule never fires inside the blaster.

**Fix.**
1. Store a full bool-rewriter configuration on `Config`: flat, elimAnd, localContext, localContextLimit, blastDistinct, blastDistinctThreshold and iteExtraRules. Hold it as a persistent `*boolRewriter`, not per-call booleans, so that `localContextCost` accumulates as `m_rw` / `m_rewriter` do in C++.
2. Initialize it the way `bool_rewriter(m)` does. Build it from the global `rewriter` module, the same way `smtcore/theory_bv.go:183-191` already builds one via `rewriter.NewBoolRewriter(m, ctx, globals, nil)`. Take all the fields from that object instead of just `Flat()` and `EliminateAnd()`.
3. In `newRewriterConfig` (the `blaster` path), override only `flat=false` and `elimAnd=true` after loading the globals, mirroring `set_flat` and `set_elim_and`.
4. Make `Config.simplify` call that persistent rewriter, for example through a new `SimplifyBooleanGateWith(rw *boolRewriter, ...)`, or a variant of `SimplifyBooleanGateConfigured` that takes the full parameter struct.
5. Update every constructor that builds a Config: `NewBitBlaster` and `NewBitBlasterRewriter`, which serves `tactic/bv/bit_blaster_tactic.go:132`, `sat/sat_solver/preprocess.go:287` and `muz/transforms/bit_blast.go:200`. Also update `smtcore/theory_bv.go:199`, replacing `SetBoolRewriterFlags` with a setter that copies the whole rewriter configuration. Each constructor needs access to the params context and globals.

**Regression test.**
- SMT-LIB vector `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/bit_blast_ite_extra_rules.smt2` with the input above. Its `scriptResults` entry in `pkg/cmd/g3/main_test.go` is the z3 output shown above, verbatim, with a comment `// AUDIT.md ast_rewriter_06-F1`. Check it with `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`.
- Unit test in `pkg/ast/rewriter/bit_blaster/rewriter_reduce_test.go`: `TestBitBlasterRewriterHonorsIteExtraRules`. Use the setup of `TestBitBlasterRewriterCircuitReductions` with the global `rewriter.ite_extra_rules=true` set. Blast `(bvashr x y)` for 4-bit constants and assert that bit 1 of the result is `(ite (or b2 b3 b1) x3 (ite b0 x2 x1))`, modulo the fresh bit names.

<a id="ast-rewriter-06-f2"></a>
#### ast_rewriter_06-F2: TRACE sites missing in the bit-blaster gates and engine (`xor3`, `xor3_sorted`, `carry`, `carry_sorted`, and the `bit_blaster` tag in `mk_udiv_urem` / `mk_rotate_left`)

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/ast/rewriter/bit_blaster/gates.go:72,165` (`Config.MkXor3`, `Config.MkCarry`); `pkg/ast/rewriter/bit_blaster/engine_division.go:11` (`Engine.MkUnsignedDivRem`); `pkg/ast/rewriter/bit_blaster/engine_logic.go:103` (`Engine.MkRotateLeft`)
- C++: `src/ast/rewriter/bit_blaster/bit_blaster.cpp:39,41,78,80`; `src/ast/rewriter/bit_blaster/bit_blaster_tpl_def.h:486-496,838-843`

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
TRACE("xor3", tout << "#" << l1->get_id() << " #" << l2->get_id() << " #" << l3->get_id(););
sort_args(l1, l2, l3);
TRACE("xor3_sorted", tout << "#" << l1->get_id() << ...);
...
TRACE("bit_blaster", tout << "a: "; ... tout << "\nb: "; ... "\nq: "; ... "\nr: "; ...);   // mk_udiv_urem
TRACE("bit_blaster", tout << n << ": " << sz << " "; for (...) tout << mk_pp(a_bits[i], m()) << " "; tout << "\n";);  // mk_rotate_left
```

**Go behavior.** None of these tags is emitted. A grep for `"xor3"`, `"carry"` and `"carry_sorted"` in `pkg` finds only the plugin declaration names. The only `bit_blaster` trace in the package is `reduce_app` (`rewriter_trace.go`).

**Impact.** With `-tr:bit_blaster`, `-tr:xor3` or `-tr:carry`, the `.z3-trace` output differs from a C++ `_TRACE` build. The `bit_blaster` tag is the most visible one: `mk_udiv_urem` runs for every udiv/urem/sdiv/srem/smod and every non-constant ext_rotate. Solver behavior does not change.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: `build/z3` is not a `_TRACE` build.

**Fix.** Add `EmitConditional` blocks that copy `rewriter_trace.go:traceApplication`. Each one gets the C++ file and line, a function name, and identical text.
- In `MkXor3`, emit `xor3` before sorting and `xor3_sorted` after it, using `#<id> #<id> #<id>` with no trailing newline. Do the same in `MkCarry` with `carry` and `carry_sorted`. These four sites are only in `bit_blaster_cfg`; the `rewriterGates` (blaster_cfg) path has no trace.
- At the end of `MkUnsignedDivRem`, emit `bit_blaster` with the `a:`, `b:`, `q:` and `r:` lines, each element printed with mk_pp followed by a space.
- At the top of `MkRotateLeft`, emit `bit_blaster` as `<n>: <sz> ` followed by the bits. Print the amount before the `n % sz` reduction.

**Regression test.** Add `TestBitBlasterTraceTags` in `pkg/ast/rewriter/bit_blaster/bit_blaster_test.go`. Bind a `diagnostic.TraceTags` with the tags enabled, following the trace tests that already use `BindTrace` / `BorrowProcessTraceTags`. Call `MkUnsignedDivRem` on two 2-bit variable vectors and `MkXor3` on three Bool constants. Assert that the captured trace contains the `a: ` / `q: ` blocks and the `#i #j #k` lines in pre-sort and sorted order. Match by tag and function, not by line number.

### Area: AST support: fpa, macros, normal forms, patterns, proofs, substitution

*ast_sub_01.* This shard has the FPA-to-BV converter (`pkg/ast/fpa`, 9 files: the converter core, arithmetic, ops, conversions, the reduce_app dispatch, and the rewriter params) and the macro subsystem (`pkg/ast/macros`, 7 files: macro_util, candidates, finder, manager, expander, quasi_macros). - **fpa2bv:** very faithful. Every function was compared statement by statement, including GCC right-to-left argument order for nested constructor calls and the C++ quirks the port keeps on purpose (mk_sub passing the bv2rm app, the `v_tp` fallback in mk_to_fp_real, c1==c2 in mk_to_fp_real_int, `sticky_h1` reused in mk_fma). No divergences found. - **macros:** four divergences. - Two are confirmed with the binaries: quasi-macros skips its own th_rewriter pass, and macro expansion's th_rewriter ignores global `rewriter.*` params. - One is a condition built with ast_util instead of bool_rewriter. - One is an uninterpreted-sort test that misses declare-sort sorts. - There is also one low-severity construction-order difference. Counts: critical 0, high 0, medium 4, low 1.

*ast_sub_02.* This shard covers the normal-form code (NNF, defined names, expression namers, skolemizer, pull_quant), pattern inference (collect, filtering, unary and multi patterns, the pattern database and matcher, reduce_quantifier) and the basic, arithmetic and hyper-resolution parts of the proof checker. Most of it follows the C++ closely. The candidate filters, sort, smaller-pattern matcher, contains-subpattern, the multi-pattern queue and the database matcher are faithful. The real divergences are in NNF and pull_quant, which use the wrong constructors and the wrong construction order, have no cache in one pull_quant path, and build a different proof term. Four were reproduced with the binaries, one of them only with a g3trace build. Counts: high 1, medium 5, low 6.

*ast_sub_03.* This shard holds the proof utilities in `pkg/ast/proofs` (post-order iterator, both hypothesis reducers, is_closed, permute_unit_resolution, push_instantiations_up, elim_aux_assertions, part of the proof checker's rules) and the term-indexing package `pkg/ast/substitution` (substitution, matcher, unifier, substitution tree). The port is faithful overall. Branch order, AST construction order and cache behavior match the C++ in nearly every function. Findings: 0 critical, 0 high, 0 medium, 5 low. None changes a sat/unsat answer. The two that can make output differ are the legacy reducer's unit map (keeps the first value where C++ keeps the last) and the proof checker's operator test (it ignores the family), which accepts some invalid premises that C++ rejects. The other three are latent: an early-stop that is lost, and two assertions that Go enforces in every build where C++ does so only in debug builds.

<a id="ast-sub-01-f1"></a>
#### ast_sub_01-F1: QuasiMacros.Apply never runs quasi_macros::m_rewriter on the expanded formulas

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/ast/macros/quasi_macros.go:465-496` (`QuasiMacros.Apply`)
- C++: `src/ast/macros/quasi_macros.cpp:334-347,365-375` (`quasi_macros::apply_macros`, both overloads)

**C++ behavior.** After `expand_macros`, every formula is always rewritten again with the member `th_rewriter m_rewriter`. This happens even when expansion left it unchanged, because `expand_macros` only th-rewrites terms it changed:
```
m_macro_manager.expand_macros(exprs[i], p, deps[i], r, pr, dep);
m_rewriter(r);
new_exprs.push_back(r);
```

**Go behavior.** It calls `ExpandMacros` and inserts its result directly. No rewriter is applied:
```
dependency, e := q.macros.ExpandMacros(row.Expression, proof, row.Dependency, out, outProof)
if e == nil { expression, x := q.manager.RefGet(out) ... e = result.Insert(Formula{Expression: expression, ...}) }
```
Neither caller adds the pass: `pkg/tactic/ufbv/macro_tactics.go:203-227` and `pkg/smtcore/smt_asserted_macros.go:121-160`.

**Impact.** When a quasi-macro is found, every formula that contains no macro application is left unsimplified. The `quasi-macros` tactic output differs, and the formulas passed to the next tactic (for example `(then quasi-macros smt)`) differ too. In the SMT `apply_quasi_macros` path the later reduce usually normalizes them, but the asserted state between the two steps differs.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed with `$S/work/ast_sub_01/qm1.smt2`:
```
(declare-fun f (Int) Int)
(declare-fun g (Int) Int)
(declare-fun a () Int)
(assert (forall ((x Int)) (= (f x) (+ x 1))))
(assert (> (+ a 0 1 1) 3))
(assert (> (g (+ 1 1)) (f a)))
(apply quasi-macros)
```
g3 prints the goal `(> (+ a 0 1 1) 3)` / `(not (<= (g 2) (+ 1 a)))`. z3 prints `(not (<= a 1))` / `(not (<= (g 2) (+ 1 a)))`.

**Fix.**
1. Give `QuasiMacros` a `*rewriter.TheoryRewriter` created once in `NewQuasiMacros` and closed by a new `Close`. This is the C++ member `m_rewriter`. Build it from the caller's `ParamsContext`/`GlobalParamsService` (see F2), not from a fresh default service.
2. In `Apply`, in the `found` branch, after `ExpandMacros` and before `result.Insert`, rewrite the expression without touching the proof (C++ ignores the rewrite proof):
   ```go
   expression, e = q.manager.RefGet(out)
   if e == nil { e = q.rewrite.Rewrite(expression, out) }
   if e == nil { expression, e = q.manager.RefGet(out) }
   ```
3. Keep the `!found` branch as it is (C++ copies the formulas unchanged there).

Update both callers (`smtcore.applyPendingQuasiMacros`, `tactic/ufbv MacroTactic.run`) to pass params and to close the object.

**Regression test.**
- Add `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/quasi_macros_rewrites_unchanged.smt2` with the input above.
- Add this `scriptResults` entry:
  `"quasi_macros_rewrites_unchanged.smt2": "(goals\n(goal\n  (not (<= a 1))\n  (not (<= (g 2) (+ 1 a)))\n  :precision precise :depth 1)\n)\n",`
- Check it against the C++ with `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`.
- Optional unit test: `TestQuasiMacrosApplyRewritesUntouchedFormulas` in `pkg/ast/macros/macro_util_test.go`, using `fixture`, `declaration` and `quantifiedMacro`. Apply one quasi macro plus the ground formula `(not (not p))`, and expect `p` in the output batch.

<a id="ast-sub-01-f2"></a>
#### ast_sub_01-F2: Macro expansion's th_rewriter uses a private default global-params service, so `rewriter.*` settings are ignored

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/ast/macros/macro_expander.go:231-255` (`newMacroTheoryNormalizer`), used at `:409`
- C++: `src/ast/macros/macro_manager.cpp:346-353` (`macro_manager::expand_macros`)

**C++ behavior.**
```
if (change) {
    th_rewriter rw(m);
    ...
    rw(r1, r, rw_pr);
```
`th_rewriter(m)` reads the process `gparams` "rewriter" module (for example `rewriter.som`, `rewriter.arith_lhs`, `rewriter.hi_div0`).

**Go behavior.** It builds a fresh `ParamsContext`, catalog and `GlobalParamsService` with `InitializeSource()`, so only defaults apply:
```
n.globals, err = uparams.NewGlobalParamsService(m.Symbols, n.context, ...)
if err = n.globals.InitializeSource(); err != nil { ...
n.rewrite, err = rewriter.NewTheoryRewriter(m, n.context, n.globals, nil)
```

**Impact.** Any user-set `rewriter.*` global (command line or `set-option`) is silently ignored after macro expansion. This affects the macro-finder tactic, the quasi-macros tactic, `smt.macro_finder` / `smt.quasi_macros` preprocessing, and asserted-macro expansion in smtcore. The output differs, and the SMT search can differ. This is the same pattern as FUZZ_I-F7 (theory_seq), but at a different site.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed with `$S/work/ast_sub_01/mf2.smt2`:
```
(set-option :rewriter.som true)
(declare-fun f (Int) Int)
(declare-fun a () Int)
(assert (forall ((x Int)) (= (f x) (* x (+ x 1)))))
(assert (> (f a) 3))
(apply macro-finder)
```
g3 prints `(not (<= (* a (+ 1 a)) 3))`. z3 prints `(not (<= (+ a (* a a)) 3))`. The command-line form `rewriter.som=true` gives the same difference.

**Fix.**
1. Thread the process `*uparams.ParamsContext` and `*uparams.GlobalParamsService` into `macros.Manager`, either with new parameters on `NewManager` or with a `SetRewriterParams(context, globals)` method stored on the Manager.
2. In `ExpandMacros`, build the rewriter with `rewriter.NewTheoryRewriter(m.manager, context, globals, nil)` and delete `macroTheoryNormalizer`'s private catalog/global service.
3. Update every `NewManager` caller to pass the globals they already hold:
   - `pkg/smtcore` (asserted macros)
   - `pkg/tactic/ufbv/macro_tactics.go`, which already receives `context, globals`
   - `pkg/smtcore` model finder
   - any cmd_context users

   Use the same params for the F1 rewriter.

**Regression test.**
- Add `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/macro_finder_rewriter_som.smt2` with the input above.
- Add this `scriptResults` entry:
  `"macro_finder_rewriter_som.smt2": "(goals\n(goal\n  (not (<= (+ a (* a a)) 3))\n  :precision precise :depth 1)\n)\n",`
- Check it against the C++ with `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference`.

<a id="ast-sub-01-f3"></a>
#### ast_sub_01-F3: Macro candidate conditions use ast_util mk_and/mk_not instead of bool_rewriter

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: medium
- Go: `pkg/ast/macros/macro_candidates.go:248-274` (`restCondition`), `:304` (`insertCandidate`, `MkAnd`), `:63` (`QuasiMacroHeadToMacroHead`, `MkAndArray`)
- C++: `src/ast/macros/macro_util.cpp:716-733` (`get_rest_clause_as_cond`), `:688` (`insert_quasi_macro`), `:430` (`quasi_macro_head_to_macro_head`)

**C++ behavior.** It uses the simplifying `bool_rewriter`:
```
bool_rewriter(m_manager).mk_not(l, neg_l);                       // get_rest_clause_as_cond
bool_rewriter(m_manager).mk_and(neg_other_lits.size(), ..., extra_cond);
bool_rewriter(m_manager).mk_and(cond, extra_cond, new_cond);     // insert_quasi_macro
```
`bool_rewriter::mk_not` maps a Boolean equality `(= a b)` to `(= (not a) b)` (`bool_rewriter.cpp:952-957`). `mk_and` flattens nested `and`s, drops `true`, removes duplicates, and turns complementary pairs into `false`.

**Go behavior.**
```
literal, e = u.manager.MkNotSimplified(literal)     // ast_util mk_not: only strips not / folds true,false
return u.manager.MkAndArray(negated)                 // ast_util mk_and: raw n-ary and
condition, e = u.manager.MkAnd(condition, extraCondition)  // raw binary and, no flattening
```

**Impact.** Conditional macro candidates get a structurally different `cond`:
- a negated Boolean-equality literal becomes `(not (= a b))` instead of `(= (not a) b)`;
- `(and (and ¬l1 ¬l2) (= x1 t))` is built instead of the flat `(and ¬l1 ¬l2 (= x1 t))`.

The smt model finder uses `cond` directly. `is_unconditional` uses `m.is_true(cond)`, and `smt_model_finder.cpp:3114` builds `mk_ite(m->get_cond(), def, fi_else)` for function interpretations. So printed models and model-finder behavior can differ. The meaning is the same, so the sat/unsat answer is unchanged. I did not get an observable difference with two quick model-finder inputs (`mc1.smt2`, `mc2.smt2` in the work dir).

**Reproduction.** Not confirmed. The smallest trigger is a quantified clause whose macro literal sits next to a Boolean-equality literal, or next to two or more other literals with a non-macro-head quasi head. One example is `(forall ((x Int)) (or (= (p x) (q x)) (= (f x) (* 2 x))))` plus a second conditional macro for `f`, so that `process` (`smt_model_finder.cpp:3097-3123`) builds an ite on `cond`.

**Fix.** Use the rewriter package's Boolean simplifier (the default `bool_rewriter`; `pkg/ast/rewriter` already provides one for `fpa.BoolSimplifier`) for:
- `restCondition`: `mk_not` per literal, and `mk_and` over the result;
- `insertCandidate`: `mk_and(cond, extra)`;
- `QuasiMacroHeadToMacroHead`: `mk_and(new_conds)`.

If `macros` cannot import `rewriter` because of an import cycle, inject a small `BoolSimplifier` interface into `Util`, the same way `fpa.NewFPA2BVConverter` takes one.

**Regression test.** Extend `TestMacroUtilQuasiConversionClauseConditionsAndHints` in `pkg/ast/macros/macro_util_test.go`, using `fixture` and `declaration`:
- Build `(forall ((x Bool)) (or (= (p x) (q x)) (= (f x) x)))` with `p q : Bool->Bool` and `f : Bool->Bool`, and call `CollectQuantifierCandidates`. Expect the candidate condition to be `(= (not (p x0)) (q x0))`, structurally equal to a term built by `MkEq(MkNot(p x0), q x0)`.
- Second case: a clause with two other literals plus a quasi head `f(x, x)`. Expect a single flat `and` with three arguments.

<a id="ast-sub-01-f4"></a>
#### ast_sub_01-F4: IsPseudoHead tests only the null family and misses declare-sort sorts

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: medium
- Go: `pkg/ast/macros/macro_numeric.go:342-349` (`Util.IsPseudoHead`)
- C++: `src/ast/macros/macro_util.cpp:313-315` (`macro_util::is_pseudo_head`), `src/ast/ast.h:1691`

**C++ behavior.**
```
sort * s = m_manager.get_sort(lhs);
if (m_manager.is_uninterp(s))   // null_family_id || m_user_sort_family_id
    return false;
```

**Go behavior.**
```
sortFamily, err := u.manager.GetFamilyID(sort)
if err != nil || sortFamily == ast.NullFamilyID {
    return head, ground, false, err
}
```
In g3, `MkUninterpretedSort` (declare-sort) creates its sorts in the user-sort family 4 with an infinite size (`pkg/ast/ast_builtin_plugins.go:120-142`). These sorts get past this check. The manager already has the correct predicate, `IsUninterpretedSort` (`ast_builtin_plugins.go:146`).

**Impact.** For `(forall X (iff (= (f X) t) def))` with `f` ranging over a declare-sort sort, Go can accept a pseudo-predicate macro that C++ rejects. `pseudo_predicate_macro2macro` then asserts `forall X. k(X) != t`. That is unsatisfiable when the uninterpreted sort has one element, so if this path is reached it is a soundness risk (a wrong unsat).

**Reproduction.** Tried `pp1.smt2`–`pp5.smt2` in the work dir: a singleton-forced sort `S` under `smt.macro_finder=true` and under the macro-finder tactic. Both binaries answered sat and gave the same output. The pseudo-predicate shape did not reach the finder (the body arrives as OP_EQ, not OP_IFF, in these paths), so I could not confirm reachability.

**Fix.** Replace the family test with:
```go
uninterp, err := u.manager.IsUninterpretedSort(sort)
if err != nil || uninterp {
    return head, ground, false, err
}
```

**Regression test.** Extend `TestMacroUtilArithmeticCandidatesAndPseudoPredicates` in `pkg/ast/macros/macro_util_test.go`:
- Make `S` with `m.MkUninterpretedSort(sym("S"), nil)`, `f : Int -> S` and a constant `c : S`.
- Build `(forall ((x Int)) (iff (= (f x) c) (p x)))`, with the iff made through the basic family OP_IFF.
- Assert that `IsPseudoPredicateMacro` returns `matched == false`.

<a id="ast-sub-01-f5"></a>
#### ast_sub_01-F5: quasi_macro_head_to_macro_head builds the head app before the condition `and`

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/ast/macros/macro_candidates.go:55-66` (`Util.QuasiMacroHeadToMacroHead`)
- C++: `src/ast/macros/macro_util.cpp:430-431`

**C++ behavior.** The condition is built first, then the head:
```
bool_rewriter(m_manager).mk_and(new_conds.size(), new_conds.c_ptr(), cond);
head = m_manager.mk_app(qhead->get_decl(), new_args.size(), new_args.c_ptr());
```

**Go behavior.** The head is built first (`MkApp(declaration, args)`), then the condition (`MkAndArray(conditions)`).

**Impact.** With two or more new equalities, the `and` node and the head app get their AST ids in the opposite order. Anything that later orders by id (hash tables, id-sorted arguments) can diverge in traces or iteration order. There is no semantic effect.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: there is no CLI-visible output.

**Fix.** Move the `MkAndArray(conditions)` call (or the bool_rewriter `mk_and` from F3) above `MkApp(declaration, args)` in `QuasiMacroHeadToMacroHead`.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/ast/macros/macro_util_test.go`, add `TestQuasiMacroHeadConditionBuiltBeforeHead`:
- Call `QuasiMacroHeadToMacroHead` on `f(x0, x0, x0)` with 1 declaration, which gives two equalities.
- Assert that `m.GetID(cond) < m.GetID(head)`, or whatever id accessor the AST package exposes.

<a id="ast-sub-02-f1"></a>
#### ast_sub_02-F1: NNF and/or uses ast_util MkAndArray/MkOrArray, so unary and/or are dropped, and with proofs the tactic fails

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/ast/normal_forms/nnf.go:397-399` (`NNF.convertApp`, OP_AND/OP_OR case); also `:430-432` (implies; harmless there because it always has 2 args)
- C++: `src/ast/normal_forms/nnf.cpp:470-475` (`nnf::imp::process_and_or`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
if (m().is_and(t) == fr.m_pol)
    r = m().mk_and(t->get_num_args(), m_result_stack.c_ptr() + fr.m_spos);
else
    r = m().mk_or(t->get_num_args(), m_result_stack.c_ptr() + fr.m_spos);
...
proof * pr = mk_proof(fr.m_pol, t->get_num_args(), ..., t, r);   // r is an app
```
`ast_manager::mk_and/mk_or(n, args)` is `mk_app(basic, OP_AND/OR, n, args)`. A unary `(and x)` stays `(and x')` and a negated one becomes `(or x')`.

**Go behavior.**
```go
if isAnd == polarity {
    value, x = m.MkAndArray(args)   // ast_util overload: 0 -> true, 1 -> args[0]
} else {
    value, x = m.MkOrArray(args)    // 0 -> false, 1 -> args[0]
}
...
proof, x = n.mkProof(polarity, t, value, ...)  // GetDecl(value) fails if value is a quantifier
```

**Impact.** Any unary and/or that contains a quantifier or label, reached through the `nnf`/`snf` tactics or any other caller that does not simplify first, gives a different formula. With proofs on, `mkProof` calls `GetDecl` on the collapsed child. When that child is a quantifier this fails, and the whole command fails with "AST source precondition".

**Reproduction.** Confirmed.
```smt2
(declare-fun p (Int) Bool)
(declare-fun q () Bool)
(assert (or (and (forall ((x Int)) (p x))) q))
(assert (or (not (or (exists ((x Int)) (p x)))) q))
(apply nnf)
```
z3: `(or (and (forall ((x Int)) (p x))) q)` and `(let ((a!1 (and (forall ((x Int)) (not (p x)))))) (or a!1 q))`.
g3: `(or (forall ((x Int)) (p x)) q)` and `(or (forall ((x Int)) (not (p x))) q)`.
With `(set-option :produce-proofs true)` and only the first assertion, z3 prints the goal and g3 prints `(error "line 5 column 10: g3: AST source precondition")`.

**Fix.** In `convertApp`'s OP_AND/OP_OR case, replace `MkAndArray`/`MkOrArray` with `m.MkFamilyApp(m.BasicFamilyID(), ast.ASTOpAnd/ast.ASTOpOr, nil, args)`, which is `ast_manager::mk_and/mk_or(n, args)`. Do the same in the implies case for consistency. `MkOr`/`MkAnd` with 2 args already use `MkFamilyApp`.

**Regression test.** Extend `pkg/ast/normal_forms/nnf_test.go` with `TestNNFUnaryAndOrKeepsConnective`. Use `nnfOwner(t, true, DefaultNNFOptions())`, build a quantifier like `TestNNFLabelsAndIntroducedDefinitions` does, wrap it with `m.MkFamilyApp(0, ast.ASTOpAnd, nil, []ast.ASTHandle{q})`, run `nnfTransform`, and assert the result's decl kind is `ASTOpAnd` with 1 arg and the proof is non-null. Repeat under `not` and expect `ASTOpOr`. Add an SMT vector `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/nnf_unary_and_or.smt2` containing the script above plus a proof variant. The expected `scriptResults` text is the z3 output quoted above. Check it with `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`.

<a id="ast-sub-02-f2"></a>
#### ast_sub_02-F2: pattern-inference pull proof uses `rewrite` instead of the pull_quant proof chain

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/ast/pattern/reduce_quantifier.go:371-380` (`reduceQuantifierNoDatabaseCore`); also the `pullRefl` stand-in at `:297-310`
- C++: `src/ast/pattern/pattern_inference.cpp:679-697` (`pattern_inference_cfg::reduce_quantifier`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
pull_quant pull(m);
pull(new_q, new_expr, new_pr);   // rewriter_tpl with ProofGen: quant-intro/pull-quant/trans proof
...
result_pr = m.mk_transitivity(new_pr, m.mk_quant_intro(result2, new_q, m.mk_reflexivity(new_q->get_expr())));
```

**Go behavior.**
```go
pulledRef, e := c.pullNoProof(preliminary)       // proof-free pull
...
pulledProof, e = c.manager.MkProofRewrite(preliminary, pulled)
...
proof, e = c.manager.MkProofTransitivity(pulledProof, proof)
```

**Impact.** With proofs on, every quantifier whose patterns are found only after pulling gets a different proof term (`rewrite` instead of `pull-quant`/`quant-intro`). `(get-proof)` output then differs, and so do proof-consuming paths such as the checker, interpolation and the proof printers.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed.
```smt2
(set-option :produce-proofs true)
(declare-fun p (Int Int) Bool)
(assert (forall ((y Int)) (or (forall ((x Int)) (p x y)) (> y 0))))
(assert (not (p 0 0)))
(check-sat)
(get-proof)
```
z3: `(trans (quant-intro (pull-quant (= $x63 $x76)) (= $x66 $x79)) (pull-quant (= $x79 $x82)) (= $x66 $x82))` followed by a quant-intro step.
g3: `(trans (rewrite (= $x66 $x77)) (quant-intro (refl (= $x75 $x75)) (= $x77 $x79)) (= $x66 $x79))`.
The ids and the final unit-resolution layout also differ.

**Fix.** When proofs are enabled, run the proof-producing pull instead of `pullNoProof`: `normal_forms.NewPullQuant(m)` and `RewriteWithProof(preliminary, out, pr)`, a fresh object per call like the C++ local `pull_quant pull(m)`. Use its proof as `pulledProof`. Remove the `pullRefl` stand-in, because the rewriter supplies the reflexivity itself. Keep `pullNoProof` for the no-proof path.

**Regression test.** Add `TestPatternInferencePullProofUsesPullQuant` to `pkg/ast/pattern/reduce_quantifier_test.go`, using that file's `patternManager` helpers with proofs enabled. Build `forall y. (or (forall x. p(x,y)) (> y 0))`, call `reduceQuantifierNoDatabaseWithProof`, and check that the returned proof is a transitivity whose first parent has kind `ASTPrQuantIntro` with a `ASTPrPullQuant` child, not `ASTPrRewrite`. SMT vector: the script above as `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/pattern_pull_proof.smt2`, with the z3 output as the expected result.

<a id="ast-sub-02-f3"></a>
#### ast_sub_02-F3: PullQuantifierNoProof has no cache for shared subterms, so pull_quant runs again on each occurrence (extra fresh names; can blow up on DAGs)

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/ast/normal_forms/pull_boolean.go:41-162` (`pullQuantCore.pullExpr`), used by `pkg/ast/pattern/pull_boolean.go` (pattern inference) and `pkg/ast/pattern/pull_quantifier.go` (MBQI model finder)
- C++: `src/ast/normal_forms/pull_quant.cpp:302-307` with `src/ast/rewriter/rewriter_def.h:108-150` (`rewriter_tpl::visit` caches shared nodes)

**C++ behavior.** `pull_quant` is a `rewriter_tpl`. A node with ref count above 1 is rewritten once, and later occurrences take the cached result (`must_cache`/`get_cached`). `pull_quant1_core` calls `m_manager.mk_fresh_var_name` for duplicate binder names, so it runs once per distinct shared subterm.

**Go behavior.** `pullExpr` recurses over the DAG as a tree, without memoization. A shared subterm that contains quantifiers is pulled again on every occurrence. Each pass draws new `mk_fresh_var_name` names, which advances the shared `m_fresh_id` counter, and the copies come out with different bound-variable names. The work is exponential in DAG depth.

**Impact.** Pattern inference (`pi.pull_quantifiers=true`, the default) and MBQI on quantifiers with shared nested quantifiers get pulled quantifiers with different variable names and a different fresh counter. Traces differ, and skolem/fresh names printed later can differ. Heavily shared inputs can hang.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed with the C++ trace build (`build_trace/z3`) and a g3 built with `-tags g3trace` in the work dir.
```smt2
(declare-fun p (Int Int) Bool)
(declare-fun q (Int Int) Bool)
(assert (forall ((y Int))
  (or (and (or (forall ((x Int)) (p x y)) (forall ((x Int)) (q x y))) (> y 0))
      (and (or (forall ((x Int)) (p x y)) (forall ((x Int)) (q x y))) (< y 5)))))
(check-sat)
```
Run with `-tr:pull_quant -tr:pattern_inference`. C++ prints 4 `Result num decls` lines per pull and `pulled quantifier: (forall ((y Int) (x!0!2 Int) (x!1 Int) (x!0 Int) (x Int)) ...`. g3 prints 5 lines (the shared `(or (forall..) (forall..))` is pulled twice) and `(forall ((y Int) (x!1 Int) (x!2 Int) (x!0 Int) (x Int)) ...` with `(p x!2 y) (q x!1 y)`. Plain sat/model output is the same for this input.

**Fix.** Give `pullQuantCore` a per-call cache keyed by the node: `map[ast.ASTHandle]ast.ASTRef`, holding a ref per entry and released at the end of `PullQuantifierNoProof`. Only nodes with `GetRefCount > 1` that are not the root, and are apps with args or quantifiers, should be cached, matching `rewriter_core::must_cache`. The simpler fix is to replace `PullQuantifierNoProof` with the existing `PullQuant` traversal (`NewPullQuant` + `RewriteWithProof`), which already follows `rewriter_tpl`. Note that rewriter_tpl also visits quantifier patterns.

**Regression test.** Add `TestPatternPullNoProofSharedSubtermPulledOnce` to `pkg/ast/pattern/pull_boolean_test.go`, following `TestPatternPullNoProofIdentityAndSourcePreconditionGuards` (`patternManager`, `newPatternCandidates`, `pullNoProof`). Build the formula above with one shared `or` node. Pull it, then check that both `and` branches carry the same inner variable names, and that `MkFreshVarName(nil)` afterwards returns `var!3`, i.e. 3 fresh names were consumed. Also add a trace-tag vector under the g3trace build, comparing `Result num decls` counts with the C++.

<a id="ast-sub-02-f5"></a>
#### ast_sub_02-F5: NNF ite/iff/xor build the two disjunctions in the wrong order (GCC evaluates arguments right to left)

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/ast/normal_forms/nnf.go:474-508` (`convertITE`), `:510-551` (`convertIffXor`)
- C++: `src/ast/normal_forms/nnf.cpp:572` (`process_ite`), `:614-617` (`process_iff_xor`)

**C++ behavior.** `app * r = m().mk_and(m().mk_or(_not_cond, _then), m().mk_or(_cond, _else));` and `r = m().mk_and(m().mk_or(not_lhs, rhs), m().mk_or(lhs, not_rhs));` (likewise in the else branch). GCC evaluates the second `mk_or` first, so it gets the smaller AST id.

**Go behavior.** `x := MkOr(na, b)` then `y := MkOr(a, c)`, and in iff/xor `a := MkOr(...)` then `b := MkOr(...)`. The first disjunction is built first.

**Impact.** The two new `or` nodes get swapped AST ids for every ite/iff/xor/bool-`=` processed by NNF. That changes id-ordered behaviour downstream (sorting by id, hash-table order, traces). The project relies on GCC's right-to-left order elsewhere (`defined_names.go:378` and 60+ other comments).

**Reproduction.** not attempted: the effect is on node ids; it would need a `-tr:` comparison of ids after nnf.

**Fix.** Build the second disjunction first in each case: in `convertITE`, `y := MkOr(a.value, c.value)` then `x := MkOr(na.value, b.value)`, then `MkAnd(x, y)`. Swap the order the same way in both branches of `convertIffXor`.

**Regression test.** Add `TestNNFIteBuildsElseDisjunctFirst` to `pkg/ast/normal_forms/nnf_test.go`. Use `nnfOwner(t, false, options with NNFFull)` on `(ite c a b)` with fresh bool constants, then check that `GetASTID` of the result's arg 1 (`(or c b)`) is smaller than that of arg 0. Do the same for iff and xor.

<a id="ast-sub-02-f6"></a>
#### ast_sub_02-F6: defined_names builds both conjuncts before quantifying either

- Severity: low

- C++: `src/ast/normal_forms/defined_names.cpp:174-188` (`defined_names::impl::mk_definition`)

**Reproduction.** not attempted: only the id order differs.

**Fix.** Call `t.boundVars(conjuncts[0], ...)` right after building `conjuncts[0]`, before building `notE`/`eqElse` and `conjuncts[1]`, then quantify `conjuncts[1]`.

**Regression test.** Add `TestDefinedNamesQuantifiesFirstConjunctFirst` to `pkg/ast/normal_forms/defined_names_test.go`. <a id="ast-sub-02-f11"></a>
#### ast_sub_02-F11: checker side conditions use the ast_util or/and, which collapse 0/1-arg cases

**Impact.** The returned side-condition ASTs differ from C++.
