<a id="tactic-arith-03-f6"></a>
#### tactic_arith_03-F6: arith-max-deg / arith-avg-deg / arith-max-bw / arith-avg-bw ignore quantifier bodies and patterns

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/arith/probe_arith_statistics_traversal.go:9-53` (`statisticApplications`)
- C++: `src/tactic/goal.h:161-166` (`for_each_expr_at`), `src/ast/for_each_expr.h:121-123` (MarkAll, patterns not ignored), `src/tactic/arith/probe_arith.cpp:79,122`

**C++ behavior.** `for_each_expr_at` uses `for_each_expr_core<..., true, false>`. That walk descends
into quantifier bodies, patterns and no-patterns, and calls the proc on every app inside them
(variables become polynomial variables in `expr2polynomial`).

**Go behavior.** `if k != ast.ASTApp { continue }`, so the walk never enters a quantifier.

**Impact.** The probe values differ on any quantified goal, so `fail-if`/`cond` strategies take
different branches.

**Reproduction.**
```
(declare-fun f (Int) Int)
(declare-const x Int)
(assert (> x 1))
(assert (forall ((y Int)) (> (* y y y (f y)) 123456789)))
(apply (fail-if (> arith-max-bw 5)))
(apply (fail-if (> arith-max-deg 1)))
```
z3 prints `(error "tactic failed: fail-if tactic")` twice. g3 prints the unchanged goal twice.

**Fix.** Build the app list with the same walk as `visitArithmeticGoal` (body, patterns,
no-patterns), for example by calling `visitArithmeticGoal(g, func(h, kind) { if kind == ast.ASTApp { out = append(out, h) }; return false, nil })`.
Sums and maxima do not depend on order.

**Regression test.** Add vector `probe_arith_quantified_stats.smt2` (the script above) with expected
`"(error \"tactic failed: fail-if tactic\")\n(error \"tactic failed: fail-if tactic\")\n"` (or the
form the runner expects for tactic failures). Also add
`TestArithmeticStatisticsDescendIntoQuantifiers` to `probe_arith_statistics_shared_test.go` using
the `statisticGoal` helper.

<a id="tactic-arith-03-f7"></a>
#### tactic_arith_03-F7: recover-01 extension model converter puts all Boolean definitions first; z3 interleaves them with each recovered variable

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/arith/recover_01_model.go:48-67` (`recover01Definitions.publishModel`)
- C++: `src/tactic/arith/recover_01_tactic.cpp:207-210,290-292` (`mk_ivar`, `process`)

**C++ behavior.** `mc1->insert(atom, bool_def)` runs in `mk_ivar` when an atom is first seen, and
`mc1->insert(x, x_def)` runs at the end of each `process(x, ...)`. The extension order is
`atoms(x1), x1, new atoms(x2), x2, ...`.

**Go behavior.** It first loops `d.booleans` (all atoms), then `d.variables`.

**Impact.** With two or more recovered variables, the printed model converter differs, and so does
the order of definitions in `get-model`.

**Reproduction.** Variables x, y Int and p, q, r Bool. Clauses
`(or p q (= x 0))`, `(or (not p) q (= x 3))`, `(or p (not q) (= x 5))`, `(or (not p) (not q) (= x 8))`,
`(or r (= y 0))`, `(or (not r) (= y 7))`, `(assert (> (+ x y) 9))`.
`(apply recover-01 :print_model_converter true)`: z3 prints `(r ...) (y ...) (p ...) (q ...) (x ...)`;
g3 prints `(r ...) (p ...) (q ...) (y ...) (x ...)`.
`(check-sat-using (then recover-01 smt))(get-model)`: z3 lists `y` before `r`; g3 lists it after.

**Fix.** Add `extensionOrder []ast.ASTHandle` to `recover01Definitions`. Append the atom in
`booleanVariable` when it is created, and the variable at the end of `build` (where
`d.variables` is appended). `publishModel` inserts the filter entries from `d.booleans` as now,
then calls `insert` in `extensionOrder` order.

**Regression test.** Add vector `recover01_two_vars_mc.smt2` (the script above). Its expected output
is z3's text. Add `TestRecover01ExtensionOrderInterleaved` to `recover_01_model_test.go` (pattern
of `TestRecover01ModelReconstruction`).

<a id="tactic-arith-03-f8"></a>
#### tactic_arith_03-F8: purify-arith adds a `quant-intro (refl ...)` step for every unchanged quantifier when proofs are on

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/arith/qfnra_purify_quantifier.go:198-213` (`processQuantifier`)
- C++: `src/tactic/arith/purify_arith_tactic.cpp:693-708`, `src/ast/ast.cpp:2798-2799`

**C++ behavior.** `result_pr = nullptr; ... if (num_vars == 0) { result = update_quantifier(q, new_body); result_pr = m().mk_quant_intro(q, result, result_pr); }`.
`mk_quant_intro` returns `nullptr` for a null premise, so an unchanged quantifier keeps its original
proof.

**Go behavior.**
```go
if bodyProof.IsNull() { bodyProof, err = m.MkProofReflexivity(body) }
proof, err = m.MkProofQuantIntro(q, result, bodyProof)
```
This runs for every quantifier, changed or not. The manifest records a deviation that keeps the
real body proof when the body changes. The unchanged case is not covered by that reason: there is
nothing to fix there.

**Impact.** Any proof-producing run that reaches purify-arith on quantified assertions gets a
different proof: an extra `(quant-intro (refl ...) (= $x $x))` and a different `mp`/`mp~` nesting.

**Reproduction.**
```
(set-option :produce-proofs true)
(declare-fun f (Int) Int)
(assert (forall ((x Int)) (> (f x) 0)))
(assert (< (f 1) 0))
(check-sat-using (then purify-arith smt))
(get-proof)
```
g3's proof has an extra line `(let ((@x64 (quant-intro (refl (= (not (<= (f ?0) 0)) (not (<= (f ?0) 0)))) (= $x33 $x33))))`
and a different `mp` chain.

**Fix.** In `processQuantifier`, when `result == q` (or when `bodyProof.IsNull()` and no
constraints or bound entries exist), return a null `proof`. Keep the recorded deviation for changed
bodies.

**Regression test.** Extend `TestPurifyUnchangedQuantifierWithProof`
(`pkg/tactic/arith/qfnra_purify_quantifier_test.go:187`) to require `goal.Proof(0) == p`, the
original asserted proof. Add vector `purify_arith_unchanged_quantifier_proof.smt2` (the script
above). Its expected output is z3's proof.

<a id="tactic-arith-03-f9"></a>
#### tactic_arith_03-F9: recover-01 rewrite loop reads past the goal after an update makes it inconsistent

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/arith/recover_01_apply.go:158-177` (`recover01Apply`)
- C++: `src/tactic/arith/recover_01_tactic.cpp:369-374` (same loop; z3 segfaults)

**C++ behavior.** `size` is read once. `new_goal->update(idx, new_curr)` with a `false` result
collapses the goal to `false`, and the next `new_goal->form(idx)` reads out of range. z3 4.7.1
crashes with a segmentation fault.

**Go behavior.** It has the same loop. `newGoal.Form(i)` returns "arena: vector index or length out
of bounds", which becomes the command's error.

**Impact.** On a goal that recover-01 rewrites to `false` before its last form, g3 reports an error
instead of the goal `false`. This is the recover-01 instance of the pattern recorded as FUZZ_J-F1
(lia2card).

**Reproduction.**
```
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const p Bool)
(declare-const b Bool)
(assert (= p (not p)))
(assert b)
(assert (> x 0))
(assert (or p (= x 0)))
(assert (or (not p) (= x 3)))
(apply recover-01)
```
z3: segmentation fault. g3: `(error "line 9 column 17: arena: vector index or length out of bounds")`.

**Fix.** At the top of the loop body, call `newGoal.Inconsistent()` and `break` if it is true. That
matches the intent of C++ `goal::update`, which returns at once when the goal is inconsistent.
Because z3 crashes, handle it as a fork fix and add the vector to `z3_bug_exclusions.txt`.

**Regression test.** Add vector `z3_bug_recover01_inconsistent_update.smt2` (the script above).
Expected output: `"(goals\n(goal\n  false\n  :precision precise :depth 1)\n)\n"`. List it in
`z3_bug_exclusions.txt`. Add a unit test in `recover_01_apply_test.go`.

<a id="tactic-arith-03-f10"></a>
#### tactic_arith_03-F10: purify-arith still builds some terms in a different order from z3 (even roots, zero power, root objects, inverse trig with proofs)

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/tactic/arith/qfnra_purify_tactic.go:475-500,519-574` (`processPower`); `pkg/tactic/arith/root_object_purify_process.go:33-87` (`processRootObjectConstraints`); `pkg/tactic/arith/qfnra_purify_inverse_trig.go:108-120`
- C++: `src/tactic/arith/purify_arith_tactic.cpp:418,435-437,486-493,557-562`

**C++ behavior (GCC right-to-left).**
- Even root, `OR(NOT(mk_ge(x,0)), AND(EQ(x, mk_power(k, n)), mk_ge(k,0)))`: order is `k>=0`, `n`,
  `k^n`, `x=k^n`, `and`, `x>=0`, `not`, `or`.
- Zero power, second constraint `OR(NOT(EQ(x,zero)), EQ(k, mk_power(zero,zero)))`: order is
  `0^0`, `k=0^0`, `not`, `or`.
- `process_irrat`: the exponent numeral and power come before the coefficient numeral, because `m`
  is computed in an earlier statement. `EQ(mk_add(...), mk_real_zero())` builds zero before the add.
- asin/acos complete: `push_cnstr(c1); push_cnstr_pr(...)` runs before `c2` is built.

**Go behavior.** Even root: `n`, `k^n`, `x=k^n`, `x>=0`, `not`, `k>=0`, `and`, `or`. Zero power:
`not` is built before `0^0`. Root object: coefficient first, and the sum before zero. Inverse trig:
both guards are built before either is added, so with proofs the th-lemma proofs come after both.

**Impact.** Only AST ids and their side effects (id-sorted output, traces). The zero-power part is
what is left of FUZZ_C-F7 after that fix.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted at the AST-id level. Printed goals for
`(^ x 0.5) (^ y (/ 1.0 3.0)) (to_int z) (asin x) (acos y) (atan z)` are identical.

**Fix.** Reorder the constructors to match the sequences above. In `qfnra_purify_inverse_trig.go`,
call `addConstraint(lowerGuard)` before building `upperGuard`.

**Regression test.** Covered by the purify-arith trace comparison used for FUZZ_C-F7. Add a
`(^ x 0.5)` vector, a `(^ x 0)` vector and a `root-obj` vector to that trace set.

### Area: Bit-vector tactics (`pkg/tactic/bv`)

*tactic_bv_01.* This shard is `pkg/tactic/bv`: bit-blaster and bv1-blaster tactics and their model converter, bv_bound_chk, propagate-bv-bounds (ctx and dom variants), reduce-bv-size, bvarray2uf, dt2bv, elim-small-bv, max-bv-sharing, the context-translation helpers, and a bv-slice tactic that has no counterpart in 4.7.1. Most files track the C++ closely. bit-blast, reduce-bv-size, bvarray2uf, max-bv-sharing and bv_bound_chk all give the same output as `build/z3` on differential inputs. elim-small-bv has a soundness bug: when `max_steps` is set, g3 turns a quantifier into `true` (confirmed: g3 says `sat` where z3 says `unsat`). Other confirmed divergences: model order after bv1-blast, a bv-bounds recognizer that treats numeral-numeral equalities as bounds, a wrong param set passed to elim-small-bv's th_rewriter, a missing `produce_models` param descriptor in bvarray2uf, and missing tactic report and help text in elim-small-bv. Counts: critical 1, high 0, medium 4, low 4.

<a id="tactic-bv-01-f1"></a>
#### tactic_bv_01-F1: elim-small-bv step counter is cumulative and loses the outer-loop guard; a quantifier becomes `true`

- Severity: critical
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/bv/elim_small_bv_tactic.go:192-205,236-328` (`elimSmallBVConfig.checkpoint`, `ReduceQuantifier`)
- C++: `src/tactic/bv/elim_small_bv_tactic.cpp:129-177` (`rw_cfg::reduce_quantifier`)

**C++ behavior.** `num_steps` is a local of `reduce_quantifier`, so it restarts at 0 for every quantifier. The step limit is checked in the outer loop and again before a variable is expanded, so a variable is either expanded or left alone. A variable never gets an empty disjunction or conjunction.
```cpp
unsigned long long num_steps = 0;
...
for (unsigned i = num_decls-1; i != ((unsigned)-1) && !max_steps_exceeded(num_steps); i--) {
    ...
    if (is_small_bv(s) && !max_steps_exceeded(num_steps)) {
        expr_ref_vector new_bodies(m);
        for (unsigned j = 0; j < bv_sz && !max_steps_exceeded(num_steps); j ++) { ... num_steps++; }
        body = q->is_forall() ? m.mk_and(new_bodies...) : m.mk_or(new_bodies...);
```

**Go behavior.** `c.steps` is a field of the config, so it keeps counting across every quantifier in the goal. Only the inner loop checks the limit (`checkpoint`, which does `if c.steps > c.maxSteps`). After the limit is hit, every later small variable gets `bodies == []`, and `MkAndArray([])` returns `true` (`MkOrArray([])` returns `false`):
```go
for i := int(n) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
    ... if width > c.maxBits { continue }
    bodies := []ast.ASTHandle{}
    for j := uint32(0); j < width; j++ {
        stop, e := c.checkpoint(); ... if stop { break }
        ... c.steps++
    }
    if forall { current, e = m.MkAndArray(bodies) } else { current, e = m.MkOrArray(bodies) }
```

**Impact.** Any goal with several small-BV quantifiers run through `elim-small-bv` with `max_steps` set. The later universal quantifiers become `true`, so their constraints are dropped and an unsat problem can be reported `sat`. The later existential quantifiers become `false`.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed with `$S/bin/g3` and `build/z3`:
```smt2
(declare-fun q ((_ BitVec 2)) Bool)
(declare-fun r ((_ BitVec 2)) Bool)
(declare-fun s ((_ BitVec 2)) Bool)
(assert (forall ((x (_ BitVec 2))) (q x)))
(assert (forall ((y (_ BitVec 2))) (r y)))
(assert (forall ((y (_ BitVec 2))) (s y)))
(assert (forall ((y (_ BitVec 2))) (= y #b11)))
(check-sat-using (then (using-params elim-small-bv :max_steps 5) smt))
```
z3: `unsat`. g3: `sat`. With six single-variable assertions `(forall ((y (_ BitVec 2))) (u y))` and `(apply (using-params elim-small-bv :max_steps 6))`, g3 prints `true` for the last two assertions. z3 expands all of them.

**Fix.** In `ReduceQuantifier`:
1. Add a local `var numSteps uint64` that starts at 0 for each call, and remove the `steps` field (or reset it at the start of each call).
2. Make `checkpoint` take the step count as an argument, for example `checkpoint(n uint64) (bool, error)`. It should cooperate, check the memory limit, and return `n > maxSteps`.
3. Copy the C++ guards. Stop the outer loop when `checkpoint(numSteps)` reports exceeded. Expand a variable only when `width <= maxBits && !exceeded`. Keep the inner check on each `j`.
```go
for i := int(n) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
    if stop, e := c.checkpoint(numSteps); e != nil { return false, e } else if stop { break }
    ... // sort, IsBitVectorSort, width
    if !is || width > c.maxBits { continue }
    if stop, e := c.checkpoint(numSteps); e != nil { return false, e } else if stop { continue }
    for j := uint32(0); j < width; j++ {
        if stop, e := c.checkpoint(numSteps); e != nil { return false, e } else if stop { break }
        ...; numSteps++
    }
```
Note that C++ calls `get_bv_size(s)` before testing `is_small_bv`, so the sort check and the call order do not change. C++ can still build a conjunction from a partial inner loop; keep that behaviour.

**Regression test.** Extend `pkg/tactic/bv/elim_small_bv_tactic_test.go` with `TestElimSmallBVStepLimitIsPerQuantifier`. Build the fixture the way `TestElimSmallBVRetainsSourceWidthBoundEnumerationAndLifecycle` does (`sharingTacticFixture`, `NewElimSmallBVTactic`, `m.MkVar`, `m.MkQuantifier`, `tactic.NewGoal`). Assert four quantifiers `forall y:bv2. p_k(y)`, built with `m.MkFreshFuncDecl` or a declared unary predicate. Pass a params ref with `max_steps = 5` through `UpdateParams`. Expect 8 result formulas `(p_k #b00)` and `(p_k #b01)`, and no `true` in the goal. Also add the SMT-LIB input above as `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/elim_small_bv_step_limit_per_quantifier.smt2`, with `"elim_small_bv_step_limit_per_quantifier.smt2": "unsat\n"` in `scriptResults`. Check it with `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`.

<a id="tactic-bv-01-f2"></a>
#### tactic_bv_01-F2: elim-small-bv passes its tactic params to the th_rewriter, and its own rewriter has no `max_steps_exceeded` hook

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/bv/elim_small_bv_tactic.go:384` (`Apply`: `NewTheoryRewriter(..., &t.params)`), `:160-205` (`elimSmallBVConfig` has no `MaxStepsExceeded`)
- C++: `src/tactic/bv/elim_small_bv_tactic.cpp:46-63` (`rw_cfg` ctor `m_simp(_m)`, `max_steps_exceeded`)

**C++ behavior.** `th_rewriter m_simp(_m)` is built with the default (empty) params. The tactic's `max_steps`, `max_memory` and `max_bits` never reach the simplifier. `rw_cfg::max_steps_exceeded(unsigned long long)` hides the default, so the enclosing `rewriter_tpl` calls it from `check_max_steps()`. That call cooperates, throws on memory, and throws a rewriter `max. steps exceeded` when the outer rewriter's step count passes `m_max_steps`.

**Go behavior.** `cfg.simplify, e = rewriter.NewTheoryRewriter(t.manager, t.context, t.globals, &t.params)`. The th_rewriter inherits `max_steps` and every other user parameter, so a small `max_steps` makes the *simplifier* throw. `elimSmallBVConfig` relies on `DefaultConfiguration.MaxStepsExceeded`, which returns false, so the outer traversal never checks steps or memory and never cooperates.

**Impact.** `(using-params elim-small-bv :max_steps k)` gives an error in g3 where z3 returns a partially expanded goal. Other th_rewriter options passed to the tactic, for example `:som true`, change elim-small-bv's output only in g3.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed:
```smt2
(declare-fun p ((_ BitVec 2) (_ BitVec 2) (_ BitVec 2)) Bool)
(declare-fun q ((_ BitVec 2)) Bool)
(assert (forall ((x (_ BitVec 2)) (y (_ BitVec 2)) (z (_ BitVec 2))) (p x y z)))
(assert (forall ((x (_ BitVec 2))) (q x)))
(apply (using-params elim-small-bv :max_steps 3))
```
z3: `(goals\n(goal\n  (forall ((x (_ BitVec 2)))\n    (and (p x #b00 #b00) (p x #b00 #b01) (p x #b01 #b00) (p x #b01 #b01)))\n  (q #b00)\n  (q #b01)\n  :precision precise :depth 1)\n)\n`. g3: `(error "line 5 column 48: max. steps exceeded")`. max_steps values 3 through 8 all differ.

**Fix.**
1. Build the simplifier with an empty params value, for example `empty := t.context.EmptyValue(); rewriter.NewTheoryRewriter(t.manager, t.context, t.globals, &empty)`. Keep `t.params` for `ElimUnusedVarsWithParams` (C++ `unused_vars_eliminator el(m, m_params)`).
2. Add `func (c *elimSmallBVConfig) MaxStepsExceeded(n uint32) (bool, error)`. It cooperates with "elim-small-bv", returns `true` when `uint64(n) > maxSteps`, and then returns `tactic.NewTacticException(tactic.TacticMaxMemoryMessage)` when allocation exceeds `maxMemory`. That is the C++ order: steps first, then memory. Use the same memory counter as the sibling tactics (`services.Memory.AllocationSize()`). The current code uses `Budget().Used()`.
3. Do this together with F1, so `ReduceQuantifier` calls the per-call counter and this hook calls the traversal count.
4. Check whether C++ resetting `m_max_steps = UINT_MAX` in the `rw_cfg` constructor matters for factory-time params. In the cmd context `using-params` always calls `updt_params`, so no difference was observed.

**Regression test.** Add the input above as `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/elim_small_bv_max_steps_simplifier.smt2`, with the z3 output quoted above in `scriptResults`, and check it with `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference`. Also add `TestElimSmallBVSimplifierIgnoresTacticParams` to `elim_small_bv_tactic_test.go`: with `max_steps = 3`, `Apply` on the two-quantifier goal must succeed, and the first formula must still be a quantifier.

<a id="tactic-bv-01-f3"></a>
#### tactic_bv_01-F3: bv1-blast model converter lists variables in insertion order, not `obj_map` order

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/bv/bv1_blaster_rewriter.go:106-150` (`constant`: `r.constants` Go map plus `r.bindings` slice), `pkg/tactic/bv/bv1_blaster_tactic.go:457-458`
- C++: `src/tactic/bv/bv1_blaster_tactic.cpp:91-111,393-394`; `src/tactic/bv/bit_blaster_model_converter.cpp:38-48`

**C++ behavior.** `m_const2bits` is an `obj_map<func_decl, expr*>`. `mk_bv1_blaster_model_converter(m(), m_rw.cfg().m_const2bits)` copies it into `m_vars`/`m_bits` in hash-table iteration order. `mk_bvs` then calls `register_decl` in that order, which sets the order of `get-model` output.

**Go behavior.** The bindings are appended in first-encounter order (`r.bindings = append(r.bindings, BitBlasterBinding{Variable: d, Bits: h})`) and passed straight to `NewBV1BlasterModelConverter`. The bit-blast tactic handles this correctly by reading `r.active.Const2Bits()`, which is backed by `ast.ObjMap`, and its comment says "mk_bit_blaster_model_converter walks const2bits in obj_map order".

**Impact.** Any `bv1-blast` run with models enabled prints model constants in a different order from z3.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed:
```smt2
(set-option :produce-models true)
(declare-const a (_ BitVec 4))
(declare-const b (_ BitVec 4))
(declare-const c (_ BitVec 4))
(declare-const d (_ BitVec 4))
(declare-const e (_ BitVec 4))
(assert (= ((_ extract 1 0) e) #b10))
(assert (= ((_ extract 1 0) d) #b01))
(assert (= ((_ extract 3 2) c) #b11))
(assert (= ((_ extract 3 2) b) #b01))
(assert (= ((_ extract 2 1) a) #b10))
(check-sat-using (then bv1-blast smt))
(get-model)
```
z3 prints e, c, d, b, a. g3 prints e, d, c, b, a. The same input with `bit-blast` matches z3.

**Fix.** Store the constant map as `*ast.ObjMap` (`ast.NewObjMap(m)`, `Insert(d, [2]ast.ASTHandle{h})`, `Find`), as the bit-blaster rewriter does (`pkg/ast/rewriter/bit_blaster/rewriter_core.go:36-38,243,294`). Build the bindings at `Apply` time from `constants.Entries()`, in place of the append-order slice. Keep the existing IncRef bookkeeping. Remove `r.bindings` or derive it from the map.

**Regression test.** Add the input above as `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/bv1_blast_model_order.smt2`, with expected `"sat\n(model \n  (define-fun e () (_ BitVec 4)\n    #x2)\n  (define-fun c () (_ BitVec 4)\n    #xc)\n  (define-fun d () (_ BitVec 4)\n    #x1)\n  (define-fun b () (_ BitVec 4)\n    #x4)\n  (define-fun a () (_ BitVec 4)\n    #x4)\n)\n"`, and check it with `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference`. A unit check can go in `bv1_blaster_cpp_test.go` next to `TestBV1BlasterModelConverterSurvivesTacticClose`: compare the order of the converter's `variables` with the `ast.ObjMap` entry order for the same inserts.

<a id="tactic-bv-01-f4"></a>
#### tactic_bv_01-F4: bv-bounds `is_bound` accepts `(= numeral numeral)` as a bound on a numeral

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/bv/bv_bounds_recognize.go:63-105` (`BVBoundsSimplifier.recognize`, equality branch)
- C++: `src/tactic/bv/bv_bounds_tactic.cpp:211-222` (`bv_bounds_simplifier::is_bound`; same code in `dom_bv_bounds_simplifier::is_bound`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
} else if (m.is_eq(e, lhs, rhs)) {
    if (is_number(lhs, n, sz)) {
        if (m_bv.is_numeral(rhs))
            return false;
        b = interval(n, n, sz, true); v = rhs; return true;
    }
    if (is_number(rhs, n, sz)) { b = interval(n, n, sz, true); v = lhs; return true; }
}
```

**Go behavior.** When the lhs is a numeral of 64 bits or fewer, Go does not check the rhs. It returns `rhs, bvBoundsSingleton(w, v), true` even when the rhs is itself a numeral. The ule/sle branch does have the `ln && rn` check. So `(= #x01 #x02)` records the bound "#x02 ∈ {1}". That bound then simplifies other atoms that mention `#x02`, and it also feeds `MaySimplify`/`containsBound`.

**Impact.** `propagate-bv-bounds` and `propagate-bv-bounds-new` simplify differently from z3 on goals that contain unsimplified numeral equalities, as happens when they run before `simplify`. The result is still equivalent, but the output goal differs.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed:
```smt2
(declare-const p Bool)
(declare-const q Bool)
(assert (or p (ite (= #x01 #x02) (= #x03 #x02) q)))
(apply propagate-bv-bounds)
```
z3: `(or p (ite (= #x01 #x02) (= #x03 #x02) q))`. g3: `(or p (and (not (= #x01 #x02)) q))`.

**Fix.** In `recognize`'s equality branch, mirror C++: if `lhs` is a numeral of 64 bits or fewer, test `rhs` with `bvBoundsNumeral` (any width). If it is also a numeral, return `found=false`. Only when `lhs` is not a usable number should the code try `rhs` as the number with `variable = lhs`:
```go
v, w, yes, e := bvBoundsNumeral(m, lhs)
if e != nil { return ... }
if yes && w <= 64 {
    _, _, rnum, e := bvBoundsNumeral(m, rhs)
    if e != nil || rnum { return variable, bound, false, e }
    return rhs, bvBoundsSingleton(w, v), true, nil
}
v, w, yes, e = bvBoundsNumeral(m, rhs)
if e != nil || !yes || w > 64 { return variable, bound, false, e }
return lhs, bvBoundsSingleton(w, v), true, nil
```
The ctx and dom tactics both use this one recognizer, so the one change fixes both.

**Regression test.** Extend `pkg/tactic/bv/bv_bounds_recognize_test.go` with `TestBVBoundsRecognizeRejectsNumeralEquality`. Use the helpers in `bv_bounds_test_support_test.go`. `recognize(MkEq(#x01, #x02))` must return `found == false`, and `recognize(MkEq(#x01, x))` must still return `x`, {1}. Add the input above as `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/bv_bounds_numeral_equality.smt2`, with expected `"(goals\n(goal\n  (or p (ite (= #x01 #x02) (= #x03 #x02) q))\n  :precision precise :depth 1)\n)\n"`, and check it with `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference`.

<a id="tactic-bv-01-f5"></a>
#### tactic_bv_01-F5: bvarray2uf does not declare `produce_models`, so `using-params` rejects it

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/bv/bvarray2uf_tactic.go:192` (`CollectParamDescrs`)
- C++: `src/tactic/bv/bvarray2uf_tactic.cpp:121-123`

**C++ behavior.** `void collect_param_descrs(param_descrs & r) override { insert_produce_models(r); }`

**Go behavior.** `func (t *BVArray2UFTactic) CollectParamDescrs(*uparams.ParamDescrs) error { return t.open() }` declares nothing.

**Impact.** `(using-params bvarray2uf :produce_models true)` fails parameter validation in g3. `(help-tactic)` also leaves out the `produce_models (bool) (default: false) model generation.` line under bvarray2uf.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed:
```smt2
(declare-const a (Array (_ BitVec 4) (_ BitVec 4)))
(assert (= (select a #x1) #x2))
(apply (using-params bvarray2uf :produce_models true))
```
z3: `(goals\n(goal\n  (= (f_t!!0 #x1) #x2)\n  :precision precise :depth 1)\n)\n`. g3: `(error "line 3 column 48: invalid using-params combinator, unknown parameter produce_models")`.

**Fix.** Change it to:
```go
func (t *BVArray2UFTactic) CollectParamDescrs(d *uparams.ParamDescrs) error {
    if err := t.open(); err != nil { return err }
    return uparams.InsertProduceModels(d)
}
```

**Regression test.** Add the input as `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/bvarray2uf_produce_models_param.smt2`, with the z3 output above in `scriptResults`, and check it with `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference`. A unit test `TestBVArray2UFDeclaresProduceModels` in `bvarray2uf_tactic_test.go` can call `CollectParamDescrs` on a fresh `ParamDescrs` and check that `produce_models` is present with kind bool.

<a id="tactic-bv-01-f6"></a>
#### tactic_bv_01-F6: elim-small-bv has no tactic report, no progress report, wrong param descriptions, and drops its traces

- Severity: low
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/bv/elim_small_bv_tactic.go:134-146` (`CollectParamDescrs`), `:345-427` (`Apply`)
- C++: `src/tactic/bv/elim_small_bv_tactic.cpp:228-251,280-284`

**C++ behavior.** `Apply` opens `tactic_report report("elim-small-bv", *g)` before the proof and core checks. It ends with `report_tactic_progress(":elim-small-bv-num-eliminated", m_num_eliminated)` and `TRACE("elim-small-bv", g->display(tout))`. The param descriptors come from `insert_max_memory`, `insert_max_steps`, and `"(default: 4) maximum bit-vector size of quantified bit-vectors to be eliminated."`. The rw_cfg also has TRACE sites `elim_small_bv`, `elim_small_bv_app` and `elim_small_bv_pre`.

**Go behavior.** There is no `NewTacticReport` and no `ReportTacticProgress`; `cfg.eliminated` is counted but never reported. The descriptions are hand-written without the "(default: …)" prefix or the trailing period. None of the trace sites are emitted.

**Impact.** With `-v:10`, z3 prints `(:elim-small-bv-num-eliminated 2)` and `(elim-small-bv :num-exprs ...)`; g3 prints neither. `(help-tactic)` text differs for elim-small-bv's three params.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed with `-v:10` on `(declare-fun p ((_ BitVec 2) (_ BitVec 2)) Bool) (assert (forall ((x (_ BitVec 2)) (y (_ BitVec 2))) (p x y))) (apply elim-small-bv)`. The `(help-tactic)` diff was also confirmed.

**Fix.** In `Apply`, call `tactic.NewTacticReport("elim-small-bv", g)` before `FailIfProofGeneration` and defer its Close. After the loop, call `tactic.ReportTacticProgress(":elim-small-bv-num-eliminated", cfg.eliminated)` before `IncDepth`. Emit the `elim-small-bv` goal trace after `AddGoal`. In `CollectParamDescrs`, use `uparams.InsertMaxMemory`, `uparams.InsertMaxSteps`, and the C++ text for `max_bits`, in that order. C++ inserts them in that order and the help printer sorts. Add the `elim_small_bv` TRACE sites in `ReduceQuantifier` as other tactics in this package do (`emit` helpers).

**Regression test.** Add a `TestElimSmallBVParamDescriptions` unit test in `elim_small_bv_tactic_test.go` that checks the three description strings. The verbose report is checked by any existing verbose-output harness. If none exists, compare the `(help-tactic)` output section for elim-small-bv in a cmd-level test.

<a id="tactic-bv-01-f7"></a>
#### tactic_bv_01-F7: bv-bounds stores negated bounds as tight, so the undo trail and `scope_level` differ

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/tactic/bv/bv_bounds_interval.go:126-157` (`sourceComplement`), used at `pkg/tactic/bv/bv_bounds_state.go:50,57`
- C++: `src/tactic/bv/bv_bounds_tactic.cpp:136-151` (`interval::negate`), `:340-354` (`assert_expr`)

**C++ behavior.** `negate` of a tight interval builds its result with the 3-argument constructor `interval(h + 1, uMaxInt(sz), sz)` (and the two other branches), so the result has `tight = false`. `assert_expr` then intersects with the stored bound and checks `if (old == intr) return true;`. `operator==` compares `tight` too. So asserting `(bvule x 4)` and then `(not (bvule 5 x))` pushes an undo record that only changes tightness, and `scope_level()` grows by one.

**Go behavior.** `sourceComplement` builds every result with `bvBoundsRangeSet` or an explicit `tight: true`. The negated bound is tight, `next.equal(old)` returns true, and no trail entry is pushed.

**Impact.** `ctx_simplify_tactic` caches results by `scope_level()` (`is_cached` requires `m_lvl == scope_level()`), so cache hits and step counts can differ. The intervals are the same, so no different simplification was found.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted at the output level. The difference shows only in internal scope levels and cache reuse.

**Fix.** Give `sourceComplement` C++ tightness for tight inputs: the result of negating a tight bound should have `tight = false` in all three branches. Keep the full/empty handling. The `!b.tight` branch is unreachable (negate is only called on `is_bound` results), and the C++ code there passes `true` as `sz`. Leave that branch as is or mark it unreachable.

**Regression test.** Extend `pkg/tactic/bv/bv_bounds_state_test.go` with `TestBVBoundsNegatedBoundIsLoose`. Assert `bvule x #x04`, then assert `(not (bvule #x05 x))`, and expect `ScopeLevel()` to go from 1 to 2. Then `Pop(1)` and expect the stored bound to be tight again.

### Area: Core tactics (`pkg/tactic/core`)

*tactic_core_01.* This shard holds the core goal tactics: blast-term-ite, cofactor-term-ite, collect-occs, collect-statistics, ctx-simplify, der, distribute-forall, dom-simplify, elim-term-ite, elim-uncnstr, injectivity, nnf/snf, occf, and the shared leaf-translation switch. Most of it is a close, statement-by-statement port. Differential runs of elim-uncnstr (models, BV/arith/array ops), collect-statistics, distribute-forall (no proofs) and dom-simplify matched z3 byte for byte. Two lifetime divergences were confirmed with the binaries: - cofactor-term-ite keeps updated parameters across `cleanup()`; the C++ drops them. - injectivity clears its rewriter cache on every application; the C++ keeps it. The remaining findings are low: a cancellation check is missing, a counter is copied on translate, a proof-mode deviation (the C++ crashes there) is not documented, and one trace has a different layout. Counts: critical 0, high 0, medium 2, low 4. The listed file `tactic/core/dom_simplify_context.go` no longer exists. Commit b63ff9c67 replaced it with `dom_simplify_subst.go`, and that file was audited instead. tactic_core_01-F4 (translated tseitin-cnf keeps numAux) duplicates tactic_core_02-F11; it adds that Go copies the counter in two places.

*tactic_core_02.* The shard holds the Go ports of eight core tactics: pb-preprocess, propagate-values, reduce-args, simplify/elim-and, solve-eqs, split-clause, symmetry-reduce and tseitin-cnf (22 files). Most of the code follows the C++ closely, statement by statement. propagate-values, reduce-args, simplify and solve-eqs (candidates, sort_vars, normalize, substitute) showed no algorithmic divergence. The real defects are in pb-preprocess. `normalize` panics on a negated PB constraint whose arguments are not literals. `pure_args` and the declassifier do not match the C++, so goals and models differ. Several verbose, help and trace outputs also differ. Counts: high 1, medium 4, low 6. Five findings are confirmed against `build/z3` (F1-F5) and the help-text finding F6 is also confirmed.

<a id="tactic-core-01-f1"></a>
#### tactic_core_01-F1: cofactor-term-ite keeps `cofactor_equalities`/`max_memory` after cleanup; C++ reverts them to the constructor params

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/cofactor_term_ite_tactic.go:126-139,158` (`UpdateParams`, `Cleanup`), `pkg/tactic/core/cofactor_term_ite_rewriter.go:107-109` (`newCofactorTermITERewriter` uses `owner.params`)
- C++: `src/tactic/core/cofactor_term_ite_tactic.cpp:52,79` (`updt_params`, `cleanup`), `src/tactic/core/cofactor_elim_term_ite.cpp:308-311,654-659,684-702` (`imp::updt_params`, `imp::imp`, `cofactor_elim_term_ite::updt_params/cleanup`)

**C++ behavior.** `cofactor_term_ite_tactic::updt_params` updates the tactic's `m_params` and forwards the call to `m_elim_ite.updt_params(p)`. That forwards to `m_imp->updt_params(p)`, which changes only `m_max_memory` and `m_cofactor_equalities`. The `m_params` inside `cofactor_elim_term_ite` and inside its `imp` both keep the constructor value. `cleanup()` (run after every application by the `clean()` wrapper) rebuilds the imp from that stale `m_params`:
```cpp
void cofactor_elim_term_ite::updt_params(params_ref const & p) { m_imp->updt_params(p); }
void cofactor_elim_term_ite::cleanup() {
    imp * d = alloc(imp, m, m_params);   // constructor params, not the updated ones
    std::swap(d, m_imp); dealloc(d); }
```
So `using-params` values (and qfnia's `max_memory 20`) apply only to the first application. Later applications of the same tactic object use the defaults (`cofactor_equalities=true`, no memory limit). `mk_simplified_app` is also always built from the constructor params (`m_mk_app(m, owner.m_params)`).

**Go behavior.** `UpdateParams` assigns into `t.params` and re-reads the policy. `Cleanup` is a no-op. The per-formula rewriter builds `NewSimplifiedApp(..., &owner.params)` from the updated params. Updated parameters therefore persist across applications and also reach the simplifier.

**Impact.** Any reuse of the tactic object after its first application differs: `then`/`par-then` over several subgoals, `repeat`, or a second application by the same solver. In those cases g3 still honours `:cofactor_equalities false` (and the 20 MB limit in QF_NIA's preamble); z3 has reverted to `true` / unlimited. The output goals differ.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed with the binaries:
```smt2
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(declare-const a Bool)
(declare-const b Bool)
(assert (or a b))
(assert (> (ite (= x 1) (+ x y) y) 0))
(apply (then split-clause (using-params cofactor-term-ite :cofactor_equalities false)))
```
z3:
```
(goals
(goal
  a
  (ite (= x 1) (not (<= (+ x y) 0)) (not (<= y 0)))
  :precision precise :depth 2)
(goal
  b
  (ite (= x 1) (not (<= y (- 1))) (not (<= y 0)))
  :precision precise :depth 2)
)
```
g3 prints the same, except that the second goal's first literal is `(not (<= (+ x y) 0))`: g3 still applies `cofactor_equalities false`, while z3 has reverted after the first subgoal.

**Fix.** Mirror the C++ split between the tactic's params and the elimination engine's params:
1. Add `engineParams uparams.ParamsRef` to `CofactorTermITETactic`. It is the `cofactor_elim_term_ite::m_params` copy, assigned once in `NewCofactorTermITETactic` from `p` and never changed by `UpdateParams`. Release it in `Close`.
2. `UpdateParams` keeps assigning `t.params` (the tactic's `m_params`, used by `Translate`) and re-reading `maxMemory`/`cofactorEqualities` from `p`, as now.
3. `Cleanup` re-reads `maxMemory`/`cofactorEqualities` from `t.engineParams` with defaults `UINT_MAX` / `true`. This is the C++ `alloc(imp, m, m_params)`.
4. `newCofactorTermITERewriter` passes `&owner.engineParams` to `rewriter.NewSimplifiedApp` (C++ `m_mk_app(m, owner.m_params)`).
5. `Translate` passes `&t.params`: C++ `alloc(cofactor_term_ite_tactic, m, m_params)` uses the tactic-level params, which are updated.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/tactic/core/cofactor_term_ite_tactic_test.go`, add `TestCofactorTermITECleanupRestoresConstructorParams`. Build the objects as `TestCofactorTermITEEliminatesArithmeticChoice` does (`solveEqFixture`, `m.RegisterDeclarationPlugins()`, `NewCofactorTermITETactic(m, c, g, nil, services)`). Call `UpdateParams` with `cofactor_equalities=false` (`c.NewValue`, `SetBoolName`) and assert `runner.cofactorEqualities == false`. Then call `runner.Cleanup()` and assert `runner.cofactorEqualities == true`.
SMT vector: `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/cofactor_params_after_cleanup.smt2`, containing the script above. Its `scriptResults` entry is the z3 output above. Check it with `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`.

<a id="tactic-core-01-f2"></a>
#### tactic_core_01-F2: injectivity resets its rewriter cache on every application; C++ keeps `m_eq`'s cache, so stale results survive

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/injectivity_apply.go:39-41` (`InjectivityTactic.Apply`)
- C++: `src/tactic/core/injectivity_tactic.cpp:271-283,300-302` (`injectivity_tactic::operator()`, `mk_injectivity_tactic`), `src/ast/rewriter/rewriter_def.h:653-679` (`main_loop` never clears the cache)

**C++ behavior.** `mk_injectivity_tactic` is not wrapped in `clean()`. `m_eq` is a `rewriter_tpl` that lives as long as the tactic, and `operator()` calls `(*m_eq)(curr, rw, pr)` with no `reset()`. Shared sub-terms cached during an earlier application (when `inj_map` did not yet know `f`) are reused unchanged later. Only `cleanup()` rebuilds `m_eq`.

**Go behavior.**
```go
if err = t.discover(goal); err != nil { return err }
if err = t.traversal.Reset(); err != nil { return err }
```
Every application starts with an empty cache, so equalities are always rewritten with the current relation set.

**Impact.** When the same injectivity tactic runs on several goals (`then`, `par-then`, `repeat`, solver reuse) and an earlier goal lacked the inverse axiom, z3 leaves shared `(= (f a) (f b))` sub-terms unrewritten in later goals, and g3 rewrites them. The goals are equisatisfiable in both, but the outputs differ.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed:
```smt2
(declare-fun f (Int) Int)
(declare-fun g (Int) Int)
(declare-const a Int)
(declare-const b Int)
(declare-const p Bool)
(declare-const q Bool)
(declare-const r Bool)
(assert (or p (forall ((x Int)) (= (g (f x)) x))))
(assert (or (= (f a) (f b)) q))
(assert (or (= (f a) (f b)) r))
(apply (then split-clause injectivity))
```
z3 second goal: `(forall ((x Int)) (= (g (f x)) x))`, `(or (= (f a) (f b)) q)`, `(or (= (f a) (f b)) r)`. g3 second goal: `... (or (= a b) q)`, `(or (= a b) r)`. The first goals are identical.

**Fix.** In `InjectivityTactic.Apply`, delete the `t.traversal.Reset()` call. The cache is then cleared only by `Cleanup`, which already resets the traversal and relations, as the C++ `cleanup()` does. Confirm that `rewriter.Traversal`'s cache holds references to its keys and values, so cross-goal entries stay live (as the C++ rewriter cache does). If the owner considers the stale cache a z3 bug, record it in `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/z3_bug_exclusions.txt` and `FORK_BUGFIXES.md` instead of changing the code.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/tactic/core/injectivity_tactic_test.go`, add `TestInjectivityCacheSurvivesApplications`. Use `newInjectivityFixture` and build two goals that share the term `(or (= (f a) (f b)) q)` with a second, cache-forcing occurrence. Only goal 2 carries the inverse axiom. Apply goal 1, then goal 2, and expect goal 2's shared equality to be unchanged. SMT vector: `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/injectivity_cache_across_goals.smt2`, containing the script above, with the z3 output as its `scriptResults` entry. Check it with `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference`.

<a id="tactic-core-01-f3"></a>
#### tactic_core_01-F3: cofactor-term-ite checkpoint omits the `m.canceled()` test

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/cofactor_term_ite_rewriter.go:131-143` (`cofactorTermITERewriter.checkpoint`)
- C++: `src/tactic/core/cofactor_elim_term_ite.cpp:34-40` (`imp::checkpoint`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
cooperate("cofactor ite");
if (memory::get_allocation_size() > m_max_memory) throw tactic_exception(TACTIC_MAX_MEMORY_MSG);
if (m.canceled()) throw tactic_exception(m.limit().get_cancel_msg());
```
**Go behavior.** Calls `Cooperate`, which does not test cancellation (`pkg/util/cooperate/cooperate.go:129`), and checks the memory limit, but has no canceled test. Compare `ContextSimplifyTactic.checkpoint`, which does test it.

**Impact.** On a timeout or resource-limit cancel, the bottom-up walk and `get_best` keep running in g3 where z3 raises a tactic exception straight away. In QF_NIA, where cofactor sits under `skip_if_failed`, cancellation is noticed later.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: it depends on timing.

**Fix.** Append to `checkpoint`:
```go
canceled, err := r.owner.manager.Canceled()
if err != nil { return err }
if canceled { return tactic.NewTacticException(r.owner.manager.ResourceLimit().CancelMessage()) }
```
**Regression test.** In `cofactor_term_ite_tactic_test.go`, add `TestCofactorTermITECheckpointHonoursCancel`: cancel the manager's resource limit (as the ctx-simplify cancellation tests do), apply to a goal with a term ITE, and expect a tactic exception carrying the cancel message.

<a id="tactic-core-01-f5"></a>
#### tactic_core_01-F5: distribute-forall under proofs builds a rewrite step; C++ leaves `result_pr` null and segfaults (undocumented fork deviation)

- Severity: low
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/distribute_forall_tactic.go:98-110` (`distributeForallConfiguration.distribute`)
- C++: `src/tactic/core/distribute_forall_tactic.cpp:26-77` (`rw_cfg::reduce_quantifier`), `src/ast/rewriter/rewriter_def.h:526-533`

**C++ behavior.** `reduce_quantifier` sets `result` but never `result_pr`. In proof mode `m_pr = mk_transitivity(m_pr, nullptr)` leaves no proof of the rewrite, and the reference build crashes.

**Go behavior.** It emits `MkProofRewrite(q, conjunction)`, giving a well-formed proof. This deviation is not documented in the source, the manifest, or `z3_bug_exclusions.txt`.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed:
```smt2
(set-option :produce-proofs true)
(declare-fun p (Int) Bool)
(declare-fun q (Int) Bool)
(assert (forall ((x Int) (y Int)) (and (p x) (q y))))
(apply distribute-forall)
```
z3: `Segmentation fault (core dumped)`. g3: prints the split goal `(forall ((x Int)) (p x))`, `(forall ((y Int)) (q y))`.

**Fix.** Keep the Go behavior, which is correct. Follow the project's fork-fix workflow: add a red C++ test, apply the matching fix in `src/tactic/core/distribute_forall_tactic.cpp` (`result_pr = m.mk_rewrite(old_q, result)` in both branches), log it in `FORK_BUGFIXES.md`, and add the vector name to `z3_bug_exclusions.txt`. Also add a comment at `distribute` citing that entry.

**Regression test.** Add vector `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/z3_bug_distribute_forall_proof.smt2` (the script above, plus `(check-sat)`), listed in `z3_bug_exclusions.txt`, with the g3 output as its `scriptResults` entry.

<a id="tactic-core-01-f6"></a>
#### tactic_core_01-F6: dom-simplify dominator-tree TRACE uses a different layout from `expr_dominators::display`

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/dom_simplify_trace.go:47-74` (`traceDominatorTree`)
- C++: `src/tactic/core/dom_simplify_tactic.cpp:155-170` (`expr_dominators::display`)

**C++ behavior.** It prints the indent and then the node, recurses into the children, and only then writes `"\n"`. A child is therefore printed on its parent's line (`A B\n\n` for root A with leaf child B).

**Go behavior.** It writes `s+"\n"` before recursing (`A\n B\n`).

**Impact.** Only the `-tr:simplify` trace text differs.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: the reference build has no traces.

**Fix.** In `walk`, write the indent and `s` without a newline, recurse into the children (skipping `child == h`), and then write `"\n"`.

**Regression test.** In a `g3trace`-tagged test in `dom_simplify_trace_test.go`, compile a two-level tree, enable the `simplify` tag, and compare the captured text with the C++ layout.

<a id="tactic-core-02-f1"></a>
#### tactic_core_02-F1: pb-preprocess `normalize` dereferences nil on a negated pbge with non-literal arguments

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/pb_preprocess_normalize.go:79-87` (`PBPreprocessTactic.normalize`)
- C++: `src/tactic/core/pb_preprocess_tactic.cpp:288-307` (`pb_preprocess_tactic::normalize`)

**C++ behavior.** It reads the coefficients and the bound straight from the pb app, for any arguments:
```cpp
if (m.is_not(e, r) && pb.is_ge(r)) {
    rational k = pb.get_k(r);
    for (unsigned j = 0; j < to_app(r)->get_num_args(); ++j) {
        sum += pb.get_coeff(r, j);
        coeffs.push_back(pb.get_coeff(r, j));
        args.push_back(negate(to_app(r)->get_arg(j)));
    }
    tmp = pb.mk_ge(args.size(), coeffs.c_ptr(), args.c_ptr(), sum - k + rational::one());
```

**Go behavior.** It goes through `parse`, which returns `(nil, nil)` as soon as one argument is not a pure literal (`pureLiteral` fails). It then reads `parsed.terms`:
```go
parsed, x := t.parse(child)
...
terms := make([]pbPreprocessTerm, len(parsed.terms))   // parsed == nil -> SIGSEGV
```

**Impact.** Any goal containing `(not ((_ pbge ...) ...))` where some argument is not a literal (for example `(and a b)` or `(not (not c))`) crashes the g3 process with a nil-pointer panic. z3 rewrites the constraint normally.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed.
```smt2
(declare-const a Bool)
(declare-const b Bool)
(declare-const c Bool)
(assert (not ((_ pbge 2 1 1) (and a b) c)))
(apply pb-preprocess)
```
g3: `panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` at `pb_preprocess_normalize.go:87`, exit code 2.
z3:
```
(goals
(goal
  ((_ pbge 1 1 1) (not (and a b)) (not c))
  :precision precise :depth 1)
)
```

**Fix.** In `normalize`, stop using `parse`. Read the pb app directly:
```go
n, x := t.manager.GetNumArgs(child)
k, x := t.rational(child, nil)
sum := new(big.Rat)
terms := make([]pbPreprocessTerm, n)
for j := uint32(0); j < n; j++ {
    c, x := t.rational(child, &j)
    a, x := t.manager.GetArg(child, j)
    sum.Add(sum, c)
    terms[j].coefficient = c
    terms[j].expression, x = t.negateLiteral(a)   // negate(): strips one not, else mk_not
}
bound := new(big.Rat).Sub(sum, k); bound.Add(bound, big.NewRat(1, 1))
```
Keep the C++ order: coefficient first, then `negate(arg)`. Also make the loop check `g.Inconsistent()` and re-read `g.Size()` on every iteration, as `!g->inconsistent() && i < g->size()` does.

**Regression test.** Extend `pkg/tactic/core/pb_preprocess_normalize_test.go` with `TestPBPreprocessNormalizesNegatedGEWithCompoundArgs`. Use `newPBPreprocessFixture`. Build `and1 := f.m.MkAnd(f.vars[0], f.vars[1])`, `ge := f.ge([]ast.ASTHandle{and1, f.vars[2]}, []string{"1","1"}, "2")`, `g := f.goal(f.m.MkNot(ge))` and call `f.apply(g)`. Expect no panic and one formula that is a pbge with bound 1 and arguments `(not (and a b))`, `(not c)`. For SMT-LIB, add `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/pb_preprocess_negated_compound.smt2` with the input above. Its `scriptResults` entry is the z3 output shown above. Check it with `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`.

<a id="tactic-core-02-f2"></a>
#### tactic_core_02-F2: pb-preprocess `pureLiteral` rejects `(not true)`/`(not false)`, which C++ `pure_args` accepts

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/pb_preprocess_terms.go:153-164` (`pureLiteral`, used by `pureArgs`, `processVars`, `parse`)
- C++: `src/tactic/core/pb_preprocess_tactic.cpp:463-472` (`pure_args`), `424-448` (`classify_vars`)

**C++ behavior.** It strips one `not`, then accepts an uninterpreted constant, `true` or `false`:
```cpp
expr* e = a->get_arg(i);
m.is_not(e, e);
if (!is_uninterp_const(e) && !m.is_true(e) && !m.is_false(e)) return false;
```
So `(or a (not false) b)` counts as pure and goes into `m_ge`. `classify_vars` then even inserts `false` as a "variable", with the `neg` polarity.

**Go behavior.**
```go
if t.manager.IsTrue(h) || t.manager.IsFalse(h) { return true, nil }
if yes, e := t.isConstant(h); ... { return yes, e }
child, yes, e := t.negated(h) ...
return t.isConstant(child)          // (not false) -> false
```
The clause goes into `m_other`, and the declassifier then removes its variables.

**Impact.** Unsimplified goals that contain negated Boolean constants give different results from `(apply pb-preprocess)` and from any strategy that runs pb-preprocess before simplification. The C++ behavior is odd: it can register `true`/`false` in the model converter. But it is what 4.7.1 does, and it is not listed in `z3_bug_exclusions.txt`.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed.
```smt2
(declare-const a Bool)
(declare-const b Bool)
(assert (or a (not false) b))
(assert (or (not a) b))
(apply pb-preprocess)
```
g3 keeps both formulas. z3 prints an empty goal: `(goals (goal :precision precise :depth 1))`.

**Fix.** Make `pureLiteral` mirror `pure_args`. First strip one `not` with `t.negated`. Then return `isConstant(e) || IsTrue(e) || IsFalse(e)`. `classifyVars` already inserts the child of a negation without checking it, which matches C++. Before matching the C++ quirk, decide whether to log it as a deliberate deviation in `z3_bug_exclusions.txt`, because it makes `true`/`false` model "variables".

**Regression test.** `pkg/tactic/core/pb_preprocess_declassify_test.go`: add `TestPBPreprocessNegatedBooleanConstantIsPure`. Use `newPBPreprocessFixture` and build the two clauses above with `f.m.MkOrArgs`/`MkNot(MkFalse())`. After `f.apply`, expect `g.Size() == 0`. Also add the vector `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/pb_preprocess_not_false.smt2`, with the z3 output above as its `scriptResults` entry.

<a id="tactic-core-02-f3"></a>
#### tactic_core_02-F3: pb-preprocess declassifier skips quantifier patterns

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/pb_preprocess_simplify.go:180-242` (`declassify`)
- C++: `src/tactic/core/pb_preprocess_tactic.cpp:186-190`, with `src/ast/for_each_expr.h:121-123` (`for_each_expr` = `for_each_expr_core<..., true, false>`, so `IgnorePatterns=false`)

**C++ behavior.** `for_each_expr(dcl, visited, g->form(m_other[i]))` visits every quantifier child, `1 + num_patterns + num_no_patterns`. A constant that appears only in a pattern is therefore removed from `m_vars`.

**Go behavior.** For a quantifier it visits only the body (`count = 1`, `GetQuantifierBody`).

**Impact.** A Boolean constant that occurs in the PB fragment and only in a pattern of another assertion is eliminated by g3 and kept by z3. That changes the goal and the model converter.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed.
```smt2
(declare-const a Bool)
(declare-fun f (Int Bool) Int)
(assert a)
(assert (forall ((x Int)) (! (> x 0) :pattern ((f x a)))))
(apply pb-preprocess)
```
g3 output: only the `forall` is left. z3 output: `a` and the `forall`.

**Fix.** In `declassify`, give a quantifier the C++ child order `body, patterns..., no_patterns...`. The helper `(*SolveEquationsTactic).children` in `solve_eqs_order.go:34-83` already builds this list. Then set `count = len(children)` and index into it.

**Regression test.** Add `TestPBPreprocessPatternOccurrenceDeclassifies` in `pkg/tactic/core/pb_preprocess_declassify_test.go`. If the fixture cannot build a quantifier with a pattern, use the SMT-LIB vector instead: `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/pb_preprocess_pattern_declassify.smt2`, holding the input above. Expected:
```
(goals
(goal
  a
  (forall ((x Int)) (! (> x 0) :pattern ((f x a))))
  :precision precise :depth 1)
)
```

<a id="tactic-core-02-f4"></a>
#### tactic_core_02-F4: pb-preprocess verbose output: an extra tactic report and the missing IF_VERBOSE(3) lines

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/pb_preprocess_tactic.go:97-101` (`Apply`), `pb_preprocess_replace.go` (`replace`), `pb_preprocess_simplify.go:435,571-633` (subsumption, `resolve`)
- C++: `src/tactic/core/pb_preprocess_tactic.cpp:145-164` (no `tactic_report`), `257`, `570-582`, `653`

**C++ behavior.** `pb_preprocess_tactic::operator()` creates no `tactic_report`. At verbosity 3 it prints `replace <f> -> <tmp>` in `replace`, `replace <g->form(k)>` in subsumption, and the `resolve: ... to ...` block in `resolve`.

**Go behavior.** `Apply` calls `tactic.NewTacticReport("pb-preprocess", g)`, so at -v:10 it prints `(pb-preprocess :num-exprs ...)`. None of the IF_VERBOSE(3) lines are emitted. The `TRACE("pb", ...)` sites (lines 203, 522, 584, 651) are not ported either.

**Impact.** Verbose output differs from z3 on every pb-preprocess run at -v:3 and above.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed with `-v:10` on:
```smt2
(declare-const a Bool)
(declare-const b Bool)
(assert (or a b))
(apply pb-preprocess)
```
g3 prints `(pb-preprocess :num-exprs 0 :num-asts 163 ...)`. z3 prints `replace (or a b) -> true`.

**Fix.** Remove the `NewTacticReport` call (and its deferred close) from `PBPreprocessTactic.Apply`. Add IF_VERBOSE(3) output with `diagnostic.ProcessVerboseEnabled(3)` / `BorrowProcessVerboseStream`, as `propagate_values_tactic.go:674-694` does:
- in `replace`, when `next != h`: `"replace " + mk_pp(h) + " -> " + mk_pp(next) + "\n"`;
- in subsumption, before `g.Update(k, truth, ...)`: `"replace " + mk_pp(fk) + "\n"`;
- in `resolve`: the two blocks at C++ 570-575 and 580-582.

The `TRACE("pb")` sites can be added with the `emit` pattern the other tactics in this package use.

**Regression test.** Extend `pkg/cmd/g3/main_test.go` with a verbose-output case, if the runner supports stderr capture with `-v:3`. Otherwise add `TestPBPreprocessVerboseReplaceLine` in `pkg/tactic/core/pb_preprocess_eliminate_test.go`: redirect the process verbose stream, set verbosity 3, apply to `(or a b)`, and expect exactly `replace (or a b) -> true\n` and no `(pb-preprocess` line.

<a id="tactic-core-02-f5"></a>
#### tactic_core_02-F5: solve-eqs and tseitin-cnf print the `report_tactic_progress` line before the tactic report

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/solve_eqs_tactic.go:285-291,402` (`SolveEquationsTactic.Apply`); `pkg/tactic/core/tseitin_cnf_encode.go:1110-1116,1191` (`TseitinCNFTactic.Apply`)
- C++: `src/tactic/core/solve_eqs_tactic.cpp:812-819`, `src/tactic/core/tseitin_cnf_tactic.cpp:888-895`

**C++ behavior.** The `tactic_report` lives inside `imp::operator()`, so its line is printed when imp returns. The outer `operator()` then calls `report_tactic_progress(":num-elim-vars", ...)` / `(":cnf-aux-vars", ...)`, so the report line comes first.

**Go behavior.** One function owns both. `report.Close()` is deferred, and `return tactic.ReportTacticProgress(...)` runs before the deferred close, so the progress line comes first.

**Impact.** The -v:10 output order differs from z3 on every run of these two tactics.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed with `-v:10`, `(apply solve-eqs)` on any goal with an equation:
g3: `(:num-elim-vars 4)` then `(solve_eqs :num-exprs 6 ...)`; z3: `(solve_eqs ...)` then `(:num-elim-vars 4)`. tseitin-cnf shows the same swap with `(:cnf-aux-vars 1)`.

**Fix.** Split each `Apply` into an inner function that owns the report (the imp body). Call `tactic.ReportTacticProgress` after that inner function returns, and only when it returned without an error (C++ does not report when an exception escapes). In tseitin-cnf, read `t.numAux` after the invocation defer has added `inv.numAux`. reduce-args and symmetry-reduce are already right, because their C++ reports progress inside imp.

**Regression test.** Add a verbose-order test next to `pkg/tactic/core/solve_eqs_trace_test.go` (`TestSolveEqsProgressAfterReport`) and to `tseitin_cnf_tactic_test.go` (`TestTseitinProgressAfterReport`). Capture the process verbose stream at level 10 and assert that the `(solve_eqs` / `(tseitin-cnf` line comes before `(:num-elim-vars` / `(:cnf-aux-vars`.

<a id="tactic-core-02-f7"></a>
#### tactic_core_02-F7: tseitin-cnf does not replace each processed formula with `true`, so AST lifetimes and ids differ

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/tseitin_cnf_encode.go:1135-1149` (`TseitinCNFTactic.Apply` loop)
- C++: `src/tactic/core/tseitin_cnf_tactic.cpp:825-828`

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
for (unsigned idx = 0; idx < size; idx++) {
    process(g->form(idx), g->dep(idx));
    g->update(idx, m.mk_true(), nullptr, nullptr); // to save memory
}
```
Unshared root formulas (for example a root `(= a (or b c))`, whose clauses are new terms) are freed before the next formula is processed, so their ids are reused by the fresh `k!n` constants and the clauses built later.

**Go behavior.** It only calls `inv.process(form, dep)`. Every root stays alive until `goal.Reset()`.

**Impact.** Downstream AST ids differ, and so does anything ordered by id (trace logs, id-sorted rewrites in later tactics). This is the same class as FUZZ_B-F9 and FUZZ_H-F6. My attempts (`(then tseitin-cnf simplify)`, `(then tseitin-cnf symmetry-reduce)`, `(then tseitin-cnf simplify propagate-values)`) did not show a stdout difference.

**Reproduction.** Not reproduced on stdout. A trace-level comparison should show it (the ids of `k!` constants).

**Fix.** After `inv.process(form, dep)`, call `goal.Update(i, true, ast.ASTHandle{}, ast.ASTDependency{})` with `true` from `MkTrue`, as C++ does.

**Regression test.** Add `TestTseitinReleasesProcessedRoots` in `pkg/tactic/core/tseitin_cnf_tactic_test.go`. Assert a root `(= a (or b c))` followed by a second formula that needs a fresh variable. Check that the AST id of the root is reused by a node created later (compare with `m.GetASTID` before and after). The other option is to compare `GetRefCount(root)` against the C++ expectation: zero references once processing has moved on.

<a id="tactic-core-02-f8"></a>
#### tactic_core_02-F8: tseitin-cnf `checkpoint` checks memory before cancellation and uses the resource-limit message

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/tseitin_cnf_encode.go:365-383` (`tseitinInvocation.checkpoint`)
- C++: `src/tactic/core/tseitin_cnf_tactic.cpp:758-764`

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
cooperate("tseitin cnf");
if (m.canceled()) throw tactic_exception(TACTIC_CANCELED_MSG);       // always "canceled"
if (memory::get_allocation_size() > m_max_memory) throw tactic_exception(TACTIC_MAX_MEMORY_MSG);
```

**Go behavior.** It checks memory first, then `NewTacticException(m.ResourceLimit().CancelMessage())`. That gives "max. resource limit exceeded" for an rlimit trip, where C++ gives "canceled".

**Impact.** When the rlimit is exhausted inside tseitin-cnf, the `reason-unknown` / tactic error message differs. When memory and cancellation both trip, a different exception wins.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: hitting the rlimit inside tseitin rather than in an earlier rewriter is hard to arrange.

**Fix.** Reorder to cooperate, then canceled, then memory. Use the fixed canceled message (the Go constant equivalent to `TACTIC_CANCELED_MSG`/`Z3_CANCELED_MSG`) instead of `CancelMessage()`.

**Regression test.** Add `TestTseitinCheckpointCancelMessage` in `pkg/tactic/core/tseitin_cnf_tactic_test.go`. Set a manager resource limit that is already exceeded (as other cancellation tests in the package do). Apply tseitin-cnf-core to a goal with a non-trivial `or`, and expect a tactic exception whose text is exactly `canceled`.

<a id="tactic-core-02-f9"></a>
#### tactic_core_02-F9: symmetry-reduce removes the selected index from T; C++ `T.erase(t)` removes the first occurrence

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/symmetry_reduce_tactic.go:228-233` (`runSymmetry`)
- C++: `src/tactic/core/symmetry_reduce_tactic.cpp:146-147`, `src/util/vector.h:382-387`

**C++ behavior.** `T.erase(t)` runs `std::find` and removes the first element equal to `t`.

**Go behavior.** `terms = append(terms[:index], terms[index+1:]...)` removes the element at the index `promisingSymmetryTerm` returned.

**Impact.** This only matters when T holds the same term twice (two range-restriction clauses over the same term) and the non-transitive comparison in `select_most_promising_term` picks the later copy. The order of T left afterwards then differs, and later tie-breaks (first index wins) can pick different terms, giving different symmetry-breaking predicates.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted (contrived).

**Fix.** After choosing `term := terms[index]`, remove the first `i` with `terms[i] == term`.

**Regression test.** Add `TestSymmetryReduceEraseFirstOccurrence` in `pkg/tactic/core/symmetry_reduce_test.go`, or a unit test on a small helper that does the erase. Input `[t, u, t]` with selected index 2 must leave `[u, t]`.

<a id="tactic-core-02-f10"></a>
#### tactic_core_02-F10: missing TRACE sites and a non-empty split-clause proof-converter display

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/tactic/core/split_clause_tactic.go:215-221,460-480`; `pkg/tactic/core/tseitin_cnf_encode.go:1186-1191`
- C++: `src/tactic/core/split_clause_tactic.cpp:113` (`TRACE("before_split_clause")`), `48-82` (`split_pc` has no `display`, so `converter::display` is empty, `src/tactic/converter.h:42`); `src/tactic/core/tseitin_cnf_tactic.cpp:844` (`TRACE("tseitin_cnf", g->display(tout))`), `146` (`TRACE("tseitin_cnf_bug")`)

**Details.** split-clause never emits `before_split_clause`, and tseitin-cnf never emits `tseitin_cnf` at the end of `operator()`. `splitClauseProofConverter.Display` prints `(split-clause <clause>)`, while the C++ `split_pc` prints nothing.

**Fix.** Add the two TRACE sites with the package's `EmitConditional` pattern (tag, function `operator()`, file and line). Make `splitClauseProofConverter.Display` return nil without writing anything.

**Regression test.** Add `TestSplitClauseProofConverterDisplayIsEmpty` in `pkg/tactic/core/split_clause_tactic_test.go`: build the converter with proofs enabled and expect `Display` to write 0 bytes. For the trace sites, extend the existing trace tests (as in `solve_eqs_trace_test.go`) to look for the tags `before_split_clause` and `tseitin_cnf`, matched by tag and function, not by line number.

<a id="tactic-core-02-f11"></a>
#### tactic_core_02-F11: tseitin-cnf `Translate` copies the aux-var statistic

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high

### Area: Tactics: aig, fpa, nlsat_smt, portfolio, smtlogics

*tactic_small_01.* This shard holds the AIG manager and `aig` tactic (19 files), the `fpa2bv` tactic (3), the `nl-purify` tactic (13), the `bounded_int2bv` solver (2) and `mk_default_tactic` (1). The AIG simplification rules (`mk_node`), max-sharing, the AIG-to-expression converters and the tactic lifecycle match the C++ closely, and so do `bounded_int2bv` and `default_tactic`. The divergences are in how temporaries are ordered and released inside the AIG gate builders (two confirmed, one changes `(apply aig)` output), a dropped parameter in `fpa2bv` (confirmed, a different result), and several places in `nl-purify` where caching, ordering or the model converter differ from the C++ (one confirmed with a C++ trace). Counts: high 0, medium 7, low 2.

*tactic_small_02.* This shard holds the logic-specific strategy factories (`pkg/tactic/smtlogics/*`), the strategic-solver dispatcher and the finite-domain solver wrappers (`pkg/tactic/portfolio/*`). Most strategy compositions match the C++ combinator trees exactly, including parameter scopes, clean wrappers, probes and route order. I found three real divergences: QF_BV picks its incremental backend without checking `rewriter.hi_div0` (confirmed by an output difference), the NRA strategy reuses the full QF_NRA portfolio in place of the C++ three-attempt NLSAT `or_else` (confirmed by a verbose-output difference; the manifest records this deviation), and the QF_NRA bit-blasting routes keep `nla2bv_max_bv_size` alive under a Go-only `using_params` wrapper. A small cluster of Go-only finite-domain tactic code (no 4.7.1 counterpart) is dead. Counts: high 0, medium 3, low 1.

<a id="tactic-small-01-f1"></a>
#### tactic_small_01-F1: `composeGate` releases gate temporaries in reverse order, so `Ite`/`Iff` free nodes in a different order and later AIG ids change

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/aig/aig_gates.go:25` (`Manager.composeGate`, used by `Ite`, `Iff`, `Or`, `Xor`, `Implies`)
- C++: `src/tactic/aig/aig.cpp:1414-1466` (`aig_manager::imp::mk_ite`, `mk_iff`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
aig_lit n1 = mk_and(c, t);  ...  aig_lit n2 = mk_and(c, e);
inc_ref(n1); inc_ref(n2); n1.invert(); n2.invert();
aig_lit r  = mk_and(n1, n2);
inc_ref(r);
dec_ref(n1);      // n1 first
dec_ref(n2);      // then n2
dec_ref_result(r);
```
When `r` does not keep `n1`/`n2` (for example `ite(q,x,x)`, where the resolution rule gives `x`), `n1` is deleted first and `n2` second. `id_gen::recycle` pushes onto a LIFO free list, so this order decides which ids the next nodes get.

**Go behavior.**
```go
result, err := build(t)
for i := len(t.refs) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {      // reverse order
    err = errors.Join(err, t.refs[i].Close())
}
```
In the default `Ite` the temporaries are `[nc, first(=¬n1), second(=¬n2)]`, so Go closes `n2` before `n1`. The same happens in the default `Iff` (`[nl, nr, first, second]`) and in both alternate encodings. The recycled ids come back in the opposite order. Every later `n1.id > n2.id` choice in `mk_node`, every `aig_lit_lt` sort in `mk_and`/`mk_or`, and so the shape of the AIG, can change from that point on.

**Impact.** `(apply aig)` and any strategy using `aig` (qfbv's `aig` step, for example) can print a different goal, and AIG traces diverge.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed. `ite2.smt2`:
```
(declare-const x Bool)
(declare-const y Bool)
(declare-const z Bool)
(declare-const p Bool)
(declare-const q Bool)
(assert (or p (ite q x x) (and y z)))
(apply aig)
```
g3: `(goals (goal (or (not (or (not y) (not z))) p x) :precision precise :depth 1))`
z3: `(goals (goal (or p x (not (or (not y) (not z)))) :precision precise :depth 1))`
With `-tr:aig_lit_count` (z3 from `build_trace`, g3 built `-tags g3trace`), the first difference is `deleting: @1` / `deleting: @0` (g3) against `deleting: @0` / `deleting: @1` (z3), right after the ITE is built.

**Fix.** In `composeGate`, release the temporaries in creation order: `for i := 0; i < len(t.refs); i++ { ... t.refs[i].Close() }`. Then check each gate against the C++ `dec_ref` order:
- default `Ite`: `nc` (no deletion), `n1`, `n2`.
- alternate `Ite`: `n1`, `nc`, `n2`.
- default `Iff`: `nl`, `nr`, `n1`, `n2`.
- alternate `Iff`: `n1`, `nl`, `nr`, `n2`.

All of these then follow `dec_ref(n1); dec_ref(n2)`. `Or`/`Xor`/`Implies` hold only negations of caller-owned refs, so the order has no effect there.

**Regression test.** Add `TestAIGIteReleasesTemporariesInSourceOrder` to `pkg/tactic/aig/aig_gates_test.go`, using `aigFixture`/`aigMust` like `TestAIGDefaultGatesTruthTablesAndFailureCleanup`. Build variables `q,x`, call `g.Ite(q,x,x)` with the default encoding, close the result, then `InternAnd` two fresh variables and check that the new node's `ID()` equals the id of the C++ `n2` (the id freed last, so reused first). Add the vector above as `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/aig_ite_same_branches.smt2` and put the z3 output above as its expected value in the `scriptResults` table of `pkg/cmd/g3/main_test.go`. `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3` checks it against the C++.

<a id="tactic-small-01-f2"></a>
#### tactic_small_01-F2: `AndArgs`/`OrArgs` sort two operands (the C++ does not) and do not apply the sort to the result stack

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed (trace divergence)
- Go: `pkg/tactic/aig/aig_gates.go:160-238` (`sortedArgs`, `AndArgs`, `OrArgs`); `pkg/tactic/aig/aig_expr.go:206` (`exprConverter.complete`)
- C++: `src/tactic/aig/aig.cpp:1353-1405` (`mk_and(unsigned, aig_lit*)`, `mk_or(unsigned, aig_lit*)`), `:487-499` (`restore_result_stack`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
switch (num) {
case 0: return m_true;
case 1: return args[0];
case 2: return mk_and(args[0], args[1]);      // no sort
default:
    std::sort(args, args+num, aig_lit_lt());   // sorts m_result_stack in place
```
`args` points into `m_result_stack`, so for three or more operands the following `restore_result_stack(spos)` releases the operands in sorted order.

**Go behavior.** `sortedArgs` sorts a copy for every arity, two included, and `AndArgs` then calls `m.And(ordered[0], ordered[1])`. `complete` closes `c.results[fr.start:]` in the original order.

**Impact.** `mk_node` is not symmetric. For example, `(a∧b)∧(c∧d)` with `a==c` becomes `(a∧b)∧d`, while the swapped call gives `(c∧d)∧b`. A binary `and`/`or`/`=>` whose first operand has the larger AIG id therefore produces a different intermediate AIG and a different `mk_and_bug` trace. `max_sharing` often reassociates the result back, so the final goal frequently matches. The deletion order of operands that are dropped (n ≥ 3) also differs, which changes id recycling in the same way as F1.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed by trace. `nary3.smt2`:
```
(declare-const x Bool)
(declare-const y Bool)
(declare-const z Bool)
(declare-const p Bool)
(declare-const q Bool)
(assert (or p (and (or q (and x y)) (and (and x z) (and x y)))))
(apply aig)
```
The `-tr:mk_and_bug` traces differ at the fourth `mk_and`: z3 calls `@2 AND @0` and returns `@3: #4 @2`, while g3 calls `@0 AND @2` and returns `@3: #5 @0`. The printed goals happen to be the same.

**Fix.** In `AndArgs`/`OrArgs`, do the sort only when `len(args) >= 3`; for two operands call `m.And(args[0], args[1])` / `m.Or(args[0], args[1])` in the given order. For n ≥ 3, sort the caller's slice in place (`sort.Slice(args, …)` on `c.results[fr.start:]`), so that `complete` releases the operands in sorted order as `restore_result_stack` does. The public `AndArgs`/`OrArgs` used by tests can keep a copying wrapper.

**Regression test.** Add `TestAIGBinaryAndKeepsOperandOrder` to `pkg/tactic/aig/aig_gates_test.go`. Make variables x, y, z, build `N1 = And(x,y)` and then `N2 = And(x,z)`, call `AndArgs([N2, N1])`, and check that the result has children `(y, N2)` (C++ `mk_and(N2,N1)`), not `(z, N1)`.

<a id="tactic-small-01-f3"></a>
#### tactic_small_01-F3: the `fpa2bv` tactic never applies the `max_steps` (and `max_memory`) parameters to its rewriter

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/tactic/fpa/fpa2bv_tactic.go:63-107` (`Pass.build`, `Pass.UpdateParams`)
- C++: `src/tactic/fpa/fpa2bv_tactic.cpp:36-46`; `src/ast/fpa/fpa2bv_rewriter.cpp:46-55` (`fpa2bv_rewriter_cfg::updt_params`, `max_steps_exceeded`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
void fpa2bv_rewriter_cfg::updt_params(params_ref const & p) {
    m_max_memory        = megabytes_to_bytes(p.get_uint("max_memory", UINT_MAX));
    m_max_steps         = p.get_uint("max_steps", UINT_MAX);
    updt_local_params(p);
}
bool fpa2bv_rewriter_cfg::max_steps_exceeded(unsigned num_steps) const {
    cooperate("fpa2bv");
    return num_steps > m_max_steps;
}
```
This runs from the rewriter constructor (with the tactic's `p`) and from `updt_params`.

**Go behavior.** `build` and `UpdateParams` only call `SetHighUnspecified`. `FPA2BVRewriter.SetLimits` exists, but nothing outside its own file calls it, so `maxSteps` stays `MaxUint32`.

**Impact.** A `max_steps` passed down to `fpa2bv` (through `using-params` on a combinator, or through the `p` of `qffp`/`qffpbv`/`qffplra`, which call `mk_fpa2bv_tactic(m, p)`) is ignored. z3 fails with "max. steps exceeded"; g3 goes on and returns a goal.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed. `fpsteps4.smt2`:
```
(declare-const a (_ FloatingPoint 3 3))
(declare-const b (_ FloatingPoint 3 3))
(assert (fp.lt (fp.add RNE a b) b))
(apply (using-params (then fpa2bv (or-else skip simplify)) :max_steps 1))
```
z3: `(error "tactic failed: max. steps exceeded")`. g3: prints the bit-blasted `(goals (goal (let ((a!1 ...` output.

**Fix.**
1. In `Pass.build` and `Pass.UpdateParams`, read `max_steps` (`GetUIntName(&p.params, "max_steps", math.MaxUint32)`) and `max_memory` (`umemory.MegabytesToBytes(GetUIntName(…, "max_memory", math.MaxUint32))`) from `p.params`, then call `p.rewriter.SetLimits(steps, memory)`.
2. Remove the memory test from `fpa2BVConfiguration.MaxStepsExceeded` (`pkg/ast/rewriter/fpa2bv_rewriter.go`). The C++ stores `m_max_memory` but never checks it there, so once the limit is set, Go would otherwise fail where z3 does not.
3. Also add the `cooperate("fpa2bv")` call that the C++ makes in `max_steps_exceeded`, if g3's cooperation owner is reachable from the rewriter.

**Regression test.** Add `TestFPA2BVTacticHonorsMaxSteps` to `pkg/tactic/fpa/fpa2bv_tactic_test.go`, built the way `TestFPA2BVTacticRewritesGoalAndPublishesSingleResult` builds its pass. Pass params `max_steps=1`, apply to `fp.lt (fp.add RNE a b) b`, and expect a rewriter/tactic error with text "max. steps exceeded". Add the SMT-LIB vector above as `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/fpa2bv_max_steps.smt2`, with expected output `(error "tactic failed: max. steps exceeded")\n` in `scriptResults`, and check it with `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference`.

<a id="tactic-small-01-f4"></a>
#### tactic_small_01-F4: the `nl-purify` Boolean-mode rewriter shares the result for a root atom, where the C++ makes a second predicate

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed (C++ trace; Go side from reading the code)
- Go: `pkg/tactic/nlsat_smt/nl_purify_predicates.go:108,179` (`nlPredicateRewriter.rewrite` memo); the same unconditional memo is in `pkg/tactic/nlsat_smt/nl_purify_interfaces.go` (`nlInterfaceRewriter.rewrite`)
- C++: `src/ast/rewriter/rewriter.h:74-79` (`rewriter_core::must_cache`), used by `rw` in `src/tactic/nlsat_smt/nl_purify_tactic.cpp:253-266,615-630`

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
bool must_cache(expr * t) const {
    return t->get_ref_count() > 1 && t != m_root &&
        ((is_app(t) && to_app(t)->get_num_args() > 0) || is_quantifier(t));
}
```
The root of each `rewrite_goal` call is never looked up in or stored to the cache, and terms with a reference count of 1 are not cached. So an atom that is asserted on its own and also occurs inside another formula is abstracted twice: `mk_interface_bool` runs twice, creating two fresh predicates and two sets of NL clauses.

**Go behavior.** `r.memo[term]` is checked for every term, the root included, and filled for every term. The second occurrence reuses the first predicate.

**Impact.** This is reachable whenever a root atom is not removed by `remove_pure_arith`: unsat cores are enabled, or the atom is not "pure" (an `Int` comparison, for example). The number of fresh `k!n` predicates, the NL clauses, the SMT assumptions and the fresh-name numbering all differ, so the search, statistics and traces diverge. Both sides stay sound.

**Reproduction.** C++ side confirmed. Input:
```
(set-option :produce-unsat-cores true)
(declare-const x Real)
(declare-const y Real)
(declare-const p Bool)
(declare-fun f (Real) Real)
(assert (< (* x x) y))
(assert (or (< (* x x) y) p))
(assert (> (f x) 2.0))
(check-sat-using nl-purify)
```
`build_trace/z3 -tr:nlsat_smt` prints `mk_interface_bool … (< (* x x) y) : k!1` and then `(< (* x x) y) : k!2`. g3 creates one predicate. `:rlimit-count` is 9 for g3 and 39 for z3. g3 has no trace for this site (see F9), so its side is from the code.

**Fix.** Give both nl-purify rewriters the `must_cache` policy:
- set a `root` field in `rewriteGoal` before each formula;
- in `rewrite`, read and write `memo` only when `term != root`, `GetRefCount(term) > 1` and the term is an app with at least one argument (constants never go through `reduce_app` caching);
- clear the memo at the start of each `rewriteGoal`, as `rewrite_goal` calls `r.reset()`.

`interfaceVar` keeps its own `m_interface_cache` and needs no change. The same policy is needed wherever a hand-written traversal in this package replaces `rewriter_tpl`.

**Regression test.** Add `TestNLPurifyRootAtomGetsFreshPredicateLikeRewriterTpl` to `pkg/tactic/nlsat_smt/nl_purify_predicates_test.go`, using the fixtures in `shared_ast_fixtures_test.go` as in `TestNLPurifyInterfaceAndPredicateGoalRewrites`. Use the goal `(< (* x x) y)`, `(or (< (* x x) y) p)` with cores enabled, and expect `len(newPredicates) == 2` and four NL clauses for that atom (two per polarity-dual predicate).

#### tactic_small_01-F5: `nl-purify` hands on nlsat's model converter when nlsat is undecided; the C++ leaves `mc` null

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/tactic/nlsat_smt/nl_purify_solve.go:118-122` (`nlCooperation.iterate`, "not a unit" branch)
- C++: `src/tactic/nlsat_smt/nl_purify_tactic.cpp:325-344`

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
model_converter_ref nl_mc; ...
(*m_nl_tac)(tmp_nl, result, nl_mc, nl_pc, nl_core);
...
if (!is_decided_sat(result)) {
    TRACE("nlsat_smt", tout << "not a unit\n";);
    break;          // mc (the tactic's out-parameter) stays nullptr
}
```

**Go behavior.**
```go
if nlResult.ModelConverter != nil {
    if err = out.SetModelConverter(nlResult.ModelConverter); err != nil {
```

**Impact.** nlsat returns an undecided goal together with a model converter when `mk_model` fails, which happens when an integer variable gets a non-integer value (`nlsat_tactic.cpp:96-127` sets `mc` even when `ok == false`). Go then attaches that converter to the `nl-purify` result. `check_sat` (`tactic.cpp:220-224`) builds a model from `mc` even for an undecided result, so after `unknown`, `(get-model)` and the API's apply result expose a partial nlsat model where z3 has none.
