#### duality_01-F4: the counterexample `(subst ...)` values come from a reconstructed proof witness instead of `tree->Eval(&edge, skolem)`

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/duality/counterexample_display.go:96-196` (`writeDerivation`), with the proof witnesses from `counterexample_proof.go`
- C++: `src/muz/duality/duality_dl_interface.cpp:423-433` (`print_proof`), and `:569-584` (`extract_proof`) for the same values in `get_proof`

**C++ behavior.**
```
expr skolem = ctx.constant(symbol(ctx,name),sort(ctx,the_sort));
out << "    (= " << skolem << " " << tree->Eval(&edge,skolem) << ")\n";
```
Variables that qe-lite projected out of the edge are evaluated in the counterexample model, so they print the model default, e.g. `0`.

**Go behavior.** The file header says: "Quantified substitutions use reconstructed original-rule witnesses so values eliminated by preprocessing are not printed as arbitrary model defaults." The values come from `extractCounterexampleProof` / `MatchProofHyperResolve`, which runs a fresh solver through `factory`. The manifest records this as a deviation. It is documented, but it changes output.

**Impact.** Every Duality `sat` certificate whose rule variable was eliminated by qe-lite prints a different value. It also costs an extra solver call per step.

**Reproduction.** `$S/fuzzgroups/F/diff_arith-duality_190.smt2`:
```
(set-option :fixedpoint.engine duality)
(declare-rel q0 (Int))
(declare-rel err ())
(declare-var x Int)
(declare-var x1 Int)
(rule (=> (and (= x 2)) (q0 x)))
(rule (=> (and (q0 x) (< x (+ x 3)) (= x1 (+ x x))) (q0 x1)))
(rule (=> (and (q0 x) (< x (+ x 2)) (= x1 (+ x 3))) (q0 x1)))
(rule (=> (and (q0 x) (< x 9) (= x1 x)) (q0 x1)))
(rule (=> (and (q0 x) (> x 4)) err))
(query err :print-certificate true)
```
In step `s!3` (rule!3), z3 prints `(= x 0)` and g3 prints `(= x 2)`. `diff_arith-duality_214` behaves the same way. The other differences in those files are the known FUZZ_F-F6.

**Fix.** Choose one of two:
1. For fidelity: in `writeDerivation`, for each bound variable `j` of the original clause, build `MkConst(name_j, sort_j)` and print `g.Eval(edge, constant)` (the `RPFP::Eval` port). Drop the proof-witness call. Do the same in `extractCounterexampleProof` for `substs[0]`.
2. To keep the correction: add the vectors to `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/z3_bug_exclusions.txt` with an explanation, as other deliberate z3-bug fixes are.

**Regression test.** Add `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/duality_subst_eliminated_var.smt2` (the script above). The expected output is z3's full output, which `$S/work/duality_01/diff_arith-duality_190.z` holds: `(step s!3 (q0 5)` / `rule!3` / `(= x 0)` / `(= x1 5)` and so on. Choosing the fix this way requires the FUZZ_F-F6 fix too. Check it with `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference`.

<a id="duality-01-f5"></a>
#### duality_01-F5: `ReallySimplifyAndOr` orders common factors by arena slot; C++ orders them by AST id

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/duality/boolean_factors.go:104-111` (`less` in `ReallySimplifyAndOr`)
- C++: `src/duality/duality_rpfp.cpp:497-504` (`PullCommonFactors`: `std::less<ast> comp; std::sort(...); std::set_intersection(...)`); `src/duality/duality_wrapper.h:1444-1449`

**C++ behavior.** `std::less<Duality::ast>` is specialized to `return s.raw()->get_id() < t.raw()->get_id();`. The common factors are sorted, intersected and emitted (`common.push_back(...)`, `SimplifyAndOr(common,!is_and)`) in AST-id order.

**Go behavior.**
```go
// The C++ set comparator orders opaque AST pointers. Arena slot identity
// provides the corresponding stable order within this manager in Go.
less := func(a, b ast.ASTHandle) bool { if a.Slot() != b.Slot() { return a.Slot() < b.Slot() } ... }
```
The comment is wrong: the comparator is the id specialization, not pointer order. Slot and id are allocated independently: `ast_core_register.go:186` sets `id = generator.Mk()`, and the slot comes from the arena free list. They diverge after any recycling.

**Impact.** The argument order of the pulled-out factors in the simplified `and`/`or` differs from C++. This affects learned annotations (RemoveRedundancy runs on every learned fact), their printing, their hash-consing and later traversal order.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted. It needs an `or` of `and`s with two or more shared conjuncts whose slot order and id order differ.

**Fix.** Use `m.GetASTID(h)` in the comparator: compute the ids once per row and sort by id, with generation/slot as a tie-break that cannot be reached. Apply the same fix to the other two places that make the same claim: `pkg/duality/model_constraints.go:201-206` (`std::map<ast,...>` order) and `pkg/duality/wrapper_ast.go:107-125` (`AST.Less`). Both are outside this shard.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/duality/boolean_factors_test.go`, add `TestDualityCommonFactorsIDOrder`:
- Create and release some ASTs so the arena reuses a low slot for a later (higher-id) term.
- Build `(or (and f1 f2 r1) (and f1 f2 r2))` with `slot(f2) < slot(f1)` but `id(f1) < id(f2)`.
- Assert the result's first two `and` arguments are `[f1, f2]`.

<a id="duality-01-f6"></a>
#### duality_01-F6: `buildFast` adds a `CheckSat(nil)` before `Solve` and so discards the proof the C++ reuses

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/duality/derivation_fast.go:51-56` (`DerivationSearch.buildFast`)
- C++: `src/duality/duality_solver.cpp:1944-1952` (`DerivationTree::Build`), `src/duality/duality_wrapper.cpp:553-554` (`interpolating_solver::interpolate_tree`)

**C++ behavior.**
```
if((underapprox || false_approx) && top->Outgoing && CheckWithUnderapprox()){ ... }
res = tree->Solve(top, 1);
```
`interpolate_tree` calls `check()` only `if(!m_solver->get_proof())`. When `CheckWithUnderapprox` (a check under leaf assumptions) has just returned unsat, its proof is still in the solver, and `Solve` interpolates that proof.

**Go behavior.**
```go
// Discard a proof derived with temporary leaf assumptions before
// interpolating the unassumed constraint tree.
if _, err := d.tree.solver.CheckSat(nil); err != nil {
```
This is an extra native check that C++ never makes. `InterpolateTree` (`interpolation_solver.go:91-98`) then sees a fresh proof.

**Impact.** In constrained derivations (`ExpandNodeFromCoverFail`/`ExpandUnderapproxNodes`, `duality_solver.cpp:1693,1749`), the interpolants and learned facts can differ. The extra check also changes SMT kernel state (statistics, learned clauses, restarts) for everything after it.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted. It needs a constrained derivation whose under-approximate check returns unsat.

**Fix.** Delete the `CheckSat(nil)` call, so `solveWithTheory` runs right after the `Check`, as in C++. If this was a deliberate soundness fix, record it as a z3-bug exclusion with a vector instead.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/duality/derivation_fast_theory_test.go`, set up a constrained `Derive` where `Check(top, leaves)` returns unsat and count native `CheckSat` calls with a wrapping solver (as the neighboring tests wrap services). Assert exactly one check between the under-approximate check and interpolation, namely the one inside `Check`.

<a id="duality-01-f7"></a>
#### duality_01-F7: AST construction order differs from the GCC build in `ElimIte` and `FourierMotzkinCheap`

- Severity: low
- Confidence: medium
- Go: `pkg/duality/elim_ite.go:104-127` (`ElimIte`, guarded equality), `pkg/duality/fourier_motzkin.go:107-131` (`FourierMotzkinCheap`, `comb`)
- C++: `src/duality/duality_rpfp.cpp:1905` (`ElimIteRec`), `:2357-2361` (`FourierMotzkinCheap`)

**C++ behavior.** `res = (c && (lhs == t)) || ((!c) && (lhs == e));` and `Term comb = neg_coeff * tpos + pos_coeff * tneg;` use overloaded operators, which are function calls. The reference GCC build evaluates their arguments right to left. So `(= lhs e)`, `(not c)` and `(and (not c) ...)` are created before `(= lhs t)` and `(and c ...)`, and `pos_coeff*tneg` is created before `neg_coeff*tpos`.

**Go behavior.** Go creates them left to right: `MkEq(lhs,t)`, `MkEq(lhs,e)`, `MkNot`, `MkAnd(c,..)`, `MkAnd(not c,..)`, `MkOr`. In FM it creates `left = nc*a` before `right = pc*b`. Go also creates `-coeff` after `canon(...)` (C++ creates `-la_coeffs[false][var]` before `comb`, but after `tpos`/`tneg`, so that part matches).

**Impact.** AST ids differ after `Unhoist` (ElimIte) and under-approximation projection, which can change hash-ordered traversals later. No answer change was seen.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted. A trace comparison over a clause set that takes `UnhoistLoop`, or `use_underapprox=true` with FM, would show it.

**Fix.** Build in GCC order:
- ElimIte: `no := MkEq(lhs,args[2])`, `neg := MkNot(args[0])`, `noAnd := MkAnd(neg,no)`, `yes := MkEq(lhs,args[1])`, `yesAnd := MkAnd(args[0],yes)`, `MkOr(yesAnd,noAnd)`.
- FM: compute `right` (`pc*b`) before `left` (`nc*a`).

**Regression test.** Extend `pkg/duality/elim_ite_test.go`: on a fresh manager, assert that the id of `(= lhs e)` is lower than the id of `(= lhs t)` after `ElimIte` of `(= y (ite c t e))`.

#### duality_01-F8: the variable projector's stdout diagnostics are missing

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/duality/gauss_elim.go:111-116` (`makeCandidate`), `pkg/duality/fourier_motzkin.go:104` (`FourierMotzkinCheap`)
- C++: `src/duality/duality_rpfp.cpp:2071` (`MakeElimCand`), `:2351-2353` (`FourierMotzkinCheap`)

**C++ behavior.** It prints `std::cout << "would have mapped a non-var\n";` when an equality has no variable side. It prints `std::cout << "would have eliminated keep var\n"; continue;` when a kept variable has both bounds.

**Go behavior.** Go returns or continues silently (`if !lv { if rv {...}; return nil }` and `if pos < 0 || neg < 0 || kept[variable] { continue }`).

**Impact.** With `fixedpoint.duality.use_underapprox=true` (`ComputeUnderapprox` → `ProjectFormula`), z3's stdout has these lines and g3's does not. None of the fuzz vectors triggered them.

**Reproduction.** Not reproduced; none of the 10 duality fuzz scripts hits these lines under `use_underapprox=true`.

**Fix.** Write the same strings, newline included, to the solver's diagnostic stdout writer at those two points. For FM, test `kept` after the `pos >= 0 && neg >= 0` check, as C++ does.

**Regression test.** Add unit tests in `pkg/duality` that call `GaussElimCheap` with `[(= (+ a b) 3)]` and `FourierMotzkinCheap` with keep `[x]` and `[(<= 0 x), (<= x 5)]`, with stdout redirected, and assert the exact lines.

<a id="duality-02-f2"></a>
#### duality_02-F2: `FixCurrentState` treats the `@underN` flags as don't-cares; the C++ passes an empty set

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/duality/implicant.go:324-348` (`(*RPFP).FixCurrentState`)
- C++: `src/duality/duality_rpfp.cpp:2519-2527` (`RPFP::FixCurrentState`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
void RPFP::FixCurrentState(Edge *edge){
    hash_set<ast> dont_cares;
    resolve_ite_memo.clear();
    timer_start("UnderapproxFormula");
    Term dual = edge->dual.null() ? ctx.bool_val(true) : edge->dual;
    Term eu = UnderapproxFormula(dual,dont_cares);
```
The edge dual built by `GetEdgeFormula(..., underapprox=true)` contains `(or (not @underK) U_K)` for each child (lines 924-928). `ImplicantRed` therefore records `(not @underK)`, or `@underK` and U_K's literals, as constraint literals.

**Go behavior.**
```go
// Underapproximation flags are temporary query controls. Fixing their
// model polarity can contradict the next expansion-selection assumptions.
for _, ref := range g.underapproxFlagRefs { ... controls = append(controls, control) }
decision, err := g.UnderapproxFormula(formula, controls)
```
Every flag is a don't-care, so no `@underK` literal is ever written into the edge constraint. The existing test `TestRPFPFixCurrentStateDoesNotFreezeUnderapproximationControls` (`implicant_controls_test.go:8`) locks this deviation in.

**Impact.** This runs on every SAT step of `DerivationTree::ExpandSomeNodes` (`duality_solver.cpp:2369-2371`, Go `derivation_advance.go:79-85`), and `UseUnderapprox` is on by default. The constraint asserted into the solver differs from the C++ one, so later `Check(root, leaves)` calls with flag assumptions can give different results and cores. Search order, the derivation chosen, and possibly restarts then differ. The answer can differ in principle where the C++ falls into its "bad" paths.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: no small script isolates it. The deviation is visible by reading the code, and the existing Go test asserts the non-C++ behavior.

**Fix.** Pass `nil` as `dontCares` in `FixCurrentState`, as the source does, and drop the `controls` loop. Rewrite `TestRPFPFixCurrentStateDoesNotFreezeUnderapproximationControls` to assert the C++ behavior: after `FixCurrentState` the last `edge.constraints` entry contains the `(not @underN)` literal when the model makes `@underN` false. If the deviation is kept on purpose, record it in `z3_bug_exclusions.txt` / TODO.md with a reproduction.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/duality/implicant_controls_test.go`, rename the test to `TestRPFPFixCurrentStateKeepsUnderapproximationFlagLiterals`. Use the same fixture it already uses (`dualityNativeSolverServicesFixture`, `derivationEvaluatorFixture`). Build an edge with one child, call `GetEdgeFormula(edge, 0, true, true)`, and run `CheckUpdateModel` with `(not @under<child>)`. Then call `FixCurrentState` and expect the new constraint, conjunct by conjunct, to contain `(not @under<child>)`.

<a id="duality-02-f3"></a>
#### duality_02-F3: decl-kind dispatch without a basic-family check: arithmetic `>` (OP_GT = 5) is taken for `and` in `UnderapproxFullFormula` and `CloneQuantAndSimp`

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: medium
- Go: `pkg/duality/implicant_full.go:76-100` (`UnderapproxFullFormula`, `visit`); `pkg/duality/quant_simplify.go:25-35` (`quantSimplification.op`, used by `collect`, `clone` and `push`)
- C++: `src/duality/duality_rpfp.cpp:1819-1851` (`ImplicantFullRed`), `:568-591` and `:546-566` (`CloneQuantAndSimp`, `PushQuantifier`), `:407-419` (`CollectJuncts`). Also `duality_wrapper.cpp:213-280` (`context::get_decl_kind`), which maps only the basic family to `And/Or/Not/Implies/Iff/Equal`.

**C++ behavior.** `f.decl().get_decl_kind()` returns `And`, `Or`, `Not` and the others only for `m_basic_fid`. An arithmetic `>` is `Gt`.
```cpp
if (k == Implies || k == Iff || k == And || k == Or || k == Not) {
    for (int i = 0; i < nargs; i++) ImplicantFullRed(memo, f.arg(i), ...);
```

**Go behavior.** Both functions compare the raw `m.GetDeclKind(h)` without checking the family:
```go
op, err := m.GetDeclKind(h)          // implicant_full.go:77
switch op {
case ast.ASTOpImplies, ast.ASTOpIff, ast.ASTOpAnd, ast.ASTOpOr, ast.ASTOpNot:
...
func (s *quantSimplification) op(h ast.ASTHandle) (int32, error) {   // quant_simplify.go:25
	... return m.GetDeclKind(h)
```
Arithmetic `OP_GT` is 5, equal to `ASTOpAnd`; `OP_ADD`/`OP_MUL` (6/9) equal `ASTOpOr`/`ASTOpNot`. For `(> a b)`:
- `UnderapproxFullFormula` recurses into the Int arguments, gets truth value 2 for both, and **drops the literal** from the cube.
- In `CloneQuantAndSimp`, under `forall` the atom matches `distribute` (`And`). Go then clones the Int arguments and calls `MkAndArgs` on Int terms, which is a sort error or a wrong formula. In `collect` it splits the atom into its Int operands.

The other dispatchers in this shard (`implicant.go`, `subterm_truth.go`, `remove_redundancy.go`, `ineq_to_eq.go`, `projection_*`) do check the family.

**Impact.** `UnderapproxFullFormula` is the cube of `InterpolateByCases`, which runs on every unsat expansion whose annotation has more than 10 and/or operators (`NodeTooComplicated`, `duality_solver.cpp:2270`). A weaker cube changes the case split and can raise `ReallyBad` or loop. `CloneQuantAndSimp` runs from `RemoveRedundancy` on quantified annotations. Reachability depends on a `>` surviving into an edge dual or an interpolant. Clause bodies go through `simplify()`, which normalizes `>`, so the main exposure is interpolants and background terms.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: forcing `InterpolateByCases`, or a quantified annotation that contains a raw `>`, needs a large search. The defect can be seen in the code.

**Fix.** In `implicant_full.go`, read the family before the switch and enter it only for the basic family:
```go
family, err := m.GetFamilyID(h)
...
if family == m.BasicFamilyID() { switch op { ... } }
```
Apply the same check to `equality` (`family == basic && op == ASTOpEq`). In `quant_simplify.go`, change `op()` to return -1 unless `m.GetFamilyID(h) == m.BasicFamilyID()`.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/duality/implicant_full_test.go`, add `TestDualityFullImplicantKeepsArithmeticGreaterThan`, using the fixture of `TestDualityFullImplicantAllBranchesAndSourceAtomOrder`. Declare Int `x`, run `CheckUpdateModel` with `(= x 3)`, and build `formula = (and p (> x 1))` with `m.MkFamilyApp(arith, 5, nil, {x, one})`. Expect `UnderapproxFullFormula(formula, true)` to be `(and p (> x 1))`, with 2 arguments. In `pkg/duality/quant_simplify_test.go`, add `TestDualityQuantifierSimplificationArithmeticGreaterThanIsAtom`. Build `forall y. (> y 0)` with a raw OP_GT body and expect `CloneQuantAndSimp` to return the quantifier unchanged, with no error.

<a id="duality-02-f4"></a>
#### duality_02-F4: `conjoin` is replaced by "true / the single literal / `and`"; the C++ always builds `(and ...)`, including `(and)` and `(and x)`

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/duality/implicant.go:86-94` (`UnderapproxFormula`); `pkg/duality/implicant_full.go:173-181`; `pkg/duality/model_constraints.go:140-148` (`EvalNodeAsConstraint`) and `:228-236` (`modelArrayEntriesAsConstraint`); `pkg/duality/project_formula.go:66-74` (`ProjectFormula`)
- C++: `src/duality/duality_rpfp.cpp:162-164` (`Z3User::conjoin`), used at `:1962`, `:1976`, `:2381`, `:2643`, `:2657`

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
Z3User::Term Z3User::conjoin(const std::vector<Term> &args){
    return ctx.make(And,args);   // mk_app(basic, OP_AND, n, args): (and) for n=0, (and x) for n=1
}
```
`ast_manager::mk_app` raises no type error for an associative `and` with fewer than 2 arguments (`ast.cpp:2161-2166`). The result is a real `(and)` or `(and x)` application.

**Go behavior.**
```go
switch len(state.literals) {
case 0: combined, err = m.MkTrue()
case 1: combined = state.literals[0]
default: combined, err = m.MkAndArgs(state.literals)
}
```
The same pattern appears at all five sites. Elsewhere (`rpfp_assert_edge.go:77`, `rpfp_reduced.go:108`, `implicant_solver.go:213`) the Go correctly uses the raw `MkAndArgs` for `conjoin` / `ctx.make(And, ...)`.

**Impact.** `FixCurrentState` asserts its result directly into the solver and records it in `edge->constraints`, so it becomes an extra term of the interpolation partition. C++ asserts `(and lit)` or `(and)` and g3 asserts `lit` or `true`. The proof steps (and-flattening `rewrite` steps), the interpolation input, AST ids and the trace all differ. Interpolants and search can then diverge. `EvalNodeAsConstraint` results become a node `Bound` (complemented), so the same applies there.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: no single-script output difference was isolated. The difference in AST shape is certain from the code.

**Fix.** At each listed site, replace the switch with `combined, err = m.MkAndArgs(literals)`. That is the raw `mk_app`, which already handles 0 and 1 arguments as the source does.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/duality/implicant_test.go`, add `TestRPFPUnderapproxFormulaSingletonConjoin`, using the fixture of `TestRPFPImplicantSourceOrderPolarityAndITE`. With the model `p = true`, expect `UnderapproxFormula(p, nil)` to be an `and` application with exactly one argument `p`. With every literal a don't-care, expect the result to be an `and` with 0 arguments. Add the same checks to `model_constraints_test.go` (a single scalar parameter gives `(and (= x_N v))`) and `implicant_full_test.go`.

<a id="duality-02-f5"></a>
#### duality_02-F5: the large-`distinct` UIF encoding is rebuilt with a fresh `@distinct` declaration on every interpolation call and is never the formula asserted in the solver; g3 hangs where z3 answers

- Severity: high
- Confidence: medium (the hang is confirmed; its attribution to this function is from reading the code)
- Go: `pkg/duality/interpolation_distinct.go:17-112` (`(*RPFP).interpolationAxiom`), called per call from `pkg/duality/interpolation_solver.go:55-64` (`InterpolateTree`). Raw axioms are asserted in `pkg/muz/duality/query_engine.go:196-210`.
- C++: `src/duality/duality.h:258-281` (`iZ3LogicSolver::assert_axiom`), `src/duality/duality_wrapper.cpp:612-615` (`AssertInterpolationAxiom`)

**C++ behavior.** The conversion happens once, when the axiom is asserted. The **converted** conjunction is both added to the interpolating solver and stored as the iZ3 theory:
```cpp
func_decl f = ctx->fresh_func_decl("@distinct",sv,ctx->int_sort());
for(int i = 0; i < nargs; i++){
    expr a = axiom.arg(i);
    expr new_cnstr = f(a) == ctx->int_val(i);   // GCC: int_val(i) is built before f(a)
    args[i] = new_cnstr;
}
expr cnstr = ctx->make(And,args);
islvr->AssertInterpolationAxiom(cnstr);       // add(t); theory.push_back(t);
```

**Go behavior.**
- The native and auxiliary solvers receive the **raw** `distinct` (`query_engine.go:196-210`).
- `InterpolateTree` calls `interpolationAxiom` on every Solve and SolveSingleNode. Each call creates a new fresh `@distinct!N` declaration and passes that conjunction to `interp.ProofInterpolants` as background. The proof's asserted leaf (raw `distinct`) is therefore not the theory term, and every call uses a different function symbol.
- The construction order also differs: Go builds the numeral `0` before the fresh declaration (`MakeIntText("0")` only to get the Int sort), and builds `f(a)` before `int_val(i)`.

**Impact.** A fixedpoint problem with a background `(assert (distinct ...))` of more than 10 arguments does not terminate in g3; z3 answers `unsat` immediately.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed (`work/duality_02/dist.smt2`):
```
(set-option :fixedpoint.engine duality)
(declare-fun c0 () Int)(declare-fun c1 () Int)(declare-fun c2 () Int)(declare-fun c3 () Int)(declare-fun c4 () Int)(declare-fun c5 () Int)
(declare-fun c6 () Int)(declare-fun c7 () Int)(declare-fun c8 () Int)(declare-fun c9 () Int)(declare-fun c10 () Int)
(declare-rel q (Int))
(declare-rel err ())
(declare-var x Int)
(rule (=> (= x c0) (q x)))
(rule (=> (and (q x) (= x c1)) err))
(assert (distinct c0 c1 c2 c3 c4 c5 c6 c7 c8 c9 c10))
(query err :print-certificate true)
```
z3 prints `unsat` and a certificate with `err = (= c0 c1)`. g3 reaches `timeout 20` (rc=124) with no output. With 3 to 10 arguments g3 instead fails with `(error "line 9 column 10: g3: invalid AST owner, kind or lifetime")`; see Needs verification. That failure suggests a second fault on the n-ary `distinct` path.

**Fix.**
1. Move the conversion to axiom-assertion time. In `pkg/muz/duality/query_engine.go`, before asserting `config.Theory`, map each axiom through a single `interpolationAxiom` call (make it a free function on `*Context`). Store the converted term in `config.Theory`, then assert **that** term into `config.Native`. Assert only the converted list into `config.Auxiliary` as well, which matches `ls->get_axioms()` for `InterpolateByCases`.
2. Remove the per-call conversion loop in `InterpolateTree` (`interpolation_solver.go:48-77`) and pass `theory` straight through.
3. In `interpolationAxiom`, get the Int sort without creating a numeral first (`m.MkIntSort()` or the arithmetic plugin's sort). Build `int_val(i)` before `f(a)` in each iteration, so the numeral is created before the application, as GCC does.

**Regression test.** Add `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/duality_background_large_distinct.smt2` with the script above. The expected `scriptResults` entry is:
```
unsat
(fixedpoint 
(define-fun err () Bool
  (= c0 c1))
(define-fun @Fail!1 () Bool
  (= c0 c1))
(define-fun q ((x!0 Int)) Bool
  (= x!0 c0))
)
```
That is the z3 output; check it with `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`. In `pkg/duality/interpolation_distinct_test.go`, extend `TestInterpolationAxiomLargeDistinctLegacySolverWorkaround` to check that the numeral `i` has a smaller AST id than `@distinct(a_i)` for every `i`, and that no numeral `0` exists before the fresh declaration.

<a id="duality-02-f6"></a>
#### duality_02-F6: `ModelValueAsConstraint` builds `iff` for Boolean parameters where the C++ `operator==` builds `=` (OP_EQ)

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/duality/model_constraints.go:77` (`ModelValueAsConstraint`) and `:218` (`modelArrayEntriesAsConstraint`)
- C++: `src/duality/duality_rpfp.cpp:2623-2645`; `duality_wrapper.h:535-537` (`operator==` → `mk_app(basic, OP_EQ, a, b)`)

**C++ behavior.** `expr res = t == expr(ctx, r);` and `select(t, k) == v` are always OP_EQ, even when the sort is Bool.

**Go behavior.** `m.MkEq(h, value)` calls `mkEquality`, which picks `ASTOpIff` when the sort is Bool (`ast_core_basic_convenience.go:14-17`).

**Impact.** For Boolean predicate arguments, or arrays with Bool range, the constraint has a different operator. `EvalNodeAsConstraint` feeds `ExpandUnderapproxNodes`, which complements the result into a node `Bound`. Later implicant passes treat `iff` (its own branch in `ImplicantRed`) differently from an `=` leaf.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted.

**Fix.** Use `m.MkFamilyApp(0, ast.ASTOpEq, nil, []ast.ASTHandle{h, value})` at both sites. Audit other uses of C++ `==` in this package the same way; `RedDualRela` is correct, because the C++ there chooses `Iff` on purpose.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/duality/model_constraints_test.go`, add `TestRPFPModelConstraintsBooleanUsesEq`. Create a node with one Bool parameter, set the model `p_N = true`, and expect `EvalNodeAsConstraint` to have a decl kind of `ASTOpEq`, not `ASTOpIff`.

<a id="duality-02-f7"></a>
#### duality_02-F7: variable projector: construction order and arity handling differ from `IsCanonIneq` / `IndexLA`

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/duality/projection_bounds.go:123-145` (`canonical`, the GE-negated case); `pkg/duality/projection_index.go:80-95,96-140` (`linear`, Sub/Times)
- C++: `src/duality/duality_rpfp.cpp:2289-2298` (`IsCanonIneq`), `:2219-2245` (`IndexLA`)

**C++ behavior.**
- `IsCanonIneq` builds `bound = -(arg1 - 1); term = -arg0;` and only then simplifies `bound` and `term`.
- `IndexLA` `Sub` indexes only `arg(0)` (with pos) and `arg(1)` (with !pos).
- `Times` uses only `arg(0)` / `arg(1)`, preferring `arg(0)` as the coefficient, whatever the arity.

**Go behavior.**
- `canonical` simplifies `bound` before it builds `(- lhs)`.
- `linear` walks every argument of an n-ary `-`, giving arguments 2 and up the positive sign.
- An n-ary `*` (more than 2 arguments) goes to `remove`.
- When both factors are numerals, Go uses `arg(1)` as the coefficient.

**Impact.** AST creation order differs in the negated-GE case, which affects ids and the trace. The n-ary cases change which variables Fourier-Motzkin may eliminate. They are reachable only if the som-simplified literals still contain an n-ary `-` (normally removed) or a nonlinear `*` of 3 or more factors.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted.

**Fix.**
- `canonical`: build `term = app(8, lhs)` right after `bound = app(8, difference)`, then normalize `bound` and then `term`.
- `linear`: for `op == 7`, visit only arguments 0 and 1. For `op == 9`, apply the rule to arguments 0 and 1 for any `n >= 2`: if `ak == 0`, use `arg0` as the coefficient; else if `bk == 0`, use `arg1`; else do nothing.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/duality/projection_index_test.go`, add `TestProjectionIndexTernaryMulUsesFirstTwoFactors`: for `(<= (* 2 x y) 5)`, expect `x` to be indexed with coefficient `-2`. In `projection_bounds_test.go`, add `TestProjectionCanonicalNegatedGeOrder`: the id of the `(- lhs)` term must be lower than the id of the simplified bound.

<a id="duality-03-f1"></a>
#### duality_03-F1: `BacktrackingDerivation.RecordAnnotationUpdate` never adds the source node to the outer `updated_nodes` set

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/duality/derivation_updates.go:35-73` (`RecordAnnotationUpdate`). The effect shows up in this shard's
  `pkg/duality/unwinding_global_candidates.go:79` (`GenCandidatesFromInductionFailure`).
- C++: `src/duality/duality_solver.cpp:2514-2529` (`DerivationTreeSlow::RecordUpdate`) → `:1574` (`UpdateNodeToNode`) →
  `:1561-1572` (`Duality::Update`)

**C++ behavior.** `RecordUpdate` does not reimplement the update. It calls the outer solver:
```
bool res = duality->UpdateNodeToNode(node->map,node);   // -> Update(node->map, node->Annotation)
...
bool Update(Node *node, const RPFP::Transformer &fact, bool eager=false){
    if(!node->Annotation.SubsetEq(fact)){
        reporter->Update(node,fact,eager); ... indset->Update(node,fact);
        updated_nodes.insert(node->map);          // <-- source node marked as updated
        node->Annotation.IntersectWith(fact);
```
`GenCandidatesFromInductionFailure(false)` then scans only the edges whose parent is in `updated_nodes`.

**Go behavior.** `RecordAnnotationUpdate` inlines `Update`: SubsetEq, reporters, `sourceCovering.Update`, IntersectWith. It omits
`updated_nodes.insert`. Only `Unwinding.update` (`unwinding_updates.go:35`) and `MakeLeaf` write `u.updatedNodes`. When the
derivation learns the fact first, the outer `UpdateWithInterpolant` then finds it redundant, and nothing ever marks the node.

**Impact.** On most recursive duality inputs with default parameters, the updates-only scan finds no candidates. g3 then prints
`msg No candidates from updates. Trying full scan.` and runs the full scan, which z3 does not do. The candidate order and the
rest of the search differ from that point on, including the conjectures, interpolants and printed certificates. This is the
first divergence in `diff_arith-duality_190/154/192/104/128`, and it is the start of FUZZ_F lead (c).

**Reproduction.** `$S/work/duality_03/upd.smt2`:
```
(set-option :fixedpoint.engine duality)
(declare-rel inv (Int Int))
(declare-rel err ())
(declare-var x Int)
(declare-var y Int)
(declare-var x2 Int)
(declare-var y2 Int)
(rule (=> (and (= x 0) (= y 0)) (inv x y)))
(rule (=> (and (inv x y) (= x2 (+ x 1)) (= y2 (+ y 2))) (inv x2 y2)))
(rule (=> (and (inv x y) (>= y 5)) err))
(query err :print-certificate true)
```
Run with `-v:1`. Both binaries print the same lines up to `[18]cover @Fail!0: 6 by 3`. Then z3 prints
`[19]induction failure: inv, children = 4` and g3 prints `[19]msg No candidates from updates. Trying full scan.`.
For a scratch verification, I copied `pkg/` to `$S/work/duality_03/pkg` and applied the fix below, then built
`$S/work/duality_03/g3fix`. With it, the `-v:1` trace of `upd.smt2` and of three recursion-bound variants (`rb1..3.smt2`)
matches z3 up to the certificate. The first divergence also moves later in fuzz scripts 104 (line 20→37), 128 (20→38),
154 (20→52), 190 (20→38) and 192 (20→32). What remains there is an interpolant difference (`(<= y 4)` against `(= y 4)`), which
is outside this shard.

**Fix.** Route the derivation update through the outer bookkeeping, as the C++ does:
1. Add `sourceUnwinding *Unwinding` to `BacktrackingDerivation` (`derivation_backtrack.go`). Set it next to every
   `sourceCovering` assignment: `unwinding_produce.go:68` (`newDerivation`) and `unwinding_expand_underapprox.go:47`.
   It is better still to replace the inlined SubsetEq/reporter/covering/intersect sequence in `RecordAnnotationUpdate` with
   `d.sourceUnwinding.update(original, node.Annotation, aux, false)`, which is exactly `Duality::Update`.
2. A minimal version (the one verified) goes just before `original.Annotation.IntersectWith`:
```go
if u := d.sourceUnwinding; u != nil {
    if u.updatedNodes == nil { u.updatedNodes = make(map[*Node]bool) }
    u.updatedNodes[original.Map] = true
}
```

**Regression test.** Extend `pkg/duality/derivation_updates_test.go` with `TestRecordAnnotationUpdateMarksOuterUpdatedNodes`.
Use the fixture in `TestDerivationUpdatesPropagateAcrossInstancesAndBacktracking` (`dualityNativeSolverServicesFixture`,
`NewRPFP`, `NewRPFPWithVocabulary`, `NewDerivationTree`, `NewBacktrackingDerivation`). The tree's original nodes must be
unwinding instances whose `Map` is a source node, so build a source RPFP, an `Unwinding` (`NewUnwinding`), and the instance with
`u.CreateNodeInstance`. Set `search.sourceUnwinding = u`, make `RecordAnnotationUpdate` learn `false`, and assert
`u.updatedNodes[sourceNode]`. For an end-to-end check, add `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/duality_updated_nodes.smt2` (the input
above). Run it with `-v:1` against `build/z3` and expect the z3 trace lines `[19]induction failure: inv, children = 4` and
no `No candidates from updates` before `[36]`. g3 currently ignores `(set-option :verbose 1)` for the reporter (see Needs
verification), so the check must pass `-v:1` on the command line.

<a id="duality-03-f2"></a>
#### duality_03-F2: `unhoistLoop` deduplicates `parent.Incoming`; z3 rewrites a repeated-child edge twice and fails

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/duality/unhoist.go:197-205` (`unhoistLoop`, incoming-edge loop)
- C++: `src/duality/duality_rpfp.cpp:3943-3963` (`RPFP::UnhoistLoop`)

**C++ behavior.** It iterates `parent->Incoming`, which has one entry per child position. An edge that uses the unhoisted node
twice is therefore processed twice. On the second pass, `GetRel` finds the already-extended literal, and `AddParamsToApp`
appends the new parameters again. `parent->Name` rejects the result and the query fails.

**Go behavior.** It processes each edge once, by design:
```go
// Incoming contains one entry per child position. Rewrite each edge once;
// its inner loop already handles every position, including repeated children.
processed := make(map[*Edge]bool)
```

**Impact.** A Horn system with a hoisted loop predicate that appears twice in one body: z3 prints an error and `unknown`, while
g3 answers. This is a documented deviation that changes the result, and it is not listed in `z3_bug_exclusions.txt`.

**Reproduction.** `$S/work/duality_03/uh2.smt2`:
```
(set-option :fixedpoint.engine duality)
(declare-rel inv (Int Int))
(declare-rel err ())
(declare-var x Int)
(declare-var n Int)
(declare-var k Int)
(declare-var y Int)
(declare-var m Int)
(rule (=> (and (= x 0) (= n (* 2 k))) (inv x n)))
(rule (=> (and (inv x n) (< x n)) (inv (+ x 1) n)))
(rule (=> (and (inv x n) (inv y m) (> x (+ n 1))) err))
(query err)
```
z3: `(error "query failed: Wrong number of arguments (4) passed to function (declare-fun inv!2 (Int Int Int) Bool)")` then
`unknown`. g3: `sat`. With one `inv` in the body (`uh1.smt2`), both answer `sat`.

**Fix.** The owner has to decide. Either (a) keep g3's correct behavior and add an entry to
`pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/z3_bug_exclusions.txt` that describes this C++ double rewrite, or (b) for fidelity, iterate
`parent.Incoming` without the `processed` set. In (b), make `AddParamsToApp`'s arity error surface as the same
`query failed: Wrong number of arguments (...)` message.

**Regression test.** Add `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/duality_unhoist_repeated_child.smt2` (the input above). Option (a) expects
`sat` and needs the exclusions entry so that `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference` skips the comparison. Option (b) expects the z3
error line and `unknown`, checked with `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`.

<a id="duality-03-f3"></a>
#### duality_03-F3: `SubstAtom` recognizes `and`/`or`/`not` by raw decl kind without checking the basic family

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/duality/subst_atom.go:41-51,86-90` (`Context.SubstAtom`, `isNot` and the And/Or test)
- C++: `src/duality/duality_rpfp.cpp:593-622,537-545` (`Z3User::SubstAtom`, `SubstAtomTriv`, `Negate`). The wrapper's
  `get_decl_kind` (`duality_wrapper.cpp:213-236`) maps kinds by family.

**C++ behavior.** `f.get_decl_kind()` returns `And`/`Or`/`Not` only for basic-family declarations. Arithmetic `OP_GT` maps to
`Gt`, `OP_ADD` to `Plus`, and so on.

**Go behavior.** `m.GetDeclKind(h)` returns the raw per-family number, and it is compared with `ast.ASTOpAnd` (5),
`ast.ASTOpOr` (6) and `ast.ASTOpNot` (9) with no family check. Arithmetic `>` (OP_GT=5) is treated as a conjunction.
`+` (OP_ADD=6), if reached, is treated as a disjunction. `isNot` matches arithmetic `*` (OP_MUL=9) and set `subset`.
`str.contains` (OP_SEQ_CONTAINS=5) is also treated as a conjunction.

**Impact.** The function is called from `RemoveRedundancy` (`remove_redundancy.go:147`), which is used on annotations and case
interpolants. A conjunct `(> a b)` would be rebuilt as `ReallySimplifyAndOr([a b], and)`, which gives an ill-sorted `and` or an
error. Today's annotations are simplified (`>` becomes `not <=`), so I did not find a reachable input.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: it needs a `>` atom to survive into an annotation.

**Fix.** At both sites, test `family == m.BasicFamilyID()` before comparing `op`, as `subterm_truth.go:56` and
`remove_redundancy.go:94` already do. In `isNot`, add the family check before `op != ast.ASTOpNot`.

**Regression test.** Add `TestSubstAtomIgnoresArithmeticOpsWithBasicKindNumbers` to `pkg/duality/subst_atom_test.go` (or
create that file), using the context fixtures from the existing remove-redundancy tests. Call `SubstAtom` on
`(and (> x 0) p)` with atom `p` and value `true`. Expect `(> x 0)` unchanged, with no error.

<a id="duality-03-f4"></a>
#### duality_03-F4: wrapper `Sort.Kind` swaps Int and Real

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/duality/wrapper_ast.go:231-234` (`Sort.Kind`)
- C++: `src/duality/duality_wrapper.cpp:281-302` (`context::get_sort_kind`); `src/ast/arith_decl_plugin.h:30-33`

**C++ behavior.** `k == INT_SORT` (1) → `IntSort`; `k == REAL_SORT` (0) → `RealSort`.

**Go behavior.** `kind == 0` → `SortInt` and `kind == 1` → `SortReal`. The rest of g3 uses Int = 1 (for example
`qe/arithmetic_equation_solve.go:20`).

**Impact.** Latent. The only live consumer in the package is `IsBool`. Any future `is_int`/`is_real` port would get the wrong
answer.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted (no live consumer).

**Fix.** Swap the two cases: `Arithmetic && kind == 1 → SortInt`, `Arithmetic && kind == 0 → SortReal`.

**Regression test.** Extend `pkg/duality/wrapper_ast_test.go` (next to the `boolean.Kind()` check at line 152). Build

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/duality/unwinding_extend.go:55` (passes `services.Bounds.Checker`, which is `UnwindingSearch.Local`) →

- C++: `src/duality/duality_solver.cpp:1666-1686` (`CheckEdgeCaching`: `RPFP_caching *checker = gen_cands_rpfp;`)

**C++ behavior.** `DoEagerDeduction` → `CheckEdgeCaching` uses `gen_cands_rpfp`, the same caching RPFP (edge clones and per-edge

**Impact.** This only matters with history proposers (`LearnFrom`, repeated queries). The per-edge solvers, cached assertions and
edge clones of the two checkers end up in different states, so later models and the search can differ. The sat/unsat result of
the eager check should not change.

**Reproduction.** Not isolated: a two-query script (`$S/work/duality_03/twoq.smt2`) diverges earlier for interpolant reasons.

**Regression test.** Extend `pkg/duality/unwinding_eager_test.go` or `unwinding_extend_test.go`. Run `Extend` with one
proposer and assert that the conjecture's edge clone was created in the `Global` checker (`checker.clones` has the edge) and
not in `Local`.

<a id="duality-03-f6"></a>
#### duality_03-F6: `CandidateFeasible` recursion-bound exit pops the solver scope that the C++ leaks

- Severity: low
- Confidence: medium
- Go: `pkg/duality/unwinding_feasible.go:94-114` (`CandidateFeasible`, deferred `checker.Pop(1)`)
- C++: `src/duality/duality_solver.cpp:870-881`

**C++ behavior.** It calls `checker->Push()`, then
`if(NodePastRecursionBound(cand.Children[i])){ timer_stop(...); return false; }`. That early return has no `Pop` and no
`delete checker`, so the shared solver keeps one extra scope for the rest of the run. The path is reachable whenever any node has
`recursion_bound < UINT_MAX` (for example `fixedpoint.duality.recursion_bound=N`).

**Go behavior.** The deferred `checker.Pop(1)` restores the scope level.

**Impact.** After the first cutoff, every later query runs one scope deeper in z3. That can change the SMT search (base-level
simplifications, lemma retention) but not the answers. I saw no stdout difference on `rb1..3.smt2`.

**Reproduction.** Not observable at the `-v:1` level in my tests.

**Fix.** For fidelity, on the `past` branch leave the scope pushed: skip the deferred Pop with a flag and record the leaked scope,
so the RPFP's scope bookkeeping still balances when the checker is closed. Otherwise list the leak in `z3_bug_exclusions.txt`.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/duality/unwinding_feasible_test.go`, set `RecursionBound=0` and a node with `RecursionBound=0` and a
back edge. Call `CandidateFeasible` and assert the native solver scope level before and after (+1 if mirrored).

<a id="duality-03-f7"></a>
#### duality_03-F7: `TermTree.Close` releases children and terms back to front

- Severity: low
- Confidence: medium
- Go: `pkg/duality/term_tree.go:84-116` (`TermTree.Close`)
- C++: `src/duality/duality_wrapper.h:1318-1327` (`~TermTree` deletes `children[0..n-1]`; then the members `terms` (front to
  back, libstdc++ `_Destroy`) and `term` are destroyed)

**C++ behavior.** Children are deleted in order 0..n-1, then the `terms` elements in order 0..n-1, then `term`.

**Go behavior.** Children are closed from n-1 down to 0, and terms from n-1 down to 0.

**Impact.** Only the order of AST reference releases differs, and so the recycling of AST ids. Interpolation output is id-order
sensitive (see FUZZ_K-F2).

**Reproduction.** Not attempted.

**Fix.** Close `children` in increasing index order, then `terms` in increasing index order, then `term`. Keep the
retry-on-error semantics by tracking a start index instead of truncating from the end.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/duality` (a `term_tree_test.go`), build a tree with two children that hold the only references to
distinct fresh constants. Close it, create two new constants, and assert the ids are reused in C++ order (child 0's id freed
first).

### Area: Interpolation (`pkg/interp`)

*interp_01.* The shard holds the iZ3 base (`iz3base`, `iz3mgr`, `iz3checker`), the frame reducer and option plumbing from `iz3interp.cpp`, and the whole `iz3proof_itp.cpp` interpolating proof system (`DirectProofInterpolator`, the `direct_proof_*.go` files). The rule dispatch is close to the C++. Most divergences are in the simplification back end: the wrong rewriter, error kinds collapsed into one, `@normal` and rewrite-chain cases dropped, and AST creation order. - **F1** (high, confirmed). The interpolator runs a `som`/`sort_sums` rewriter where the C++ runs plain `z3_simplify`. This alone explains every monomial-order difference that FUZZ_K-F2 attributed to AST lifetimes. With a one-line change, all 4 F2 scripts and 5 new fuzz cases match `build/z3` byte for byte. - **F2** (high, confirmed). On LRA, `eq_from_ineq` treats a Real `0.0` like the Int `0`, so g3 returns an interpolant where z3 fails. - **F3** (high, confirmed). A lifetime bug in `reconstructFarkasWithDual` (outside the shard) makes g3 fail with `invalid AST owner, kind or lifetime`. Counts: high 5, medium 9, low 3 (17 findings; 5 confirmed with the binaries). interp_01-F1 (ReallySimplify som/sort_sums) duplicates interp_02-F2.

*interp_02.* This shard covers the iZ3 translation layer and its helpers: `iz3translate.cpp` (translation_*.go), parts of `iz3mgr.cpp/.h` (manager_*.go), `iz3interp.cpp` orchestration, `iz3proof.cpp` (proof.go), `iz3scopes`, `iz3pp`, `iz3profiling`, and the interp params. Scopes, params, frame handling, unit resolution, the Farkas, GCD and Gomory rules, the commutativity helpers and certificate reconstruction match the C++ statement by statement, apart from the items below. Four of the defects were confirmed with `build/z3`, and three fixes were verified in a scratch build (`S/work/interp_02/g3fix`): - **F1, critical.** The quantifier-instantiation idiom never fires, so g3 prints interpolants built from internal proof terms (`@rewrite_A`, `@cong`, `@mp` ...). - **F2, high.** The Go `ReallySimplify` turns on `som`/`sort_sums`, but the C++ never does: the C++ calls `z3_simplify` at those sites, and the colon-prefixed keys of `z3_really_simplify` have no effect anyway. With this fixed, all four FUZZ_K-F2 monomial-order scripts match `build/z3` byte for byte, along with every other interpolation script that was tried. Counts: 1 critical, 1 high, 9 medium, 0 low.

#### interp_01-F2: `equalityEndpointsFromInequality` accepts a Real `0.0` where `eq_from_ineq` requires the Int numeral 0 (pointer compare)

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/interp/direct_proof_eq2leq.go:229-233` (`equalityEndpointsFromInequality`)
- C++: `src/interp/iz3proof_itp.cpp:1907-1929` (`eq_from_ineq`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
ast srhs = arg(ineq,0);
if(op(srhs) == Plus && num_args(srhs) == 2 && arg(ineq,1) == make_int(rational(0))){
    lhs = arg(srhs,0); rhs = arg(srhs,1);
    if(op(rhs) == Times){ rhs = arg(rhs,1); return; }
}
if(op(ineq) == Leq || op(ineq) == Geq){ lhs = srhs; rhs = arg(ineq,1); return; }
```
`ast_r ==` compares node pointers. `make_int` builds an **Int**-sorted 0, so a Real `0.0` never matches.

**Go behavior.**
```go
rightValue, rightNumeral, err := p.base.manager.Numeral(right)
...
if leftOp == OperatorPlus && rightNumeral && rightValue.Sign() == 0 {
```
This matches any zero numeral, Real included.

**Impact.** For LRA, `simplify_rotate_eq2leq` (mixed equality used in a bound) takes a different path. g3 splits `(+ x (* -1 y))` into `x`/`y`, while z3 keeps the sum and `0.0`. In practice z3 then fails with `bad term position!`, and g3 returns an interpolant. Mixed EUF+LRA problems are common in Ivy. With the fix applied in a scratch build (`S/work/interp_01/g3_eq`), g3 fails on the same inputs. The error message still differs; that is F4.

**Reproduction.** `S/work/interp_01/n5.smt2`:
```
(declare-fun f (Real) Real)(declare-const a Real)(declare-const b Real)(declare-const c Real)
(compute-interpolant (interp (and (<= a c) (>= a c) (> (f a) 0.0))) (and (<= b c) (>= b c) (< (f b) 0.0)))
```
`build/z3`: `(error "line 2 column 105: bad term position!")`
`S/bin/g3`: `unsat (interpolants (not (<= (f c) 0.0)) (not (<= (f c) 0.0)))`
`n7.smt2` (`(= a (+ c d))` form) behaves the same way. The Int versions (`n4`, `n6`) agree.

**Fix.** Replace the numeric test with the pointer test against the Int numeral:
```go
intZero, err := p.base.manager.MakeIntText("0")
if err != nil { return ast.ASTHandle{}, ast.ASTHandle{}, err }
if leftOp == OperatorPlus && right == intZero {
```
Keep the `len(args) == 2` and `Times` checks as they are. Check the sibling sites that compare with `make_int(...)` by value instead of by node. `simplifySum`'s `args[1] != make_int(1)`, `divideInequality`, `arithmeticRewriteCoefficient` and `LinearCombination` are equivalent today because the coefficients are always Int-sorted. `distributeSumCoefficient` and the `y == make_int(0)` test in `simplify_rotate_leq2eq` are not: see F6 and the Needs-verification list.

**Regression test.** Vector `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/interp_lra_eq_from_ineq.smt2` (the input above), expected `"(error \"line 2 column 105: bad term position!\")\n"` once F4 is also fixed (until then g3 prints the `theory not supported ...` message). Add it to `scriptResults` and to the `parseErrorScripts`/error list the runner uses for `(error ...)` vectors. Check it with the CPP reference run. Unit test `TestDirectProofEqFromIneqRealZeroKeepsSum` in `direct_proof_test.go`, using `interpRewritingManagerFixture` and `RealType`: for `(<= (+ x (* -1 y)) 0.0)`, `equalityEndpointsFromInequality` must return `((+ x (* -1 y)), 0.0)`. For the Int form it must return `(x, y)`.

<a id="interp-01-f3"></a>
#### interp_01-F3: `reconstructFarkasWithDual` uses Farkas temporaries after the inner `IsSAT` solver has freed them (out of shard, found by fuzzing)

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/interp/translation_reconstruct.go:446-460` (`FullTranslation.reconstructFarkasWithDual`), with `pkg/interp/base_solver.go:61-65` (`Base.IsSAT` closes its solver)
- C++: `src/interp/iz3translate.cpp:1440-1480` (the dual-LP Farkas reconstruction), `src/interp/iz3base.cpp:263-298` (`is_sat`)

**C++ behavior.** All the coefficients `@c`, the `dual` sums, `zero` and the constraint vector are `ast_r` values held in `std::vector<ast>`. Each holds a reference, so the temporary solver in `is_sat` (asserts, then `solver = nullptr`) cannot delete them.

**Go behavior.** `coefficients`, `constraints`, `zero` and the `dual` entries are plain `ast.ASTHandle` values with refcount 0. The first `t.base.IsSAT(constraints, nil)` asserts them into a fresh solver and `s.Close()` releases that solver's references, which deletes the nodes. The next loop iteration then calls `Make(OperatorEqual, coefficient, zero)` on a dead handle (`STALE handle slot=373 ... live=false`, stack through `translation_reconstruct.go:449` → `:542 reconstructFarkas` → `:562 translateEqualityPropagation`).

**Impact.** On mixed EUF+LIA/LRA problems whose proof has an eq-propagate lemma that needs dual-LP Farkas reconstruction, g3 fails where z3 returns an interpolant. 9 of about 1300 unsat cases in two 1500-script random mixed runs (`fzm`, `fzm2`) hit this, all at `translation_reconstruct.go:449`. It is by far the most frequent divergence the fuzzing found.

**Reproduction.** `S/work/interp_01/fzm/m3_1232.smt2`:
```
(declare-const c Int)
(declare-const d Int)
(declare-const a0 Int)
(declare-const b0 Int)
(declare-const a1 Int)
(declare-fun f (Int) Int)
(compute-interpolant (interp (and (= b0 c) (= (+ d b0) (* (- 3) d)) (= (f d) c))) (and (not (= a1 d)) (<= (f d) d) (>= (f d) d) (<= a1 c) (>= a1 c)))
```
`build/z3`: `unsat` followed by an interpolant, `(let ((a!1 (>= (+ d (* (- 1) (f d))) 0)) ...) (and a!2 a!4))` printed twice. `S/bin/g3`: `(error "line 7 column 148: g3: invalid AST owner, kind or lifetime")`. Also `fzm/m3_477.smt2` and `m3_489.smt2` (LRA).

**Fix.** In `reconstructFarkasWithDual` (and in `reconstructFarkas` and any other caller of `Base.IsSAT` whose inputs are Go-only handles), pin every handle that a C++ `ast_r` would hold until the function returns:
- each `coefficient` from `FreshConstant`;
- `zero` and `one`;
- every `dual[variable]` value as it is replaced, releasing the previous value, which mirrors `ast_r` assignment;
- `rhs`;
- every element appended to `constraints`.

Use a local `[]ast.ASTRef` released in reverse order on return, the same idiom as `DirectProofInterpolator.hold`. Audit the other `IsSAT` callers (`translation_reconstruct.go:209,454,466`) the same way.

**Regression test.** Vector `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/interp_dual_farkas_lifetime.smt2` (the input above). The expected output is exactly what `build/z3` prints (run it and paste the result into `scriptResults`), checked with the CPP reference run.

<a id="interp-01-f4"></a>
#### interp_01-F4: error kinds collapsed: `iz3_exception` messages, `proof_error` and `cannot_simplify` all become `ProofError`, and the `@sum` fallback catches all of them

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed (message), high (catch scope)
- Go: `pkg/interp/direct_proof_simplify.go:102-107` (`simplifyProofTerm` sum fallback). The `ProofError{}` returns are listed at `direct_proof_rewrite.go:23,32,203,207,628,632,668,...`, `direct_proof_chain_arithmetic.go:63,89,120`, `direct_proof_eq2leq.go:153,252,294,324,366,383,424`, `direct_proof_normal.go:65` and `direct_proof_sum.go:151,201,345,394,398,458,500,508,742`. `orchestration.go:39-49` (`interpolationTranslationError`) maps them to `InterpolationError`.
- C++: `src/interp/iz3proof_itp.cpp:543-572` (`simplify_rec` catch); throw sites `:1001,1012` ("bad inequality rewriting"), `:1443` ("bad term position!"), `:1428` ("bad position!"), `:1465` ("bad rewrite"), `:1722,1824` ("bad rewrite chain"), `:1676-1705` ("bad negative equality chain"), `:1995` ("what?"), `:2006,840,881` ("help!"), `:1161,1175` ("bad exmid"/"bad cong"), `:591` ("foo!"), `:571` (`throw "interpolation failure"`)

**C++ behavior.** There are four distinct kinds:
- `cannot_simplify`, which is caught only in `simplify_rec`. For `@sum` the term is cloned; any other rule rethrows as `const char*` `"interpolation failure"`, which becomes `interpolation_failure`.
- `iz3proof_itp::proof_error`, which `translate` turns into `interpolation_error`.
- `iz3_exception(msg)` and its subclasses `bad_ineq_inference`, `cannot_split` and `subterm_normals_failed`. These propagate to the command, which prints `(error "...: <msg>")`.
- `unsupported`.

**Go behavior.** All of the above are returned as `ProofError{}`, and the `@sum` fallback catches every one of them:
```go
if err != nil {
	var proofError ProofError
	if declaration == p.sum && errors.As(err, &proofError) {
		result, err = p.base.manager.Clone(current, args)
```

**Impact.**
- The command prints `theory not supported by interpolation or bad proof` where z3 prints `bad term position!`, `interpolation failure` and so on. This was confirmed on `n5.smt2` once F2 is fixed.
- Worse: when a `@sum` simplification hits a C++ `iz3_exception` or a `proof_error`, for example `linear_comb` on a non-inequality, `make_normal` on a non-inequality or `subst_in_pos` out of range, z3 aborts but g3 silently keeps the unsimplified `@sum` term and carries on. That can produce an interpolant containing `@sum`/`@p!n` junk, or a different one.

**Fix.**
1. Introduce three error types in `exception.go`: `cannotSimplifyError{}`, the existing `ProofError` (for `proof_error`) and `Error{message}` (already present, for `iz3_exception(msg)`).
2. Return the matching one at each site, using the C++ text. Examples: `NewError("bad term position!")` in `substituteAtPosition`, `NewError("bad rewrite chain")` in `extractRewrites` and `headRewriteChain`, `NewError("bad inequality rewriting")` in `subtermNormals`.
3. In `simplifyProofTerm`, catch only `cannotSimplifyError`. For `@sum` clone the term; for any other rule return `InterpolationFailure{Message: "interpolation failure"}`.
4. Keep `errSubtermNormals`, which corresponds to `subterm_normals_failed`, and give `splitRewriteChain` a dedicated `errCannotSplit` so that `modusPonensForward` catches only that error, not every `ProofError`.
5. In `interpolationTranslationError`, map `ProofError`/`UnsupportedProofError` to `InterpolationError`, and pass `Error` and `InterpolationFailure` through unchanged so the command prints the C++ message.

**Regression test.** The F2 vector `interp_lra_eq_from_ineq.smt2` with expected `(error "line 2 column 105: bad term position!")`. Unit test `TestDirectProofSumFallbackOnlyCatchesCannotSimplify` in `direct_proof_test.go`: build `@sum((<= 0 0), 1, (and p q))`, where `(and p q)` is not an inequality, so `sum_cond_ineq` raises cannot_simplify. Assert that the result is the cloned `@sum`. Then make `linear_comb` fail with a `proof_error`, for example by passing a strict `P` that `LinearCombination` rejects, and assert that `SimplifyProofTerm` returns an error rather than a clone.

<a id="interp-01-f5"></a>
#### interp_01-F5: `@normal` and rewrite-chain cases dropped in `simplifyRotatedSum`, `divideInequality` and `simplifyRotatedLeqToEq`

- Severity: high
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/interp/direct_proof_sum.go:389-391` (`rotate` closure in `simplifyRotatedSum`), `:305-364` (`divideInequality`), `:527-550` (`simplifyRotatedLeqToEq`)
- C++: `src/interp/iz3proof_itp.cpp:749-765` (`rotate_sum_rec`), `:734-747` (`idiv_ineq`), `:767-777` (`simplify_rotate_leq2eq`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
ast rotate_sum_rec(const ast &pl, const ast &pf, ast &Aproves, ast &Bproves, ast &ineq){
    if(pf == pl){
        if(sym(ineq) == normal)
            return ineq;
        return simplify_ineq(ineq);
...
ast idiv_ineq(const ast &ineq1, const ast &divisor){
    if(sym(ineq1) == normal){
        ast in1,n1; destruct_normal(ineq1,in1,n1);
        in1 = idiv_ineq(in1,divisor);
        return make_normal(in1,n1);
    }
...
    return make(op(ineq),mk_idiv(arg(ineq,0),divisor),mk_idiv(arg(ineq,1),divisor));
...
ast xleqy = round_ineq(ineq_from_chain(pf1,Aproves1,Bproves1));
ast yleqx = round_ineq(ineq_from_chain(pf2,Aproves1,Bproves1));
```

**Go behavior.**
- `rotate`: `if proof == placeholder { return p.base.manager.SimplifyInequality(current) }`. There is no `@normal` check, so a normal accumulator reaches `SimplifyInequality`, which returns `NewError("not an inequality")`.
- `divideInequality`: there is no `@normal` case. Any operator other than `LT`/`LE` returns `ProofError` (C++ builds `make(op(ineq), ...)` for any operator).
- `simplifyRotatedLeqToEq`: calls `roundInequality(xLeqY)` directly. It never calls `ineq_from_chain`, so a rewrite-chain premise (`@concat`) is rejected with `ProofError`.

**Impact.** Whenever a mixed equality chain enters a rotated Farkas sum (the `sum_normal_ineq` path), a cut rule over a normalized inequality, or a mixed `leq2eq` whose premises are rewrite chains, z3 produces an interpolant and g3 fails. These are exactly the mixed EUF+arithmetic cases Ivy generates. None of the fuzz runs hit them, so this is not reproduced.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted to the end. 3600 random mixed scripts never created an `@normal` node in z3's trace (`grep -c '@normal '`). A hand-built unit test is the way to pin it down (below).

**Fix.**
1. In the `rotate` closure: `if proof == placeholder { if normal, _ := p.isNormalWrapper(current); normal { return current, nil }; return p.base.manager.SimplifyInequality(current) }`.
2. At the top of `divideInequality`: if `isNormalWrapper(inequality)`, `destructNormal`, recurse on the body and `makeNormal(body, chain)`. Replace `if op != OperatorLE { return ProofError{} }` with building `Make(op, idiv(left), idiv(right))`. Compute the right-hand `idiv` first (GCC evaluation order, see F11).
3. In `simplifyRotatedLeqToEq`: after the two `destructConditionalInequality` calls, compute `xLeqY = roundInequality(ineqFromChain(xLeqY, &aProof1, &bProof1))` and then `yLeqX` the same way. `ineqFromChain` is `rewriteChainToNormalInequality` when the term is a `@concat`, and the term itself otherwise, as in `sumConditionalInequality`. This must happen in that order, with both `round`s after their own `ineq_from_chain`.

**Regression test.** In `direct_proof_test.go`, using `interpRewritingManagerFixture` and the `TestDirectProofNormalInequalitySumAndFinalSubstitution` setup:
- `TestDirectProofRotatedSumKeepsNormal`: `@rotsum(lit, ph(lit))` whose accumulator has become a `@normal(...)` must simplify to that `@normal` term, not an error.
- `TestDirectProofIdivNormal`: `divideInequality(@normal((<= x 3), chain), 2)` returns `@normal((<= (div x 2) 1), chain)`.
- `TestDirectProofRotatedLeqToEqFromChain`: a `@leq2eq` whose second argument is a one-step A rewrite chain yields the C++ two-rewrite chain.

<a id="interp-01-f6"></a>
#### interp_01-F6: `MakeLeqToEq` lacks the mixed-term branch that falls back to `make_axiom`

- Severity: high
- Confidence: medium (reachability)
- Go: `pkg/interp/direct_proof_arithmetic.go:69-105` (`MakeLeqToEq`)
- C++: `src/interp/iz3proof_itp.cpp:2632-2655` (`make_leq2eq`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
default: { // mixed equality
    if(get_term_type(x) == LitMixed || get_term_type(y) == LitMixed){
        if(y == make_int(rational(0)) && op(x) == Plus && num_args(x) == 2){ }
        else {
            std::vector<ast> lits;
            lits.push_back(con); lits.push_back(make(Not,xleqy)); lits.push_back(make(Not,yleqx));
            return make_axiom(lits);
        }
    }
    ... make_contra_node(make(leq2eq, ...), conjs, 1);
```

**Go behavior.** Go always builds the `@leq2eq` contra node and never checks `TermSide(x)`/`TermSide(y)`.

**Impact.** When an endpoint of the equality is a mixed term, the C++ interpolates the lemma as a localized axiom (localization variables, possibly quantifiers), and the Go produces a `@leq2eq` placeholder node that later simplification handles differently or rejects. Two cases reach this:
- a mixed sum with 3 or more summands;
- because `y == make_int(0)` is a pointer test, any **Real** `(= (+ a b) 0.0)` (see F2).

**Reproduction.** Not reproduced. The fuzz runs did not produce a mixed-endpoint triangle-eq lemma.

**Fix.** After the `TermA`/`TermB` early returns, add:
```go
xSide, _ := p.TermSide(x); ySide, _ := p.TermSide(y)
if xSide == TermMixed || ySide == TermMixed {
	intZero, _ := p.base.manager.MakeIntText("0")

		ny, _ := p.base.manager.Make(OperatorNot, yLeqX)
		return p.keep(p.MakeAxiom([]ast.ASTHandle{conclusion, nx, ny}))
	}

```
Propagate the errors. Note that C++ uses `make(Not, ...)`, not `mk_not`.

#### interp_01-F7: `simplifySymmetry` wraps a commuted negation chain in the condition; the C++ drops it

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/interp/direct_proof_rewrite.go:1402-1418` (`simplifySymmetry`)
- C++: `src/interp/iz3proof_itp.cpp:941-951` (`simplify_symm`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
ast cond = mk_true();
ast equa = sep_cond(args[0],cond);
if(is_equivrel_chain(equa)) return my_implies(cond,reverse_chain(equa));
if(is_negation_chain(equa)) return commute_negation_chain(equa);   // cond dropped

```

**Go behavior.**
```go
} else {
	...
	chain, err = p.commuteNegationChain(chain)
}
...
return p.base.manager.MkImplies(condition, chain)
```
The condition is applied in both branches.

**Reproduction.** Not reproduced end to end. Visible with a unit test.

**Fix.** In the negation branch, `return p.commuteNegationChain(chain)` directly, without `MkImplies(condition, ...)`.

**Regression test.** Extend `TestDirectProofNegationChainSymmetrySimplification` (`direct_proof_test.go:791`). Wrap the chain as `(=> q chain)` before `@symm`, and assert that the simplified result is a `@concat` (`chainParts` succeeds), not an `Implies`.

<a id="interp-01-f8"></a>
#### interp_01-F8: `simplifyModusPonens` omits `normalize(nQ2)` for inequality conclusions

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/interp/direct_proof_rewrite.go:978-996` (`simplifyModusPonens`)
- C++: `src/interp/iz3proof_itp.cpp:1137-1150` (`simplify_modpon`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
if(is_normal_ineq(Q2)){
    ast nQ2 = rewrite_chain_to_normal_ineq(chain,Aproves,Bproves);
    sum_cond_ineq(nQ2,make_int(rational(1)),Q2,Aproves,Bproves);
    interp = normalize(nQ2);
}
```

**Go behavior.** Go calls `sumConditionalInequality` and then wraps `converted` directly in `MkImplies`/`MkAnd`. A `@normal(...)` result is never normalized here. Only the top-level `normalizeProofTerm` in `simplifyProofTerm` sees it, and only when the modus-ponens node is the root.

**Impact.** When an `@mp` over an inequality is nested inside another rule (a sum, a rotation or a resolvent), g3 passes a `@normal` term upward where z3 passes the substituted inequality. The later `sum_normal_ineq` then merges normal chains that z3 has already eliminated, which gives a different interpolant or an error.

**Fix.** After `sumConditionalInequality`, call `converted, e = p.normalizeProofTerm(converted)`. This is `normalize`, which returns its argument unchanged when it is not normal. Then wrap.

**Regression test.** `TestDirectProofModusPonensNormalizesInequality` in `direct_proof_test.go`. Reuse `TestDirectProofNormalInequalitySumAndFinalSubstitution` to obtain a chain whose `rewriteChainToNormalInequality` yields `@normal`. <a id="interp-01-f9"></a>
#### interp_01-F9: `chainSideConjunction` folds `chain_conditions`/`chain_formulas` in reverse order

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/interp/direct_proof_rewrite.go:479-512` (`chainSideConjunction`); used by `contradictChains`, `chainSideProof`, `unmixedEqToInequality`
- C++: `src/interp/iz3proof_itp.cpp:1837-1857` (`chain_conditions`, `chain_formulas`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
ast cond = chain_conditions(t,rest);          // recurse first: earliest rewrite first
if(is_rewrite_side(t,last))
    cond = my_and(cond,rewrite_cond(last));
```
This gives `(and (and c1 c2) c3)` for chain `r1;r2;r3`.

**Go behavior.** Go loops from the last element down, `result = MkAnd(result, entry)`, which gives `(and (and c3 c2) c1)`.

**Impact.** Interpolants built by `contra_chain`/`chain_side_proves` with two or more same-side rewrites at independent positions (`chain_formulas` is always non-trivial) list the conjuncts in the opposite order. Different AST ids and terms follow, and `(and ...)` keeps its order in the printed interpolant.

**Fix.** Collect the matching entries into a slice while walking from the last element, then fold `MkAnd` from the earliest element to the latest. Alternatively, write it recursively like the C++.

Assert that `chainSideConjunction(TermA, chain, false)` is `(and c1 c2)` and that the formulas version is `(and e1 e2)`.

<a id="interp-01-f11"></a>
#### interp_01-F11: AST creation order does not follow GCC's right-to-left argument evaluation, and a placeholder is created eagerly

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed (trace)
- Go:
  - `direct_proof_equality.go:199-211` (`makeMixedCongruence`: numeral before `mk_not`/placeholder);
  - `direct_proof.go:351-384` (`hypothesis`, exmid branch: placeholder(P) before placeholder(¬P));
  - `direct_proof_resolution.go:40-83` (`MakeSymmetry`);
  - `direct_proof_arithmetic.go:91-98,130-137,164-171` (`MakeLeqToEq`, `MakeEqToLeq`, `MakeCutRule` placeholders in left-to-right order);
  - `direct_proof.go:429-449` (`MakeReflexivity`);
  - `direct_proof_sum.go:355-363` (`divideInequality`);
  - `direct_proof_rewrite.go:241-249` (`updateRewrite`: `MkAnd` before the new equality), `:565-587` (`chainSideProof`), `:734-795` (`contradictChains`);
  - `direct_proof_mixed_resolution.go:83-94` (`collectContraResolvents` creates `placeholder(¬lit)` before the loop, even when the loop adds nothing).
- C++: `src/interp/iz3proof_itp.cpp:2505, 2345-2348, 2378-2381, 2650-2654, 2674, 2697, 2362, 746, 1506/1512, 2011, 1121-1134, 283`

**C++ behavior.** The reference build is GCC, which evaluates the arguments of `make(...)`, `my_and(...)` and so on from right to left. For example, `make(cong,foo,make_int(rational(pos)),get_placeholder(mk_not(con)))` creates `(not con)` and `@p!k` before the numeral, and `make(exmid,P,get_placeholder(P),get_placeholder(mk_not(P)))` creates the ¬P placeholder first. In `collect_contra_resolvents`, `get_placeholder` runs only inside the loop, for an `f != pivot`.

**Go behavior.** Arguments are built left to right, and the placeholder is created once before the loop. The first trace divergence on the simplest mixed case (`t1.smt2` below):
```
z3: [mk-app] #94 not #72 / #95 @p!0 / #96 Int / #97 @cong #93 #96 #95
g3: [mk-app] #94 Int / #95 not #72 / #96 @p!0 / #97 @cong #93 #94 #96
```

**Impact.** AST ids and `@p!n` numbering differ from that point on. Ids feed `iz3base::simplify` (`Equal` orientation by id), `fix_normal`/`merge_normal_chains` (ordering by `ast_id`) and the final rewriter's id-sorted sums, so this can change interpolant text as well as the trace.

**Reproduction.** `S/work/interp_01/t1.smt2`:
```
(declare-const a Int)
(declare-const b Int)
(declare-const x Int)
(compute-interpolant (interp (and (= a x) (> a 0))) (and (= b x) (< b 0)))
```
Run both binaries with `trace=true trace_file_name=...` and diff; the first divergence is at line 201, shown above. The printed output is the same.

**Fix.** At each listed site, build the arguments in GCC order, from the last argument to the first, recursively. For example, in `makeMixedCongruence` compute `negatedConclusion` and `conclusionPlaceholder` before `positionTerm`. In `hypothesis` (exmid), take `placeholder(negated)` first. In `MakeSymmetry`, follow the order `mk_not(con)`, `ph(¬con)`, `ph(premcon)`, `symm(ph premcon)`, `exmid`, then for the And: third, second, first. In `MakeEqToLeq`/`MakeCutRule`, take the placeholder of `conjs[1]` first. In `MakeLeqToEq`, take the placeholders from index 2 down to 0. In `MakeReflexivity`, build the second contra first. In `divideInequality`, compute the right-hand `idiv` first. In `collectContraResolvents`, move `placeholder(...)` into the loop, under `entry != pivot`.

**Regression test.** Vector `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/interp_trace_order_mixed_cong.smt2` (`t1.smt2`), added to the trace-identity runner the project already uses for `trace=true` comparisons (the one FUZZ_K used). Expect an identical `[mk-app]` log against `build/z3` once FUZZ_K-F2's lifetime work lands. Unit test `TestDirectProofMixedCongruenceCreationOrder`: after `makeMixedCongruence` on a fresh manager, `ASTID(placeholder(¬con)) < ASTID(numeral pos)`, with `pos` chosen as a numeral not created earlier, for example 7.

#### interp_01-F12: `makeMixedCongruence` picks the first matching argument position; `make_mixed_congruence` picks the last

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/interp/direct_proof_equality.go:180` → `findCongruencePosition` (`:219-254`, returns at the first match)
- C++: `src/interp/iz3proof_itp.cpp:2497-2504` (`make_mixed_congruence`)

```cpp
int pos = -1;
for(int i = 0; i < nargs; i++)
    if(x == arg(arg(con,0),i) && y == arg(arg(con,1),i))
        pos = i;          // no break: last match wins
```
The vector `make_congruence` uses `find_congruence_position`, which does return the first match, so the Go helper is right there.

**Go behavior.** `makeMixedCongruence` reuses the first-match helper.

**Impact.** For a mixed congruence `(= (g x x) (g y y))` with a single premise `x = y`, the `@cong` position is 1 in z3 and 0 in g3, so `chain_pos_add` rewrites a different argument and the interpolant differs.

<a id="interp-01-f13"></a>
#### interp_01-F13: `Base.simplifyConjunction` re-examines the element swapped in from the back; `simplify_and` skips it

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/interp/base_simplify.go:50-54`
- C++: `src/interp/iz3base.cpp:124-140` (`simplify_and`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
for(unsigned i = 0; i < conjuncts.size(); i++){
    if(is_false(conjuncts[i])) return conjuncts[i];
    if(is_true(conjuncts[i]) || memo.find(conjuncts[i]) != memo.end()){
        std::swap(conjuncts[i],conjuncts.back());
        conjuncts.pop_back();             // then i++: the swapped-in element is never checked
    }
```

**Go behavior.** `continue` without `i++`, so the swapped-in element is checked for `false`, `true`, duplicates and contradictions.

**Impact.** This is on the live path: `InterpolationProof.Interpolate` → `Base.Simplify` (`proof.go:131`, C++ `iz3proof.cpp:565`). For example, `[E, E', ¬E]`, where `E` and `E'` canonicalize to the same equality, gives `(and E ¬E)` in z3 and `false` in g3. `[true, p, true]` gives `(and true p)` versus `(and p)`. The later rewriting by the command usually masks the text, but the ASTs and the trace differ.

**Fix.** Mirror the C++ exactly:
```go
for i := 0; i < len(conjuncts); i++ {
	... if isTrue || seen[...] { conjuncts[i] = conjuncts[len-1]; conjuncts = conjuncts[:len-1]; continue } ...
}
```
That is, keep the loop's `i++` on the swap path.

**Regression test.** Extend `TestInterpolationBaseSimplification` (`base_test.go:70`). `Simplify((and true p true))` must give `(and true p)`: 2 arguments, the first `true`. Also check `[p, p, (not p)]` through `simplifyConjunction` gives `(and p (not p))`, not `false`.

<a id="interp-01-f14"></a>
#### interp_01-F14: `localizeTerm` handles an empty-scope `select` array, and a cache hit, differently from `localize_term`

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: medium
- Go: `pkg/interp/direct_proof_localization.go:119-137` (Select), `:84-86` (cache hit)
- C++: `src/interp/iz3proof_itp.cpp:2813-2819`, `:2788-2791,2843-2844`

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
else if(o == Select){
    prover::range srng = pv->ast_scope(arg(e,0));
    if(!(srng.lo > srng.hi) &&  pv->ranges_intersect(srng,rng)) frng = pv->range_glb(srng,rng);
    else frng = srng;                     // includes the EMPTY case
```
After a cache hit, `e = it->second` still goes through `if(ranges_intersect(ast_scope(e),rng)) return e;` and otherwise gets a new localization variable.

**Go behavior.** `if !arrayScope.IsEmpty() { ... }`: for an empty array scope Go keeps `argumentScope = scope`. A cache hit returns `cached` immediately, with no intersection check.

**Impact.**
- **Select.** A `select` over a mixed array term (for example `(store a i v)` with `a` from A and `v` from B) gets its arguments localized to the empty range in z3 (fresh `%n` variables) and to the full requested range in g3. The interpolants differ on array problems (Ivy).
- **Cache hit.** Unreachable in the binary (two-frame) translation the port now uses. Keep it faithful anyway.

**Fix.** Change the Select branch to `if !arrayScope.IsEmpty() && intersects { glb } else { argumentScope = arrayScope }`. On a cache hit, set `term, proof = cached, maps.proofs[term]` and fall through to the common `RangesIntersect(ASTScope(term), scope)` test and the fresh-variable code. Do not return directly.

**Regression test.** `TestDirectProofLocalizeSelectOverMixedArray` in `direct_proof_test.go` (fixture from `TestDirectProofRecursiveAtomicLocalization`). Localize `(select (store a i v) j)` with `a` A-local and `v` B-local; the index `j` must be replaced by a `%k` localization variable.

```
(interpolants
```

```
(interpolants
```

```cpp
simp_params.set_bool(":sort-sums",true);
```
`params::set_bool(char const*)` stores the key verbatim (`symbol(":som")`, util/params.cpp:946-953). The rewriter looks up `p.get_bool("som", g, false)`, and `GET_VALUE` compares `it->first == k` (params.cpp:827-833). So the colon-prefixed keys never match and `som`/`sort_sums` stay false.

**Go behavior.** `rewrite(term, true)` sets the normalized names `som` and `sort_sums`, and the three call sites above use `ReallySimplify`. Sums are therefore put in sum-of-monomials form and sorted by AST id. The C++ leaves them in rewriter order.

**Impact.** Every interpolant that contains a linear sum can print with its monomials in a different order (and normal forms that depend on `som` can differ too). These are the "FUZZ_K-F2" symptoms. With only this change, all four FUZZ_K-F2 scripts (`diff_interp_ir_30091`, `ir_30390`, `iu_30121`, `hand_get_interpolant_order`) match `build/z3` byte for byte. So the lifetime explanation in FUZZ_K-F2 is not what drives these outputs (lifetimes may still matter for trace logs).

**Reproduction.** `S/work/FUZZ_K/t1/order1.smt2`:
```
(set-option :produce-interpolants true)
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(declare-const z Int)
(assert (! (> x y) :named A))
(assert (! (> y z) :named B))
(assert (! (> z x) :named C))
(check-sat)
(get-interpolant (and A B) C)
```
z3: `(not (<= (+ (* (- 1) z) x) 1))`. g3: `(not (<= (+ x (* (- 1) z)) 1))`. Also `S/work/interp_02/l1.smt2`:
```
(declare-const x Int)
(declare-const y Int)
(declare-const z Int)
(compute-interpolant (interp (and (= (* 2 x) (+ y 1)) (>= y 0))) (and (= y (* 2 z)) (<= z 10)))
```
z3 `(+ (div (+ (- 1) (* (- 1) y)) 2) (div (+ 1 y) 2))`, g3 `(+ (div (+ 1 y) 2) (div (+ (- 1) (* (- 1) y)) 2))`. `S/work/interp_02/g3simp` (with `ReallySimplify` made identical to `Simplify`) matches z3 on all of them. With F1, F2 and F3 applied, `S/work/interp_02/g3fix` matches z3 on all 16 scripts in `fuzzgroups/K` plus `test_vectors/interp*.smt2` (the current g3 differs on 4 of them).

**Fix.** Change the three call sites to `Simplify` (the C++ `z3_simplify`): `FullTranslation.ownedSimplify`, `DirectProofInterpolator.ownedSimplify`, and `DirectProofInterpolator.Interpolate`. Then either delete `ReallySimplify` (it has no live C++ consumer) or make it reproduce the inert C++ keys, i.e. `rewrite(term, false)`. Verified patch: `S/work/interp_02/fix_simplify.patch`.

**Regression test.** Add vector `interp_sum_order_get_interpolant.smt2` (order1 above) with expected `"unsat\n(interpolants\n (not (<= (+ (* (- 1) z) x) 1)))\n"`, and `interp_sum_order_div.smt2` (l1 above) with expected `"unsat\n(interpolants\n (let ((a!1 (+ (div (+ (- 1) (* (- 1) y)) 2) (div (+ 1 y) 2))))\n  (<= 0 a!1))\n (let ((a!1 (+ (div (+ (- 1) (* (- 1) y)) 2) (div (+ 1 y) 2))))\n  (<= 0 a!1)))\n"`. Run the CPP reference test as well. In `pkg/interp/manager_rewrite_test.go`, change `TestInterpolationManagerTheorySimplifiers` so the polynomial `(+ (+ x 1) (+ 2 x))` simplified at the translation call sites equals `Simplify`'s result. Keep the `x+0 -> x` check.

#### interp_02-F4: unsupported proof rule does not print the `IF_VERBOSE(0)` "Unsupported proof rule:" line

- Severity: medium

- C++: `src/interp/iz3translate.cpp:2053-2057`

```cpp

    throw_unsupported(proof);
```
**Go behavior.** `return ast.ASTHandle{}, UnsupportedProofError{Proof: proof}` with no diagnostic.

