<a id="interp-02-f5"></a>
#### interp_02-F5: array theory lemma ignores `expect_clause` when building the axiom literals

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/interp/translation_rules.go:420-437` (`FullTranslation.translateTheoryLemma`, `ArrayTheory`)
- C++: `src/interp/iz3translate.cpp:1741-1746,2000-2006`

**C++ behavior.** `lits` is `get_Z3_lits(con)` when `expect_clause` is true and `{con}` otherwise. The array case uses `lits`:
```cpp
if(get_store_array(con,store_array)) res = iproof->make_axiom(lits,ast_scope(store_array));
else res = iproof->make_axiom(lits);
```
**Go behavior.** `literals, e := t.clauseLiterals(conclusion)` always splits the `or`. `expectClause` is not passed to `translateTheoryLemma`.

**Impact.** When an array theory lemma whose conclusion is an `or` is translated as a term premise (`expect_clause == false`, e.g. an MP or congruence premise), the axiom has per-literal localization instead of one formula. The resulting interpolant can differ.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: no small proof with this shape was found within the time budget.

**Fix.** Pass `expectClause` into `translateTheoryLemma` (or pass the precomputed `t.proofLiterals(conclusion, expectClause)`), and use that slice in both `MakeAxiom` and `MakeAxiomInRange`.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/interp/manager_rewrite_test.go` (following `TestFullTranslationTriangleEqualityTheoryLemma`), build an array `th-lemma` proof with conclusion `(or (= i j) (= (select (store a i v) j) (select a j)))`. Call `translateMain(proof, false, ...)` and check that `MakeAxiomInRange` received one literal, the whole `or`. With `expectClause=true` it should receive two literals.

<a id="interp-02-f6"></a>
#### interp_02-F6: `PR_COMMUTATIVITY` builds `comm_equiv` with a hard-coded `Iff` instead of `op(con)`

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/interp/translation_rules.go:349-362`
- C++: `src/interp/iz3translate.cpp:2036-2040`

**C++ behavior.** `ast comm_equiv = make(op(con),arg(con,0),arg(con,0));`. For a commutativity of a non-Boolean application (`(= (f a b) (f b a))`, OP_EQ) this is `Equal`.

**Go behavior.** `t.base.manager.Make(OperatorIff, left, left)`. For non-Boolean `left` this is ill-sorted (an error, or a different AST).

**Impact.** Proofs with commutative congruence over non-Boolean terms (EUF `cg` over commutative operators) fail or translate differently. Boolean equalities behave the same as in C++.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: z3 rarely emits `commutativity` over non-Boolean apps.

**Fix.** Use `op, e := t.base.manager.Operator(conclusion)` and `Make(op, left, left)`.

**Regression test.** Unit test in `pkg/interp/manager_rewrite_test.go`: build a `PR_COMMUTATIVITY` proof of `(= (+ x y) (+ y x))` over Int, call `translateMain(proof, false, direct, newTranslationMemo())`, and check that the result is commuted and that its second argument is `(= (+ x y) (+ x y))` (Equal, not an error).

<a id="interp-02-f7"></a>
#### interp_02-F7: `localityRecursive` drops the `PR_QUANT_INST` side effect `iproof->make_axiom(lits)`

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: medium
- Go: `pkg/interp/translation_analysis.go:209-249` (`FullTranslation.localityRecursive`)
- C++: `src/interp/iz3translate.cpp:187-192` (`get_locality_rec`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
else if(dk == PR_QUANT_INST){
    std::vector<ast> lits; ast con = conc(proof);
    get_Z3_lits(con, lits);
    iproof->make_axiom(lits);
}
```
The first `get_locality(root)` walks the whole proof DAG. For every `quant-inst` it calls `make_axiom` with the full range. That localizes mixed literals (fresh `%N` variables, entries in `localization_maps_per_range[full]`, assumption/transitivity ASTs) in DFS order, before any rule is translated, including instances under subproofs that are never translated.

**Go behavior.** The `rule != ast.ASTPrQuantInst` branch only skips the premises. Nothing is localized, and `Locality` has no access to the `DirectProofInterpolator`.

**Impact.** Localization variable numbering (`%0`, `%1` ... which appear in printed interpolants, as in F1's output), AST ids, and the full-range localization memo can differ from the C++ when a problem has two or more localization sources. The cases tried here do not show it.

**Reproduction.** Not reproduced (the F1 examples have a single localization variable).

**Fix.** Pass the current `*DirectProofInterpolator` into `Locality`/`localityRecursive` (from `translateMain` and from the F1 call site). In the `PR_QUANT_INST` branch, compute `clauseLiterals(conc)` and call `direct.MakeAxiom(lits)`, discarding the node. Keep the result `INT_MAX`. The `locality` memo persists across frames as in C++, so the side effect happens only in the frame where the node is first visited.

**Regression test.** Add a vector with two independent mixed instantiations (one inside a subproof that becomes a local assumption) and compare `%N` naming against `build/z3` through `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference`. Also add a unit test checking that, after `Locality(root)`, the direct interpolator holds a full-range localization entry for the mixed instance literal.

<a id="interp-02-f8"></a>
#### interp_02-F8: `scanSkolemsRecursive` drops the `ast_scope(arg(conc(proof),1))` call, which freezes memoized scopes in C++

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: medium
- Go: `pkg/interp/translation_analysis.go:111-151`
- C++: `src/interp/iz3translate.cpp:131-145`

**C++ behavior.** After `add_frame_range(frame,arg(conc(proof),1));` it executes `r = ast_scope(arg(conc(proof),1));`. `iz3base::ast_scope` memoizes (`scope_computed`, iz3base.cpp:60-73) and is never invalidated by later `add_frame_range` calls. The scopes of the skolemized formula and all its subterms are therefore fixed at this point of the scan.

**Go behavior.** The call is omitted, so these scopes are computed lazily later, after all skolems have been assigned frames.

**Impact.** When a later skolemization adds frames to symbols that occur in an earlier skolemized formula (for example, the same skolem subterm across A and B), C++ and Go compute different scopes. That changes `is_local`/locality decisions and therefore the interpolant. This only affects quantified (skolemizing) interpolation problems.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted.

**Fix.** After `t.base.addFrameRange(frame, skolem)` succeeds, call `_, err = t.base.ASTScope(skolem)`.

**Regression test.** Unit test in `pkg/interp/translation` tests: build a proof with two `PR_SKOLEMIZE` steps whose second formula shares a subterm with the first, assigned to different frames. After `ScanSkolems`, check that `ASTScope(firstFormula)` equals the range observed right after the first skolemization.

<a id="interp-02-f9"></a>
#### interp_02-F9: AST construction order differs from the GCC build in several translation helpers

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Go / C++ pairs:
  1. `pkg/interp/translation_rules.go:753-813` (`translateAssignBounds`, no-premise case): the Go makes the `n-1` hypotheses inside the argument loop, before `SumInequalities`/`NormalizeInequality`/`DivideInequalities`. `iz3translate.cpp:1125-1153` (`AssignBounds2Farkas`) makes all `make_hypothesis(my_cons[i])` after `farkas_con` is computed, with `mk_not(farkas_con)` last. Mixed hypotheses create ASTs (`iz3proof_itp.cpp:2322-2348`).
  2. `pkg/interp/translation_rules.go:684-699` (`gcdToDivisionRule`): Go runs idiv(t), idiv(c), simplify(t), simplify(c). C++ (`iz3translate.cpp:1071-1072`) runs `t = z3_simplify(mk_idiv(t,d)); c = z3_simplify(mk_idiv(c,d));`.
  3. `pkg/interp/translation_reconstruct.go:556-564` (`translateEqualityPropagation`): Go makes `Leq` and `Geq` first and then reconstructs both. C++ (`iz3translate.cpp:1627-1631`) interleaves make Leq, reconstruct, make Geq, reconstruct.
  4. `pkg/interp/translation_commute.go:68-76` (`commuteEqualityIff`): C++ `make(Iff, commute_equality(arg0), commute_equality(arg1))` evaluates right to left under GCC, so `arg1` is commuted first.
  5. `pkg/interp/translation_commute.go:174-182` (`makeCommutedMonotonicity`) and `pkg/interp/translation_idioms.go:349-357` (iff-false idiom): C++ `make(Iff, make(Not,x), make(Not,y))` builds `(not y)` first and uses raw `make(Not, ...)`. Go builds `x` first and uses `MkNot`, which also folds `true`/`false`/double negation.
  6. `pkg/interp/translation_arithmetic.go:229-241` (`RHSNormalizeInequality`): Go makes `"1"` before `(<= 0 0)`. C++ (`iz3translate.cpp:909-911`) makes `(<= 0 0)` first.

**Impact.** These produce new AST ids in a different order (and in item 5, possibly a different AST). The arithmetic rewriter and the `std::set<ast>` hypothesis order sort by id, so output order and trace logs can diverge, as in FUZZ_K-F2. Not separately reproduced once F2 was fixed.

**Fix.** Reorder each site to match the C++ (for nested calls, GCC's right-to-left argument order):
- (1) Collect `inputs` first, compute `sum`, `normalizedConsequence`, `divisor`, `farkasConclusion` and `negative`, then make the hypotheses for `inputs[0..]` followed by `negative`.
- (2) Run `left=simplify(idiv(left)); right=simplify(idiv(right))`.
- (3) Loop over `i`: make inequality `i`, then reconstruct `i`.
- (4) Commute `right` before `left`.
- (5) Use `Make(OperatorNot, right)` before `Make(OperatorNot, left)`.
- (6) Make `(<= 0 0)` before `"1"`.

**Regression test.** Use trace-order tests in the style of `pkg/interp/profiling_order_test.go`: for each helper, record `GetASTID` of the ASTs created (via `ast` creation hooks or by comparing ids of the returned subterms) and assert the C++ order. Also run `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference` on the `fuzzgroups/K` vectors with `trace=true` and compare the `[mk-app]` order.

<a id="interp-02-f10"></a>
#### interp_02-F10: interpolation profile output lacks the `iz3proof::interpolate` timers and prints times with full precision

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/interp/proof.go:124-136` (`InterpolationProof.Interpolate`), `pkg/interp/profiling.go:64` (`profileSeconds`)
- C++: `src/interp/iz3proof.cpp:461-566`, `src/interp/iz3profiling.cpp:52-54`

**C++ behavior.** `iz3proof::interpolate` wraps `find_B_lits` in `timer_start/stop("Blits")`, the node loop in `"interp_proof"`, and `pv->simplify(bar)` in `"simplifying"`. Times are written with `os << double` (default precision 6, `%g`-like).

**Go behavior.** `Interpolate` starts no timers. `profileSeconds` uses `fmt.Sprintf("%g")`, which prints the shortest exact representation (up to 17 digits).

**Reproduction.** `z3 interp.profile=true q2.smt2` prints under `Proof interpolation` the children `simplifying`, `Blits` and `interp_proof`, with values such as `0.00085327`. `g3 interp.profile=true q2.smt2` has no children there and prints values such as `0.002312848`.

**Fix.** Give `InterpolationProof.Interpolate` access to the `RunConfig` profiler (or the process profiler). Wrap a no-op `"Blits"` phase, the lemma selection as `"interp_proof"`, and `p.base.Simplify` as `"simplifying"`, in that order. Format times with `strconv.FormatFloat(v, 'g', 6, 64)` and strip trailing zeros as iostream does: C++ default `<<` behaves like `%.6g`, so use `fmt.Sprintf("%.6g", ...)`. (The C++ child ordering is by `const char*` address in `std::map` and cannot be reproduced; leave insertion order.)

**Regression test.** Extend `pkg/interp/profiling_order_test.go` with a fake clock (`Profiler.now`). Assert `profileSeconds(1234567*time.Nanosecond) == "0.00123457"`, and that after `ProofInterpolants` the tree under `Proof interpolation` contains `Blits`, `interp_proof`, `simplifying` in that start order.

<a id="interp-02-f11"></a>
#### interp_02-F11: `PrettyPrintProblem` declares symbols through `ast_pp_util` instead of `free_func_visitor` + `mk_smt_pp`, and names duplicate constraints differently

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: medium
- Go: `pkg/interp/pp.go:110-137` (`PrettyPrintProblem`)
- C++: `src/interp/iz3pp.cpp:119-177` (`iz3pp`)

**C++ behavior.** It collects decls/sorts with `for_each_expr(free_func_visitor)` into a `func_decl_set`/`obj_hashtable` and prints them in hash-table iteration order:
- every user sort as `mk_smt_pp(sort)`, i.e. `(declare-sort U)` plus the printer's newline;
- every null-family decl as `mk_smt_pp(f)`, i.e. the legacy `(declare-fun f (U) U)`, followed by `"\n"`.

All names are assigned first (`cnames[cnsts[i]] = "f!"+(i+1)`), and each assert then prints `cnames[r]`. A constraint that appears twice therefore uses its last name in both asserts.

**Go behavior.** It uses `ast.NewASTPPUtil(...).CollectAll/DisplayDeclarations`, which has decl-collector order with dependency ordering and the modern declaration printer. Names are assigned and printed per constraint, so duplicates print `f!1` and then `f!2`.

**Impact.** `Z3_write_interpolation_problem` output differs (declaration order and format; names for duplicate constraints). API only.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted (API-only path). The duplicate-name divergence is clear from reading: for `[p, p]`, C++ prints `:named f!2` twice and Go prints `f!1`, then `f!2`.

**Fix.** Port `free_func_visitor` (all `app` decls, plus sorts with null family id, deduplicated in an obj-hashtable-equivalent order) and print with the legacy printer's `DisplayAST` for sorts and decls (plus `"\n"` after decls). Assign all names before printing the asserts, and print `names[constraint]` (the final value) for each assert.

**Regression test.** Extend `TestInterpolationPrettyPrintDuplicateAndBadTree` (`pkg/interp/pp_test.go:74`) to expect two `(assert (! true :named f!2))` lines. Add a test with a user sort and function checking the exact `(declare-sort U)` / `(declare-fun f (U) U)` text produced by the C++ API (generate the expected text once with `build/z3` through a small C API harness).

### Area: Solver framework, ackermannization, arena, commands

*solver_misc_01.* This shard covers the generic solver layer (`check_sat_result`, `combined_solver`, `solver_na2as`, `solver`, `mus`, `smt_logics`, `tactic2solver`, `solver2tactic`), the ackermannization package (lackr eager and lazy paths, `ackr_info`, the model converter, the bound probe, `ackermannize_bv_tactic`), the engine process glue, and the Go-only `arena` storage package. Most of the port follows the C++ closely: combined-solver scheduling, the MUS loop, the lackr encoding and lazy model check (including source hash-table iteration order) and the model converter all match branch for branch. Findings: 0 critical, 0 high, 1 medium (confirmed by differential run), 2 low. The most visible divergence: `tactic2solver` drops tactic labels, but the Go `TacticSolver` reports them, so `(labels)` differs from z3 on the first check-sat for strategic logics such as AUFLIA.

*solver_misc_02.* This shard is mostly infrastructure: the `arena` storage pools (`SmallBytes` maps to `small_object_allocator`, and `Words`/`Vectors*` are Go-only vector storage), the glibc `rand()` stream (`clibrand`), maintainer tools (`portcheck`, `cmd/portcheck`, `cmd/partial-list`), a test-only SAT oracle, and the `g3` command entry point (`cmd/g3/main.go`, which corresponds to `src/shell/main.cpp::main`). The C++-derived pieces are faithful: - `SmallBytes` matches `small_object_allocator` in its size classes, direct-allocation threshold, chunk-fill test, LIFO free lists and `consolidate` relink order. - `clibrand` was checked against the system glibc `srand`/`rand` for 7 seeds, including 0, 2^31 and 2^32-1. The output is byte-identical. Findings: 0 critical, 0 high, 0 medium, 1 low (confirmed). The one finding is that `cmd/g3/main.go` handles `-h` and `-version` itself, so the ported usage and version printers in `pkg/shell` are never used. Open-file diagnostics for DIMACS, MPS and Datalog also differ, but parsers_shell_01-F12 already records that (see Needs verification).

<a id="solver-misc-01-f1"></a>
#### solver_misc_01-F1: TacticSolver.Labels returns the tactic's labels; C++ tactic2solver::get_labels returns none

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/solver/tactic_solver.go:227` (`TacticSolver.Labels`), fed by `pkg/solver/tactic_solver.go:490` (`CheckSatCore`, `result.SetLabels(labels.Values)`)
- C++: `src/solver/tactic2solver.cpp:69` (`tactic2solver::get_labels`), `src/solver/tactic2solver.cpp:148-150` (`check_sat_core`)

**C++ behavior.** `check_sat_core` gives a local `labels_vec labels` to `::check_sat` and then discards it. Nothing is stored in `m_result`, and the override is empty:
```cpp
void get_labels(svector<symbol> & r) override {}
...
labels_vec labels;
switch (::check_sat(*m_tactic, g, md, labels, pr, core, reason_unknown)) { ... }
```
`simple_check_sat_result::get_labels` is empty too (`check_sat_result.cpp`). Only `check_sat_tactic_result` (the `check-sat-using` path) reports labels.

**Go behavior.**
```go
if err = result.SetLabels(labels.Values); err != nil {   // CheckSatCore
...
func (s *TacticSolver) Labels() ([]usymbol.Symbol, error) {
	...
	return s.result.Labels()
}
```
`SimpleCheckSatResult.Labels` returns whatever was stored, so the smt tactic's relevant labels reach `(labels)`.

**Impact.** Take a non-incremental `check-sat` whose combined solver selects solver 1 (the tactic solver), which is the normal case for a single query under a strategic logic. A `(labels)` command after it prints labels where z3 prints `(labels)`. The same applies to the progress sample that prints labels.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed with the prebuilt binaries:
```smt2
(set-logic AUFLIA)
(declare-fun f (Int) Int)
(declare-const x Int)
(assert (! (> (f x) 2) :lblpos L1))
(check-sat)
(labels)
```
`$S/bin/g3`: `sat` / `(labels L1)`. `build/z3`: `sat` / `(labels)`.

**Fix.** Make `TacticSolver.Labels` match the empty override. After `open()`, return `[]usymbol.Symbol{}` and never consult `s.result`. Also delete the `result.SetLabels(labels.Values)` call at `tactic_solver.go:490-492`. Keep the `labels` local and its `defer labels.Close()`, because `tactic.CheckSat` still needs somewhere to write. Do not change `SimpleCheckSatResult.SetLabels` or `Labels`: `cmd_context/tactic_commands.go:530` (the `check_sat_tactic_result` equivalent), `smtcore/smt_solver.go:778` and `cmd_context/optimization.go:771` rely on them, and those C++ counterparts do report labels.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/solver/tactic_solver_test.go`, add `TestTacticSolverLabelsAlwaysEmpty`. Build the solver the way `TestTacticSolverSATUnknownScopesAndFailureReason` does (`solverTestManager`, `solverTestParams`, `NewTacticSolver`), but with a small test tactic in the style of the existing `errorTactic` wrapper. That tactic should mark the goal decided-sat and install a model converter built with `tactic.NewStoredModelWithLabels(md, []usymbol.Symbol{label})`. Run `CheckSat(nil)` and expect `lbool.True`, then require `Labels()` to return a zero-length slice. Also add the SMT-LIB vector above as `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/tactic_solver_labels.smt2` with the `scriptResults` entry `"tactic_solver_labels.smt2": "sat\n(labels)\n"` in `pkg/cmd/g3/main_test.go`. `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3` checks it against the C++.

<a id="solver-misc-01-f2"></a>
#### solver_misc_01-F2: DefaultGetConsequences drops errors from the non-Boolean consequence branch (`:=` shadowing)

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/solver/solver.go:384-397` (`DefaultGetConsequences`)
- C++: `src/solver/solver.cpp:132-148` (`solver::get_consequences_core`)

**C++ behavior.** In the non-Boolean branch, any exception thrown by `get_unsat_core`, `mk_and`, `mk_implies` or `push_back` propagates. `solver::get_consequences` then records the reason and rethrows, or returns `l_undef` if the manager is canceled.

**Go behavior.**
```go
if e == nil && status == lbool.False {
	core, e := s.UnsatCore()          // new e shadows the outer e
	if e == nil {
		var consequence ast.ASTHandle
		consequence, e = appendConsequence(manager, core, literal)
		if e == nil {
			consequence, e = retainConsequence(s, consequence)
			...
}
e = errors.Join(e, scope.Close(), manager.DelRef(&literalRef))  // outer e: nil
```
Errors from `UnsatCore`, `appendConsequence` and `retainConsequence` go to the inner `e` and are lost. The loop then continues as if the variable were unfixed: no consequence is added, the final result is `l_true`, and no reason-unknown is set.

**Impact.** Only on error paths: budget exhaustion or a manager failure while building the implication. The result is a silently incomplete consequence list where C++ would raise an error. Callers are `TacticSolver.GetConsequences` and any solver using the default algorithm.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: it needs an injected allocation failure (`Budget.FailAfter`) between the check and the implication construction.

**Fix.** Do not redeclare `e`. Write `var core []ast.ASTHandle; core, e = s.UnsatCore()` inside the `if`, so all three errors reach the `errors.Join` at line 397 and return through the existing `"consequence query or cleanup"` path. The Boolean branch (lines 338-358) returns immediately inside its own scope, so it needs no change.

**Regression test.** Extend `pkg/solver/solver_test.go`, following `TestSolverDefaultConsequenceForNonBooleanValue` (the `solverFixture` built over `NewSimpleCheckSatResult`). Add `TestSolverDefaultConsequenceUnsatCoreErrorPropagates` with a fixture variant whose `UnsatCore()` returns a sentinel error on the second check. Call `DefaultGetConsequences` with one non-Boolean variable and require that the returned error wraps the sentinel (`errors.Is`) and the status is `lbool.Undef`.

<a id="solver-misc-01-f3"></a>
#### solver_misc_01-F3: SolverTactic (solver2tactic) carries smt_tactic-only policy: preserved-precision checks, candidate models, a different unknown message and extra parameters

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/solver/solver_tactic.go:479-513` (`SolverTactic.Apply`), `:525-568` (`UpdateParams`, `CollectParamDescrs`)
- C++: `src/solver/solver2tactic.cpp:104-156` (`solver2tactic::operator()`), `:95-102`

**C++ behavior.** `solver2tactic` has no `candidate_models` or `fail_if_inconclusive` parameters and makes no `sat_preserved`/`unsat_preserved` checks. On `l_undef` it throws `tactic_exception(Z3_CANCELED_MSG)` when canceled and otherwise `tactic_exception(local_solver->reason_unknown())`. `collect_param_descrs` only forwards to the solver.

**Go behavior.** On `True` and `False` it throws `"over-approximated goal found to be sat"` or `"under-approximated goal found to be unsat"` when the goal's precision is not preserved. On `Undef` it may install a candidate model. With the default config (`failIfInconclusive() == true`, `CandidateModels == false`) it throws `"smt tactic failed to show goal to be sat/unsat " + reason` instead of `reason`. It also inserts `candidate_models` and `fail_if_inconclusive` into the parameter descriptions. All of this is `smt_tactic.cpp` logic (lines 213-260 there), not `solver2tactic`.

**Impact.** Latent today. The only production constructor is `portfolio.NewFDTactic` (`pkg/tactic/portfolio/fd_tactic.go:30`). The live QF_FD/SAT path uses `NewFDSolverWithOutput` directly, which matches C++, where `mk_special_solver_for_logic` short-circuits `mk_tactic_for_logic`. `NewFDTacticFactory` and `NewLazyFDTactic` are referenced only from tests. If the FD tactic is wired in, unknown results get a different reason-unknown text and parameter validation accepts two extra keys.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: no command-line path reaches `SolverTactic`.

**Fix.** Make `Apply`'s switch match the C++. For `lbool.True`, call `applySAT`. For `lbool.False`, call `applyUNSAT`. For the default case, return `tactic.NewTacticException(messages.Canceled)` when canceled, else `tactic.NewTacticException(reason)`. Remove `applyCandidateModel`, the `CandidateModels`, `FailIfInconclusive` and `InconclusivePolicyConfigured` config fields, and the extra inserts in `CollectParamDescrs`. `UpdateParams` should just do `Append(&t.params, p)` and then `t.solver.UpdateParams(p)`. Keep `Translate` passing `&t.params` (see Needs verification).

**Regression test.** In `pkg/solver/solver_tactic_test.go`, add `TestSolverTacticUnknownUsesSolverReason`. Use a stub `Solver` whose `CheckSat` returns `lbool.Undef` and whose `ReasonUnknown` returns `"incomplete"`; that file already has helpers for the solver stub. Require that `Apply` returns a tactic exception whose message is exactly `"incomplete"`. A second test should require that a `CollectParamDescrs` result contains neither `candidate_models` nor `fail_if_inconclusive`.

<a id="solver-misc-02-f1"></a>
#### solver_misc_02-F1: `runArgumentsWithDiagnostics` prints Go-only `-h` / `-version` text instead of the ported `display_usage` / `display_version`

- Severity: low
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/cmd/g3/main.go:56-63` (`runArgumentsWithDiagnostics`)
- C++: `src/shell/main.cpp:59-104,153-162` (`display_usage`, `display_version`, `parse_cmd_line_args`)

**C++ behavior.** `parse_cmd_line_args` calls `display_usage(); exit(0);` for `-h`/`-?` and `display_version(); exit(0);` for `-version`. These print:
```
Z3 [version 4.7.1 - 64 bit]. (C) Copyright 2006-2016 Microsoft Corp.
Usage: z3 [options] [-file:]file
...
```
and `Z3 version 4.7.1 - 64 bit`.

**Go behavior.** The ported printers already exist. `shell.WriteUsage` (`pkg/shell/usage.go`) and `shell.WriteVersion` (`pkg/shell/version_output.go`) are reached through `CommandLine.WriteTerminalAction` (`pkg/shell/command_line_output.go:25-30`). However, `main.go` checks for these actions first and prints its own text:
```go
if command.Action == shell.CommandHelp {
    _, err = fmt.Fprintln(output, "g3 Go SMT and optimization runner\nUsage: g3 [-smt2|-dimacs|-bpo|-wcnf|-log] <file> | ...")
    return err
}
if command.Action == shell.CommandVersion {
    _, err = fmt.Fprintln(output, "g3 (Go SMT-LIB backend)")
    return err
}
if command.Action != shell.CommandContinue {
    return command.WriteTerminalAction(output)
}
```
The manifest entry for `src/shell/main.cpp` lists "Full source help/version output" as still open, but nothing next to the code documents this as intentional. The ported printers are dead code from the shell.

**Impact.** Anyone running `g3 -h`, `g3 -?` or `g3 -version` gets different output from z3. Scripts that parse `-version` for "4.7.1" fail with g3. The exit status (0) matches.

**Reproduction.** Both binaries were run with no input file:
```
$ build/z3 -version          -> Z3 version 4.7.1 - 64 bit
$ bin/g3   -version          -> g3 (Go SMT-LIB backend)
$ build/z3 -h | head -2      -> Z3 [version 4.7.1 - 64 bit]. (C) Copyright 2006-2016 Microsoft Corp.
                                Usage: z3 [options] [-file:]file
$ bin/g3   -h | head -2      -> g3 Go SMT and optimization runner
                                Usage: g3 [-smt2|-dimacs|-bpo|-wcnf|-log] <file> | g3 [...] -in
```

**Fix.** In `pkg/cmd/g3/main.go`, delete the two `if command.Action == shell.CommandHelp {...}` and `if command.Action == shell.CommandVersion {...}` blocks. The following `if command.Action != shell.CommandContinue { return command.WriteTerminalAction(output) }` then sends both actions to `WriteUsage` and `WriteVersion`. If the owner wants a g3-specific banner, add it as a clearly separate flag rather than replacing the source text.

**Regression test.** Add `TestHelpAndVersionMatchSource` in a new file `pkg/cmd/g3/help_version_test.go`. Build it the way `dimacs_frontend_unsat_test.go` does: `var out bytes.Buffer; err := runArguments([]string{"-version"}, strings.NewReader(""), &out)`. Expect a nil error and `out.String() == "Z3 version 4.7.1 - 64 bit\n"`. Then run `runArguments([]string{"-h"}, ...)` and expect output that starts with `"Z3 [version 4.7.1 - 64 bit]. (C) Copyright 2006-2016 Microsoft Corp.\nUsage: z3 [options] [-file:]file\n"`. Both expectations assume a 64-bit build. To compare the whole text, generate it from `build/z3 -h` into `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/z3_help_output.txt` and compare byte for byte.

### Area: API (`pkg/api`)

*api_01.* This shard is the first slice of `pkg/api`: the Go counterpart of the Z3 C API in `src/api/api_algebraic.cpp`, `api_arith.cpp`, `api_ast.cpp`, `api_ast_map.cpp`, `api_ast_vector.cpp`, `api_bv.cpp`, `api_config_params.cpp`, `api_context.cpp`, `api_datalog.cpp`, `api_datatype.cpp`, `api_fpa.cpp` and `api_goal.cpp`, plus several Go-only conveniences (arrays, fixedpoint facade, datalog run/profile). Most files are thin, faithful wrappers. The enumeration tables in `Z3_get_decl_kind` were checked against the C++ enums and match, including the C++ quirk that maps `OP_BSREM0` to `Z3_OP_BUREM0`. Eight findings: 2 high, 2 medium, 4 low. Four were confirmed by running `build/libz3.so` from a small C harness alongside a Go test injected with `go test -overlay`, which wrote nothing into the repository. The serious ones: - `Substitute` uses the wrong C++ replacer and captures bound variables. - Datatype testers come back as the named `OP_DT_RECOGNISER` declaration, where the C API returns the `OP_DT_IS` declaration. - `ASTVector` and `ASTMap` `String` print function declarations and line breaks differently from the C++. - `Simplify` goes through the `simplify` *command* path instead of the API path.

*api_02.* This shard is the second half of `pkg/api`: interpolation context and file I/O, models, numerals, optimize, params, parsers, polynomial, probes, PB, QE, quantifiers, RCF, sequences, the simple/strategic solver objects, statistics, tactics, trace/version, plus thin Go-only wrappers over the MPS/OPB/WCNF shell frontends. Most files are faithful thin wrappers over ported cores. I found 9 divergences from the C++ API. Every one except F9 was reproduced against `build/libz3.so` with small C programs, and against the Go package with a scratch module (inputs and outputs are given inline). Counts: high 2, medium 4, low 3.

*api_03.* This shard is the Z3 log machinery: the `z3_replayer` scanner/interpreter, the `z3_log_frontend` driver, the logger (`z3_logger.h`/`api_log.cpp`), and about 50 "generated" command files that rebuild `api_commands.cpp` (661 commands) as Go handlers keyed by replay object IDs. The command table is right: all 661 IDs/names match `register_z3_replayer_cmds` exactly (checked by script), and the argument positions/kinds I compared against the `exec_*` functions match. The main divergence is error behaviour. The C++ replayer installs `Z3_replayer_error_handler` on every context and catches every `z3_exception` thrown by a command; the Go replayer does neither, so a log that makes any API call fail is aborted (or the failure is silent) where z3 prints a line and keeps going. Several other confirmed output differences follow from Go-only argument checks. Counts: high 1, medium 5, low 4 (7 confirmed with `build/z3` vs `bin/g3`).

<a id="api-01-f1"></a>
#### api_01-F1: `SMTContext.Substitute` uses `default_expr_replacer` instead of `expr_safe_replace` (bound variables captured, not shifted)

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/api/api_ast_substitution.go:184-215` (`SMTContext.Substitute`)
- C++: `src/api/api_ast.cpp:768-799` (`Z3_substitute`), `src/ast/rewriter/expr_safe_replace.cpp:40-120`

**C++ behavior.** `Z3_substitute` uses `expr_safe_replace`. At a quantifier, it shifts every source and destination by the number of bound variables before replacing inside the body, so a free `(:var 0)` in `from` does not match the binder's own `(:var 0)`. It also walks children through an explicit stack, last argument first.
```cpp
expr_safe_replace subst(m);
for (unsigned i = 0; i < num_exprs; i++) subst.insert(from[i], to[i]);
expr_ref new_a(m);
subst(a, new_a);
...
// expr_safe_replace::operator() quantifier case:
for (unsigned i = 0; i < m_src.size(); ++i) {
    shift(m_src[i].get(), num_decls, src);
    shift(m_dst[i].get(), num_decls, dst);
    replace.insert(src, dst);
}
```

**Go behavior.** Go builds an `expr_substitution` and runs `rewriter.NewDefaultExprReplacer`, which is a port of `default_expr_replacer` (`rewriter_tpl` with `get_subst`). That replacer calls `get_subst` on every subterm under binders and never shifts.
```go
substitution, err := m.NewExprSubstitution()
replacer, err := rewriter.NewDefaultExprReplacer(m)
... m.ExprSubstitutionInsert(substitution, from[i], to[i], ...)
replacer.SetSubstitution(&substitution)
replacer.Rewrite(term, result)
```

**Impact.** Any API user who substitutes a term that contains de Bruijn variables, or whose replacement contains them, gets a different and semantically wrong result when the term has quantifiers: the bound variable is captured. For ground `from`/`to` the two results agree logically. Even then, the C++ walks arguments in a different order (stack, last child first), so AST creation order and IDs differ.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed. C harness against `build/libz3.so`:
```c
Z3_sort i = Z3_mk_int_sort(c);
Z3_ast v0 = Z3_mk_bound(c,0,i);
Z3_ast body = Z3_mk_gt(c, v0, Z3_mk_int(c,0,i));
Z3_symbol x = Z3_mk_string_symbol(c,"x");
Z3_ast q = Z3_mk_forall(c,0,0,0,1,&i,&x,body);
Z3_ast d = Z3_mk_const(c,Z3_mk_string_symbol(c,"d"),i);
Z3_ast r = Z3_substitute(c,q,1,&v0,&d);   // prints (forall ((x Int)) (> x 0))
```
The same input through Go (`f.c.BoundVariable(0,int)`, `ArithmeticGT`, `Forall`, `Substitute(q, {v0}, {d})`) prints `(forall ((x Int)) (> d 0))`.

**Fix.** In `Substitute`, replace the substitution/replacer block with the existing port `rewriter.NewExprSafeReplace(m)` (`pkg/ast/rewriter/expr_safe_replace.go`): call `Insert(from[i], to[i])` for each pair in order, run it once on `term` to fill the result ref, then close it. Keep the sort check loop, which matches the C++ `Z3_SORT_ERROR` pre-check. `SubstituteVariables` (`var_subst(m,false)`) is correct and needs no change.

**Regression test.** Extend `pkg/api/api_ast_substitution_test.go` with `TestSubstituteDoesNotCaptureBoundVariable`. Use `newSMTAPIFixture(t, "ALL", nil)`, `f.pin`, `f.c.IntegerSort`, `f.c.BoundVariable(0, intSort)`, `f.c.Numeral("0", intSort)`, `f.c.ArithmeticGT`, `f.c.Forall([]ast.ASTHandle{intSort}, []string{"x"}, body)` and `f.c.Constant("d", intSort)`. Call `Substitute(q, {v0}, {d})`, read the result with `f.m.RefGet` and check that `ASTString(..., APIASTPrintSMT2)` equals `(forall ((x Int)) (> x 0))`. Optionally also check that the result handle equals `q`; this holds if `update_quantifier` on an unchanged body hash-conses back to `q`, which I did not verify. Add a second case with a ground substitution under several arguments to check that the result matches the C++ text.

<a id="api-01-f2"></a>
#### api_01-F2: datatype testers returned as `OP_DT_RECOGNISER` ("is_c") where the C API returns `get_constructor_is` (`OP_DT_IS`, "is")

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/api/api_datatype_queries.go:66-76` (`DatatypeRecognizer`). It is used by `pkg/api/api_datatype_enumeration.go:123` (`EnumerationSortWithSymbol`) and `pkg/api/api_datatype_list.go:180,188` (`ListSortWithSymbol`). The same call appears in `pkg/api/api_datatype_constructor_query.go:32` (`QueryFields`).
- C++: `src/api/api_datatype.cpp:140-145` (`Z3_mk_enumeration_sort`), `:189-200` (`Z3_mk_list_sort`), `:289-293` (`Z3_query_constructor`), `:510-530` (`Z3_get_datatype_sort_recognizer`); `src/ast/datatype_decl_plugin.cpp:796-801`

**C++ behavior.** Every public tester path calls `datatype_util::get_constructor_is`. That builds the generic `OP_DT_IS` declaration, named `is` and parameterized by the constructor:
```cpp
decl = dt_util.get_constructor_is(decl);          // Z3_get_datatype_sort_recognizer
...
func_decl * util::get_constructor_is(func_decl * con) {
    parameter ps[1] = { parameter(con)};
    return m.mk_func_decl(m_family_id, OP_DT_IS, 1, ps, 1, &datatype);
}
```

**Go behavior.** `DatatypeRecognizer` calls `m.DatatypeConstructorRecognizer(constructor)`. That is the port of `get_constructor_recognizer`, which builds `OP_DT_RECOGNISER` named `is_<ctor>`. The correct port, `ASTManager.DatatypeConstructorIs`, exists in `pkg/ast/ast_datatype_definition.go:597` but these paths do not use it.
```go
return m.DatatypeConstructorRecognizer(constructor)
```

**Impact.** The C API returns a different `func_decl` than the C++ does. Its name is `is_red` instead of `is`, `Z3_get_decl_kind` gives `Z3_OP_DT_RECOGNISER` instead of `Z3_OP_DT_IS`, and printed terms differ. The two declarations are distinct ASTs, so terms built with them are not hash-consed with terms the C++ path would build.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed. C harness: `Z3_mk_enumeration_sort(c, "Color", 2, {red, green}, consts, testers)`.
- C++: tester name `is`, kind `2050` (`Z3_OP_DT_IS`); `Z3_get_datatype_sort_recognizer(s,1)` is also named `is`, kind 2050. `Z3_ast_to_string` of the tester applied to `x` printed `is`.
- Go: `EnumerationSort("Color", {"red","green"})` gives `Recognizers[0]` named `is_red`, with `PublicDeclarationKind` = `APIDeclarationDatatypeRecognizer`; the application prints `(is_red x)`.

**Fix.** Change `DatatypeRecognizer` to `return m.DatatypeConstructorIs(constructor)`. Make the same change in `APIDatatypeConstructorObject.QueryFields` (line 32). `EnumerationSortWithSymbol` and `ListSortWithSymbol` call `DatatypeRecognizer` and are fixed with it. If a public accessor for the named recognizer is still wanted, add it under a separate name.

**Regression test.** Extend `pkg/api/api_datatype_enumeration_test.go` with `TestEnumerationTesterIsGenericIsDecl`. Using `newSMTAPIFixture(t,"ALL",nil)`, call `EnumerationSort("Color", []string{"red","green"})`. Expect `DeclarationName(e.Recognizers[0]) == "is"` and `PublicDeclarationKind(e.Recognizers[0]) == APIDeclarationDatatypeIs`. Also check that `DatatypeRecognizer(e.Sort, 1)` returns the same kind. Add the matching check for `ListSort` (`IsNil`/`IsCons`) in `api_datatype_list_test.go` and for `QueryFields().Recognizer` in `api_datatype_constructor_query_test.go`.

<a id="api-01-f3"></a>
#### api_01-F3: `ASTVector.String` / `ASTMap.String` print function declarations as their bare name and drop the `mk_ismt2_pp` indent (2 / 3)

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/api/api_ast_vector_object.go:177-214` (`apiASTVectorObject.string`, `writeAPIAST`), `pkg/api/api_ast_map_object.go:187-211` (`apiASTMapObject.string`), `pkg/api/api_ast_map_display.go:15-57` (`writePublicASTMapNode`, `ASTMap.String`)
- C++: `src/api/api_ast_vector.cpp:118-130` (`Z3_ast_vector_to_string`), `src/api/api_ast_map.cpp:139-157` (`Z3_ast_map_to_string`), `src/ast/ast_smt2_pp.cpp:1165-1245`

**C++ behavior.** Both functions print each element with `mk_ismt2_pp`. That prints a `func_decl` in full as `(declare-fun f (Int) Bool)`, and the `indent` argument (2 for vectors, 3 for maps) wraps the format in `mk_indent`, which shifts every continuation line:
```cpp
buffer << "\n  " << mk_ismt2_pp(to_ast_vector_ref(v).get(i), mk_c(c)->m(), 2);
...
buffer << "\n  (" << mk_ismt2_pp(it->m_key, mng, 3) << "\n   " << mk_ismt2_pp(it->m_value, mng, 3) << ")";
```

**Go behavior.** Go routes through `SimpleASTPrinterContext` with indent `0`. For a `func_decl`, `DisplayFuncDecl` is the `simple_ast_printer_context` overload, which prints only the name.
```go
if x := writeAPIAST(printer, &out, h, 0); x != nil {     // vector
...
case ast.ASTFuncDecl:
    return printer.DisplayFuncDecl(out, h, indent)        // prints just "f"
```

**Impact.** The string form of any AST vector or map that holds a function declaration differs from the C++, and so does any element long enough to break across lines.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed. A vector holding `f : Int -> Bool` and `(and a_rather_long_constant_name_0 ... _7)`, plus a map `{f -> that and}`:
```
C++ (build/libz3.so):
(ast-vector
  (declare-fun f (Int) Bool)
  (and a_rather_long_constant_name_0
       a_rather_long_constant_name_1
...
(ast-map
  ((declare-fun f (Int) Bool)
   (and a_rather_long_constant_name_0
        a_rather_long_constant_name_1
Go:
(ast-vector
  f
  (and a_rather_long_constant_name_0
     a_rather_long_constant_name_1
...
(ast-map
  (f
   (and a_rather_long_constant_name_0
     a_rather_long_constant_name_1
```

**Fix.** Replace `writeAPIAST` and `writePublicASTMapNode` with a helper that implements `mk_ismt2_pp(ast, m, indent)` for all three kinds. Use `SMT2PPExprTreeWithParams` / `SMT2PPSort` / `SMT2PPDeclareFun`, then `FormatIndent(indent, ...)` when `indent > 0`, then `PrintFormat`; this is the same sequence as `APIASTPrinter.smt2StringIndented` in mode `APIASTPrintSMT2`, so reuse that function. Keep `"null"` for a null element. Call it with indent `2` in `apiASTVectorObject.string`, and with indent `3` for key and value in `apiASTMapObject.string` and `ASTMap.String`.

**Regression test.** Strengthen `pkg/api/api_ast_vector_display_test.go` (`TestASTVectorStringUsesSourceEnvelopeAndKinds`) and `pkg/api/api_ast_map_display_test.go` (`TestPublicASTMapDisplay`) to compare full strings. Build the vector with `NewASTVectorValues(fd, big)`, where `fd = Function("f", {IntegerSort}, BoolSort)` and `big = And(8 constants named a_rather_long_constant_name_0..7)`. Expect exactly the C++ text quoted above. For the map, `Insert(fd, big)` must produce the C++ map text above.

<a id="api-01-f4"></a>
#### api_01-F4: `SMTContext.Simplify` runs the `simplify` *command* path, not the `Z3_simplify` API path (wrong timeout default, extra rlimit, attached th_solver)

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/api/api_ast_simplify_interrupt.go:80-96` (`simplifyWithAPIInterrupt`) → `pkg/cmd_context/simplify.go:111-190` (`Context.simplifyWithDetails`)
- C++: `src/api/api_ast.cpp:671-697` (static `simplify`), compared with `src/cmd_context/simplify_cmd.cpp:94-105`

**C++ behavior.** The API takes its default timeout from the context (`context_params::m_timeout`). It builds a bare `th_rewriter` with no solver attached and applies no rlimit scope.
```cpp
unsigned timeout     = p.get_uint("timeout", mk_c(c)->get_timeout());
bool     use_ctrl_c  = p.get_bool("ctrl_c", false);
th_rewriter m_rw(m, p);
cancel_eh<reslimit> eh(m.limit());
api::context::set_interruptable si(*(mk_c(c)), eh);
{ scoped_ctrl_c ctrlc(eh, false, use_ctrl_c); scoped_timer timer(timeout, &eh); m_rw(a, result); }
```

**Go behavior.** `c.command.Simplify` is the port of `simplify_cmd`. It defaults the timeout to `UINT_MAX` and ignores the context timeout. It pushes `rlimit` from the params, and it attaches `simplifyExpressionSolver` (the command's `th_solver`) to the theory rewriter.
```go
timeout, err := c.config.Params.GetUIntName(local, &timeoutName, math.MaxUint32)
rlimit, err := c.config.Params.GetUIntName(local, &rlimitName, math.MaxUint32)
m.ResourceLimit().Push(rlimit)
checker := &simplifyExpressionSolver{context: c}
value.SetSolver(checker)
```

**Impact.**
- A context timeout set with `UpdateParamValue("timeout", ...)` (or `Config` "timeout") does not bound `Simplify`.
- `SimplifyWithParameters` with `rlimit` is enforced in Go but ignored by `Z3_simplify_ex`.
- With a solver attached, `seq_rewriter`'s regex-to-automaton path (`re2aut::set_solver`) can simplify differently from the C API, which has no solver.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: the first two effects depend on timing or resource counts. The code paths are unambiguous.

**Fix.** Do not call `c.command.Simplify` from `simplifyWithAPIInterrupt`. Build `rewriter.NewTheoryRewriter(m, params, globals, parameters)` directly, with no `SetSolver`. Take `timeout` from the params with default `c.contextTimeout()`. Read `ctrl_c` only for parity (no-op). Wrap the rewrite in a `control.NewScopedTimer(timeout, handler)` with the existing `smtContextCancelHandler`, and do not push `rlimit`. Return rewriter errors as errors, matching `handle_exception` returning null.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/api/api_ast_simplify_interrupt_params_test.go`, add `TestSimplifyIgnoresRLimitParam`. Using `newSMTAPIFixture(t,"ALL",nil)`, `NewParameterSet` and `SetUInt("rlimit", 1)`, simplify a term large enough to need more than one rewriter step, such as a nested sum of 50 numerals. The C API returns the fully folded value, so `SimplifyWithParameters` must succeed with that value. Add a unit test in the same file that checks `contextTimeout()` is the value used when the params carry no `timeout`, for example by checking that the timer constructor receives it through a small seam.

<a id="api-01-f5"></a>
#### api_01-F5: `DeclarationName` / `SortName` / `DeclarationSymbolParameter` render numerical and null symbols as `k!N` / `null`

- Severity: low
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/api/api_ast_inspection.go:124-135` (`DeclarationName`, `SortName`), `pkg/api/api_ast_declaration_parameters.go:109-124` (`DeclarationSymbolParameter`)
- C++: `src/api/api_ast.cpp:291-304` (`Z3_get_symbol_string`), `:377-381` (`Z3_get_decl_name`), `:549-555` (`Z3_get_sort_name`)

**C++ behavior.** The name is a `Z3_symbol`; the C-API way to get text is `Z3_get_symbol_string`. That prints a numerical symbol as its decimal number (`7`) and a string symbol as `bare_str()`, so a null symbol comes back as `""`.

**Go behavior.** Go returns `m.Symbols.Display(name)`, which is `symbol::operator<<`: `k!7` for a numerical symbol and `null` for a null one. `SMTContext.SymbolString` in `api_ast_construction.go` implements the C++ rule correctly but is not used here.

**Impact.** API callers reading names of numerically named declarations or sorts get `k!7` instead of `7`.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed. A declaration made with `Z3_mk_int_symbol(c,7)` gives `"7"` from C++ `Z3_get_symbol_string(Z3_get_decl_name(...))`. Go `DeclarationName(FunctionWithSymbol(usymbol.Numerical(7), nil, Bool))` gives `"k!7"`.

**Fix.** In `DeclarationName` and `DeclarationSymbolParameter`, call `c.SymbolString(name)` instead of `m.Symbols.Display(name)`.

**Regression test.** Add `TestDeclarationNameNumericalSymbol` to `pkg/api/api_ast_inspection_test.go` (or a new `api_ast_symbol_names_test.go`). With `newSMTAPIFixture`, `FunctionWithSymbol(usymbol.Numerical(7), nil, BoolSort)` must give `DeclarationName == "7"`, and `UninterpretedSortWithSymbol(usymbol.Symbol{})` must give `SortName == ""`.

<a id="api-01-f6"></a>
#### api_01-F6: `BenchmarkSMT2` treats empty strings as absent symbols

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/api/api_ast_benchmark.go:19-24` (`apiBenchmarkSymbol`)
- C++: `src/api/api_ast.cpp:853-878` (`Z3_benchmark_to_smtlib_string`), `src/ast/ast_smt_pp.h:66-68`, `src/ast/ast_smt_pp.cpp:936-944`

**C++ behavior.** `set_benchmark_name("")` and `set_status("")` store `symbol("")`, which is not null. `display_smt2` therefore prints `"; \n"` for an empty name and `(set-info :status )` for an empty status. Only a NULL pointer leaves the default: no name line, and status `unknown`.

**Go behavior.** `apiBenchmarkSymbol("")` returns the null symbol. An empty `Name` therefore prints nothing, and an empty `Status` prints `unknown`.

**Impact.** Benchmark text differs whenever a caller passes empty name or status strings, which is common in bindings.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: the difference follows directly from the two code paths above.

**Fix.** Intern `""` as a real symbol for `Name` and `Status`; logic, source and category are already filtered by the `!= symbol("")` test in the printer. To keep a way to express NULL, add pointer fields or a `HasName`/`HasStatus` pair to `APIBenchmarkConfig`.

**Regression test.** Add `TestBenchmarkSMT2EmptyNameAndStatus` to `pkg/api/api_ast_benchmark_test.go`. With `newSMTAPIFixture`, call `BenchmarkSMT2(Bool(true), APIBenchmarkConfig{Name: "", Status: ""})` and expect the output to begin `"; \n(set-info :status )\n"`.

<a id="api-01-f7"></a>
#### api_01-F7: AST construction order differs in `BitVectorToInt(signed)` and `BitVectorSDivNoOverflow`

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/api/api_bitvectors.go:215-249` (`BitVectorToInt`), `pkg/api/api_bitvector_overflow.go:246-276` (`BitVectorSDivNoOverflow`)
- C++: `src/api/api_bv.cpp:115-150` (`Z3_mk_bv2int`), `:325-347` (`Z3_mk_bvsdiv_no_overflow`)

**C++ behavior.** `Z3_mk_bv2int(signed)` builds `r = bv2int(n)`, then the Int numeral `2^sz`, then the BV zero, then `bvslt(n, 0)`, then `(- r bound)`, then `ite`. `Z3_mk_bvsdiv_no_overflow` builds `min`, then `(= t1 min)`, then the `-1` numeral, then `(= t2 -1)`, then `and`, then `not`.

**Go behavior.** `BitVectorToInt` builds the zero and the `bvslt` before the `2^sz` numeral. `BitVectorSDivNoOverflow` builds the `-1` numeral before `(= a min)`.

**Impact.** The node graphs are the same, but AST IDs are assigned in a different order. That can change later hash-table, cache and trace order in the solver (trace-identity requirement).

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: the order difference is in AST IDs, which neither binary prints for this input.

**Fix.** Reorder the Go statements to the C++ sequence:
- `BitVectorToInt`: create `limit` (`ArithmeticIntegerNumeralText(2^bits)`) right after `unsigned`/`bits`, then `zero`, then `negative`, then `adjusted`, then `ite`.
- `BitVectorSDivNoOverflow`: create `x := MkEq(a, min)` before `minusOne`.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/api/api_bitvector_overflow_test.go`, add `TestBVSDivNoOverflowConstructionOrder`. Record `ASTID` of the `-1` numeral and of `(= a min)` after the call (look them up with `BitVectorValue(-1, sort)` and `Equal(a, min)`, which return the hash-consed nodes) and assert the equality's ID is smaller. Add the analogous check for `BitVectorToInt(a, true)`: the ID of the `2^sz` Int numeral must be smaller than the ID of `bvslt(a, 0)`.

<a id="api-01-f8"></a>
#### api_01-F8: `APIGoal.Translate` rejects same-context translation; `APIGoal.DIMACS` has no 4.7.1 counterpart

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/api/api_goal_translation.go:21-23` (`APIGoal.Translate`), `pkg/api/api_goal_dimacs.go:12-28` (`APIGoal.DIMACS`)
- C++: `src/api/api_goal.cpp:154-165` (`Z3_goal_translate`); `src/api/api_goal.cpp` has 181 lines and no `Z3_goal_to_dimacs_string`

**C++ behavior.** `Z3_goal_translate` has no `c == target` check; translating into the same context succeeds and returns a copy of the goal. 4.7.1 has no DIMACS export for goals.

**Go behavior.** `Translate` returns `ErrASTDomain` when `target` is the same context. `DIMACS` is a Go-only public API whose `// Source:` header cites `api_goal.cpp:198-214`, which does not exist.

**Impact.** A same-context goal translation fails in Go where the C++ succeeds. `DIMACS` is new surface with no C++ behavior to compare against.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: the missing check and the missing C++ function are visible in the sources cited above.

**Fix.**
- `Translate`: drop the same-context rejection, matching `Z3_goal_translate` (the `ast_translation` of a manager onto itself is the identity copy).
- `DIMACS`: either remove it, or mark it as a documented Go extension and fix its `// Source:` header.

**Regression test.** Add `TestGoalTranslateSameContext` to `pkg/api/api_goal_translation_test.go`. Use `NewGoal(false,false,false)`, `Assert(Constant("p", Bool))` and then `Translate(f.c)`; it must succeed, and `String()` of the copy must equal the original's.

<a id="api-02-f1"></a>
#### api_02-F1: `SMTContext.Numeral` accepts any text; `Z3_mk_numeral` rejects characters outside its numeral alphabet

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/api/api_numerals.go:14-92` (`SMTContext.Numeral`)
- C++: `src/api/api_numeral.cpp:50-91` (`Z3_mk_numeral`)

**C++ behavior.** The character filter runs for every sort before anything else is built:
```
while (*m) {
    if (!(('0' <= *m && *m <= '9') || ('/' == *m) || ('-' == *m) ||
          (' ' == *m) || ('\n' == *m) || ('.' == *m) || ('e' == *m) || ('E' == *m) ||
          (is_float && (('p' == *m) || ('P' == *m) || ('+' == *m))))) {
        SET_ERROR_CODE(Z3_PARSER_ERROR);
        RETURN_Z3(nullptr);
    }
    ++m;
}
```
**Go behavior.** The filter exists only inside the floating-point branch, and there it also accepts `+`, `p` and `P`. For Int, Real, BitVec and finite-domain sorts the text goes straight to `RationalManager.SetString`, which silently skips any non-digit (a port of `mpq_manager::set`, which assumes its input has already been filtered).

**Impact.** Any API caller that passes bad numeral text gets a numeral of some made-up value instead of an error: `"abc"`→0, `"+5"`→5, `"0x10"`→10, `"1_000"`→1000. It also affects the `IntNumeral`/`UintNumeral` wrappers and any frontend that relies on the API to validate input.

**Reproduction.** Go scratch program (`c.Numeral(s, IntegerSort)` then `NumeralString`): `Numeral("abc") -> 0`, `Numeral("+5") -> 5`, `Numeral("0x10") -> 10`, `Numeral("1_000") -> 1000`. C program against `build/libz3.so`: `Z3_mk_numeral(c, s, Int)` returns NULL with error code 4 (`Z3_PARSER_ERROR`) for all four strings.

**Fix.** At the top of `Numeral`, before the BitVec branch, compute whether the sort is a float (`fpautil().is_float`: FPA family *and* float kind, not rounding mode). Then reject any byte outside `0-9 / - space \n . e E`, plus `p P +` only when the sort is a float. Return a dedicated `errAPINumeralParse` (the analogue of `Z3_PARSER_ERROR`). Drop the duplicate loop in the FP branch. Keep the order of C++: sort check first, then the character filter.

**Regression test.** Add `TestAPINumeralRejectsNonNumeralText` to `pkg/api/api_numerals_test.go`, using `newSMTAPIFixture(t, "ALL", nil)` and `f.pin(f.c.IntegerSort())` / `f.c.BitVectorSort(8)`. For each of `"abc"`, `"+5"`, `"0x10"`, `"1_000"` on Int and on BV8, expect a non-nil error. Also check that `"1/2"` on Real and `"-7"` on Int still succeed.

<a id="api-02-f2"></a>
#### api_02-F2: `Optimize.ParseFile` ignores the `.opb` / `.wcnf` extension and always parses SMT-LIB

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/api/api_optimize_parse.go:28-35` (`APIOptimize.ParseFile`)
- C++: `src/api/api_opt.cpp:285-345` (`Z3_optimize_from_stream`, `Z3_optimize_from_file`)

**C++ behavior.**
```
if (ext && std::string("opb") == ext) { unsigned_vector h; parse_opb(*to_optimize_ptr(opt), s, h); return; }
if (ext && std::string("wcnf") == ext) { unsigned_vector h; parse_wcnf(*to_optimize_ptr(opt), s, h); return; }
...
Z3_optimize_from_stream(c, d, is, get_extension(s));
```
**Go behavior.** `ParseFile` opens the file and always calls `o.Parse`, which is `smt2.ParseAssertions`.

**Impact.** Loading an OPB or WCNF file into an optimize object fails with an SMT-LIB parse error where z3 loads the constraints and objectives.

**Reproduction.** File `t.opb` = `min: 1 x1 +2 x2;\n1 x1 +1 x2 >= 1;\n`. With C++, `Z3_optimize_from_file` gives `assertions=1 objectives=1 check=1`. With Go, `o.ParseFile("t.opb")` gives `err: line 1 column 1: unexpected input, expected token`, 0 assertions and 0 objectives.

**Fix.** In `ParseFile`, compute the extension the way `get_extension` does (the text after the last `.`). For `opb`, parse with the retained OPB parser (`opt.ParseOPB`/the document type behind `cmd_context.Context.LoadOPB`) and load it into `o.command`. Do the same for `wcnf` (`LoadWCNF`). Note that `LoadOPB` has its own known deviations (FUZZ_J-F4, cmd_context_01-F16). Leave `Parse`/`ParseString` as SMT-LIB only, since C++ passes `ext=nullptr` for those.

**Regression test.** Add `TestAPIOptimizeParseFileDispatchesOPBAndWCNF` to `pkg/api/api_optimize_parse_test.go`. Write `min: 1 x1 +2 x2; 1 x1 +1 x2 >= 1;` to `t.TempDir()/p.opb` and `p wcnf 1 1 5\n5 1 0\n` to `w.wcnf`, use the fixture helpers in `api_optimize_test_helpers_test.go`, and expect `NumObjectives()==1`, `len(Assertions())==1` and `Check()==lbool.True` for the OPB file. For the WCNF file, expect one soft objective.

<a id="api-02-f3"></a>
#### api_02-F3: `Optimize.Parse` parses into the optimizer's own command context, so declarations persist across calls and `push`/`pop` in the text change the optimizer's scopes

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/api/api_optimize_parse.go:14-21` (`APIOptimize.Parse`)
- C++: `src/api/api_opt.cpp:300-325` (`Z3_optimize_from_stream`)

**C++ behavior.** Every call uses a fresh, temporary `cmd_context` (with `install_opt_cmds` and `set_ignore_check(true)`). Only the assertions left at the end of the stream are added with `add_hard_constraint`; soft constraints and objectives go to the opt context through the installed commands.
```
scoped_ptr<cmd_context> ctx = alloc(cmd_context, false, &m);
install_opt_cmds(*ctx.get(), to_optimize_ptr(opt));
...
for (; it != end; ++it) to_optimize_ptr(opt)->add_hard_constraint(*it);
```
**Go behavior.** `smt2.ParseAssertions(o.command, input)` runs the commands directly against the optimize object's persistent `cmd_context.Context`. Declarations stay registered and a `(push)` in the text pushes the optimizer itself.

**Impact.** Calling `ParseString` twice with the same `declare-const` fails in Go (z3 accepts it, because both temporary contexts share the AST manager). The Go call reports an error, yet the assertion after the failed declaration is still added. Scope commands in a parsed string leave the optimizer at a different scope level than z3.

**Reproduction.** `ParseString("(declare-const x Int)(assert (> x 0))")` and then `ParseString("(declare-const x Int)(assert (< x 5))")`. C++: no error, 2 assertions. Go: the second call returns `line 1 column 21: invalid declaration, 'x' (with the given signature) already declared` (and 2 assertions).

**Fix.** Mirror `Z3_optimize_from_stream`: create a temporary parser context with `newSMT2ParserContext`, wire its objective and soft-constraint commands to `o.command` (the `install_opt_cmds` equivalent), parse with ignore-check, then call `o.command.Assert` for each remaining assertion of the temporary context, in order. Close the temporary context afterwards.

**Regression test.** Add `TestAPIOptimizeParseUsesFreshCommandContext` to `pkg/api/api_optimize_parse_test.go`: two `ParseString` calls that both declare `x` must both succeed and leave 2 assertions. A third string `(declare-const y Int)(push)(assert (> y 3))` must leave the optimizer's scope level unchanged, with 3 assertions.

<a id="api-02-f4"></a>
#### api_02-F4: `IsNumeral` returns false for `true`/`false`; `Z3_is_numeral_ast` returns true

- Severity: medium

- Go: `pkg/api/api_numerals.go:112-118` (`SMTContext.IsNumeral`)
- C++: `src/api/api_numeral.cpp:142-153` (`Z3_is_numeral_ast`); `src/ast/dl_decl_plugin.cpp:718-725` (`dl_decl_util::is_numeral_ext`)

**C++ behavior.**
```
return autil().is_numeral(e) || bvutil().is_numeral(e) || fpautil().is_numeral(e) ||
       fpautil().is_rm_numeral(e) || datalog_util().is_numeral_ext(e);
// is_numeral_ext: ... return m.is_true(c) || m.is_false(c);
```
**Go behavior.** `IsNumeral` is defined as "`NumeralString` succeeds". `NumeralString` follows `Z3_get_numeral_string`, which has no Boolean case, so Booleans are not numerals.

**Impact.** API clients that walk terms and use `is_numeral` to detect values (model printers, value checks) classify `true`/`false` differently from z3.

<a id="api-02-f5"></a>
#### api_02-F5: `SMTContext.String` does not decode escape sequences; `Z3_mk_string` builds `zstring(str, ascii)`, which does

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/api/api_sequences.go:65-78` (`SMTContext.String`, `StringValue`)
- C++: `src/api/api_seq.cpp:47-56,101-112` (`Z3_mk_string`, `Z3_get_string`); `src/ast/seq_decl_plugin.cpp:49-140` (`is_escape_char`, `zstring::zstring(char const*, encoding)`)

**C++ behavior.** `zstring s(str, zstring::ascii)` turns `\xHH`, octal escapes, `\a \b \f \n \r \t \v \\` and so on into single characters. `Z3_get_string` returns `str.encode()`, which uses the escaped form.

**Go behavior.** `m.MkString(value)` treats `value` as raw bytes (it only escapes them for the symbol), and `StringValue` returns the raw decoded bytes. Neither side follows the escape semantics of the C API.

**Impact.** The same input string gives a different term: `String("a\\x41")` is the 5-character string `a\x41` in Go and `"aA"` in z3. Results of `str.len`, equalities and models differ for any API client that passes escape sequences, as z3 bindings do.

**Reproduction.** C: `Z3_mk_string(c, "a\\x41")` gives `Z3_get_string = 'aA'` and prints as `aA`. Go: `StringValue(String("a\\x41"))` = `"a\\x41"` (len 5), printed `"a\\x41"`.

**Fix.** In `String`, decode `value` with a Go port of `is_escape_char`/`zstring(char const*, ascii)` (mask 0xFF) before calling `MkString`. In `StringValue`, return the `zstring::encode` spelling. If the raw-byte API is intended, add explicit `StringRaw`/`StringRawValue` names and document the deviation instead.

**Regression test.** Add `TestAPIStringDecodesSourceEscapes` to `pkg/api/api_sequences_test.go`. `StringValue(String("a\\x41"))` must equal `"aA"`, `String("\\n")` must have length 1, and `StringValue` of a string holding byte 0x0A must be `"\\n"`.

<a id="api-02-f6"></a>
#### api_02-F6: `WriteInterpolationProblem` with one sequence constraint does not mark it as an interpolant

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/api/api_interp_write.go:76-100` (`InterpolationContext.WriteInterpolationProblem`)
- C++: `src/api/api_interp.cpp:427-447` (`parents_vector_to_tree`)

**C++ behavior.** In sequence mode the first constraint is always wrapped, even when `num == 1`:
```
res = Z3_mk_interpolant(ctx, cnsts[0]);
for (int i = 1; i < num - 1; i++) { ... }
if (num > 1) { Z3_ast bar[2] = { res, cnsts[num - 1] }; res = Z3_mk_and(ctx, 2, bar); }
```
**Go behavior.** The loop `for index := 0; index < len(constraints)-1` marks nothing when there is one constraint, and the root is the bare constraint.

**Impact.** The emitted problem file has a different `get-interpolant` pattern, so replaying it in z3 asks a different question.

**Reproduction.** One Boolean constant `p`, `parents=nil`. C++ output ends with `(get-interpolant (interp f!1))`. Go output ends with `(get-interpolant f!1)`.

**Fix.** Handle `parents == nil` separately, as in C++: `res = MkInterp(c0)`; for `i = 1..n-2`, `res = MkInterp(MkAnd(res, ci))`; if `n > 1`, `res = MkAnd(res, c_{n-1})`. The tree branch (`parents != nil`) already matches `chs`/`and_vec`.

**Regression test.** Add `TestInterpolationWriteProblemSingleSequenceConstraint` to `pkg/api/api_interp_write_test.go` using `newInterpolationFixture`, `f.variable("w-a", boolean)` and `WriteInterpolationProblem(&buf, []ast.ASTHandle{a}, nil, nil)`. Expect the output to end with `(get-interpolant (interp f!1))\n`.

<a id="api-02-f7"></a>
#### api_02-F7: `ReadInterpolationProblem` handles a one-assertion file and the `;! THEORY=` value differently from `Z3_read_interpolation_problem`

- Severity: low
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/api/api_interp_read.go:101-143` (`interpolationTheoryCount`, `interpolationConjuncts`)
- C++: `src/api/api_interp.cpp:340-362,527-582` (`get_file_params`, `iZ3_parse`, `Z3_read_interpolation_problem`)

**C++ behavior.** `iZ3_parse` takes `Z3_get_app_num_args` of `Z3_parse_smtlib2_file`'s result. With a single assertion (`api::context::mk_and` returns it unwrapped), the result is that assertion's *arguments*. The THEORY value is read with `atoi` (prefix digits, last occurrence wins, no error), and the line must begin exactly with `;!`.

**Go behavior.** A non-`and` result is treated as one assertion. THEORY is read with `ParseUint`, which returns an error on `"1x"`. The first occurrence wins, and the line is `TrimSpace`d first.

**Impact.** Input files are interpreted differently: the C++ behavior on one assertion is a z3 quirk, but it is not recorded in `z3_bug_exclusions.txt`.

**Reproduction.** File `(declare-const a Bool)(declare-const b Bool)(assert (or a b))`: C++ `num=2` (`a`, `b`), Go `num=1`. File starting with `;! THEORY=1x` and three assertions: C++ `ok=1 num=2 theory=1`; Go returns the error `invalid THEORY count "1x"`.

**Fix.** Either port these exactly (split the arguments of the single assertion, `atoi`-style prefix parse, last key wins, no trimming), or record both as deliberate exclusions in `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/z3_bug_exclusions.txt`.

**Regression test.** Add `TestInterpolationReadProblemSourceQuirks` to `pkg/api/api_interp_read_test.go` with the two files above as `strings.NewReader` input to `ReadInterpolationProblem(r, false)`. Expect `len(Constraints)` 2 and 2 respectively, with `len(Theory)==1` in the second case (or assert the documented exclusion behavior).

<a id="api-02-f8"></a>
#### api_02-F8: `PatternString` prints with let-aliases; `Z3_pattern_to_string` (`Z3_ast_to_string`) disables them

- Severity: low
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/api/api_quantifiers.go:238-257` (`SMTContext.PatternString`)
- C++: `src/api/api_ast.cpp:819-843` (`Z3_ast_to_string`)

**C++ behavior.** In the default SMTLIB_FULL mode it sets `max_depth = min_alias_size = UINT_MAX` before `mk_pp`, so no `let` is introduced.

**Go behavior.** Uses `ast.NewSimpleASTPrinterContext(...).DisplayExpr`, which pretty-prints with the default sharing thresholds and ignores the API print mode.

**Impact.** Pattern text differs for any pattern with repeated subterms.

**Reproduction.** Pattern over `t = f(t,t)` iterated 8 times starting from `(:var 0)`. Go prints 233 bytes beginning `(let ((a!1 (f (f (f (:var 0) (:var 0)) ...`. C++ `Z3_pattern_to_string` prints 4351 bytes with no `let`, beginning `((f (f (f (f (f (f (f (f (:var 0) (:var 0)) ...`.

**Fix.** Implement `PatternString` as `c.ASTString(value, <context print mode>)` (`api_ast_typed_string.go`), after the `IsPattern` check, so it shares the `Z3_ast_to_string` mode handling and full-mode parameters.

**Regression test.** Add `TestAPIPatternStringHasNoAliases` to `pkg/api/api_quantifiers_test.go`: build the nested `f` term above with `f.c.Function`, `f.c.BoundVariable(0, I)`, `f.c.Apply` and `f.c.Pattern`. Expect `!strings.Contains(s, "(let")` and a length of 4351.

<a id="api-02-f9"></a>
#### api_02-F9: `ParameterDescriptions.Kind`/`Documentation` normalize the name; `Z3_param_descrs_get_kind`/`get_documentation` look it up verbatim

- Severity: low

**Go behavior.** Applies `apiParameterName` (`NormParamName`) before the lookup.

**Impact.** Descriptor queries with dash or upper-case spellings succeed in Go and fail in z3.

**Reproduction.** Simple solver descriptors. C: `kind(random-seed)=6` (`Z3_PK_INVALID`), `kind(random_seed)=0`. Go: both return `ParameterUInt` (0).
