<a id="api-03-f1"></a>
#### api_03-F1: replay never installs `Z3_replayer_error_handler`; API errors abort the replay or are silent

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/api/z3_generated_context_commands.go:74` (`replayCreateContextWithConfig`), `pkg/api/z3_replayer_parse.go:89-103,143-148` (`Parse`, case `'C'`), `pkg/api/api_context_check_sorts.go:17` (`setErrorCode`, handler field never set)
- C++: `src/api/api_commands.cpp:4,34-43` (`Z3_replayer_error_handler`, `exec_Z3_mk_context[_rc]`), `src/api/api_context.cpp:147-152,274-282` (`set_error_code`, `invoke_error_handler`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
void Z3_replayer_error_handler(Z3_context ctx, Z3_error_code c) { printf("[REPLAYER ERROR HANDLER]: %s\n", Z3_get_error_msg(ctx, c)); }
void exec_Z3_mk_context(z3_replayer & in) {
  Z3_context result = Z3_mk_context(reinterpret_cast<Z3_config>(in.get_obj(0)));
  in.store_result(result);
  Z3_set_error_handler(result, Z3_replayer_error_handler);}
...
void context::set_error_code(Z3_error_code err) { m_error_code = err; if (err != Z3_OK) invoke_error_handler(err); }
```
Every API failure inside a replayed call (`SET_ERROR_CODE`, or a `Z3_CATCH` turning an exception into `Z3_EXCEPTION`) prints `[REPLAYER ERROR HANDLER]: <Z3_get_error_msg text>` on stdout. The call returns null, `= ptr` stores null, and replay continues. `Z3_get_error_msg(c, Z3_EXCEPTION)` returns the exception text. Contexts made by `Z3_mk_interpolation_context` get only the default handler (`printf("Error: %s\n", ...); exit(1)`, `api_context.cpp:57-59`), because `exec_Z3_mk_interpolation_context` does not install the replayer handler.

**Go behavior.** `replayCreateContextWithConfig` never sets `apiContextResults.errorHandler` (nothing in the package ever assigns it). There are two outcomes:
(a) API failures that Go reports as a returned `error` (sort mismatch, invalid index, tactic failure, `Z3_params_validate`, `Z3_param_descrs_get_documentation` miss, `Z3_get_string` on a non-string, quantifier sort error, ...) leave `Parse` as `r.failure(err.Error())`. The replay stops, `Error at line N: <msg>` goes to stderr, and the rest of the log is skipped.
(b) Failures that Go models with `owner.results.setErrorCode(...)` (`Z3_parse_smtlib2_string`, `Z3_eval_smtlib2_string`, `Z3_fixedpoint_from_string/file`, `Z3_set_error`, ...) print nothing at all.

**Impact.** Any log recorded from a program that hit an API error, which is the usual reason to replay a log, gives different stdout. g3 also stops at the first error, so later `M` messages and `[z3 exception]` lines never appear.

**Reproduction.** Case (a), confirmed (`work/api_03/e1.log`):
```
R
P 0
C 6
= 10
R
P 10
C 33
= 11
R
P 10
C 32
= 12
R
P 10
$ |x|
P 11
C 51
= 13
R
P 10
$ |y|
P 12
C 51
= 14
R
P 10
P 13
P 14
C 56
= 15
M "after"
R
P 10
C 8
```
z3: `[REPLAYER ERROR HANDLER]: Sorts Int and Bool are incompatible` / `after` / memory / time.
g3: stderr `Error at line 30: Sorts Int and Bool are incompatible`, no `after`.

Case (b), confirmed (`work/api_03/e4.log`): `Z3_parse_smtlib2_string` on `"(assert (foo"`, then `Z3_set_error(c, 2)`. z3 prints `[REPLAYER ERROR HANDLER]: parser error` and `[REPLAYER ERROR HANDLER]: index out of bounds`; g3 prints neither.

**Fix.**
1. In `replayCreateContextWithConfig`, take a flag for whether to install the handler. Set it `true` from `replayMkContext`/`replayMkContextRC` and `false` from `replayMkInterpolationContext`. When `true`, set `results.errorHandler = func(c *apiContextResults, code uint32) { fmt.Fprintf(r.output, "[REPLAYER ERROR HANDLER]: %s\n", <Z3_get_error_msg text for code>) }`. Use the existing Go equivalent of `_get_error_msg` (it must return the last exception message for `Z3_EXCEPTION`).
2. For contexts without the replayer handler, emulate `default_error_handler`: print `Error: <msg>\n` to stdout and end the replay with exit status 1, skipping the memory/time report, as `exit(1)` does.
3. Add one central conversion for case (a), e.g. in `Parse` case `'C'`, or by wrapping each handler. When a command returns an API-level error (anything that is not a replayer-argument error, see F2), map it to the C++ error code (`Z3_SORT_ERROR`, `Z3_IOB`, `Z3_INVALID_ARG`, `Z3_EXCEPTION` with message, ...). Then call `owner.results.setErrorCode(code)` so the handler prints, set `r.result = 0`, and continue. The command's context is argument 0 for almost every command; the context-less commands (0-5, 327, 342-347) never go through `SET_ERROR_CODE`.
4. Once results can be null, later commands must accept a null (0) object argument and fail the way the API does (see F4).

**Regression test.** Extend `pkg/cmd/g3/z3_log_frontend_test.go` with `TestZ3LogFrontendReplayerErrorHandler`. It feeds the two logs above to `runArgumentsWithDiagnostics([]string{"-log","-in"}, strings.NewReader(log), &out, &diagnostics)`, the helper `TestZ3LogFrontendReplaysQuantifier` already uses.
- Expect `diagnostics.Len()==0`.
- Expect `strings.HasPrefix(out.String(), "[REPLAYER ERROR HANDLER]: Sorts Int and Bool are incompatible\nafter\nmax. heap size:")` for e1.
- Expect `"[REPLAYER ERROR HANDLER]: parser error\nafter-parse\n[REPLAYER ERROR HANDLER]: index out of bounds\nafter-set-error\nmax. heap size:"` for e4.

<a id="api-03-f2"></a>
#### api_03-F2: replayer argument errors inside a command are fatal instead of `[z3 exception]: ...` and continue

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/api/z3_replayer_parse.go:89-103` (`Parse`, case `'C'`), `pkg/api/z3_replayer_values.go:30-40` (`value`), `pkg/api/z3_replayer_errors.go:16-21`
- C++: `src/api/z3_replayer.cpp:72-83,510-528` (`check_arg`, case `'C'`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
try { m_cmds[idx](m_owner); }
catch (z3_error & ex) { throw ex; }
catch (z3_exception & ex) { std::cout << "[z3 exception]: " << ex.msg() << std::endl; }
```
`z3_replayer_exception` is `default_exception`, so a `get_obj`/`get_uint`/... kind or position failure inside an `exec_*` prints `[z3 exception]: expecting object at position 0 but got int64` (or `invalid argument reference`) and replay continues.

**Go behavior.** `value()` returns `fmt.Errorf("%w: expecting ...", ErrZ3ReplayReference, ...)`. That is not a `*Z3ReplayCommandError` (nothing in the package ever builds one, so the `[z3 exception]` branch is dead). `Parse` therefore aborts with `Error at line N: api: invalid Z3 replay argument reference: expecting ...`. The same `api: invalid Z3 replay argument reference:` prefix also changes the text of the top-level `*`/`@` errors (C++: `Error at line 11: expecting object at position 1 but got int64`).

**Impact.** Malformed logs, and well-formed C++ logs that hit a C++ log/exec mismatch (see F3, and `Z3_mk_fpa_numeral_float`, which logs `D` but reads `get_float`), give a different stdout and stop the replay.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed: `R/P 0/C 6/= 10/R/I 5/C 33/M "after"/R/P 10/C 8`.
z3: `[z3 exception]: expecting object at position 0 but got int64` / `after`.
g3: `Error at line 7: api: invalid Z3 replay argument reference: expecting object at position 0 but got int64`.

**Fix.**
1. Make `value()` return `&Z3ReplayCommandError{Message: ...}` built with the C++ texts: `"invalid argument reference"` when `position >= len(args)`, and `"expecting <k> at position <p> but got <k2>"` on a kind mismatch.
2. `Float` must use `"invalid argument reference"` for both failures, as `get_float` calls `throw_invalid_reference`.
3. In `Parse`, case `'*'` and case `'@'` are outside a command: report the bare message (no `api:` prefix) as a fatal `Z3ReplayError`.
4. Keep "invalid command" (unregistered ID) fatal, as in C++.
5. Handlers that today return `ErrZ3ReplayReference` for an unknown replay ID correspond to a dangling pointer in C++ (undefined behaviour). They can stay fatal.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/cmd/g3/z3_log_frontend_test.go`, add `TestZ3LogFrontendCommandArgumentException`. It uses the log above and expects `out` to start with `"[z3 exception]: expecting object at position 0 but got int64\nafter\nmax. heap size:"` and `diagnostics` to be empty. Add a second case `R/P 0/C 6/= 10/R/P 10/I 3/* 21 1` expecting diagnostics exactly `Error at line 11: expecting object at position 1 but got int64\n`.

<a id="api-03-f3"></a>
#### api_03-F3: `Z3_mk_pble`/`pbge`/`pbeq` replay succeeds although 4.7.1 always throws (log writes `u`, exec reads `get_int_array`)

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/api/z3_generated_pseudo_boolean_commands.go:41-48` (`replayPseudoBoolean`)
- C++: `src/api/api_log_macros.cpp:1636-1646` (`log_Z3_mk_pble`), `src/api/api_commands.cpp:1529-1555` (`exec_Z3_mk_pble/pbge/pbeq`)

**C++ behavior.** The logger writes the coefficients as `U ...` followed by `Au(n)`, which is a `UINT_ARRAY`. The exec reads them with `in.get_int_array(3)`, which does `check_arg(pos, INT_ARRAY)`. The replay always throws `expecting int_array at position 3 but got uint_array`, prints it as `[z3 exception]`, and no AST is stored (`m_result` stays null after `R`).

**Go behavior.** `raw, e := r.UintArray(3)` accepts the `u` array, converts each word to `int32`, and builds the PB term silently.

**Impact.** Every replay of a log that uses these three APIs differs from 4.7.1: the stdout line is missing, and a non-null term is bound where z3 binds null. A later `Z3_solver_assert` of that term then succeeds in g3, but in z3 it reports a null-argument error.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed (`work/api_03/e5.log`):
```
R
P 0
C 6
= 10
R
P 10
C 32
= 11
R
P 10
$ |a|
P 11
C 51
= 12
R
P 10
$ |b|
P 11
C 51
= 13
R
P 10
U 2
P 12
P 13
p 2
U 1
U 2
u 2
I 2
C 224
= 14
M "after-pble"
R
P 10
C 8
```
z3: `[z3 exception]: expecting int_array at position 3 but got uint_array` / `after-pble`.
g3: `after-pble` only.

**Fix.** There are two options; pick one per project policy.
(a) Fidelity: replace `r.UintArray(3)` with `r.IntArray(3)`. After F2 that produces exactly the C++ `[z3 exception]` line, and the result stays 0.
(b) Treat it as a 4.7.1 bug: add an entry to `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/z3_bug_exclusions.txt` and leave the code as is.
`Z3_mk_fpa_numeral_float` (595, logged with `D`, read with `get_float`) already fails in both builds; once F2 is fixed it prints the same `[z3 exception]: invalid argument reference`.

**Regression test.** Add `TestZ3LogFrontendPseudoBooleanCoefficientKind` to `pkg/cmd/g3/z3_log_frontend_test.go` with the log above. Under option (a), expect `out` to start with `"[z3 exception]: expecting int_array at position 3 but got uint_array\nafter-pble\n"`.

<a id="api-03-f4"></a>
#### api_03-F4: a null object argument is a fatal replay error; `Z3_inc_ref(c, NULL)` is a no-op in C++

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/api/z3_generated_ast_owners.go:54-66` (`astObject`/`astByID`), `pkg/api/z3_generated_ast_commands.go:116-157` (`replayIncAST`, `replayDecAST`)
- C++: `src/api/api_context.cpp:370-388` (`Z3_inc_ref`, `Z3_dec_ref`), `src/ast/ast.h` (`ast_manager::inc_ref(ast*)` ignores null)

**C++ behavior.** `Z3_inc_ref(c, a)` calls `m().inc_ref(to_ast(a))`, which does nothing for null. The other APIs check null arguments with `CHECK_NON_NULL`/`CHECK_VALID_AST`, which set `Z3_INVALID_ARG`; with F1 that prints the handler line and continues. `Z3_dec_ref` decides by the AST's real reference count (which includes trail/last-result/parent references), not by how many times the log called `inc_ref`.

**Go behavior.** `astByID(owner, 0)` returns `ErrZ3ReplayReference`, so the replay stops for any null AST argument. `replayDecAST` also fails when `entry.references == 0`, i.e. when the log never called `Z3_inc_ref` on that ID, even though the C++ ref count may be positive.

**Impact.** rc-mode clients (Python/.NET/Java wrappers) routinely `inc_ref` every result, including null results after an API error. With F1 fixed those nulls become common, and g3 would still abort.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed: `R/P 0/C 7/= 10/R/P 10/P 0/C 9/M "after"/R/P 10/C 8`.
z3: `after`.
g3: `Error at line 8: api: invalid Z3 replay argument reference`.

**Fix.**
1. In `replayIncAST`, return nil when `r.Object(1)` is 0 (as the vector/model/goal/tactic inc/dec handlers already do).
2. In `replayDecAST`, on null do what C++ does (`to_ast(a)->get_ref_count()` on null crashes in C++; leave it fatal).
3. Make the zero-reference check use the manager's real ref count (`owner.results.manager` reference count of `entry.handle`) and, when it is 0, call `setErrorCode(Z3_DEC_REF_ERROR)` instead of failing.
4. Give `astObject` a nullable variant for the many APIs whose C++ body starts with `CHECK_NON_NULL`/`CHECK_VALID_AST`. For those, null should produce `setErrorCode(Z3_INVALID_ARG)` plus a null result, not a fatal error.

**Regression test.** Add `TestZ3LogFrontendIncRefNull` in `pkg/cmd/g3/z3_log_frontend_test.go` with the log above. Expect `out` to start with `"after\nmax. heap size:"` and `diagnostics` to be empty.

<a id="api-03-f5"></a>
#### api_03-F5: `Z3_solver_from_string`/`Z3_fixedpoint_from_string` parse errors do not print the parser's `(error ...)` line

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/api/z3_generated_solver_commands.go:319-331,472-482` (`replaySolverFromString/File`), `pkg/api/z3_generated_fixedpoint_commands.go` case 534/535 (`replayFixedpointCommand`); the underlying loaders are `pkg/api/api_simple_solver_load_string.go:7`, `pkg/api/api_fixedpoint_object_load_queries.go:16`
- C++: `src/api/api_solver.cpp:131-139` (`solver_from_stream`), `src/api/api_datalog.cpp:357-369` (`Z3_fixedpoint_from_stream`)

**C++ behavior.** Both create `cmd_context ctx(false, &m)` and never redirect its regular stream (unlike `parse_smtlib2_stream`/`Z3_optimize_from_stream`, which redirect to a stringstream). `parse_smt2_commands` therefore writes `(error "line L column C: ...")` to stdout, then `SET_ERROR_CODE(Z3_PARSER_ERROR)` fires the handler.

**Go behavior.** The solver loader returns a Go error, so the replay stops (F1) with no `(error ...)` line. The fixedpoint path calls `setErrorCode(4)` and prints nothing.

**Impact.** Logs that load text through these APIs give different stdout on parse errors.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed. Solver (`e8.log`): `R/P 0/C 6/= 10/R/P 10/C 408/= 11/R/P 10/P 11/S "(assert (foo"/C 426/M "after"/R/P 10/C 8`.
z3: `(error "line 1 column 10: invalid expression, '(' or symbol expected")` / `[REPLAYER ERROR HANDLER]: parser error` / `after`.
g3: `Error at line 13: line 1 column 10: symbol expected`.

Fixedpoint (`e7.log`, `S "(declare-rel q ())(rule q)(foo"`, command 534).
z3: `(error "line 1 column 28: invalid command, symbol expected")` / `[REPLAYER ERROR HANDLER]: parser error` / `after`.
g3: `after`.

**Fix.**
1. Give the solver and fixedpoint stream loaders an output writer for parser diagnostics, and have the replay commands pass `r.output`, matching the default `cmd_context` regular stream.
2. On parse failure, return a parser-error marker so the replay command calls `setErrorCode(Z3_PARSER_ERROR)` (handler from F1) and continues.
3. Do not change `Z3_parse_smtlib2_string`/`Z3_eval_smtlib2_string`/`Z3_optimize_from_*`, which redirect in C++.

The differing message text (`symbol expected` vs `invalid expression, '(' or symbol expected`) is a parser issue outside this shard; see Needs verification.

**Regression test.** Add `TestZ3LogFrontendSolverFromStringParseError` and `TestZ3LogFrontendFixedpointFromStringParseError` to `pkg/cmd/g3/z3_log_frontend_test.go`. Use the logs above and expect the exact z3 stdout prefixes quoted.

<a id="api-03-f7"></a>
#### api_03-F7: datatype accessor/constructor/recognizer queries skip `save_ast_trail`

**C++ behavior.** IDs 212, 214, 216, 217 and 218 all call `mk_c(c)->save_ast_trail(decl)`. In rc mode this replaces `m_last_result`, releasing the previous last result; otherwise it pushes onto `m_ast_trail`.

```go
if id == 221 { return r.storeBorrowedAST(owner, result) }

```

|---|---|---|
| `U x` | `invalid unsigned` | `invalid integer` |
| `P z` | `invalid ptr` | `invalid pointer` |
| bad escape | `invalid scaped character` | `invalid escaped character` |
| EOF in string | `unexpected end of file` | `unexpected EOF` |
| `D x` | `invalid double` / `invalid float` | `invalid floating point value` |
| `U 99999999999999999999` | wraps silently | `strconv.ParseUint: ... value out of range` |
| `D 1-2` | `strtod` prefix parse, accepted | `strconv.ParseFloat ... invalid syntax` |
| `P 1x5` | parses `0x15` | parse error |

Also: `blanks()` accepts `\r`, so a CRLF log replays in g3, while z3 gives `Error at line 1: unknown log command`. C++ prints `[replayer] N operations executed` every 100000 commands under `IF_VERBOSE(1)`; Go never does.

**Fix.**
1. Use the C++ message strings, with distinct errors for unsigned/int/ptr/float/double and `"unexpected end of file"`.
2. Accumulate integers with wrapping `uint64`/`int64` arithmetic instead of `strconv` (`v = 10*v + d`), and hex the same way, skipping an `x`/`X` at position 1 anywhere.
3. Parse floats by taking the longest valid prefix (`strtod` semantics), returning 0 for an empty numeric prefix.
4. Drop `'\r'` from `blanks()`.
5. Add the verbose tick counter (`verbosity >= 1`, stdout, `[replayer] %d operations executed`).

**Regression test.** `pkg/api/z3_replayer_scanner_test.go` (new) `TestZ3ReplayScannerDiagnostics`: a table of the inputs above run through `NewZ3Replayer(...).Parse()`, checking `(*Z3ReplayError).Message` equals the z3 text, and that `R\r\n` fails with `unknown log command`.

<a id="api-03-f10"></a>
#### api_03-F10: log writer escapes bytes >= 0x80 differently from `ll_escaped` (signed `char`); `D` of inf/nan differs

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/api/z3_log_escape.go:13-30` (`z3LogEscape`), `pkg/api/z3_log_scalars.go:19-22` (`Double`)
- C++: `src/api/z3_logger.h` (`operator<<(ostream&, ll_escaped const&)`, `D`)

**C++ behavior.** `char c` is signed on x86-64. Byte 0xC3 (-61) is written as `\0*/` (`'0'+0`, `'0'+(-6)`, `'0'+(-1)`); z3's own replayer then rejects it (`invalid scaped character`). `D(inf)` prints `inf`, `D(nan)` prints `nan`.

**Go behavior.** It writes `\195`, which round-trips, and `+Inf`/`NaN`.

**Impact.** Log files written by g3 for non-ASCII strings or non-finite doubles differ byte-for-byte from z3's. Not reachable from the shell; API-only.

**Fix.** If byte-identical logs are wanted, compute the three digits from `int8(c)` exactly as C++ does, and map ±Inf/NaN to `inf`/`-inf`/`nan`. Otherwise record it as an intentional deviation, since the C++ output is unreplayable.

**Regression test.** `pkg/api/z3_log_lifecycle_test.go`: assert `z3LogEscape("\xc3") == "\\0*/"` (if fidelity is chosen) and that `Double(math.Inf(1))` writes `D inf\n`.

### Area: Command context (`pkg/cmd_context`)

*cmd_context_01.* 63 files of `pkg/cmd_context` (9342 lines): `cmd_context.cpp` core (builtins, mk_app, declarations, push/pop, check-sat, model completion/validation, set-option paths), `check_logic`, the `apply` command, echo/probe tactics, interpolation commands, the legacy Datalog parser (`datalog_parser.cpp`), the fixedpoint command glue (`dl_cmds.cpp`), the OPB loader, and the cmd_context side of `opt::context`. `check_logic.go`, `echo_tactic.go`, `function_references.go`, `info.go`, `model_completion.go` (completion part) and `optimization_model_comparison.go` are close ports. The rest has real divergences, most of them confirmed with the binaries. The reference `build/z3` was being rebuilt partway through the audit. Repros marked "(z3 = build_dbg/z3)" used `<repo>/build_dbg/z3`, which has the same `-D_EXTERNAL_RELEASE` release flags. All other repros used `build/z3`. Findings: 0 critical, 4 high, 6 medium, 6 low (14 confirmed with the binaries, 2 from reading).

*cmd_context_02.* This shard covers the second half of `pkg/cmd_context`: optimization normalization and Pareto glue (opt_context.cpp / opt_pareto.cpp), the WCNF and WPA loaders, get-option, get-assignment / get-unsat-core / get-proof / eval / get-consequences, check-sat-using, sort declarations and sort info (pdecl.cpp), the symbol dictionary, the polynomial and subpaving debug commands, the tactic registry and descriptions, user tactics, and the solver factories. Most of it is a faithful port. The `symbolDictionary` hashtable port, the tactic registry order and all ADD_TACTIC descriptions check out exactly. Several command-level divergences were confirmed with both binaries. Counts: high 1, medium 9, low 4 (14 findings). 12 of them were reproduced with `$S/bin/g3` vs `build/z3`. Note: `build/z3` was missing for a few minutes while someone rebuilt it (rebuilt 15:59). Every z3 comparison quoted below was re-run against the rebuilt binary.

<a id="cmd-context-01-f1"></a>
#### cmd_context_01-F1: `MakeApp` rejects overloads that differ only in range ("ambiguous function reference")

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/applications.go:221-264` (`Context.MakeApp`)
- C++: `src/cmd_context/cmd_context.cpp:1082-1103` (`cmd_context::mk_app`), `:195-213` (`func_decls::find`)

**C++ behavior.** With more than one declaration, `fs.find(m, num_args, args, range)` walks the `func_decl_set` and returns the **first** declaration whose range (when one is given), arity and domain match. It never reports ambiguity:
```
for (func_decl * f : *fs) {
    if (range != nullptr && f->get_range() != range) continue;
    if (f->get_arity() != arity) continue;
    ... if (i == arity) return f;
}
```

**Go behavior.** It collects every match and fails on the second one:
```
if matches {
    if !match.IsNull() {
        return ast.ASTHandle{}, fmt.Errorf("ambiguous function reference %s", name)
    }
    match = decl
}
```

**Impact.** `declare-fun` allows `g : Int -> Int` and `g : Int -> Real` together. Every unqualified application of `g` then fails in g3, so assertions are dropped and the answer changes. z3 picks one declaration deterministically (the first in the `obj_hashtable` slot order of the set).

**Reproduction.**
```
(declare-fun g (Int) Int)
(declare-fun g (Int) Real)
(assert (= (g 1) 2))
(check-sat)
(get-model)
(eval (g 1))
```
g3: `(error "line 3 column 15: ambiguous function reference g")`, `sat`, an empty `(model \n)`, then `(error "... ambiguous function reference g")`.
z3: `sat`, a model with `(define-fun g ((x!0 Int)) Int (ite (= x!0 1) 2 2))`, then `2`.

**Fix.** Port `func_decls::find` as written. Iterate `c.funcDictionary().find(name).funcs.entries()` (the existing set-order emulation in `symbol_dictionary.go`) rather than the insertion-ordered `c.functions[name]`, and return the first candidate that passes the range/arity/domain filters. Remove the ambiguity error. Keep the sole-declaration fast path (C++ `!more_than_one() → first()`).

**Regression test.** Add `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/overload_same_domain_range.smt2` with the script above. Its `scriptResults` entry is the z3 output above. Check it with `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`. Also add a unit test `TestMakeAppOverloadPicksFirstSetEntry` to `pkg/cmd_context/context_test.go`, using the `NewContext`/`DeclareFunction` setup that the existing tests in that file use, and assert that `MakeApp("g", {1}, nil, null)` succeeds.

<a id="cmd-context-01-f2"></a>
#### cmd_context_01-F2: wrong error texts for declarations and applications

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/context.go:1233-1236` (`publishFunctionDeclaration`), `pkg/cmd_context/datatype_declarations.go:211-214` (`insertDatatypeFunction`), `pkg/cmd_context/applications.go:214-216, 261-263` (`MakeApp`)
- C++: `src/cmd_context/cmd_context.cpp:797-803` (`insert(symbol, func_decl*)`), `:1071-1099` (`mk_app`)

**C++ behavior.**
```
msg += f->get_arity() == 0 ? "constant" : "function";   // "invalid declaration, constant 'f' (with ...) already declared"
...
if (num_args == 0 && range == nullptr) { ... if (f->get_arity() != 0) throw cmd_exception("invalid function application, missing arguments ", s); ... }
... buffer << "unknown constant " << s << " " << " (" sorts ") " range "\ndeclared: " decl ...
```

**Go behavior.** It prints `invalid declaration, '%s' (with the given signature) already declared`, without "constant"/"function". A bare reference to a function is handed to `m.MkApp`, which reports the manager's arity error. When no signature matches, Go prints `unknown constant %s or no matching function signature`.

**Impact.** Error text differs from z3 for duplicate declarations, bare function names and failed overload resolution.

**Reproduction.**
- `(declare-const f Int)(declare-const f Int)`: g3 `invalid declaration, 'f' (with the given signature) already declared`; z3 `invalid declaration, constant 'f' (with the given signature) already declared`. `declare-fun` gives the same diff with `function`.
- `(declare-fun f (Int) Int)(assert (= f 1))`: g3 `Wrong number of arguments (0) passed to function (declare-fun f (Int) Int)`; z3 `invalid function application, missing arguments f`.
- `(declare-fun g (Int) Int)(declare-fun g (Real) Int)(assert (= (g 1.0) 2))(assert (= (g true) 2))`: g3 `unknown constant g or no matching function signature`; z3 `unknown constant g  (Bool) \ndeclared: (declare-fun g (Int) Int) \ndeclared: (declare-fun g (Real) Int) `.

**Fix.**
1. In both duplicate checks, build the message as in C++: `kind := "function"; if arity == 0 { kind = "constant" }; fmt.Errorf("invalid declaration, %s '%s' (with the given signature) already declared", kind, name)`.
2. In `MakeApp`, when `len(args)==0 && rangeSort.IsNull()`: take `first()`; if its arity is not 0, return `invalid function application, missing arguments <name>`.
3. For a failed overload match, build the C++ buffer: `"unknown constant " + name + " " + " ("`, the argument sorts space-separated via the sort printer, `") "`, then `range + " "` if given, then one `"\ndeclared: " + <decl pp> + " "` per entry in `funcDecls.entries()` order.

**Regression test.** Add the three scripts as `test_vectors/decl_error_texts_*.smt2` with the z3 outputs above in `scriptResults`, and check them with `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference`.

<a id="cmd-context-01-f3"></a>
#### cmd_context_01-F3: objectives and soft constraints go through `check_logic`, which `opt::context` never does

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/optimization.go:129` (`AddObjective`), `:172` (`AddSoftConstraint`)
- C++: `src/opt/opt_cmds.cpp:85-105, 133-138`; `src/opt/opt_context.cpp:91-117, 227-235` (`scoped_state::add`)

**C++ behavior.** `assert-soft` and `maximize`/`minimize` call `opt::context::add_soft_constraint` / `add_objective`. These check only the sort (Bool, or bit-vector/int/real). `m_check_logic` runs only in `cmd_context::assert_expr` and `insert(func_decl)`.

**Go behavior.**
```
if err = c.logicChecker.CheckExpression(expression); err != nil {
    return err
}
```
This runs in both functions.

**Impact.** Under a declared logic, an objective or soft constraint outside that logic is rejected. Example: a product of variables under `QF_LIA`. z3 optimizes it. g3 drops it, and `get-objectives` comes out different.

**Reproduction.**
```
(set-logic QF_LIA)(declare-const x Int)(declare-const y Int)(assert (< 0 x 3))(assert (< 0 y 3))(maximize (* x y))(check-sat)(get-objectives)
```
g3: `(error "line 1 column 114: logic does not support nonlinear arithmetic")`, `sat`, `(objectives\n)`.
z3 (= build_dbg/z3): `sat`, `(objectives\n ((* x y) 4)\n)`.
With `(assert-soft (= (* x y) 4))` in place of the maximize line, g3 errors and z3 prints ` ( 0)`.

**Fix.** Delete the two `c.logicChecker.CheckExpression` calls. While there, align the messages with C++: `Invalid type for expression. Expected Boolean type.` (opt_cmds.cpp:88) and `Objective must be bit-vector, integer or real` (opt_context.cpp:112). g3 currently prints lower-case variants, confirmed with both binaries.

**Regression test.** Add `test_vectors/opt_objective_outside_logic.smt2` (the script above) with expected `sat\n(objectives\n ((* x y) 4)\n)\n`. Add `test_vectors/opt_message_texts.smt2` with `(declare-const x Int)(assert-soft x)` and `(declare-const b Bool)(minimize b)` and the z3 errors. Check both with `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference`.

<a id="cmd-context-01-f4"></a>
#### cmd_context_01-F4: `runOptimize` drops the quantified-constraints warning and the "unbounded objectives on quantified constraints" error

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/optimization.go:480-552` (`runOptimize`); the `execute_min_max` part belongs to `pkg/opt` (`ArithmeticSolver.Check`)
- C++: `src/opt/opt_context.cpp:268-270` (`optimize`), `:366-375` (`execute_min_max`)

**C++ behavior.**
```
update_solver();
if (contains_quantifiers()) {
    warning_msg("optimization with quantified constraints is not supported");
}
...
if (result == l_true && m_optsmt.is_unbounded(index, is_max) && contains_quantifiers()) {
    throw default_exception("unbounded objectives on quantified constraints is not supported");
}
```

**Go behavior.** Nothing in `pkg/cmd_context` or `pkg/opt` ports `contains_quantifiers`; grep finds it only in the vendored `cppsrc` copy. The run goes straight from `UpdateSolver` to `assertOptimizerHard` and reports `sat` with an unbounded value.

**Impact.** For an unbounded objective over quantified hard constraints, g3 answers `sat` where z3 reports an error. The stderr warning is also missing.

**Reproduction.**
```
(declare-fun f (Int) Int)(declare-const x Int)(assert (forall ((y Int)) (> (f y) x)))(maximize x)(check-sat)(get-objectives)
```
g3: `sat` then `(objectives\n (x oo)\n)`.
z3 (= build_dbg/z3): `WARNING: optimization with quantified constraints is not supported` on stderr, `(error "line 1 column 108: unbounded objectives on quantified constraints is not supported")`, then `(objectives\n (x oo)\n)`.

**Fix.**
1. In `runOptimize`, after `optimizer.UpdateSolver` and before `assertOptimizerHard`, port `contains_quantifiers()`. It is true if any hard constraint (`c.assertions` or the override) or objective term has a quantifier. When true, emit `warning_msg` through the process warning service.
2. In `pkg/opt`, after a lex/min-max objective returns `l_true` and is unbounded, return a `z3exception.Z3Exception` with that text if the problem contains quantifiers. Then F5's fix must turn it into a cmd error rather than "unknown".

**Regression test.** Add `test_vectors/opt_quantified_unbounded.smt2` (the script above) with expected stdout `(error "line 1 column 108: unbounded objectives on quantified constraints is not supported")\n(objectives\n (x oo)\n)\n`. Add the file to `parseErrorScripts` if needed, and check with `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference`.

<a id="cmd-context-01-f5"></a>
#### cmd_context_01-F5: an exception during `check-sat` with objectives becomes `unknown`; C++ raises a command error

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/optimization_failure.go:10-28` (`handleOptimizationFailure`), `optimization_unknown_result.go:12-33`
- C++: `src/cmd_context/cmd_context.cpp:1465-1492` (`cmd_context::check_sat`, opt branch)

**C++ behavior.** `m_check_sat_result = get_opt();` is set before optimizing. Then:
```
try { r = get_opt()->optimize(); ... }
catch (z3_error & ex) { throw ex; }
catch (z3_exception & ex) { throw cmd_exception(ex.msg()); }
```
No `sat`/`unknown` line is printed. The check-sat result stays the opt context, whose status was never set, so `(get-info :reason-unknown)` prints `"unknown"`.

**Go behavior.** A cancellation, or any `Z3Exception`, is published as an `unknown` result whose reason is the exception text.

**Impact.** On resource-limit exhaustion or other exceptions inside optimize, the printed answer and the reason-unknown differ from z3.

**Reproduction.**
```
(set-option :rlimit 10)(declare-const x Int)(assert (< x 10))(maximize x)(check-sat)(get-info :reason-unknown)
```
g3: `unknown`, `(:reason-unknown "max. resource limit exceeded")`.
z3 (= build_dbg/z3): `(error "line 1 column 84: max. resource limit exceeded")`, `(:reason-unknown "unknown")`.
With `:timeout 1` both print `unknown`: the optimizer returns `l_undef` there without throwing.

**Fix.** Keep the fatal `Z3Error` path. For the canceled case and the `Z3Exception` case, publish a check-sat result that stands for `get_opt()`: status unset/unknown, reason-unknown `"unknown"`, which is what `opt::context::reason_unknown` returns there. Then return the exception message as a plain command error, so the parser prints `(error "...")` and no `unknown`. Distinguish an exception from an `l_undef` return: only an error propagating out of `runNormalizedOptimization` takes this path.

**Regression test.** Add `test_vectors/opt_rlimit_exception.smt2` (the script above) with the z3 output, and check with `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference`.

<a id="cmd-context-01-f6"></a>
#### cmd_context_01-F6: `set-option` handling of built-in options does not follow `set_option_cmd`

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/context.go:619-845` (`SetBoolOption`, `SetUIntOption`, `SetNumeralOption`, `rationalOptionText`, `SetSymbolOption`, `SetStringOption`). The routing of integer tokens to `SetUIntOption` and the error column are in `pkg/parsers/smt2/commands.go:446-510` (outside this shard).
- C++: `src/cmd_context/basic_cmds.cpp:367-541` (`set_option_cmd`), `:325-333` (`is_builtin_option`)

**C++ behavior.**
- `set_symbol` calls `to_bool(value)` for every Boolean built-in (`invalid option value, true/false expected`).
- `:print-warning` calls `enable_warning_messages`.
- `:expand-definitions` sets `m_unsupported` (prints `unsupported` plus the `;` diagnostic).
- `check_not_initialized` throws `error setting ':<opt>', option value cannot be modified after initialization`, naming `:produce-assertions` for `:interactive-mode` and `:global-decls` for `:global-declarations`.
- Numerals: only `:random-seed`, `:reproducible-resource-limit` (written to `ctx.params().set_rlimit`, not gparams) and `:verbosity` are special. Any other built-in throws `option value is not a numeral`. Everything else is `set_param(val.to_string())`, and `rational::to_string` prints `3/2`.
- Strings: built-ins other than the two channels throw `option value is not a string`.

**Go behavior.**
- Boolean built-ins are matched only when the parser has already seen `true`/`false`. Anything else goes to `Globals.SourceSetName`, which gives the gparams "unknown parameter" list.
- `print_warning` and `expand_definitions` are not handled.
- The initialization error lacks the `error setting ':…', ` prefix.
- `rationalOptionText` prints `1.5`, not `3/2`.
- `timeout`/`rlimit` decimals give `option value is too big to fit in a machine integer.`.
- `reproducible_resource_limit` is renamed to the gparams-visible `rlimit`.

**Impact.** Front-end leads 2, 3 and 4 in `leads/front_end.md` are rooted here. The text diffs below are wrong error messages. `(set-option :smt.qi.eager_threshold 1.5)` stores a different value: z3 parses `3/2` with strtod and gets 3, g3 stores 1.5, so the solver runs with a different parameter.

**Reproduction.** g3 vs z3:
- `(set-option :expand-definitions true)`: g3 `unknown parameter 'expand_definitions' ...`; z3 `unsupported` / `; :expand-definitions line: 1 position: 1`.
- `(set-option :print-success 3)`: g3 `unknown parameter 'print_success'`; z3 `option value is not a numeral`.
- `(set-option :produce-models foo)`: g3 `unknown parameter 'produce_models'`; z3 `invalid option value, true/false expected`.
- `(set-option :int-real-coercions foo)`: g3 unknown parameter; z3 `invalid option value, true/false expected`.
- `(set-option :random-seed "a")`: g3 `unknown parameter 'random_seed', this is an old parameter name...`; z3 `option value is not a string`.
- `(set-option :print-warning false)(get-option :print-warning)`: g3 errors on the set; z3 accepts it (then the get prints `unsupported`).
- `(set-option :produce-proofs true)(declare-const x Int)(set-option :produce-proofs false)`: g3 `option value cannot be modified after initialization`; z3 `error setting ':produce-proofs', option value cannot be modified after initialization`. With `:interactive-mode` z3 names `':produce-assertions'`.
- `(set-option :smt.qi.eager_threshold 1.5)(get-option :smt.qi.eager_threshold)`: g3 `1.5`; z3 `3`. With `0.25`, z3 prints `1`.
- `(set-option :timeout 1.5)`: g3 `option value is too big to fit in a machine integer.`; z3 `Expected values for parameter timeout is an unsigned integer. It was given argument '3/2'`.
- `(set-option :reproducible-resource-limit 5)(get-option :rlimit)`: g3 `5`; z3 `0`.

**Fix.**
1. Replace the per-kind entry points with one port of `set_option_cmd`. Keep the original keyword. Add `isBuiltinOption(name)` with the C++ list (no `numeral_as_real`, `error_behavior`, `int_real_coercions`).
2. Symbol value: dispatch as in `set_symbol`, calling `toBool(value)` on each Boolean built-in. Wire `print_warning` to the warning service enable flag. Make `expand_definitions` return an "unsupported" marker the parser prints. Use the C++ `check_not_initialized` text and option names. The "built-in → `option value is not a symbol`" branch comes before the gparams fallback.
3. Numeral value: `random_seed` / `reproducible_resource_limit` (context param only) / `verbosity` with `to_unsigned`. Other built-ins: `option value is not a numeral`. Everything else: `rational::to_string` text (`num/den` for non-integers, no decimal rendering), so delete `rationalOptionText`'s decimal branch.
4. String value: the two channels; other built-ins: `option value is not a string`.
5. In `commands.go`, pass integer tokens through the numeral path (`SetNumeralOption`), not `SetUIntOption`, so that `:timeout 99999999999` reaches gparams as z3 does. Raise the error at the value token's position (C++ throws from `set_next_arg`), which also fixes the column lead 5.

**Regression test.** Add one `test_vectors/set_option_builtin_*.smt2` per bullet above with the z3 outputs in `scriptResults`, and check them with `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference`. Extend `pkg/cmd_context/context_test.go` with `TestSetNumeralOptionUsesRationalText`: `SetNumeralOption("smt.qi.eager_threshold", 3/2)` must leave the global `"3"` after strtod semantics (or `"3/2"` as the stored text).

<a id="cmd-context-01-f7"></a>
#### cmd_context_01-F7: the fixedpoint `query` command uses the global `timeout`, and a canceled query is reported as a positioned error

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/fixedpoint_timeout.go:17-32` (`fixedpointTimeout`), `pkg/cmd_context/fixedpoint_query_exception.go:15-23` (`classifyFixedpointQueryException`) together with `pkg/muz/fp/query_exception.go:19`
- C++: `src/muz/fp/dl_cmds.cpp:247-268` (`dl_query_cmd::execute`); `src/muz/base/fixedpoint_params.pyg:4`

**C++ behavior.** `unsigned timeout = m_dl_ctx->get_params().timeout();` is `fixedpoint.timeout`, default `UINT_MAX`. The global `timeout` is not consulted. Every `z3_exception` from `rel_query`, cancellation included, prints `(error "query failed: <msg>")` and then the status switch (`unknown`, plus a status line where one applies).

**Go behavior.**
```
defaultTimeout, err := c.config.Params.GetUIntName(&c.params, &name, math.MaxUint32)  // c.params "timeout" = (set-option :timeout N)
```
A cancellation error is not one of the classified "source default exceptions". It therefore escapes the command as `(error "line L column C: <wrapped message>")`, with no `unknown`.

**Impact.** `(set-option :timeout N)` cancels Horn queries that z3 runs to completion. Cancellation output differs in form and text.

**Reproduction.**
```
(set-option :timeout 200)
(declare-rel inv (Int Int))
(declare-rel err ())
(declare-var x Int)
(declare-var y Int)
(rule (inv 0 0))
(rule (=> (and (inv x y) (< x 300)) (inv (+ x 1) (+ y 2))))
(rule (=> (and (inv x y) (= x 300) (= y 600)) err))
(query err)
```
g3: `(error "line 9 column 10: canceled")` after 0.24 s. z3: `sat` after 0.6 s.
With `(set-option :fixedpoint.timeout 200)` instead: g3 `(error "line 9 column 10: muz/pdr: reachability check: muz/pdr: Farkas lemma extraction: canceled")`; z3 `(error "query failed: canceled")` then `unknown`.

**Fix.**
1. In `fixedpointTimeout`, use `math.MaxUint32` as the default, not the context's `timeout`: `GetUIntFallbackName(params, "timeout", &module, math.MaxUint32)`.
2. In `classifyFixedpointQueryException` (or `fp.SourceDefaultExceptionMessage`), treat a resource-limit cancellation as a caught `z3_exception` whose message is the limit's cancel message (`canceled`). The parser then prints `query failed: canceled` and goes on to the status switch (`unknown`; `canceled` plus the profile only when `dlctx.get_status()==CANCELED`). Strip the Go wrapping prefixes from the message.

**Regression test.** Add `test_vectors/fixedpoint_global_timeout_ignored.smt2` (the script above), expected `sat\n`, and `test_vectors/fixedpoint_query_canceled.smt2`, expected `(error "query failed: canceled")\nunknown\n`. Mark the second one timing-sensitive or use a deterministic `fixedpoint.timeout` with a long-running instance. Check with `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference`.

<a id="cmd-context-01-f8"></a>
#### cmd_context_01-F8: `WriteEcho` doubles embedded quotes in SMT-LIB2-compliant mode

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/echo_command.go:31-33` (`WriteEcho`)
- C++: `src/cmd_context/basic_cmds.cpp:294-296` (`echo_cmd`)

**C++ behavior.** `ctx.regular_stream() << (smt2c ? "\"" : "") << arg << (smt2c ? "\"" : "") << std::endl;` wraps the string in quotes and nothing else.

**Go behavior.** `value = "\"" + strings.ReplaceAll(value, "\"", "\"\"") + "\""`. The comment documents the doubling as intended, and `echo_command_mode_test.go:21` asserts it.

**Impact.** In compliant mode, `echo` output differs from z3 for any string that contains `"`.

**Reproduction.** A file with `(set-option :smtlib2_compliant true)` and `(echo "a""b")`: g3 prints `"a""b"`, z3 prints `"a"b"`.

**Fix.** Use `value = "\"" + value + "\""`. Update `TestWriteEchoUsesRawAndCompliantSourceRepresentations` to expect `"\"a\"b\"\n"`.

<a id="cmd-context-01-f9"></a>
#### cmd_context_01-F9: the Datalog front end is a re-implementation, not a port of `dlexer`/`dparser`

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/datalog_lexer.go:47-166`, `datalog_parser_domains.go:19-103`, `datalog_parser_rules.go`, `datalog_parser_declarations.go`, `datalog_parser_terms.go`, `datalog_parser_errors.go`
- C++: `src/muz/fp/datalog_parser.cpp:230-463` (`dlexer`), `:566-1048` (`dparser`)

**C++ behavior (selected).**
1. `parse_domain` for `X int` returns the `TK_NEWLINE` token without consuming it, so `parse_domains` returns at once: an `int` domain ends the domain section.
2. `read_id` stops only at `( ) # , : =`, `.` (outside domains) and whitespace. `<`, `>` and `!` are ordinary ID characters, so `X<Y` is one identifier, and `<`/`>` are recognized only through `reserved_symbols` on a whole token.
3. Backslash: `save_char('\\')`, then `lookahead_newline` keeps the spaces in the buffer. `\ #comment` is a line continuation.
4. `|..|` contents go through `string2dtoken`, so `|_|` is a wildcard.
5. Errors are `default_exception("%s at line %u '%s' found '%s'\n")`. The driver prints them and then `ERROR: failed to parse file`.
6. A finite domain of size 0 reaches `register_finite_sort`, which errors with `Domain size of sort 'V' may not be 0`.
7. A predicate first used in a body is registered as a declaration (no error).
8. Constant numbering comes from `context::get_constant_number`; overflow reports `sort V contains more constants than its declared size 2`.

**Go behavior.**
1. After `int` it consumes the newline and keeps parsing domains.
2. `<`, `>` and `!` always end an identifier.
3. A continuation drops the spaces, and `\ #comment` becomes the identifier `\`.
4. Quoted identifiers are always identifiers.
5. Errors are `datalog:L:C: expected …, found …`.
6. Size 0 gives `invalid domain size "0"`.
7. A body predicate not seen before gives "must be declared before use".
8. Overflow gives `constant "3" exceeds finite domain size 2`.

**Impact.** Some files that z3 rejects are accepted by g3 (and the reverse), and every Datalog error message differs.

**Reproduction.** (`<f>.datalog`, g3 vs z3)
- `V int\nW 5\n\nedge(a:W, b:W) printtuples\nedge(1,2).\n`: g3 prints the `edge` tuples. z3 prints `unexpected token at line 2 '5' found '<num>'` and `ERROR: failed to parse file`.
- `V 10\n\nedge(a:V, b:V) printtuples\nedge(1,2)\n`: g3 `ERROR: Datalog parse t.datalog: datalog:4:10: expected :- or period, found newline ""`; z3 `'.' expected at the end of rule at line 5 '' found '\n'` / `ERROR: failed to parse file`.
- `V 0\n...`: g3 `invalid domain size "0"`; z3 `Domain size of sort 'V' may not be 0`.
- `V 2\n\nedge(a:V) printtuples\nedge(1).\nedge(2).\nedge(3).\n`: g3 `constant "3" exceeds finite domain size 2`; z3 `sort V contains more constants than its declared size 2`.

**Fix.** Port `dlexer` character by character: `m_prev_char`/`m_curr_char`, the `next_token` switch, `read_id` terminators, `read_bid` plus `string2dtoken`, `lookahead_newline`, `read_comment`'s `line_comment`, and `m_line` incremented only where C++ increments it. Port `dparser` with its token-returning structure, including `parse_domain`'s unconsumed newline after `int`, `parse_pred`'s declaration-on-first-use, `unexpected`'s message format and `dtoken_strings`, and constant numbering through the datalog context's `get_constant_number`. The shell driver must print the message followed by `ERROR: failed to parse file`.

**Regression test.** Put the four inputs in `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/datalog_*.datalog` and compare them with `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference` (or the Datalog front-end test in `pkg/shell`). Extend `pkg/cmd_context/datalog_lexer_test.go` with `TestDatalogLexerIdentifierTerminators` (`X<Y` lexes as one ID; `X < Y` gives ID, `<`, ID; `|_|` is a wildcard) and `datalog_parser_test.go` with `TestDatalogIntDomainEndsDomainSection`.

<a id="cmd-context-01-f10"></a>
#### cmd_context_01-F10: a popped macro name still blocks bare function-declaration references in C++ but not in Go

- Severity: low
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/macros.go:121-125` (`restoreMacros` deletes the map entry), `function_references.go:62-73`
- C++: `src/cmd_context/cmd_context.cpp:272-277, 308-312` (`erase_last` keeps the `m_macros` entry), `:918-920` (`find_func_decl(s)` tests `contains_macro(s)`)

**C++ behavior.** `erase_macro` pops the last `macro_decl` but leaves the empty `macro_decls` entry in `m_macros`, so `contains_macro(s)` stays true after `pop`. A bare func-decl reference then fails with `named expressions (aka macros) cannot be referenced`.

**Go behavior.** `delete(c.macros, name)` when the last body is popped.

**Impact.** The lookup succeeds in g3 and fails in z3.

**Reproduction.** `(push)(define-fun g ((x Bool)) Bool x)(pop)(declare-fun g (Bool) Bool)(declare-map m (Int) g)(echo "ok")`: g3 prints `ok`; z3 prints `(error "line 1 column 92: invalid function declaration reference, named expressions (aka macros) cannot be referenced g")` then `ok`.

**Fix.** Keep a (possibly empty) entry per name: in `restoreMacros`, set `c.macros[name] = values[:len(values)-1]` even when it becomes empty. In `FindFunctionDeclaration`'s bare form, test key presence (`_, found := c.macros[name]`), not a non-empty slice. `reset_macros` is the only place that removes entries.

**Regression test.** Add `test_vectors/macro_name_survives_pop.smt2` (the script above) with the z3 output, and check it with `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference`.

<a id="cmd-context-01-f11"></a>
#### cmd_context_01-F11: `DeclareMap` checks and error texts differ from `declare_map_cmd`

- Severity: low
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/array_map.go:14-61` (`DeclareMap`)
- C++: `src/cmd_context/basic_cmds.cpp:773-806` (`declare_map_cmd`)

**C++ behavior.** `set_next_arg(sorts)` throws `invalid map declaration, empty sort list` when the sort list is parsed. `execute` throws `Array sort is not available` when the logic hides `Array`, and builds the sorts with `array_sort->instantiate` (psort instantiation). A null declaration gives `invalid array map operator`.

**Go behavior.** All checks run at execute. There is no `Array` availability check, so the error comes from check_logic: `logic does not support arrays`. The sorts come from `m.MkArraySort`, and plugin errors are wrapped as `invalid array map operator: %w`.

**Impact.** Different error texts and columns.

**Reproduction.**
- `(set-logic QF_UF)(declare-map u (Bool) (or (Bool Bool) Bool))`: g3 `logic does not support arrays`; z3 `Array sort is not available`.
- `(declare-map u () (or (Bool Bool) Bool))`: g3 `line 1 column 40`; z3 `line 1 column 19`.

**Fix.** At the top of `DeclareMap`, add `if !c.BuiltinSortAvailable("Array") { return …"Array sort is not available" }`. Check the empty list in the parser when the sort list closes, and the arity when the func-decl argument is parsed. Drop the `: %w` suffix.

**Regression test.** Add `test_vectors/declare_map_errors.smt2` with both lines and the z3 outputs.

<a id="cmd-context-01-f14"></a>
#### cmd_context_01-F14: `Pop` releases declarations and macros in a different order than `cmd_context::pop`

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/context.go:1368-1392` (`Pop`), `:1395-1432` (`restoreDeclarations`), `pkg/cmd_context/macros.go:110-129` (`restoreMacros`)
- C++: `src/cmd_context/cmd_context.cpp:1425-1450` (`pop`), `:1343-1352` (`restore_func_decls`), `:1377-1386` (`restore_macros`)

**C++ behavior.** `restore_func_decls` → `restore_psort_decls` → `restore_macros` → `restore_aux_pdecls` → `restore_assertions` → `restore_psort_inst`. Function declarations and macro bodies are `dec_ref`ed in forward stack order.

**Go behavior.** It runs `restorePSortDecls`, then `restoreMacros` (backward), then `restoreDeclarations`. That one erases forward from the dictionary but drops the owning trail refs backward. Sorts are also released backward.

**Impact.** AST ids are recycled LIFO by the Go manager emulation, so the order in which declarations die after a `pop` decides the ids of new terms. That changes hash-table orders, and so search order and traces, in incremental scripts with scoped declarations.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: needs an id-sensitive trace comparison.

**Fix.** Reorder `Pop` to: functions (release each trail ref forward, at the point `erase_func_decl_core` would `dec_ref`), psorts, macros (forward over `macroTrail[size:]`, erasing the last body of each name), aux pdecls/sort constructors, assertions, psort instances. Then truncate the trails.

**Regression test.** Add `TestPopReleasesDeclarationsForward` in `pkg/cmd_context/context_test.go`. Declare `a`, `b`, `c` inside a push, pop, then create three fresh constants, and compare their AST ids with the ids the C++ order produces (forward release, so LIFO reuse gives `c`'s id first). Or record the release order through the manager's debug-ref-count hook.

<a id="cmd-context-01-f15"></a>
#### cmd_context_01-F15: `validateModel` builds its evaluator without `max_degree`/`sort_store`, and its under-specified scan skips quantifier bodies

- Severity: low
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/model_completion.go:176-187, 256-305` (`validateModel`, `hasUnderSpecifiedModelOps`)
- C++: `src/cmd_context/cmd_context.cpp:1771-1808` (`validate_model`), `src/ast/for_each_expr.h:24-102`

**C++ behavior.** `p.set_uint("max_degree", UINT_MAX); p.set_uint("sort_store", true); p.set_bool("completion", true); model_evaluator evaluator(*md, p);`. `for_each_expr` visits quantifier children (body, patterns) too.

**Go behavior.** `model.NewModelEvaluator(md, c.config.ModelEvaluator)` plus `SetModelCompletion(true)`, with the default `max_degree` and `sort_store`. `hasUnderSpecifiedModelOps` `continue`s on non-app nodes, so it never descends into a quantifier.

**Impact.** With `model_validate=true`, g3 can raise `an invalid model was generated` where z3 stays silent: an assertion that evaluates to an algebraic number above degree 64, store-sorted array equalities, or a ground quantified assertion that contains `store`/an accessor and evaluates to false.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted.

**Fix.** Pass a params ref with `max_degree=4294967295` and `sort_store=true` to the evaluator, or add the setters. In the scan, push the quantifier body, patterns and no-patterns for `ast.ASTQuantifier`.

<a id="cmd-context-01-f16"></a>
#### cmd_context_01-F16: the OPB loader builds a different AST from `opb::parse`

- Severity: low
- Confidence: medium
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/opb_loader.go:20-87`, `opb_terms.go:10-35`, `opb_variables.go:9-27`
- C++: `src/opt/opt_parse.cpp:198-302` (`opb::parse_id`, `parse_ids`, `parse_term`, `parse_objective`, `parse_constraint`, `parse`)

**C++ behavior.**
- Variables are `m.mk_const(symbol(id), bool)`, a **numerical** symbol, not a cmd_context declaration.
- A product of literals is `m.mk_and(result, parse_id())`: nested binary `and`s.
- `parse_term` builds the coefficient first, then the literals, then a fresh `0`.
- Objectives and constraints are built in file order.
- The opt frontend uses a plain `opt::context` with no logic.

**Go behavior.**
- Variables are declared with the **string** symbol `"5"`.
- A product is one flat `MkAndArray`.
- `0` is built once before anything else, and the literals before the coefficient.
- All objectives are built before all constraints.
- The shell selects `QF_LIA` (`pkg/shell/opb_frontend.go:43`; the comment at `opb_loader.go:17-19` documents it).

**Impact.** AST shapes and ids differ for OPB input, and so do symbol hashes and the solver logic, which may change search order and statistics. The objective values printed on the test file matched. The `-st` difference seen is the already-recorded FUZZ_J-F6.

**Reproduction.** Not separable from FUZZ_J-F6 with stdout.

**Fix.** Port `opb::parse` directly. Keep the same token loop and construction order; create variables with `m.MkConst(usymbol.Numerical(id), bool)`; nest `and` binarily; build the constraint/objective as soon as it is read. Drop `SetLogic("QF_LIA")` in the shell so the solver logic is null, as in `opt_frontend.cpp`.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/cmd_context`, add `TestOPBLoaderBuildsSourceShapes`. Load `+3 x1 x2 x3 >= 2 ;` and assert that the left side prints as `(ite (and (and k!1 k!2) k!3) 3 0)`.

<a id="cmd-context-02-f1"></a>
#### cmd_context_02-F1: `get-consequences` leaves no model and an empty reason-unknown (Context.Consequences / SMTSolver.GetConsequences)

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/result_access.go:62-86` (`Context.Consequences`); root in `pkg/smtcore/smt_solver.go:868-930` (`SMTSolver.GetConsequences`)
- C++: `src/cmd_context/cmd_context.cpp:1535-1557` (`cmd_context::get_consequences`)

**C++ behavior.**
```
m_check_sat_result = m_solver.get(); // solver itself stores the result.
...
r = m_solver->get_consequences(assumptions, vars, conseq);
catch (z3_exception & ex) { m_solver->set_reason_unknown(ex.msg()); r = l_undef; }
m_solver->set_status(r);
display_sat_result(r);
```
The solver is the check-sat result. After a sat `get-consequences`, the solver's model is available to `get-model` / `eval` / `get-value`, and its `reason_unknown()` is "unknown".

**Go behavior.** `Consequences` clears the result (`clearCheckSatResult`) and sets `c.status, c.checked`. `SMTSolver.GetConsequences` installs a fresh empty `SimpleCheckSatResult` (`replaceResult(result)`) and never stores the kernel model or a reason into it. So `checkSatResult()` returns a result without a model, and its reason text is "".

**Impact.** Any script or API client that asks for the model after `get-consequences` gets an error instead of the model, and `(get-info :reason-unknown)` prints "" instead of "unknown".

**Reproduction.** Confirmed.
```
(set-option :produce-models true)(declare-const x Bool)(assert x)(get-consequences () (x))(get-model)
```
g3: `sat` / `` / `(=> true x)` / `(error "line 1 column 101: model is not available")`
z3: `sat` / `` / `(=> true x)` / `(model (define-fun x () Bool true))`

```
(declare-const x Bool)(assert x)(get-consequences () (x))(get-info :reason-unknown)
```
g3: `(:reason-unknown "")`; z3: `(:reason-unknown "unknown")`.

**Fix.**
1. In `SMTSolver.GetConsequences`, publish the kernel's model (`s.kernel.GeneratedModel()`, the model `smt_solver::get_model` returns) into the result it installs. Also set the status. For the reason, use what `smt_solver::reason_unknown` returns after `context::get_consequences` (z3 prints "unknown", so mirror `last_failure_as_string()` and do not leave it empty).
2. In `Context.Consequences`, make the solver the check-sat result: leave `tacticResult` and `retainedSolverResult` nil so `checkSatResult()` returns `c.solver`.
3. Turn a non-fatal z3 exception into `SetReasonUnknown(msg)` plus `l_undef`, as the C++ catch does, instead of returning the error.

**Regression test.** Add `consequences_get_model.smt2` to `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/` with the first script above. Expected `scriptResults` entry: `"sat\n\n(=> true x)\n(model \n  (define-fun x () Bool\n    true)\n)\n"` (copy the exact model text from z3). Add a second vector with the reason-unknown script, expected output ending in `(:reason-unknown "unknown")`. Check both with `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3`.

<a id="cmd-context-02-f2"></a>
#### cmd_context_02-F2: WCNF input runs normalize's simplify_fmls; opt::context::m_is_clausal is not ported

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/wcnf_loader.go:14-44` (`LoadWCNF`); `pkg/cmd_context/optimization_normalized_execution.go:51,91-139` (`runNormalizedOptimization`, `useSimplifier`)
- C++: `src/opt/opt_parse.cpp:155-157` (`wcnf::wcnf` → `opt.set_clausal(true)`); `src/opt/opt_context.cpp:748-751` (`simplify_fmls`)

**C++ behavior.**
```
wcnf(opt::context& opt, ...) { opt.set_clausal(true); }
...
void context::simplify_fmls(expr_ref_vector& fmls) {
    if (m_is_clausal) { return; }
```
The C++ also creates WCNF variables with the numeric symbol `symbol(var)` (printed `k!N`) through `m.mk_const`, without a cmd_context declaration (opt_parse.cpp:138).

**Go behavior.** No clausal flag exists anywhere in `pkg`. `LoadWCNF` asserts and adds soft clauses into the command context. `runNormalizedOptimization` then always runs the simplify / propagate-values / solve-eqs / simplify chain and, with `opt.elim_01`, dt2bv / elim01 / lia2card / eq2bv / simplify. Variables are string symbols "N" declared through `DeclareFunction`.

**Impact.** Every WCNF run does preprocessing that z3 skips. Propagate-values and solve-eqs eliminate variables (the verbose output shows `(:num-elim-vars 2)`), so the MaxSAT search, its statistics and its rlimit count diverge. The optimum stays the same.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed with `a.wcnf`:
```
p wcnf 4 6 10
10 1 0
10 -1 2 0
3 -2 0
2 3 4 0
4 -3 0
1 -4 0
```
`g3 -v:10 a.wcnf` begins `(simplifier ...)(propagate-values ...)(:num-elim-vars 2)(solve_eqs ...)(simplifier ...)(dt2bv ...)(elim01 ...)(cardinality-intro ...)(eq2bv ...)(simplifier ...)`.
`z3 -v:10 a.wcnf` begins `(optimize:check-sat)(card2bv ...)` with no simplify_fmls stages. Its maxres trace prints cores over `k!2`, `k!3`, `k!4`.
Both print `sat` / `   4`.

**Fix.**
1. Add `optimizationClausal bool` to `Context` with a `SetOptimizationClausal(bool)` setter, and call it from `LoadWCNF` (not from `LoadOPB`; opb never sets it).
2. In `runNormalizedOptimization`, when clausal, skip `simplifyOptimizationFormulas` but still run from_fmls: `fmls` passes through unchanged.
3. In `makeWCNFClause`, build the variable as `mk_const(symbol(var), Bool)` with a numerical symbol (the symbol manager needs a numeric-symbol constructor, as the API's `Z3_mk_int_symbol` path has). Do not publish it as a cmd_context declaration.
4. Reset the flag where opt::context is recreated.

**Regression test.** Extend the shell WCNF tests in `pkg/shell` (next to the existing `wcnf_frontend` tests). Run `a.wcnf` with verbosity 10 and assert that no line starts with `(simplifier` before the first `(card2bv`. Also check that the maxres core lines name `k!2`.

<a id="cmd-context-02-f3"></a>
#### cmd_context_02-F3: get-assignment walks named terms in insertion order, not the m_macros dictionary order

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/results.go:330-359` (`WriteAssignment`)
- C++: `src/cmd_context/basic_cmds.cpp:129-162` (`get_assignment_cmd`)

**C++ behavior.**
```
dictionary<macro_decls> const & macros = ctx.get_macros();
for (auto const& kv : macros) { ... for (auto md : _m) { ... print (name val) ... } }
```
`dictionary<T>` is a `core_hashtable` keyed by symbol hash. Iteration is in table order. `erase_macro` only `erase_last`s the vector and leaves the key in the table until `reset_macros`.

**Go behavior.** `for _, name := range c.macroTrail` (insertion order, first occurrence).

**Impact.** Any `get-assignment` with two or more named Boolean terms prints the pairs in a different order.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed with `asg.smt2`:
```
(set-option :produce-assignments true)
(declare-const a Bool)(declare-const b Bool)(declare-const c Bool)
(assert (! a :named zeta))(assert (! (not b) :named alpha))(assert (! (or c a) :named mid))
(assert (! (and a (not b)) :named beta))(assert (! c :named omega1))
(check-sat)(get-assignment)
```
g3: `((zeta true) (alpha true) (mid true) (beta true) (omega1 true))`
z3: `((omega1 true) (beta true) (zeta true) (alpha true) (mid true))`

**Fix.**
1. Keep an m_macros dictionary using the existing `symbolDictionary` (`symbol_dictionary.go`): add a `macros bool` payload, and call `insertIfNotThere(name)` in `defineFunction` (`insert_macro`).
2. Do not erase the key in `restoreMacros` (C++ `erase_macro` leaves it). Call `reset()` only in reset_macros (context reset).
3. In `WriteAssignment`, iterate `dict.entries()` and, for each, `c.macros[name]` in vector order.

**Regression test.** Add `get_assignment_order.smt2` to `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/` with the script above. Expected `scriptResults` entry: `"sat\n((omega1 true) (beta true) (zeta true) (alpha true) (mid true))\n"`. Check it with `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference`.

<a id="cmd-context-02-f4"></a>
#### cmd_context_02-F4: define-fun-rec with a variable body: the macro is scoped and checked in Go; C++ insert_macro is neither

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/recursive_functions.go:80-90` (`DefineRecursiveFunction`) → `pkg/cmd_context/macros.go:47-110` (`defineFunction`)
- C++: `src/cmd_context/cmd_context.cpp:878-884` (`insert_rec_fun`), `:297-306` (`insert_macro`)

**C++ behavior.**
```
if (is_var(e)) { ... insert_macro(f->get_name(), domain.size(), domain.c_ptr(), e); return; }
```
`insert_macro` does no builtin or duplicate checks (it only `VERIFY`s), and nothing is pushed on `m_macros_stack`, so `pop` does not remove the macro.

**Go behavior.** It calls `c.defineFunction(text, domain, body, true)`. That runs the builtin and `containsMacro` checks and appends to `c.macroTrail`, so `pop` removes the macro.

**Impact.** Results differ after push/pop around such a definition.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed.
```
(push)(define-fun-rec f ((x Int)) Int x)(pop)(assert (= (f 1) 2))(check-sat)
```
g3: `(error "line 1 column 61: unknown function/constant f")` then `sat`. z3: `unsat`.
```
(push)(define-fun-rec f ((x Int)) Int x)(pop)(declare-fun f (Int) Int)(assert (= (f 1) 2))(check-sat)
```
g3: `sat`. z3: `(error "line 1 column 70: invalid declaration, named expression already defined with this name f")` then `unsat`.

**Fix.** Add `insertMacroUnscoped(name, domain, body)`: pin the refs, `append(c.macros[name], d)`, and record the name in the macro dictionary from F3, but without a `macroTrail` entry and without the builtin, `containsMacro` or declaration checks. Call it from `DefineRecursiveFunction` instead of `defineFunction`. If a z3 4.7.1 bug exclusion is wanted instead, add it to `z3_bug_exclusions.txt` and document it next to the code.

**Regression test.** Add `define_fun_rec_var_body_pop.smt2` to `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/` with the first script. Expected `scriptResults` entry: `"unsat\n"`.

<a id="cmd-context-02-f5"></a>
#### cmd_context_02-F5: get-option matches the built-in keywords after "-"→"_" normalization; C++ compares the raw keyword

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/options.go:18` (`GetOption`)
- C++: `src/cmd_context/basic_cmds.cpp:564-625` (`get_option_cmd::set_next_arg`)

**C++ behavior.** `if (opt == m_print_success)` and the other branches compare against the keyword symbols `:print-success`, `:produce-models` and so on. Any other spelling goes to `gparams::get_value(opt)`, which throws for these names, so z3 prints `unsupported`.

**Go behavior.** `name = strings.ReplaceAll(strings.TrimPrefix(name, ":"), "-", "_")` runs before the switch, so `:produce_models`, `:print_success`, `:random_seed` and `:int_real_coercions` return values.

**Impact.** Underscore spellings of the SMT-LIB options print a value in g3 and `unsupported` in z3.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed.
`(get-option :produce_models)`: g3 `true`; z3 `unsupported` (plus the `; :produce_models line: 1 position: 1` diagnostic).
The same happens for `:print_success` (false), `:random_seed` (0) and `:int_real_coercions` (true).
`timeout`, `rlimit` and the module parameters match.

**Fix.** Switch on the raw keyword with its dashes (`":print-success"`, `":interactive-mode"`, `":produce-assertions"`, ...). Strip only the colon for the `gparams` fallback. Normalize nothing before the switch. Keep the `expand-definitions` branch as unsupported. `timeout` and `rlimit` are not C++ branches; let them fall through to the globals lookup if its output matches.

**Regression test.** Add `get_option_underscore.smt2` with `(get-option :produce_models)(get-option :print_success)`. Expected stdout: `"unsupported\nunsupported\n"`. Also add a focused unit test in `pkg/cmd_context` (look at `options_test.go`, or create it) asserting that `GetOption(":produce_models")` returns `supported == false`.

<a id="cmd-context-02-f6"></a>
#### cmd_context_02-F6: check-sat-using: print_unsat_core printed only for unsat, and core/model/proof stored regardless of the produce_* options

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/tactic_commands.go:509-532` (`CheckSatUsing`); printer at `pkg/parsers/smt2/tactics.go:707` (outside this shard)
- C++: `src/cmd_context/tactic_cmds.cpp:255-285` (`check_sat_using_tactict_cmd::execute`)

**C++ behavior.**
```
if (ctx.produce_unsat_cores()) { ... result->m_core.append(...);
    if (p.get_bool("print_unsat_core", false)) { "(unsat-core" ... ")" } }
if (ctx.produce_models() && md) { result->m_model = md; ... if (status == l_true) ctx.validate_model(); }
if (ctx.produce_proofs() && pr) { result->m_proof = pr; ... }
```
The core is printed for any status.

**Go behavior.** The core, model and proof are always stored (`r.SetModel`, `r.SetProof`, `r.SetUnsatCore`). The parser prints the core only when `status == lbool.False`. `validateModel` runs whenever the status is true. On a caught tactic exception, `CheckSatUsing` returns early, before the core, model, proof and statistics blocks the C++ still executes.

**Impact.** Output differs for sat runs with `:print_unsat_core true`. A model is available after `check-sat-using` even with `produce-models` false, where C++ reports "model is not available".

**Reproduction.** Confirmed.
```
(set-option :produce-unsat-cores true)(declare-const x Bool)(assert (! x :named a))(check-sat-using smt :print_unsat_core true)
```
g3: `sat`; z3: `sat` / `(unsat-core)`.

**Fix.**
1. In `CheckSatUsing`, guard the three setters with `state.UnsatCore`, `state.Model && model != nil` and `state.Proof && !proof.IsNull()`, and call `validateModel` only inside the model guard.
2. In `tactics.go`, drop the `status == lbool.False` condition on printing the core.
3. On the caught-exception path, return after the same core, model and proof blocks, so `print_statistics` and the core still print.

**Regression test.** Add `check_sat_using_print_core_sat.smt2` with the script above. Expected `scriptResults` entry: `"sat\n(unsat-core)\n"`.

<a id="cmd-context-02-f9"></a>
#### cmd_context_02-F9: Z3_optimize_to_string is the Go-only replay exporter, not opt::context::to_string

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: high
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/replay_smt2.go:264-317` (`WriteReplaySMT2`, no C++ counterpart), used by `pkg/cmd_context/optimization_api.go:91` and `pkg/api/api_optimize_display.go:27` (API id 556)
- C++: `src/opt/opt_context.cpp:1461-1528` (`context::to_string`)

**C++ behavior.**
1. `ast_pp_util` collects the hard constraints and objective terms.
2. It prints the declarations, then `display_asserts(out, hard, m_pp_neat)`.
3. It prints `(maximize ..)`, `(minimize ..)`, and `(assert-soft t :weight w.ddd :id id)` with `display_decimal(…,3,true)`.
4. It prints `m_params.display_smt2(out, "opt", descrs)`, then `(check-sat)\n`.

**Go behavior.** It prints `(set-option :produce-models …)` / `:produce-proofs` / `:produce-unsat-cores` / `:global-declarations` lines and `(set-logic …)`. It replays the push structure with `(push 1)` and per-scope declarations, then the objectives. There are no opt parameter lines and no `(check-sat)`.

**Impact.** API clients calling `Z3_optimize_to_string` get a different string. The trace replay discards the string, but AST creation during printing may still differ.

**Reproduction.** Not attempted: the API is only reachable through the API trace replayer. Reading `WriteReplaySMT2` against the C++ settles it.

**Fix.**
1. Implement `Context.WriteOptimizationSMT2` as a port of `to_string`, using `ast.NewASTPPUtil`: `Collect` the hard constraints, then each objective's term or soft terms in order, then `DisplayDeclarations` and the asserts.
2. Print the objectives, then the opt-module parameter display, then `(check-sat)`.
3. Point `APIOptimize.SMT2` at it.
4. Keep `WriteReplaySMT2` only for Go-only callers, or delete it if it has no other consumer.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/api`, extend `api_optimization_objectives_order_test.go`, which already builds `newSMTAPIFixture(t, "ALL", nil)` with `Minimize`, `AssertSoft` and `Maximize`. Add `TestAPIOptimizeToStringMatchesSource`, asserting that the string ends with `(check-sat)\n` and contains `(assert-soft objective-order-p :weight 5.000 :id soft-middle)` (or the exact z3 output obtained through the C API).

#### cmd_context_02-F10: get_objective of a one-term MaxSMT group is wrapped in `+`

<a id="cmd-context-02-f11"></a>
#### cmd_context_02-F11: WPA directory benchmarks are implemented in Go; the C++ reference aborts (dead code on Linux)

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/wpa_parser.go`, `wpa_discover.go`, `wpa_map.go`, `wpa_map_line.go`, `wpa_relation.go`, `wpa_relation_line.go`, `wpa_rules.go`
- C++: `src/muz/base/dl_util.cpp:554-599` (`get_file_names` is `NOT_IMPLEMENTED_YET()` outside `_WINDOWS`), `src/muz/fp/datalog_parser.cpp:1173-1480`

**C++ behavior.** On Linux, `get_file_names` prints `NOT IMPLEMENTED YET!` and reaches `UNREACHABLE()`, which is `__builtin_unreachable` in the release build. So `wpa_parser_impl::parse_directory` never works, and the reference binary hangs.

**Go behavior.** A full loader. It also differs from the Windows C++ wherever that could be compared:
- `finishSorts` registers sorts in alphabetical order, where the C++ walks the `sym2nums` hash map.
- It silently ignores a map-name mismatch, where the C++ prints `warning_msg`.
- It rejects map files named BOOL or SHORT.
- It sorts file names.

**Reproduction.** Confirmed. Directory `wpa/` contains `V.map` (`1 a\n2 b\n`), `r.rules` (`e(x:V, y:V) input` / `p(x:V, y:V) printtuples` / `p(X,Y) :- e(X,Y).` / `p(X,Z) :- p(X,Y), e(Y,Z).`) and `e.rel` (`1 2\n2 1\n`). Running `-dl wpa`: g3 prints four tuples and exits 0; z3 prints `NOT IMPLEMENTED YET!` and is killed by `timeout 20` (rc 124).

**Fix.** Per project policy (port only live C++), replace `ParseWPADirectory` with the reference behavior: write `NOT IMPLEMENTED YET!` to stderr and exit with `ERR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED_YET`. Delete the seven wpa files. If the owner wants to keep the loader, record it as a deliberate deviation and at least iterate sorts in `sym2nums` order and emit the C++ warnings.

**Regression test.** Add a shell test in `pkg/shell` (next to the datalog frontend tests) that runs a directory input and expects the `NOT IMPLEMENTED YET!` diagnostic and the C++ exit code. Keep the input files under a `test_vectors` directory.
