<a id="cmd-context-02-f14"></a>
#### cmd_context_02-F14: declare-sort (arity 0) and define-sort create their sorts eagerly; C++ instantiates lazily

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: medium
- Go: `pkg/cmd_context/sort_declarations.go:44-56` (`DeclareSortConstructor`), `:85-94` (`DefineSort`)
- C++: `src/parsers/smt2/smt2parser.cpp:2159-2162` (`parse_declare_sort`), `src/cmd_context/pdecl.cpp:310-327` (`psort_user_decl::instantiate`)

**C++ behavior.** `declare-sort U` only inserts `mk_psort_user_decl(0, id, nullptr)`. The uninterpreted sort is created (and cached, `save_info`) on its first use, and never if it is unused. define-sort keeps a psort and instantiates it at use.

**Go behavior.** `MkUninterpretedSort` is called at declaration time. For a 0-ary define-sort, the body sort is built when the definition is parsed.

**Impact.** The AST creation order, and so the AST ids of every later term, differ whenever a sort is declared before other terms are built or never used. Anything keyed on ids (obj_map iteration orders, traces) can diverge. No stdout difference was found in quick probes.

**Fix.** Store 0-ary declarations as `sortConstructorDeclaration{arity:0}` and instantiate through `instantiateSortConstructor` (with its cache) on first lookup, as `psort_user_decl::instantiate` does. Do the same for 0-ary define-sort bodies by keeping the body unevaluated.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/cmd_context`, add a test that declares `U`, then a constant of sort Int, then a constant of sort U. Assert that the AST id of sort `U` is greater than the id of the Int constant's declaration.

### Area: Parsers and shell (`pkg/parsers`, `pkg/shell`)

*parsers_shell_01.* This shard holds the SMT-LIB2 command parser (`pkg/parsers/smt2`, a hand-written recursive-descent replacement for `smt2parser.cpp` plus the `basic_cmds`/`tactic_cmds`/`dbg_cmds` command bodies it dispatches to), the small `pkg/parsers/util` package (cost parser, simple parser, scanner, pattern validator, parser params), and the `pkg/shell` front ends (command line, SMT-LIB, DIMACS, Datalog, LP, OPB/WCNF, timeout). The scanner, local-binding environment and sorted-variable code follow the C++ closely. The command dispatcher does not. It replaces `parse_ext_cmd` and the per-command `parse_*` functions with Go code that checks `)` before it applies the command's effect, returns different error texts, and drops several semantic checks. These checks are missing: Boolean assert, empty binder list, `match`, built-in set-option kinds, and `:error-behavior`. Most findings were confirmed with both binaries. `build/z3` disappeared during the run (it was apparently being rebuilt). Later checks used `build_trace/z3`, which is the same C++ source with tracing enabled. Counts: 4 high, 9 medium, 6 low. The earlier front-end leads in this shard are now all fixed: items 1 (get-info/get-option order) and FUZZ-F4 (set-logic).

<a id="parsers-shell-01-f1"></a>
#### parsers_shell_01-F1: `assert` accepts a non-Boolean term (missing `is_bool` check)

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/parsers/smt2/commands.go:750-760` (`commandParser.command`, case `"assert"`); `pkg/cmd_context/context.go:1251` (`Context.AssertWithText`)
- C++: `src/parsers/smt2/smt2parser.cpp:2471-2482` (`parser::parse_assert`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
if (expr_stack().empty())
    throw cmd_exception("invalid assert command, expression required as argument");
expr * f = expr_stack().back();
if (!m().is_bool(f)) {
    throw cmd_exception("invalid assert command, term is not Boolean");
}
```

**Go behavior.** The Go code parses the expression, checks `)`, then calls `AssertWithText`. No sort check happens anywhere on that path. A search for `term is not Boolean` finds no Go code. The non-Boolean term goes to the solver.

**Impact.** Any script that asserts a non-Boolean term gets a different answer, and the solver is fed an ill-sorted assertion. `(assert 0)(check-sat)`: z3 rejects the assertion and prints `sat`. g3 prints `unknown`. `(declare-const x Real)(assert (* x x))(check-sat)(get-model)`: z3 prints `sat` and an empty model. g3 prints `unknown` and `model is not available`.

**Reproduction.**
```
(declare-const x Int)
(assert x)
(check-sat)
```
z3: `(error "line 2 column 9: invalid assert command, term is not Boolean")` then `sat`. g3: `sat` and no error. With `(assert 0)(check-sat)`, z3 gives the error then `sat`; g3 gives `unknown`.

**Fix.** In the `"assert"` case, after `p.assertionExpression()`, do what `parse_assert` does. First get the expression's sort. If it is not `MkBoolSort()`, return `errors.New("invalid assert command, term is not Boolean")`. Do this before the `)` check, as the C++ does (see F2). The error carries the position of the current token, which is the `)` after the term in the C++.

**Regression test.** Add `TestSMT2AssertRejectsNonBoolean` to `pkg/parsers/smt2/assertions_test.go`. Use `cmd_context.NewStandaloneContext()` and `ParseShellCommands` into a `bytes.Buffer`, as `TestSMT2EvalCommandMatchesCPP` in `commands_test.go` does. Input: `(assert 0)(check-sat)`. Expected output: `(error "line 1 column 10: invalid assert command, term is not Boolean")\nsat\n`. Add `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/assert_non_boolean.smt2` with that script and `scriptResults["assert_non_boolean.smt2"] = "(error \"line 1 column 10: invalid assert command, term is not Boolean\")\nsat\n"`. `G3_CPP_REFERENCE=<repo>/build/z3 go test -run TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference ./cmd/g3` checks it against the C++.

<a id="parsers-shell-01-f2"></a>
#### parsers_shell_01-F2: commands check `)` before applying their effect; the C++ applies the effect first

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/parsers/smt2/commands.go` cases `"assert"` (755-760), `"declare-fun"/"declare-const"` (679-684), `"define-sort"` (644-649), `"set-option"` (446-510), `"get-info"` (1071-1100), `"check-sat-assuming"` (`check_sat_assumptions.go:33-38` plus `check_sat_command.go:16-18`); `expressions.go:501-504` (`defineFunction`)
- C++: `src/parsers/smt2/smt2parser.cpp:2384-2386, 2402-2405, 2186-2191, 2209-2212, 2476-2486, 2584-2589, 2824-2845` (`parse_declare_fun`, `parse_declare_const`, `parse_define_sort`, `parse_define_fun`, `parse_assert`, `parse_check_sat_assuming`, `parse_ext_cmd`)

**C++ behavior.** Every built-in `parse_*` acts first and checks `)` second. Examples: `m_ctx.assert_expr(f); ... check_rparen("invalid assert command, ')' expected");`. `m_ctx.insert(c); check_rparen("invalid constant declaration, ')' expected");`. `m_ctx.insert(id, num_vars, ...); check_rparen("invalid function/constant definition, ')' expected");`. Extension commands call `set_next_arg` as each argument is read, so a value already takes effect (`set-option`, `get-info` printing). Only then does `parse_ext_cmd` throw `invalid command, too many arguments`. `check-sat-assuming` runs `m_ctx.check_sat` before the final `next()`.

**Go behavior.** Each case calls `p.requireEnd()` (`invalid command, ')' expected`) before the `p.context.*` call. A malformed command therefore leaves no trace. Only `define-fun-rec` and `push`/`pop` keep the C++ order.

**Impact.** Malformed scripts get different results. The worst case changes sat to unsat: `(assert false 3)(check-sat)` gives z3 `unsat`, g3 `sat`. Declarations, definitions, option values and info printing also differ after such an error. The error texts differ too (F8).

**Reproduction.** All confirmed with both binaries:
- `(assert false 3)(check-sat)`: z3 `(error "line 1 column 15: invalid assert command, ')' expected")` then `unsat`. g3 `(error "line 1 column 15: invalid command, ')' expected")` then `sat`.
- `(declare-const x Int 3)(assert (= x 1))(check-sat)`: z3 prints the error then `sat`. g3 prints the error, then `unknown constant x`, then `sat`.
- `(define-fun f () Int 3 4)(simplify f)`: z3 prints the error then `3`. g3 prints the error, then `unknown constant f`.
- `(define-sort S () Int 3)(declare-const y S)`: g3 adds `unknown sort 'S'`.
- `(set-option :timeout 5 6)(get-option :timeout)`: z3 prints `5`, g3 prints `4294967295`.
- `(get-info :name 3)`: z3 prints `(:name "Z3")` before the error. g3 prints only the error.
- `(declare-const x Bool)(check-sat-assuming (x) 3)`: z3 prints `sat`, then `invalid command, '(' expected`. g3 prints only an error.

**Fix.** In each listed case, move the `p.context.*` effect before the `p.requireEnd()`/`p.expect(RightParenToken)`, and use the C++ message:
- `assert`: `"invalid assert command, ')' expected"`.
- `declare-fun`: `"invalid function declaration, ')' expected"`.
- `declare-const`: `"invalid constant declaration, ')' expected"`.
- `define-sort`: `"invalid sort definition, ')' expected"`.
- `define-fun` and `define-const`: `"invalid function/constant definition, ')' expected"` and `"invalid constant definition, ')' expected"`, in `defineFunction`.
- `set-option` and `get-info`: apply the value or print the info right after the value token is read, before `advance()`. Then report a non-`)` token as `"invalid command, too many arguments"`.
- `check-sat-assuming`: after the closing `)` of the literal list, run `CheckSat` and print the result. Only then check for the command's `)`. A stray token then reaches the top-level loop, which reports `invalid command, '(' expected` (see F8).

**Regression test.** Add vectors to `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/` with these `scriptResults` entries:
- `assert_effect_before_rparen.smt2` = `(assert false 3)\n(check-sat)\n`, expected `(error "line 1 column 15: invalid assert command, ')' expected")\nunsat\n`.
- `declare_const_effect_before_rparen.smt2` = `(declare-const x Int 3)(assert (= x 1))(check-sat)`, expected `(error "line 1 column 22: invalid constant declaration, ')' expected")\nsat\n`.
- `define_fun_effect_before_rparen.smt2` = `(define-fun f () Int 3 4)(simplify f)`, expected `(error "line 1 column 24: invalid function/constant definition, ')' expected")\n3\n`.

Also add `TestSMT2CommandEffectPrecedesRParen` to `pkg/parsers/smt2/commands_test.go` with the same scripts. Run `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference` against `build/z3`.

<a id="parsers-shell-01-f3"></a>
#### parsers_shell_01-F3: `match` expressions are not supported

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/parsers/smt2/expressions.go:299-416` (`expressionWithQuantifier`, `LeftParenToken` branch); `pkg/parsers/smt2/local_match_variable.go` (`bindMatchVariable` is only called from tests)
- C++: `src/parsers/smt2/smt2parser.cpp:1322-1352, 1355-1470, 1828-1830` (`push_match_frame`, `compile_patterns`, `check_patterns`, `bind_match`, `parse_match_pattern`, the dispatch in `push_expr_frame`)

**C++ behavior.** `push_expr_frame` does `else if (curr_id_is_match()) push_match_frame();`. That parses the scrutinee and each `(pattern term)` case, binding pattern variables in a new `m_env` scope. `compile_patterns` then walks the cases backwards and folds them into an `ite` chain over the recognisers, substituting the accessor terms for the pattern variables. `check_patterns` raises `pattern matching is only supported for algebraic datatypes`, `non-exhaustive pattern match` and `a constructor is missing from pattern match`.

**Go behavior.** The `LeftParenToken` branch has cases for `root-obj`, `forall`, `exists`, `let`, `!`, `_` and `as`. `match` falls through as an ordinary function name. Its first case `((nil 0) ...)` then fails with `qualified identifier expected`. The matching helper `bindMatchVariable` exists but nothing in production calls it.

**Impact.** Every SMT-LIB 2.6 script that uses `match` fails to parse. The assertion is dropped, so later commands give different answers and models.

**Reproduction.**
```
(declare-datatypes ((L 0)) (((nil) (cons (hd Int) (tl L)))))
(declare-const l L)
(assert (= 3 (match l ((nil 0) ((cons h t) h)))))
(check-sat)
(get-value ((hd l)))
```
z3: `sat` then `(((hd l) 3))`. g3: `(error "line 3 column 28: qualified identifier expected")`, `sat`, `(((hd l) (hd nil)))`.

**Fix.** Add a `case "match":` to the `LeftParenToken` symbol switch in `expressionWithQuantifier` that implements `push_match_frame`:
1. Parse the scrutinee with `p.expression()`, take its sort, and expect `(`.
2. For each case, open a scope with `p.env.beginScope()`, save `p.bindings`, and expect `(`.
3. Port `parse_match_pattern`. A bare symbol that is a nullary constructor becomes a constructor application. Any other bare symbol becomes a variable via `bindMatchVariable`. `(C x1 ... xn)` becomes the constructor applied to fresh variables.
4. Parse the case body with `p.expression()`, restore `p.bindings`, call `endScopeWithOwningCleanup`, and expect `)`.
5. Port `check_patterns` and `compile_patterns`/`bind_match` as written, including the reverse case order, `var_subst` and `inv_var_shifter`. Build the `ite`s in the same order as the C++.
6. Push the result with `pinExpression` and expect the closing `)`.

**Regression test.** Add `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/match_list_head.smt2` with the script above. Expected `scriptResults` entry: `"sat\n(((hd l) 3))\n"`. Add negative vectors for `match` on `Int` (`pattern matching is only supported for algebraic datatypes`) and for a missing constructor. Add `TestSMT2MatchExpression` to `pkg/parsers/smt2/datatypes_test.go`, using the `NewStandaloneContext` and `ParseShellCommands` pattern of that file.

<a id="parsers-shell-01-f4"></a>
#### parsers_shell_01-F4: a quantifier with an empty variable list is accepted

- Severity: high
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/parsers/smt2/expressions.go:507-538` (`commandParser.quantifier`)
- C++: `src/parsers/smt2/smt2parser.cpp:1313-1315` (`push_quant_frame`)

**C++ behavior.**
```cpp
unsigned num_vars = parse_sorted_vars();
if (num_vars == 0)
    throw parser_exception("invalid quantifier, list of sorted variables is empty");
```

**Go behavior.** `quantifier` calls `sortedVariables()` and goes on with zero names. It builds a zero-variable quantifier through `MkQuantifier`, and the assertion is kept.

**Impact.** A different sat/unsat answer. `(assert (exists () false))(check-sat)`: z3 rejects the assertion and answers `sat`. g3 answers `unsat`.

**Reproduction.** Script `(assert (exists () false))\n(check-sat)\n`. z3: `(error "line 1 column 20: invalid quantifier, list of sorted variables is empty")` then `sat`. g3: `unsat`. `(assert (forall () true))` also prints no error in g3.

**Fix.** In `quantifier`, right after `p.sortedVariables()` succeeds, add `if len(names) == 0 { return ..., errors.New("invalid quantifier, list of sorted variables is empty") }`. Do this before `bindSortedVariables`. The position must be that of the token after `()`, which is what the C++ reports.

**Regression test.** Add `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/quantifier_empty_binders.smt2` with the script above. Expected: `(error "line 1 column 20: invalid quantifier, list of sorted variables is empty")\nsat\n`. Add `TestSMT2EmptyQuantifierBinderRejected` to `pkg/parsers/smt2/annotations_test.go`.

<a id="parsers-shell-01-f5"></a>
#### parsers_shell_01-F5: set-option built-in options: wrong value-kind handling, `:print-warning` rejected, `:expand-definitions` not "unsupported", wrong messages

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/parsers/smt2/commands.go:446-510` (case `"set-option"`); `pkg/cmd_context/context.go:619-845` (`SetBoolOption`, `SetUIntOption`, `SetNumeralOption`, `SetSymbolOption`, `SetStringOption`)
- C++: `src/cmd_context/basic_cmds.cpp:326-334, 367-541` (`set_get_option_cmd::is_builtin_option`, `set_option_cmd::set_symbol/set_next_arg/execute`, `check_not_initialized`, `to_bool`)

**C++ behavior.** `set_symbol` dispatches each built-in option. `print-warning` calls `enable_warning_messages(to_bool(value))`. `expand-definitions` sets `m_unsupported`, so `execute` calls `print_unsupported`. `to_bool` throws `invalid option value, true/false expected`. `check_not_initialized` throws `error setting '<:opt>', option value cannot be modified after initialization`, naming `:produce-assertions` for interactive-mode and `:global-decls` for global-declarations. Any other built-in reached with the wrong value kind throws `option value is not a symbol`, `... not a numeral` or `... not a string`. Only non-built-ins go to `gparams::set`. A numeral for a non-built-in goes to `gparams` as text, with no 32-bit range check in the parser.

**Go behavior.**
- The parser picks a setter from the token kind.
- `SetBoolOption` has no case for `print_warning` or `expand_definitions`. Both fall through to `Globals.SourceSetName`, which reports `unknown parameter`.
- An integer token always goes to `SetUIntOption`. That function never checks `is_builtin_option` (`SetNumeralOption` does). An integer token is also cut off at 32 bits by `p.unsigned()` (`unsigned numeral is out of range`), even for module parameters.
- A non-true/false symbol, or a string, always goes to the global catalog.
- The initialization error lacks the `error setting '...', ` prefix.

**Impact.** Ordinary scripts fail. `(set-option :print-warning false)` is a standard option and errors in g3. Error texts differ throughout.

**Reproduction.** All confirmed:
- `(set-option :print-warning false)(echo "ok")`: z3 `ok`. g3 `unknown parameter 'print_warning'` plus the list of legal parameters.
- `(set-option :expand-definitions true)`: z3 prints `unsupported` and `; :expand-definitions line: 1 position: 1`. g3 reports an unknown parameter.
- `(set-option :print-success 3)`: z3 `option value is not a numeral`. g3 reports an unknown parameter.
- `(set-option :produce-models foo)`: z3 `invalid option value, true/false expected`.
- `(set-option :produce-models "x")`: z3 `option value is not a string`.
- `(set-option :random-seed foo)` and `(set-option :verbosity true)`: z3 `option value is not a symbol`.
- `(set-option :regular-output-channel 3)`: z3 `option value is not a numeral`.
- `(set-option :random-seed 5000000000)`: z3 `option value is too big to fit in a machine integer.`, g3 `unsigned numeral is out of range`.
- `(set-option :smt.random_seed 5000000000)`: z3 accepts it silently, g3 errors.
- `(set-option :produce-proofs true)(declare-const x Int)(set-option :produce-proofs false)`: z3 `error setting ':produce-proofs', option value cannot be modified after initialization`. g3 gives the message without the prefix.
- `(set-option :interactive-mode true)(declare-const x Int)(set-option :interactive-mode false)`: z3 names `':produce-assertions'`.

**Fix.** Restructure the `set-option` case to mirror `set_option_cmd`:
1. Read the keyword without normalising it.
2. On a numeral token (`IntegerToken`, `DecimalToken`, `BitVectorToken`), call one `SetNumeralOption(key, rat)`. That function handles random-seed, reproducible-resource-limit and verbosity through `to_unsigned`, throws `option value is not a numeral` for the other built-ins, and passes `val.to_string()` to `SourceSetName` otherwise. Remove the `p.unsigned()` pre-check.
3. On a symbol, call a new `SetSymbolOptionValue(key, sym)` that ports `set_symbol` branch by branch:
   - print-success, then print-warning (via `diagnostic.BorrowProcessWarningService().Enable`), then expand-definitions (return an "unsupported" flag).
   - interactive-mode/produce-assertions, produce-proofs, produce-interpolants, produce-unsat-cores and produce-unsat-assumptions, each with `check_not_initialized` and its exact name.
   - produce-models, produce-assignments, global-decls/global-declarations, numeral-as-real, int-real-coercions, error-behavior.
   - any other built-in throws `option value is not a symbol`; anything else goes to `set_param`.
   - `to_bool` throws `invalid option value, true/false expected`.
4. On a string, port `set_next_arg(char const*)`: the two output channels, `option value is not a string` for the other built-ins, else `set_param`.
5. When the unsupported flag is set, print `unsupported` to the regular stream and `; :expand-definitions line: L position: P` to the diagnostic stream, the same way as the fixed `get-info` path.
6. Apply all of this before the `)` check (F2).

**Regression test.** Add `TestSMT2SetOptionBuiltinKinds` to `pkg/parsers/smt2/command_globals_test.go`. Make it table-driven over the scripts above, with the exact z3 outputs above as expectations. Add `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/set_option_print_warning.smt2` = `(set-option :print-warning false)(echo "ok")` with `scriptResults` `"ok\n"`. Add `set_option_expand_definitions.smt2` with `scriptResults` `"unsupported\n"`; the `;` line goes to stderr.

<a id="parsers-shell-01-f6"></a>
#### parsers_shell_01-F6: `:error-behavior immediate-exit` and `parser.error_for_visual_studio` are ignored by the parser's error reporting

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/parsers/smt2/commands.go:219-234` (`reportParserError`), `146-178` (error loop)
- C++: `src/parsers/smt2/smt2parser.cpp:434-452` (`parser::error`), `2930-3012` (`updt_params`, `use_vs_format`)

**C++ behavior.** `error()` first calls `m_ctx.set_cancel(false)`. If `use_vs_format()` is on, it writes `Z3(<line>, <pos>): ERROR: <msg>` to the diagnostic stream. Otherwise it writes `(error "...")` to the regular stream. It then calls `_Exit(1)` if `m_ctx.exit_on_error()`.

**Go behavior.** `reportParserError` always writes the `(error ...)` form to `p.out`. It never reads `ParserParams.ErrorForVisualStudio()`, which is defined but has no caller. It never checks `context.ExitOnError`, so parsing continues after the error.

**Impact.** Scripts that set `:error-behavior immediate-exit` keep running after the first error and print more results. Users of `parser.error_for_visual_studio=true` get the wrong format on the wrong stream.

**Reproduction.**
- `(set-option :error-behavior immediate-exit)(foo1 (bar))(assert 1 2)(check-sat)`: z3 stops after the first error, exit 1, no `sat`. g3 goes on and prints `sat`.
- `(assert 1 2)\n(check-sat)\n` with `parser.error_for_visual_studio=true`: z3 writes `Z3(1, 11): ERROR: invalid assert command, term is not Boolean` to stderr, then `sat`. g3 writes `(error "line 1 column 11: invalid command, ')' expected")`.

**Fix.**
1. In `configurePatternOptions`, also cache `params.ErrorForVisualStudio()` in a new `p.errorForVS`. It is refreshed after each `set-option`, as the C++ `updt_params` hack does.
2. In `reportParserError`, if `p.errorForVS` is set, write `Z3(%d, %d): ERROR: %s` to `p.context.DiagnosticOutput()`, adding `\n` unless the message ends with one.
3. After reporting, if `p.context.ExitOnError`, stop parsing and return a sentinel error. `cmd/g3` maps that sentinel to exit status 1 with no further output.
4. Call `p.context.SetCancel(false)` at the start of the report.

**Regression test.** Add `TestSMT2ErrorBehaviorImmediateExitStops` and `TestSMT2ErrorForVisualStudioFormat` to `pkg/parsers/smt2/commands_test.go`, using the scripts above with separate stdout and stderr buffers. Add `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/error_behavior_immediate_exit.smt2`, expected stdout `"unsupported\n(error \"line 1 column 66: invalid assert command, term is not Boolean\")\n"` and exit status 1. It needs F1 fixed for the second line.

<a id="parsers-shell-01-f7"></a>
#### parsers_shell_01-F7: global `-T` timeout does not end the SMT-LIB run; later commands still execute

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/shell/smtlib_frontend.go:94-150` (`SMTLIBFrontend.Run`)
- C++: `src/util/timeout.cpp:31-44` (`g_timeout_eh`); `src/shell/smtlib_frontend.cpp:47-53` (`on_timeout`)

**C++ behavior.** The timer handler prints `timeout` and calls `g_on_timeout`. For SMT-LIB that is `on_timeout`: `display_statistics(); exit(0);`. The process ends at once.

**Go behavior.** The timeout callback only calls `f.context.SetCancel(true)`. `smt2.ParseShellCommands` goes on: the cancelled `check-sat` prints `unknown`, and every later command runs.

**Impact.** Anyone using `-T:` sees extra output after `timeout`: `unknown` and the remaining commands' output.

**Reproduction.** `hard.smt2`:
```
(declare-const a Int)(declare-const b Int)(declare-const c Int)
(assert (= (+ (* a a a) (* b b b)) (* c c c)))
(assert (> a 1000))(assert (> b 1000))
(check-sat)
(echo "after")
(check-sat)
```
`z3 -T:1 hard.smt2` prints `timeout`, exit 0. `g3 -T:1 hard.smt2` prints `timeout`, `unknown`, `after`, `unknown`, exit 0.

**Fix.** Once the callback fires, the parser must stop before printing anything else. Give the parser a stop hook that the timeout callback sets, checked at the top of the `for p.token != EOFToken` loop and before any command prints a result. One way: `ParseShellCommands` takes a `stop func() bool`, and `checkSatCommand`, `checkSatUsing` and the other result printers return a sentinel when it is true. `Run` then writes the final statistics, if `-st`, and returns success. This mirrors `display_statistics(); exit(0)`. The DIMACS and optimisation front ends already return without writing results; check them against the same rule.

**Regression test.** Add `TestSMTLIBFrontendGlobalTimeoutStopsParsing` to `pkg/shell/runner_smtlib_test.go`. Use a `NewTimeoutService` with a 1 ms `SetTimeout`, the script above, and `SMTLIBFrontendConfig{Timer: ...}`. Expect the output to be exactly `"timeout\n"`.

<a id="parsers-shell-01-f8"></a>
#### parsers_shell_01-F8: hand-written dispatch gives different syntax-error texts and accepts what `parse_ext_cmd` rejects

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/parsers/smt2/commands.go` (`expect`, `requireEnd`, `symbol`, `unsigned`, the per-command cases, `set-info` 511-535, default case 1544-1559), `echo_command.go:8`, `tactics.go`, `annotations.go`
- C++: `src/parsers/smt2/smt2parser.cpp:2410-2448, 2619-2637, 2700-2790, 2796-2848, 3039`; `src/cmd_context/tactic_cmds.cpp:420-700`

**C++ behavior.** Generic commands go through `parse_ext_cmd` and `parse_next_cmd_arg`. These give fixed texts: `invalid command, argument(s) missing`, `invalid command, too many arguments`, and `invalid command argument, <kind> expected` (string, keyword, symbol, numeral, unsigned integer, true/false). `CPK_OPTION_VALUE` accepts only a numeral, symbol or string token (`invalid option value`). The built-in `parse_*` functions have command-specific texts. The top level reports `invalid command, '(' expected`. `parse_unknown_cmd` prints `unsupported` first (regular stream) and then `; name line: L position: P` (diagnostic stream).

**Go behavior.** Generic texts are used instead: `invalid command, ')' expected`, `symbol expected`, `unsigned numeral expected`, `option keyword expected`, `unexpected input, expected token 1`, `string expected`, `invalid parameter value, true or false expected`. `set-info` passes any s-expression or keyword value to `skipSExpr`. Unknown commands print the `;` line before `unsupported`.

**Impact.** Error output differs from z3 on malformed input. Some malformed `set-info` commands are accepted. With `:diagnostic-output-channel "stdout"`, the unknown-command lines come out in the wrong order.

**Reproduction.** Each pair is z3 then g3. All are 1-line scripts, confirmed with both binaries.
- `(exit 3)`, `(get-assertions 1)`, `(get-proof 1)`, `(get-unsat-core 1)`, `(set-logic QF_LIA 3)`, `(set-info :status sat 3)`, `(help-tactic 1)`: `invalid command, too many arguments` vs `invalid command, ')' expected`.
- `(get-option)`, `(set-option)`, `(set-option :foo)`, `(set-info :foo)`, `(display)`, `(minimize)`: `invalid command, argument(s) missing` vs `option keyword expected` / `symbol expected` / `attribute value expected` / `invalid expression, unexpected input`.
- `(push -1)`: `invalid push command, value is negative.` vs `unsigned numeral is out of range`.
- `(push x)`: `invalid push command, integer expected` vs `unsigned numeral expected`.
- `(push 5000000000)`: `...too big to fit in an unsigned machine integer` vs `unsigned numeral is out of range`.
- `(push 1 2)`: `invalid push command, ')' expected`.
- `(declare-fun f (Int) Int 3)`: `invalid function declaration, ')' expected`.
- `(define-sort S (X) Int 3)`: `invalid sort definition, ')' expected`.
- `(define-const c Int 3 4)`: `invalid constant definition, ')' expected`.
- `(define-const c Int true)`: `invalid constant definition, sort mismatch` vs `invalid function/constant definition, sort mismatch`.
- `(declare-datatypes ((A 0)) (((a))) 3)`: `invalid datatype declaration` vs `invalid command, ')' expected`.
- `foo (check-sat)` and `) (check-sat)`: `invalid command, '(' expected` vs `unexpected input, expected token 1`.
- `(echo foo)`: `invalid command argument, string expected` vs `string expected`.
- `(get-info 3)`: `invalid command argument, keyword expected` vs `information keyword expected`.
- `(declare-rel r (Int) 3 4)`: `invalid command argument, symbol expected` vs `symbol expected`.
- `(assert-soft true :weight x)`: `invalid command argument, numeral expected` vs `rational numeral expected`.
- `(apply simplify :timeout foo)`: `invalid command argument, unsigned integer expected` vs `invalid parameter value, unsigned integer expected`.
- `(apply simplify :print 1)` and `(eval 1 :completion 3)`: `invalid command argument, true/false expected` vs `invalid parameter value, true or false expected`.
- `(assert-soft true :foo 1)` (col 19 vs 24) and `(eval 1 :foo 2)` (col 9 vs 14): `invalid keyword argument` at a different column; g3 also prints `unsupported assert-soft option :foo` for the first.
- `(assert-soft 1)`: `Invalid type for expression. Expected Boolean type.` vs `invalid type for expression: expected Boolean type`.
- `(assert-soft)`: `assert-soft requires a formulas as argument.` vs `invalid expression, unexpected input`.
- `(simplify)`: `invalid simplify command, argument expected`.
- `(eval)`: `model is not available`.
- `(query)`: `invalid query command, argument expected`.
- `(rule)`: `invalid rule, expected formula`.
- `(assert)`: `invalid expression, unexpected ')'` vs `... unexpected input`.
- `(assert ())`: `invalid expression, '(' or symbol expected` vs `symbol expected`.
- `(assert ((foo f) 1))`: `invalid qualified/indexed identifier, '_' or 'as' expected` vs `qualified identifier expected`.
- `(assert (forall ((x Int)) ))`: `invalid quantified expression, syntax error: ...` vs `invalid expression, unexpected input`.
- `(assert (! true :named))`: `invalid attribute value, symbol expected` vs `symbol expected`.
- `(assert (forall ((x Int)) (! (> x 0) :weight foo)))`: `invalid weight attribute, integer expected`.
- `(assert (! true :foo))`: `invalid s-expression, unexpected ')'` vs `attribute value expected`.
- `:pattern (x)` with a local `x`: `invalid function application, arguments missing` vs `unknown constant x`.
- `(set-option :foo 1)` and `(set-option :fixedpoint.default_relation pentagon)`: column 18/42 vs 19/50. This is lead item 5; the cause is F2's order.
- Tactic texts:
  - `(apply (try-for simplify))`: `invalid try-for combinator, two arguments expected` vs `unsigned numeral expected`.
  - `(apply (repeat simplify foo))`: `...second argument must be an unsigned integer`.
  - `(apply (if size simplify))`: `invalid if/conditional combinator, three arguments expected`.
  - `(apply (foo simplify))`: `invalid tactic, unknown tactic combinator foo` vs `invalid tactic combinator foo` (col 21 vs 13).
  - `(apply ())`: `invalid empty s-expression`.
  - `(apply (then))`: `invalid and-then combinator, ...`.
  - `(apply (using-params simplify :som))`: `...parameter value expected`.
  - `(apply 3)`: `invalid tactic, unexpected input`.
- `(set-info :foo (a b))` and `(set-info :foo :bar)`: z3 `invalid option value`. g3 accepts both.
- `(set-option :diagnostic-output-channel "stdout")(foo)`: z3 prints `unsupported` then `; foo line: 1 position: 53`; g3 prints them in the reverse order.

**Fix.**
1. Add the `parse_ext_cmd` arity logic (missing arguments, too many arguments) and the `parse_next_cmd_arg` checks with their exact texts. Use them in every case that ports an extension command (everything except the built-ins listed in `smt2parser.cpp:2880-2925`).
2. Make each built-in case use its own texts: `parse_opt_unsigned` for push and pop; `check_rparen` messages; `invalid command, '(' expected` at the top level, in `command()` when the token is not `(`; `invalid expression, unexpected ')'`.
3. `set-info` reads its value through a `parseOptionValue` that accepts only numeral, symbol and string tokens.
4. Swap the two writes in the default (unknown command) case.
5. Port the tactic messages from `tactic_cmds.cpp`: parse the tactic as an s-expression first, then convert it, as `sexpr2tactic` does. That also fixes the reported positions.

**Regression test.** Add a table-driven test `TestSMT2CommandArgumentErrorsMatchCPP` to `pkg/parsers/smt2/commands_test.go` with the scripts above and the z3 texts. Add the most common ones as `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/parse_errors_*.smt2`, recorded in `parseErrorScripts`/`scriptResults` in `pkg/cmd/g3/main_test.go`, and check them with `TestSMTLibRunnerCPPReference`.

<a id="parsers-shell-01-f9"></a>
#### parsers_shell_01-F9: `apply` and `eval` accept `:rlimit`, which the C++ commands reject

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/parsers/smt2/apply_tactic.go:12-22` (`applyTacticParameterKinds`); `pkg/parsers/smt2/commands.go:1244-1260` (case `"eval"`)
- C++: `src/cmd_context/tactic_cmds.cpp:150-155, 296-305` (`exec_given_tactic_cmd::init_pdescrs`, `apply_tactic_cmd::init_pdescrs`); `src/cmd_context/eval_cmd.cpp:38-42`

**C++ behavior.** `init_pdescrs` inserts `timeout`, `max_memory` and `print_statistics`, plus each command's own keys (`model_evaluator` params and `model_index` for eval). There is no `rlimit`. `parametric_cmd::set_next_arg` throws `invalid keyword argument` for unknown keys. `p.get_uint("rlimit", ...)` in `execute` therefore always sees the default.

**Go behavior.** Both keyword tables include `rlimit`, and the value is applied: `options.RLimit` for eval, and the tactic `options` for apply.

**Impact.** `(apply simplify :rlimit 10)` runs and prints goals where z3 errors. `(eval t :rlimit n)` sets a resource limit that z3 never sets.

**Reproduction.**
- `(apply simplify :rlimit 10)`: z3 `(error "line 1 column 17: invalid keyword argument")`. g3 prints `(goals ...)`.
- `(eval 1 :rlimit 3)`: z3 `(error "line 1 column 9: invalid keyword argument")`. g3 `model is not available` at column 18.

`check-sat-using` and `simplify` already reject `:rlimit`.

**Fix.**
1. Remove `"rlimit"` from `applyTacticParameterKinds`.
2. Remove `rlimit` from the eval keyword switch, and with it `EvaluationOptions.RLimit`, or always leave it 0.
3. `apply`'s `print_proof` is guarded by `_EXTERNAL_RELEASE` (FUZZ-F7); drop it together with that fix.
4. Report `invalid keyword argument` at the keyword's own position, before `advance()`.

**Regression test.** Add `TestSMT2ApplyEvalRejectRLimit` to `pkg/parsers/smt2/apply_tactic_goals_test.go` with the two scripts. Expect `(error "line 1 column 17: invalid keyword argument")\n` and `(error "line 1 column 9: invalid keyword argument")\n`.

<a id="parsers-shell-01-f10"></a>
#### parsers_shell_01-F10: probe expressions: n-ary `+`/`*` fold differently, and binary `-`, `/`, `=>` accept any number of arguments

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/parsers/smt2/tactics.go:359-389` (`parseProbe`)
- C++: `src/cmd_context/tactic_cmds.cpp:722-760` (`MK_BIN_PROBE`, `MK_NARY_PROBE`)

**C++ behavior.** `MK_NARY_PROBE` starts with `r = child(1)` and `i = 1`. The first loop step computes `NAME(prev, child(1))` again, so the first argument is used twice: `(+ a b)` is `(a+a)+b`, and `(* a b)` is `(a*a)*b`. `and`/`or` are unaffected because the operation is idempotent. `-`, `/` and `=>` use `MK_BIN_PROBE`, which requires exactly two arguments (`invalid probe expression, two arguments expected`).

**Go behavior.** Go folds `arguments[1:]` onto `arguments[0]`, the mathematically correct sum and product. Only kinds `ProbeEqual..ProbeGreater` are treated as binary; `ProbeImplies`, `ProbeSubtract` and `ProbeDivide` are folded as n-ary.

**Impact.** Strategies whose `if`/`when`/`fail-if` conditions use `+` or `*` take the other branch, so the tactic, the answer and the output differ. `(- 5 1 1)` is accepted by g3 and rejected by z3. This is a z3 4.7.1 bug, but it is not in `z3_bug_exclusions.txt`.

**Reproduction.**
```
(check-sat-using (if (= (+ 1 2) 4) (fail-if 1) smt))
(check-sat-using (if (= (* 2 3) 12) (fail-if 1) smt))
(check-sat-using (if (= (+ 1 2) 3) (fail-if 1) smt))
```
z3: `unknown`, `unknown`, `sat`, so z3 computes (+ 1 2) = 4 and (* 2 3) = 12. g3: `sat`, `sat`, `unknown`. `(apply (echo "a " (- 5 1 1)))`: z3 `invalid probe expression, two arguments expected`; g3 runs it.

**Fix.** Either reproduce the C++ fold and record it, or list it as a deliberate exclusion in `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/z3_bug_exclusions.txt` with this reproduction. The owner decides.
- To reproduce it: in the n-ary branch start with `result = arguments[0]` and fold over `arguments[0:]`, not `arguments[1:]`. Keep the single-argument shortcut.
- In either case, give `=>`/`implies`, `-` and `/` the binary arity check.
- Evaluate sub-probes in the C++ order, child by child, as `sexpr2probe` does.

**Regression test.** Add `TestSMT2ProbeArithmeticFold` to `pkg/parsers/smt2/commands_test.go` with the three-line script. Expect `"unknown\nunknown\nsat\n"`, or the exclusion record if that route is taken. Add `TestSMT2BinaryProbeArity` for `(- 5 1 1)` expecting `invalid probe expression, two arguments expected`. Add `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/probe_nary_fold.smt2` for the reference runner.

<a id="parsers-shell-01-f11"></a>
#### parsers_shell_01-F11: `declare-datatype(s)` adds a Go-only arity check, does not pre-insert SMT-LIB 2.6 sort headers, and words two errors differently

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/parsers/smt2/datatypes.go:111-135, 186-188, 269-271, 346-360` (`declareDatatypes`)
- C++: `src/parsers/smt2/smt2parser.cpp:858-866, 886-978, 2111-2147` (`parse_constructor_decls`, `parse_declare_datatypes`, `parse_sort_decl_or_params`)

**C++ behavior.**
- `parse_sort_decl_or_params` inserts `pm().mk_psort_dt_decl(u, dt_name)` into the context for each `(name arity)` header right away. The sorts stay declared even when the body fails.
- The declared arity is never compared with the `par` binder count.
- An empty constructor list throws `invalid datatype declaration, datatype does not have any constructors`.
- A field name repeated inside one constructor fails at commit with `invalid declaration, function 'x' (with the given signature) already declared`.

**Go behavior.**
- Headers only go into a local map, so a failed declaration leaves no sort behind.
- Go raises an extra `datatype sort %s declares arity %d but defines %d parameters` error.
- The empty-constructor message says `...datatype must have at least one constructor`.
- Duplicate accessors get `invalid datatype declaration, repeated accessor identifier 'x'`.

**Impact.** Some declarations that z3 accepts fail in g3, and later commands then fail too. After a failed declaration, z3 still knows the sort and g3 does not. Error texts differ.

**Reproduction.**
- `(declare-datatypes ((A 1)) (((a))))(declare-const x (A Int))`: z3 prints nothing. g3 prints `datatype sort A declares arity 1 but defines 0 parameters` and then `unknown sort 'A'`.
- `(declare-datatypes ((A 0)) (((a (x B)))))(declare-const y A)`: z3 prints only `unknown sort 'B'`; g3 adds `Invalid constant declaration: unknown sort 'A'`.
- `(declare-datatypes ((A 0)) (((a (x B)))))(declare-sort A)`: z3 adds `invalid sort declaration, sort already declared/defined`; g3 accepts.
- `(declare-datatypes () ((A)))`: message wording differs, as listed above.
- `(declare-datatypes ((A 0)) (((a (x Int) (x Int)))))`: message differs, as listed above.
- `(declare-datatypes ((A 0)) ((par (T) ((a (f T))))))`: z3 crashes, so it is not comparable.

**Fix.**
1. In the modern-header loop, call `p.context` to insert a datatype psort declaration of the given arity for each header right away. That needs a `cmd_context` hook mirroring `mk_psort_dt_decl` + `insert`. Leave it inserted on error.
2. Delete the `expectedArity` check, or ignore the arity as the C++ does; `mk_pdatatype_decl` gets `m_dt_name2arity.find(dt_name)`.
3. Change the empty-constructor message to `invalid datatype declaration, datatype does not have any constructors`.
4. Check duplicates the way the C++ does: `check_duplicate` across constructors with the `(line, pos)` of the command. A duplicate inside one constructor is left to declaration commit, which produces the `function ... already declared` text.

**Regression test.** Add `TestSMT2DeclareDatatypesHeaderSemantics` to `pkg/parsers/smt2/datatypes_test.go` with the scripts above and the z3 outputs. Add vector `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/datatype_header_arity_unchecked.smt2` with `scriptResults` `""`.

<a id="parsers-shell-01-f12"></a>
#### parsers_shell_01-F12: Datalog, DIMACS and MPS front ends: open failures and Datalog parse failures give different messages and exit codes

- Severity: medium
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/shell/datalog_frontend_load.go:15-31` (`DatalogFrontend.Load`); `pkg/shell/runner_input.go:24-31`; `pkg/shell/lp_frontend_report.go:12-15`; the wording and exit codes are produced in `pkg/cmd/g3/main.go:95-104, 254-269` (out of shard)
- C++: `src/shell/datalog_frontend.cpp:144-158`; `src/shell/dimacs_frontend.cpp:140-146`; `src/shell/lp_frontend.cpp:73-76`; `src/shell/main.cpp:342-356`

**C++ behavior.**
- **Datalog:** `parser->parse_file` prints its own message (for example `ERROR: could not open file 'x'.`, or a syntax message). `read_datalog` then prints `ERROR: failed to parse file` to stderr and returns 1. `main` ignores the return value, so the exit status is 0.
- **DIMACS:** `read_dimacs` prints `(error "failed to open file 'x'")` and exits with `ERR_OPEN_FILE` (108).
- **MPS:** the reader prints its message, then `cannot process x` goes to **stderr**, and the exit status is 0.

**Go behavior.**
- Datalog: `os.Stat` fails, or the parse error is wrapped as `Datalog parse <file>: ...`. Either way it ends as `ERROR: ...` with exit status 110.
- DIMACS and MPS: the runner opens the file itself and `main` prints `ERROR: failed to open file "x".`, exit 108.
- MPS: `cannotProcess` writes to `f.output`, which is stdout, and returns an error.

**Impact.** Wrapper scripts and test harnesses see different stderr text and exit codes.

**Reproduction.** Each case is z3 then g3:
- `nofile.cnf`: `(error "failed to open file 'nofile.cnf'")` rc 108, vs `ERROR: failed to open file "nofile.cnf".` rc 108.
- `nofile.dl`: `ERROR: could not open file 'nofile.dl'.` and `ERROR: failed to parse file`, rc 0, vs `ERROR: stat nofile.dl: no such file or directory` rc 110.
- `ok.dl` containing `P\nQ\nP.\nQ :- P.\n`: `numeral or 'int' at line 2 '' found '\n'`, blank line, `ERROR: failed to parse file`, rc 0, vs `ERROR: Datalog parse ok.dl: datalog:1:2: expected domain size or int, found newline ""` rc 110.
- `nofile.mps`: `setting m_is_OK to false` and `cannot process nofile.mps`, rc 0, vs `ERROR: failed to open file "nofile.mps".` rc 108.

**Fix.**
- **Datalog:** remove the `os.Stat` pre-check. Pass the path to the Datalog parser, which should print the C++ `could not open file` and syntax messages itself. On failure write `ERROR: failed to parse file\n` to the diagnostic stream and return success.
- **DIMACS:** open the file in the DIMACS front end and print `(error "failed to open file '%s'")`, exit 108.
- **MPS:** let `FloatMPSReader` take the file name, print `cannot process` to the diagnostic stream, and return nil. Stop opening these files in `cmd/g3/main.go` and `runner_input.go`.

**Regression test.** In `pkg/shell/runner_datalog_file_test.go`, add `TestRunnerDatalogMissingFileMatchesCPP`, checking stderr and exit status 0. Add the matching DIMACS and MPS tests to `runner_dimacs_test.go` and `runner_lp_test.go`. Use `RunnerConfig` with `bytes.Buffer` stdout and diagnostics, as the neighbouring runner tests do.

<a id="parsers-shell-01-f13"></a>
#### parsers_shell_01-F13: `-st` on a DIMACS file omits `:total-time` (time rounded to 0.00 before `update`)

- Severity: low
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/shell/dimacs_statistics.go:15` (`DIMACSFrontend.writeStatistics`)
- C++: `src/shell/dimacs_frontend.cpp:32-41` (`display_statistics`)

**C++ behavior.** `st.update("total time", (end_time - g_start_time) / CLOCKS_PER_SEC);` stores the exact CPU time. `statistics::update` drops only an exact 0.0, so a fast run still prints `:total-time 0.00`.

**Go behavior.** `st.UpdateDouble("total time", float64(time.Since(f.start).Milliseconds()/10)/100)` rounds down to 10 ms first. A run under 10 ms becomes 0, and the entry is dropped. This is lead item 10.

**Reproduction.** `printf 'p cnf 2 2\n1 2 0\n-1 0\n' > d.cnf`. `z3 -st d.cnf` ends with ` :total-time          0.00)`. `g3 -st d.cnf` ends with ` :mk-bool-var         3)`.

**Fix.** Pass the unrounded seconds: `time.Since(f.start).Seconds()`. To match exactly, use process CPU time as C++ `clock()` does. `display_smt2` does the 2-decimal formatting.

**Regression test.** Add `TestDIMACSFrontendStatisticsIncludeTotalTime` to `pkg/shell/runner_dimacs_test.go`. Run with `DisplayStatistics: true` and assert the output contains `:total-time`.

<a id="parsers-shell-01-f14"></a>
#### parsers_shell_01-F14: `(help)` output loses its final newline, and `(help-tactic)` changes the `if` combinator text

- Severity: low
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/parsers/smt2/help_commands.go:308-313` (`helpCommands`), `:330` (`helpTactic`)
- C++: `src/cmd_context/basic_cmds.cpp:72-95` (`help_cmd::execute`); `src/cmd_context/tactic_cmds.cpp:101`

**C++ behavior.** `help_cmd::execute` writes `"` and then each entry straight to the stream; each description ends with `\n`. It then writes `"\n`, so the closing quote is on its own line. The help-tactic text reads `... Otherwise execute the second.\n`.

**Go behavior.** Go builds the body and passes it through `escaped.String(&text, true, 0)`. With `trim_nl=true` this drops the final newline and escapes the body a second time. The closing quote therefore lands at the end of the last description. The help-tactic line reads `Otherwise execute the second tactic.`

**Reproduction.**
- `(help echo push)`: z3's last two lines are `    push 1 (or <number>) scopes.` and `"`. g3's last line is `    push 1 (or <number>) scopes."`.
- Full `(help)` diff: only line 429 differs, apart from FUZZ-F7.
- `(help-tactic)`: line 7 differs.

**Fix.** Write `"`, then `body.String()` unescaped (each part was already escaped), then `"\n`. Change the help-tactic string to `Otherwise execute the second.\n`.

**Regression test.** Add `TestSMT2HelpClosingQuoteOnOwnLine` to `pkg/parsers/smt2/commands_test.go`. Input `(help echo push)`; expected `"\" (echo <string>)\n    display the given string\n (push <number>?)\n    push 1 (or <number>) scopes.\n\"\n"`.

<a id="parsers-shell-01-f15"></a>
#### parsers_shell_01-F15: `dbg-sexpr` prints atoms differently from `sexpr::display`

- Severity: low
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/parsers/smt2/debug_commands.go:610-626` (`debugSExpr`)
- C++: `src/util/sexpr.cpp:123-185` (`sexpr::display_atom`)

**C++ behavior.**
- Numerals print as rationals: `0.25` becomes `1/4`.
- Bit-vectors print as `#x..` when the size is a multiple of 4, else `#b..`, zero-padded.
- Strings print as `"` + `escaped(...)` + `"`, so an embedded `"` becomes `\"`.

**Go behavior.**
- Decimals print as `FloatString`.
- Bit-vectors print as `(_ bvN size)`.
- An embedded `"` is doubled.

**Reproduction.** `(dbg-sexpr ("a""b\n" #x0f #b1 -3 0.25 (dbg-sexpr)))`. z3: `("a\"b\n" #x0f #b1 -3 1/4 (dbg-sexpr))`. g3: `("a""b\n" (_ bv15 8) (_ bv1 1) -3 0.25 (dbg-sexpr))`.

**Fix.** Build a real s-expression with the existing `usexpr.SexprManager` (as `parseRootObjectSExpr` does) and print it with that package's C++-faithful display. If no such display exists, port `display_atom` into it.

**Regression test.** Add to `pkg/parsers/smt2/debug_commands_test.go` the case above with the z3 output as expected.

<a id="parsers-shell-01-f16"></a>
#### parsers_shell_01-F16: pattern validator warns once per occurrence; C++ `for_each_expr` visits each shared node once

- Severity: low
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/parsers/util/pattern_validation.go:46-115` (`PatternValidator.Validate`)
- C++: `src/parsers/util/pattern_validation.cpp:58-104` (`pattern_validation_functor`, `pattern_validator::process`)

**C++ behavior.** `for_each_expr(f, n)` visits the DAG with a visited mark. A forbidden application, or a free variable, shared several times in a pattern is reported once. The traversal also enters quantifiers.

**Go behavior.** An explicit stack walks the pattern as a tree. Every occurrence is visited and warned about. Quantifiers are not entered.

**Reproduction.**
```
(declare-fun h (Int) Bool)
(declare-fun g (Bool Bool) Bool)
(assert (forall ((x Int)) (! (g (not (h x)) (not (h x))) :pattern ((g (not (h x)) (not (h x)))))))
(check-sat)
```
z3 prints one `WARNING: (3,96): 'not' cannot be used in patterns.`; g3 prints it twice.

**Fix.** Keep a `visited map[ast.ASTHandle]bool` and skip handles already visited. Also traverse quantifier children. `for_each_expr` visits a quantifier's body, patterns and no-patterns. Use the C++ visit order: post-order over arguments, as `for_each_expr_core` does, so several distinct warnings come out in the same order.

**Regression test.** Add `TestPatternValidatorWarnsOncePerSharedNode` to `pkg/parsers/util/` in a new `pattern_validation_test.go`, using a `bytes.Buffer` warnings writer. Add `pkg/cmd/g3/test_vectors/pattern_shared_forbidden.smt2` with the script (stdout `sat\n`). Check stderr by hand or with the CPP reference runner.

<a id="parsers-shell-01-f17"></a>
#### parsers_shell_01-F17: simple/cost parser writes `parser error` without the `WARNING: ` prefix, bypassing the warning service

- Severity: low
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/parsers/util/simple_parser.go:30-35, 164-168` (`NewSimpleParser`, `Parse`)
- C++: `src/parsers/util/simple_parser.cpp:121-133` (`simple_parser::parse`)

**C++ behavior.** On a parse error it calls `warning_msg("parser error")`. That prints `WARNING: parser error` and respects `-nw`/`warning=false`.

**Go behavior.** `io.WriteString(p.warnings, "parser error\n")`, where `p.warnings` defaults to `os.Stderr`. There is no prefix and no enable check.

**Reproduction.** Run a quantified script, for example `(declare-fun f (Int) Int)(assert (forall ((x Int)) (> (f x) 0)))(assert (< (f 3) 0))(check-sat)`, with `smt.qi.cost=(foo)`. z3 repeats `WARNING: parser error` and `WARNING: invalid cost function '(foo)', switching to default one`. g3 repeats `parser error` only. The second, missing warning belongs to `pkg/smtcore/smt_qi_cost.go` `parseWithFallback`, which is outside this shard.

**Fix.** Replace the direct write with `diagnostic.BorrowProcessWarningService().Warning("parser error")`, or with an injected `*diagnostic.WarningService`. Also add the `invalid cost function '%s', switching to default one` warning in `smt_qi_cost.go`, at the point where C++ `qi_queue::setup` emits it.

**Regression test.** Add `TestSimpleParserErrorUsesWarningService` to a new `pkg/parsers/util/simple_parser_test.go`. Bind a `WarningService` to a buffer, parse `(foo)` and expect `WARNING: parser error\n`.

<a id="parsers-shell-01-f18"></a>
#### parsers_shell_01-F18: invalid command-line option message keeps the `:argument` part

- Severity: low
- Confidence: confirmed
- Go: `pkg/shell/command_line.go:237-238` (`CommandLine.Parse`)
- C++: `src/shell/main.cpp:146-151, 260-263` (`parse_cmd_line_args`)

**C++ behavior.** `char * colon = strchr(arg, ':'); if (colon) { opt_arg = colon + 1; *colon = 0; }` cuts `arg` at the colon in place. The later message `invalid command line option: " << arg` therefore prints only `-foo`.

**Go behavior.** It prints the original `arg`, `-foo:bar`.

**Reproduction.** `z3 -foo:bar s.smt2` prints `Error: invalid command line option: -foo`. `g3` prints `... -foo:bar`. Both exit 109.

**Fix.** In the default case use the truncated text: `"invalid command line option: " + arg[:1+len(prefix)+len(name)]`. Simplest is to record `truncated := arg` and cut it at the first `':'` when computing `value`.

**Regression test.** Add `TestCommandLineInvalidOptionTruncatesAtColon` to `pkg/shell/command_line_test.go`. Parse `[]string{"-foo:bar"}` and assert the `CommandLineError.Message` is `invalid command line option: -foo`.

### Area: Files added during the audit (sorting port, theory_str scope)

*late_01.* Two files added by recent fix commits: the approved libstdc++ `std::sort` port (`util/sorting/libstdcxx_sort.go`) and the C++-lifetime scope helper for z3str3 axioms (`smtcore/theory_str_scope.go`, commit 714fb39b7, used by `instantiateSubstring`). Both are faithful. The sort port was compared line by line with GCC 13 `bits/stl_algo.h` / `bits/stl_heap.h` (`build/z3` was built with GCC 13.3.0, confirmed with `strings build/z3`). All three callers pass a strict weak order in the C++ argument order. `instantiateSubstring` matches `theory_str::instantiate_axiom_Substr` in construction order and owner release order. Findings: 0 critical, 0 high, 0 medium, 0 low.

No findings.

At line 107443, g3 makes a fresh decision `[assign] #375 decision` (`<= #51 #162`, with new `* #154 #23` terms) where z3 goes straight to `[resolve-lit]` after the bound `(not #388)` is assigned. **FUZZ_I**

In `src/tactic/core/pb_preprocess_tactic.cpp:181`, `classify_vars(i, ...)` records the m_ge index, and `replace`/`resolve` use it as a goal index. z3 therefore rewrites the wrong formula (`replace (<= x1 x1) -> true`, `replace (distinct 5 x0) -> (not (= 5 x0))`). The deviation is documented at `pkg/tactic/core/pb_preprocess_simplify.go:6-11`, but it is not in `test_vectors/z3_bug_exclusions.txt`; add vectors `pb/m20282.smt2` and `pb/m20106.smt2` and exclusion entries.

**FUZZ_J**

- `pkg/opt/maxres_core_batch_process.go:9-15` (`processCoreBatch` calls `pivotCorrection` before each core) compared with `src/opt/maxres.cpp:470-474`. C++ `process_unsat(cores)` just runs `process_unsat(core)` for each core; the only pivot is the one inside it, after the core is processed (Go: `pivotAfterCore`). `pivotCorrection` reuses an `e.correction` left by an earlier `pivotAfterCore` that declined to pivot, and can skip processing a core, which the C++ never does. Turning it off changed no output on f70, 300 random WCNF files or 440 SMT-LIB scripts. Recommend deleting it (no C++ counterpart). After F2 its `weights == nil` filter no longer means "inactive".
- FUZZ_A-F1 explains 15 of the 16 OPB bounds files. Its verified binary (`S/work/FUZZ_A/g3final3`) matches z3 on all of them except f170, which also needs F4 here. FUZZ_A's patch (`S/work/FUZZ_A/FUZZ_A_verified.patch`) does not apply cleanly to `S/dbg/pkg` (rejected hunks in `objective_decomposition_batch.go` and `smt_theory_arith_eq.go`). I verified the combination by building FUZZ_A's tree plus F1 and F4 (`S/work/FUZZ_J/combo/pkg`). Whoever merges FUZZ_A-F1 should also delete the fallback `[(* (- 1) oo):oo]` printer in `shell/opb_frontend_output.go:38-44` (and the WCNF twin), as FUZZ_A already noted.

### SMT core and theories (`pkg/smtcore`, from `src/smt`)

**smtcore_01**

  `pkg/smtcore/smt_theory_propagation.go:373` (`PropagateCore`) does not mirror.

  `pkg/smtcore/theory_dense_diff_equality.go:225` use `searchBaseLevel` in the same restart-pair test.
- Out of shard: `pkg/smtcore/smt_internalizer.go:369-377` marks an AUX_LEMMA for reinit when
  `firstValue == False || (secondValue == False && firstValue == Undef)`; `src/smt/smt_internalizer.cpp:1358-1364`

  `mark_for_reinit(cls, m_scope_lvl, ...)` changes `reinit_clauses`.
- `pkg/smtcore/smt_asserted_reduce.go:90`: the per-formula results are released formula first, proof second;
  `simplify_fmls::operator()` (`src/smt/asserted_formulas.cpp:400-401`) destroys `result_pr` before `result`.
  Matters only with proofs when both die (formula dropped as `true` or after an inconsistency) and only
  for AST id recycling order.
- `pkg/smtcore/smt_asserted_ite.go:40-42`, `smt_asserted_pull_quant.go:19`, `smt_asserted_bounds.go:120`,
  `smt_asserted_reduce.go:143`, `smt_asserted_macros.go:24`: `push_app_ite_rw`, `pull_nested_quant`,

  pass. Results are the same (pure rewriters) but cached terms die earlier in Go; settle by comparing

  (`ctx_solver_simplify_tactic.cpp:46-48`).

  solver; C++ member order builds `m_solver` first (`src/smt/expr_context_simplifier.cpp:313-317`). Only
  relevant if kernel construction creates declarations or sorts (ids come from the declaration id generator).

  0-ary term) before the warning; `cost_parser` cannot build such terms. `smtCostNumeral` parses any size
  where C++ uses `get_int64()`.

  `pkg/smtcore/old_interval.go:384-420` (the dependency join is computed even when the bound is infinite;

  production (all three owners set `source = true`; LRA and dense difference logic have their own

**smtcore_02**

- `pkg/smtcore/smt_search.go:467-479` vs `src/smt/smt_context.cpp:3588-3612` (other shard): `dynamicAck.propagate()` is inside `if !inconsistent`; C++ calls `m_dyn_ack_manager.propagate_eh()` after every resolved conflict, also when the learned clause left a conflict. Read both; not reproduced in isolation.
- `pkg/smtcore/smt_search.go:468` / `smt_restart.go:29-31` vs `smt_context.cpp:3595` (other shard): `restarts.due(scopeLevel, baseLevel)` gets the search level (`session.baseLevel`), C++ tests `m_scope_lvl - m_base_lvl > 2`; with assumptions the two differ by one. **smtcore_03**

- `pkg/smtcore/smt_search.go:640` and `smt_clause_maintenance.go:211` versus `src/smt/smt_context.cpp:3595-3610`: Go runs lemma GC inside `resolveSearchConflict`, before the restart and conflict-limit returns. C++ runs `del_inactive_lemmas()` after them, so a GC that falls due on a restart conflict happens after the restart. A run past 5000 conflicts with a restart on the GC conflict would settle it.
