- DIMACS `-st` output: z3 printed ` :total-time 0.00)` on a tiny instance where g3 omitted the line. C++ drops a double statistic only when it is exactly 0.0 (`clock()` based); check which clock the Go front end uses.
- `pkg/sat/sat_clause_set.go:393-405` (`satClauseSetIterator.Next`) returns `arena.ErrInvalidSlot` if the set changed since `Iter()`. The C++ iterator is a raw pointer pair with no such check. No consumer in this shard mutates during iteration; the simplifier's uses of `m_sub_todo` should be checked by the shard that owns `sat_simplifier*.go`.

**sat_02**

- `pkg/sat/sat_solver_parallel_exchange.go:5-52` (`exchangeParallelBound`, reached from `popReinit` in this shard) has no counterpart of `IF_VERBOSE(1, "(sat-sync out: N in: M)")` at `src/sat/sat_solver.cpp:920-922`; the string `sat-sync` is absent from non-test Go. Outside this shard; needs a parallel run to settle.
- At `-v:20` z3 prints `:avg-clause-size 2.44` and g3 `2.44444` for the same input (at `-v:10` both print `2.44444`), apparently because z3's earlier `(allocator-consolidate ... :memory 2.78)` message leaves `std::fixed`/`setprecision(2)` set on the verbose stream and g3 has no such message. Outside this shard; not traced to source.
- `src/sat/sat_clause_use_list.h:39,56,66,78` `STRACE("clause_use_list_bug", ...)` have no Go counterpart; they print object addresses, so identical output is not possible anyway.

**sat_03**

- `pkg/sat/sat_solver_gc.go:157` (`restart`, geometric case) vs `src/sat/sat_solver.cpp:1359`: `satGCUnsigned` returns `arena.ErrBounds` when `m_restart_threshold * m_restart_factor` exceeds `UINT_MAX`, where the C++ cast (undefined, in practice truncating on x86-64) continues. Needs `sat.restart=geometric` and about 44 restarts, which normal search cannot reach but the `get_consequences` loop (one `restart()` per iteration once `m_conflicts > max_conflicts`) could. Decide whether to wrap like the reference build.
- `pkg/sat/sat_solver_probing.go:168-174` and `sat_solver_probing_algorithm.go:280-289` vs `src/sat/sat_probing.cpp:45,204`: the probing cache is disabled when `memory::get_allocation_size()` (process-wide) exceeds `probing_chache_limit` (1024 MB); the Go compares the SAT `Runtime`'s own accounting (`:memory 8.18` vs `2.77` on the same run). Above 1 GB the two can disagree on whether `try_lit` uses cached implications, which changes search. Not reproducible with small inputs.
- `pkg/sat/sat_solver_parallel_exchange.go:34-36`: `uint32(literal.variable()) >= s.parallelNumVars` returns `ErrSATAssertion` unconditionally; the C++ `SASSERT(lit.var() < m_par_num_vars)` is compiled out in release. Unreachable as long as every lane filters exports with the same `m_par_num_vars`; should be under `satStorageSourceDebug` for consistency.
- Outside this shard, seen while testing F2: `pkg/sat/sat_solver_search_verbose.go:83` prints `s.conflict.conflicts` (`m_conflicts`) in `(sat-restart :conflicts ...)`, C++ prints `m_stats.m_conflict` (`sat_solver.cpp:1351`). They differ only after `copyParallelMainStatistics` replaced the statistics (a later check on the same solver).
- Outside this shard, seen while testing mutex extraction: with `-v:1` on an `assert-soft` problem `build/z3` prints `(optimize:check-sat)`, `(maxsmt)`, `(opt.maxsat mutex size: ...)`, `(opt.pd-maxres [..])`, `is-sat: l_true`, ... (37 lines), the Go binary prints nothing; stdout is identical. Input: `$S/work/sat_03/mx1.smt2`.
- Dead code kept in production files (policy, not behavior): `coreChunking`, `coreChunk`, `coreChunkCheck`, `bruteForceConsequences`, `satConsequencePruneUnfixed`, `satConsequenceBackRemove` (`sat_solver_consequences_chunking.go`) are reached only from tests, matching the C++ `if (false && asms.empty())`; `satSolverMUSMembers.verifyCore` ports `mus::verify_core`, which has no caller in C++ and omits its `IF_VERBOSE(3, ...)` line.
- Differential checks that found no difference (for the record): 120 random `get-consequences` instances with and without `sat.restart.max` (order-only differences, F1); 90 random `check-sat-assuming` + `get-unsat-core` instances with `sat.core.minimize=true`, plus hand-built cores of 40 and 70 literals covering `mus1`, `mus2`/`qx` and `core.minimize_partial`, compared including the full `-v:3` stream; 88 runs of random 150-variable 3-SAT under 22 parameter sets (`sat.gc` = glue, psm, glue_psm, psm_glue, dyn_psm with small `gc.initial`, `gc.k`, `gc.small_lbd`; `sat.phase` = random, always_true, always_false; `random_freq`, `random_seed`; `dyn_sub_res=false`; `minimize_lemmas=false`; `restart=geometric`; `probing=false`; `burst_search=0`) compared on all `-st` counters.

**sat_04**

- `rlimit-count` differs between `build/z3` and `bin/g3fix5` on 58 of 60 random incremental QF_BV scripts (`$S/work/sat_04/rnd/r*.smt2`). g3 is consistently a few units lower; all other statistics and all answers, models and cores are identical. In a minimal script that reaches the SAT core (`s2.smt2`, push plus one bvmul assertion) the counts match (279/279). A non-incremental single check (`s1.smt2`) already differs (z3 45, g3 42) before any SAT work, so the gap probably lies in the rewriter/preprocessing resource accounting, outside this shard. Settle it by bisecting `s1.smt2` with `-tr:` tags on the rewriter `checkpoint`/`inc` sites.

**sat_05**

- The rlimit-count gap with named assertions is outside this shard (cmd_context / named-assertion handling). With `:produce-unsat-cores true`, each `(assert (! a :named nI))` costs z3 3 rlimit steps and g3 2. With n=1/2/3 named assertions, `(get-info :all-statistics)` gives z3 6/9/12 and g3 4/6/8. The same gap shows up after `check-sat-using sat`, `apply skip` and `check-sat`. Unnamed assertions match. This is probably one missing `m.inc()`/`canceled()` per named assert (for example in `mk_fresh`/`mk_iff`/`mk_implies` for the label). Settle it by tracing which C++ calls charge `rlimit` in `cmd_context::assert_expr(name, t)`.

### Rewriters (`pkg/ast/rewriter`, from `src/ast/rewriter`)

**ast_rewriter_01**

- `pkg/ast/rewriter/arith_polynomial.go:513-635` (`rewriteAdd`) is a re-design of
  `mk_flat_add_core`/`mk_nflat_add_core`, not a transcription: one map pass, then
  sort, then `hoistEqualCoefficients`. No difference showed up in about 140 fuzz
  scripts without `hoist_mul`. When `sort_sums` and `hoist_cmul` are both on, the
  C++ skips the `mon_lt` sort and only runs `hoist_cmul`, while Go sorts first. A
  targeted `:sort_sums true :hoist_cmul true` differential would settle whether
  the order can differ.
- `pkg/ast/rewriter/arith_polynomial.go:181` and `arith_poly_mul.go:410`: Go
  uses `sort.SliceStable` where the C++ uses `std::sort` with `mon_lt`/`ast_lt`.
  With a non-strict-weak comparator (`mon_lt` ordinals can tie), the C++
  introsort order of tied elements can differ from a stable sort.
- `pkg/ast/rewriter/arith_rewriter.go:1194` (`MkEqCore`): the power reduction and
  `elim_to_real` run before the `m_arith_lhs || is_arith_term(...)` gate that
  C++ `mk_eq_core` applies first. I could not build an input where this matters,
  because a zero numeral or a `to_real` already makes a side an arithmetic term.

**ast_rewriter_02**

- `pkg/ast/rewriter/bv_bounds_convert.go:292-452` (`AddConstraint`) and `bv_bounds.go:436-459` (`AddBoundSigned`) port `bv_bounds::add_constraint`/`add_bound_signed`, which the C++ never calls (only `bv_bounds::rewrite` is used, from `bv_bound_chk_tactic.cpp:74`). Go `AddBoundSigned` is not a port of `add_bound_signed`: it goes through `convertSigned`/`record`, which clip against the current bounds, emit extra `record0`/`record1`/`convert_signed` traces, and lack the `&&` short-circuit. This is dead in both trees today. Either delete it per the dead-code policy or port `add_bound_signed` literally.
- `pkg/ast/rewriter/bv_bounds.go:417-426` (`convertSigned`, negated mixed-sign case): C++ (`bv_bounds.cpp:488-490`) always evaluates both `record` calls. Go returns after the first UNSAT, so the second `record0`/`record1` trace lines and the extra `nis` entry are skipped. The result is the same (UNSAT); only the trace differs.
- Outside this shard, seen while testing. A sort-mismatched application in `simplify`, e.g. `(bvadd (concat #x3 y) x)` with 8-bit `x`, prints `(error "line 15 column 50: g3: AST source precondition")`, while z3 prints `... Argument x at position 1 does not match declaration (declare-fun bvadd ((_ BitVec 12) (_ BitVec 12)) (_ BitVec 12))`. Also, CLI `pp.flat_assoc=false` is ignored by g3 (nested `bvmul` still printed flat). Both belong to the parser and printer shards.
- `rlimit-count` differs between g3fix5 and z3 even on a trivial BV `check-sat` (1704 vs 1671). This is not caused by this shard. It may already be covered by the resource-counter findings.

**ast_rewriter_03**

- `pkg/ast/rewriter/elim_bounds.go:177-182` vs `src/ast/rewriter/elim_bounds.cpp:84`. The C++ checks `is_mul(arg2)` without an arity test and takes `arg(1)`, so `(* -1 y z)` makes `y` a lower bound. Go requires exactly two multiplicands. The C++ behavior looks unsound: `y` can be eliminated even though `z` multiplies it. An AUFNIRA+ attempt did not show a difference. If the difference is real, record it as a z3 bug exclusion rather than copy it.
- `pkg/ast/rewriter/der.go:296-345` vs `src/ast/rewriter/der.cpp:269-315`. `der_sort_vars` checks the `done` mark only for nodes with `ref_count > 1`, while Go always marks and skips. Nodes with a reference count of 1 can be revisited in C++, and a revisited candidate variable could be pushed to `order` twice. Settle it with a crafted quantifier whose variable occurs exactly once.

**ast_rewriter_04**

- `pkg/ast/rewriter/fpa2bv_rewriter.go:132-134` vs `src/ast/fpa/fpa2bv_rewriter.cpp:52-55`. Go `MaxStepsExceeded` also checks `Budget().Used() > maxMemory`, which C++ does not. `SetLimits` is never called, so the `max_steps`/`max_memory` tactic params that the C++ constructor reads (`updt_params`) are ignored. This looks unreachable from SMT-LIB: `fpa2bv` rejects `:max_steps` in `using-params` in both binaries. An API test with tactic params would settle it.
- `pkg/ast/rewriter/fpa2bv_rewriter.go:103-109,319-320` vs `fpa2bv_rewriter.h:43-48`. Go `Reset`/`Cleanup` clear `bindings`, while C++ `reset()` is empty and `cleanup_buffers()` only finalizes `m_out`. This only matters after a rewrite aborted inside a quantifier, when C++ keeps stale bindings.
- `pkg/ast/rewriter/expr_safe_replace.go:60-62` vs `expr_safe_replace.cpp:27`. Go returns `ErrASTDomain` on a sort mismatch in release builds; C++ only `SASSERT`s. Check whether any caller inserts Int/Real-mixed pairs.
- `pkg/ast/rewriter/pb2bv_rewriter.go:121-126` (`network.SetEncoding(grouped)`). 4.7.1 `psort_nw` has no encoding selection (`src/util/sorting_network.h`). Check that `PsortASTGrouped` in `pkg/ast/util_psort_*` is exactly the 4.7.1 network (out of shard).
- `(and (< (* x x) y) (= (* z z) (* x y)))` under `(using-params qe :qe_nonlinear true)` differs: z3 has `(not (or (= 0.0 y) (not (<= 0.0 y))))`, g3 has `(not (<= y 0.0))`. This is probably the recorded qe_04-F1 (nlarith `assign`/`subst` skip factor_rewriter + th_rewriter) and not this shard, but worth rechecking after F1 is fixed.
- `pkg/ast/rewriter/factor_rewriter.go:115-137` (`negateNumeral`) uses the numeral's own Int/Real flag, while C++ `mk_numeral(-v, s)` uses the sort of `m_muls[0][0]`. These agree unless a mul mixes sorts; unlikely to matter.

**ast_rewriter_05**

- `pkg/ast/rewriter/string_regex_automaton.go:88-117` (`materialize`) against `src/math/automata/automaton.h:107-121,611-616`. The Go rebuilds the graph from `m_delta` in source order, so its inverse lists (`m_delta_inv`) are in source order. In C++ they are in `add()` call order: the constructor's `mvs` order, then the moves `add_final_to_init_moves` appends. One case where the two differ is `(re.++ (re.* "a") "b")`: the inverse list of the joined state is `[2->3, 1->3]` in C++ and `[1->3, 2->3]` in Go. `compress()` walks `m_delta_inv` and removes moves by swapping with the back of the list, so the compressed move order could differ. In 930 random `str.in.re` simplifications through both binaries I found no output difference. Settle it by comparing `Moves()` after `Compress` with the C++ `display` for star-then-concat regexes, or by keeping the inverse order in `sequenceAutomaton`.
- `pkg/ast/rewriter/seq_rewriter.go:1570-1580` (`RewritePrefix`) against `seq_rewriter.cpp:897-900`. When `a1` is the literal `""` inside an unsimplified concat, the C++ calls `mk_concat(0, ...)`, which raises "Invalid function application". The Go builds an empty sequence instead. This is reachable only with un-rewritten `(str.++ "" x)` arguments.
- `pkg/ast/rewriter/th_rewriter.go:209-224` (`ReduceQuantifier`). If `MkQuantifier` fails, `updated` stays null and the code drops into the annotation branch, which overwrites `err`. The merge error is lost. This is a Go-only error-path hazard, with no C++ equivalent.

**ast_rewriter_06**

- `pkg/ast/rewriter/bit_blaster/rewriter_traversal.go:280-285` (`Cleanup`) vs `src/ast/rewriter/rewriter_def.h:605-612`. The C++ `rewriter_tpl::cleanup()` calls `m_cfg.cleanup()`, which is the empty default for `blaster_rewriter_cfg`, so the cfg's `m_bindings` (blast_quant) survive. Go `Cleanup` also releases `r.bindings`. This is only observable after an exception thrown inside a quantifier with `blast_quant=true`, followed by reuse of the same rewriter. The question is whether any retained caller does that.
- `pkg/ast/rewriter/bit_blaster/engine_rotate.go:16-23` vs `bit_blaster_tpl_def.h:1044`. The C++ takes the constant rotate shortcut only when `k.is_unsigned()`, so k < 2^32. For larger constant amounts on a 64-bit or wider vector it builds the urem/eqs circuit. That circuit should fold to the same bits, but it is never constructed in Go. A 64-bit `ext_rotate_left` by `#x0000000100000003` through `bit-blast` in both binaries would settle it.
- `pkg/ast/rewriter/bit_blaster/engine_multiplier.go:205` (`constCaseMultiplier`). C++ computes `circuit_size = sz*sz*5` as `unsigned`, which wraps for sz >= 29309, and `case_size` can overflow. Go uses `int`. Only reachable for absurd widths.

### AST support: fpa, macros, normal forms, patterns, proofs, substitution

**ast_sub_01**

- `pkg/ast/macros/macro_numeric.go:296-310` (`IsVarPlusGround`) vs `src/ast/rewriter/poly_rewriter_def.h:1034`. C++ combines the ground parts with `poly_rewriter::mk_add(args, t)`, which goes through `mk_add_core` (folds numerals, merges monomials). Go uses the raw `mkAdd` (and a binary bvadd chain for BV). They only differ when two or more ground summands are found, which needs a non-flattened nested add such as `(+ 1 (+ 2 x))`. To settle it, run a model-finder test with an unflattened quantifier body.
- `pkg/ast/macros/macro_numeric.go:123-125` (`MkZero`) calls `MkDatalogNumeral`, which registers the arith, bv and datalog plugins on first use (`ast_datalog_finite.go:125-135`). If the datalog family is not registered yet at that point, family-id numbering could differ from C++, where `reg_decl_plugins` registers everything up front. Settle it by checking that every g3 entry point pre-registers datalog. Calling the arith/bv numeral constructors directly would avoid the side effect.
- `pkg/ast/macros/quasi_macros.go:458-497` vs `src/ast/macros/quasi_macros.cpp:334-363` (the expr_ref_vector overload used by `quasi_macros_tactic`). In C++, a successful pass pushes a null proof `ps` for every formula, and the `!found` branch pushes no dependencies. Go keeps the expansion proof and the dependencies in both branches. This is only observable with proofs or unsat cores enabled in the quasi-macros tactic. The C++ tactic would index past the end of the empty deps vector when cores are on, so it is probably excluded as a z3 bug. Check against `z3_bug_exclusions.txt`.
- `pkg/ast/macros/macro_candidates.go:256`: `make([]ast.ASTHandle, 0, n-1)` with `n uint32` panics with a huge capacity if `ClauseNumLiterals` ever returns 0 (an `(or)` with no arguments). C++ has no such allocation. This is probably unreachable because the simplifier removes empty ors.

**ast_sub_02**

- `pkg/ast/normal_forms/name_exprs.go:200-330` vs `src/ast/rewriter/rewriter_def.h:231-235` (`constant_fold`): for ite, the C++ rewriter skips the dead branch once the condition has been rewritten to literal `true`/`false`, so names are not generated for it. The Go namer always visits all three children. This is reachable only when an ite with a literal Boolean condition reaches the namer. Settle it with a unit test on `(ite true A B)` as namer root.
- `pkg/ast/normal_forms/nnf.go:306-328` vs `nnf.cpp:373-378`: Go `convert` inserts results for constants and variables (the `skip` results, e.g. `not c`) into the act-caches when the ref count is above 1. The C++ never caches those. This changes cache occupancy, eviction timing and node lifetimes (id reuse).
- `pkg/ast/normal_forms/pull_quant.go:40` (`ReduceApp`) builds `before := MkApp(d, children)` even when proofs are off; the C++ builds it only inside `if (proofs_enabled())`. `:58` (`ReduceQuantifier`) returns `ErrASTPending` for an `exists`; the C++ release build hits `UNREACHABLE()` (a no-op) and returns false. With `smt.pull_nested_quantifiers=true nnf.skolemize=false` and an exists, g3 printed `unknown` while z3 segfaulted, so there is no clean comparison.
- `pkg/ast/normal_forms/pull_boolean.go:80-92`: a forall whose pulled body is an `exists` (or an outer exists) returns `ErrASTPending`. The C++ release build just calls `update_quantifier`. This is unreachable when the input is in SNF.
- `pkg/ast/proofs/checker.go:66-84` vs `proof_checker.cpp:900-905` (`add_premise`): Go marks a proof when it is popped, the C++ marks it when pushed. For shared sub-proofs the visit order, and so the order of side conditions, can differ. Validation verdicts are unaffected.

**ast_sub_03**

- `pkg/ast/proofs/reduce_hypotheses.go:314` vs `src/ast/proofs/proof_utils.cpp:522`: Go calls `inHypotheses(fact, hyps)` whenever `hyps != nil`. C++ calls it only when `hyps->size() == 1`, because `&&` short-circuits. The extra call can build a transient `(not fact)` that is then released. This matters only if the Go manager does not recycle the id the way C++ `id_gen` does, or under memory traces. Fix: compute `whole` only when `len(hyps) == 1`.
- `pkg/ast/substitution/substitution.go:436`, `offset.go:80-86` vs `src/ast/substitution/var_offset_map.h:90-101`: a variable index `>= vars_capacity` returns `ErrASTDomain` in Go. C++ release reads slot `v + off*num_vars`, which may be another variable's binding. This is only a concern if some muz caller under-reserves; checking each caller's `Reserve` against the maximum free-variable index of its inputs would settle it.
- `pkg/ast/substitution/substitution.go:66-74` vs `var_offset_map.h:64-72`: Go `Reserve` refuses with `ErrASTPending` while bindings exist. C++ silently invalidates them (the timestamp is bumped, while `m_vars`/`m_refs` stay). Every current caller resets first, and `substitution_tree::visit`'s `reserve_vars` runs with no bindings, so this looks unreachable.
- `pkg/ast/substitution/substitution_tree_compile.go:209-211` vs `substitution_tree.cpp:108-120`: `processArgs` errors when the in/out arities differ. C++ iterates over `out`'s arity (there is a `subst_tree_bug` CTRACE for this). That can only differ for variadic decls, and the only user indexes fixed-arity predicates.

### AST (`pkg/ast`, from `src/ast` and `src/util`)

**ast_01**

- `pkg/ast/ast_builtin_plugins.go:27-76` vs `src/ast/ast.cpp:1167-1196`: label and label-literal declaration failures return `ErrASTDomain`; the C++ raises "invalid label declaration" or "invalid label literal declaration". `pkg/ast/ast_basic_plugin.go:278-302` likewise returns `ErrASTDomain` where `basic_decl_plugin::mk_func_decl` raises "Invalid proof object.". Both look reachable only through internal or API construction, not SMT-LIB. Settle it by finding any API path that surfaces the message.
- `pkg/ast/ast_bv_conversion.go:55` and `pkg/ast/ast_bv_fixed_decl.go:116` reject a width of `MaxUint32` (an int2bv parameter of -1) with `ErrASTDomain`. The C++ wraps `bv_size+1` to 0 and builds a very-big sort. This is an undefined-behaviour corner and probably not worth matching.
- `pkg/ast/ast_array_names.go:110` (`IsAsArrayTree`) pushes the else and then branches in the opposite order to `array_util::is_as_array_tree`. The result is a pure boolean with no side effects, so this is not observable today.

**ast_02**

- `pkg/parsers/smt2/commands.go:1823-1833` vs `src/parsers/smt2/smt2parser.cpp` (`parse_indexed_sort`). This is outside the shard. The Go calls `p.advance()` past the closing `)` before it instantiates the indexed sort, while the C++ instantiates before `next()`. As a result, every sort-instantiation error is reported one column later: column 30 vs 29 for `(_ BitVec 0)`.
- Also outside the shard: `((_ sign_extend -1) x)` prints `unsigned numeral is out of range` in g3 but `invalid indexed identifier, index is too big to fit in an unsigned machine integer` in z3. This is the parser's index reader, not `bv_decl_plugin`.
- `pkg/ast/ast_bv_parameterized_decl.go:57-63,87-93` (`bvCheckedSize`). It returns `ErrASTDomain` when concat, extend or repeat widths overflow int32, where the C++ wraps (signed overflow is UB) and goes on. This is only reachable with widths near 2^31, so it is effectively unreachable; it is a documented, deliberate deviation.

**ast_03**

- `pkg/ast/ast_core_fresh_factories.go:100,129` (`MkFreshSort`, `MkFreshVarName`) format `m.freshID` as unsigned. C++ `string_buffer::append(unsigned)` uses `"%d"` (`src/util/string_buffer.h:92-100`), so fresh ids at or above 2^31 print as negative numbers. `freshNamedDecl` already casts with `int32`. These two should match it. Unreachable in practice.
- `pkg/ast/ast_datalog_sorts.go:169-196` (`DatalogFiniteSortSize`) only accepts finite-domain datalog sorts. C++ `dl_decl_util::try_get_size` (`src/ast/dl_decl_plugin.cpp:737-744`) succeeds for any sort with a finite `num_elements` (Bool, finite datatypes). Callers include `pkg/muz/rel/udoc_relation_factory.go:83` and `pkg/cmd_context/datalog_parser_terms.go:103`. Also, C++ `udoc_plugin::num_sort_bits` special-cases Bool before `try_get_size` (`src/muz/rel/udoc_relation.cpp:278`), and Go `sortWidth` does not (outside this shard). A Bool column in a udoc relation would settle it.
- `pkg/ast/ast_datalog_*.go`: every `dl_decl_plugin` failure returns `ErrASTDomain`. C++ raises specific messages: `check_bounds` "unexpected number of arguments, value is not within bound L <= v <= U", "sort miss-match for relational access", "index out of bound", "Domain size of sort 'X' may not be 0", "value is out of bounds", "operator not recognized". Most of these are reachable only from the API or the muz engine.
- `pkg/ast/ast_datalog_sorts.go:70-73` (`datalogRelationSort`) switches to very-big on uint64 overflow and stops. C++ keeps multiplying a rational, so a later size-0 column would make the result finite 0. C++ also keeps checking that the remaining parameters are sorts. This needs a size-0 finite sort.
- `pkg/ast/ast_datatype_definition.go:55-63,190-192` (`MkDatatypes`) rolls back a block that is not well-founded. C++ leaves the new `def`s in `m_defs` (and has already run `u().reset()`), so a later lookup or redeclaration of those names behaves differently. Check after the F2 fix.
- `pkg/ast/ast_core_plugin_dispatch.go:142-175`: a proof application with bad arguments returns `ErrASTDomain`, where C++ `basic_decl_plugin::mk_func_decl` raises "Invalid proof object.". Only reachable with proofs enabled.
- `pkg/ast/ast_core.go:305-346` (`closeCore`) finalizes and destroys each plugin in one loop. C++ `~ast_manager` runs `finalize()` on every plugin first and then `dealloc`s them all. This only matters for teardown order and leak traces.
- Outside this shard: `(eval y :model_completion true)` reports `line 7 column 26` in g3 and `line 7 column 8` in z3 (cmd_context keyword error position).

**ast_04**

- `pkg/ast/ast_expr2var.go:128-132` vs `src/ast/expr2var.cpp:27-35`. `Expr2Var.Insert` returns
  `ErrASTDomain` when the key is already mapped. The C++ `obj_map::insert` overwrites the value (and leaks a ref).
  The only plausible re-insert is `nlqsat::init_expr2var` (`src/qe/nlqsat.cpp:709-725`), if two
  quantifier blocks ever contain the same constant. Check whether hoisted qvars can repeat.
- `pkg/ast/ast_expr2polynomial.go:319-329` vs `src/ast/expr2polynomial.cpp:153-161`. When the shared
  expr2var already maps `t`, the Go still records `var2expr`/`varIsInt`, while the C++ leaves `m_var2expr`
  unset (C++ `to_expr` would then read null). This affects only `to_expr` after a shared mapping. nlsat
  does not call `to_expr`, so it looks harmless. Also, `variableExpression` uses the local `varIsInt` rather than
  `variables.IsExprPolynomialInteger` (the C++ `m_wrapper.is_int`) for the `to_real` decision.
- `pkg/ast/ast_format_flat.go:266-280` (group-choice shortcut). It assumes that flattening the first
  argument of a group choice creates no new nodes. That holds only when the first argument is already flat.
  Choices built directly with `FormatChoice` whose first argument contains line breaks would make the C++
  create extra format-manager nodes. Only format-manager node ids and the app trace could differ; printed
  text is unchanged.
- `pkg/ast/ast_family.go:170-189`. `AppendDom`/`AppendRange` iterate in insertion order, while the C++
  `symbol_table::get_dom/get_range` iterate in hash-table order. No non-test Go caller was found, so this is latent.

**ast_05**

- `pkg/ast/ast_func_decl_dependencies.go:389-405` vs `src/ast/func_decl_dependencies.cpp:58-69`: `FuncDeclDependencies.Reset` erases the `layout` ObjMap entry by entry. The C++ calls `m_deps.reset()`, which clears every slot with no tombstones and halves capacity when the table is sparse.
  - After a reset, Go keeps tombstones and capacity, so later inserts can trigger an earlier expand or rehash. The next `Reset` then dec_refs in a different table order.
  - The model finder resets these dependencies every MBQI round (`smtcore/smt_model_finder.go:638`).
  - Possible effect: AST-id reuse order. Likely nil when the dependency decls are still referenced elsewhere.
  - Fix idea: release refs in layout order, then call `d.layout.Reset()`.
- `pkg/ast/ast_lt.go:333-334` vs `src/ast/ast_lt.cpp:110`: quantifier weights are compared as `uint32`, while the C++ `check_value` compares `int`. The results differ only for weights ≥ 2^31, which are negative in C++ and only reachable through the API.
- A nullary FPA special constant applied to an argument, `((_ +zero 3 3) f)`: g3 prints `g3: AST source precondition`, z3 prints `Wrong number of arguments (1) passed to function (declare-fun +zero () (_ FloatingPoint 3 3))` (confirmed). `floatingPointSpecialDecl` correctly ignores arity, so the arity check after the decl in `mkAppHeldDecl` (outside this shard) seems not to produce the `check_args` message for FPA decls. Settle by tracing where `ErrASTDomain` comes from in `mkAppHeldDecl`.
- `pkg/ast/ast_label.go:13-15`: `MkLabel` with no names returns `ErrASTDomain` in release builds. The C++ only asserts, then `label_decl_plugin` raises "invalid label declaration". No caller passes an empty name list today.
- `pkg/ast/ast_fpa_bv2rm_decl.go:42-44`: with a null range, the Go synthesizes the RoundingMode sort. The C++ `is_rm_sort(range)` dereferences null. Unreachable from SMT-LIB because `bv2rm` has no surface name.
- `pkg/ast/ast_fpa_model_value.go`: the `t_fpa` / `t_fpa_detail` TRACE records of `fpa_value_proc::mk_value` and `fpa_rm_value_proc::mk_value` (`src/smt/theory_fpa.cpp:129-132,190-195,207-210,226`) are not emitted here. They may be emitted by the smtcore caller; check `smtcore/theory_fpa*.go` before reporting.

**ast_06**

- `pkg/ast/ast_pb_util.go:196-220` (`MkPseudoBooleanLT`) against `src/ast/pb_decl_plugin.cpp:165-182`. `pb_util::mk_lt` complements its arguments with `ast_util` `mk_not`, which strips a `not` and folds true/false. Go builds a raw `(not x)` with `mkFamilyApp(0, ASTOpNot, ...)`. The function has no Go caller, and `mk_lt` has no caller in the C++ tree either, so it looks like dead code that was ported. Either delete it or use the `mk_not` helper.
- `pkg/ast/ast_pb_recognizers.go:140-200` (`PseudoBooleanCoefficient`, `PseudoBooleanHasUnitCoefficients`) do not check that the decl belongs to the pb family before treating kinds 0/1 as cardinality. For a non-PB app of kind 0/1 they return 1/true. The C++ `is_at_most_k` tests the family. All current callers seem to pass PB atoms only (where the C++ has a `SASSERT`); a grep of callers would settle it.
- `pkg/ast/ast_printer.go:268-298` (`SimpleASTPrinterContext.displayFormat`/`DisplayFuncDecl`). When indent is non-zero, Go prepends spaces to the first line and after every newline, and lays out the format without the indent. The C++ wraps the format in `mk_indent`, which indents only after line breaks and affects width decisions. `display(func_decl)` prints only `f->get_name()`, with no indent. Every current Go caller passes indent 0, so this is latent.
- `pkg/ast/ast_parameter.go:270-275` (`parameterHash`, the double case) returns an error for negative or out-of-range doubles. The C++ does `static_cast<unsigned>(m_dval)`, which is UB but does not throw. This is only reachable if a double parameter is ever hashed.
- Outside this shard: on `t5.smt2` line 4 (`:pattern ((p (not (not x))) (not (not x)))`), g3 prints the warning `'not' cannot be used in patterns.` four times, while z3 prints it twice. This points at the parser or pattern validator (`pkg/parsers/smt2` / pattern_validation), not at this shard.

**ast_07**

- `pkg/cmd_context/sort_info.go:213` (`Context.SMT2FuncDecls`), outside this shard, vs `src/cmd_context/cmd_context.cpp:441,452`. The C++ `pp_env::pp_fdecl` / `pp_fdecl_ref` also look `f` up under its alias (`m_func_decl2alias`) and then print the *alias* symbol. The Go looks up only `f`'s own name and always prints `f`'s name (`SMT2Fdecl` uses `SMT2FdeclNameDecl`). This matters only if some Go command inserts a func_decl under a name different from its own (`cmd_context::insert(s, f)` with `s != f->get_name()`).
- `pkg/ast/ast_translation_datatype.go:91-151` vs `src/ast/datatype_decl_plugin.cpp:172-188` (`plugin::inherit`).
  - The Go re-creates datatypes in the target with `MkDatatypes`, ordered by class id and then by name.
  - The C++ translates each `def` in `m_defs` hash order via `def::translate`, keeps the source class ids, and then sets `m_class_id = m_defs.size()`. Constructors are created lazily.
  - The two orders of AST construction in the target manager differ, so target AST ids, and with them id-ordered heuristics in translated solvers, may diverge.
  - A related point: the C++ `ast_translation::mk_func_decl` (`ast_translation.cpp:139-142`) builds `new_fi` without `private_parameters`, while the Go (`ast_translation.go`, `buildNode`) passes `n.info.private`. Whether this is visible depends on which equal decl the target creates first. `decl_info::operator==` ignores the private flag, and so does Go `infoEqual`.
- `pkg/api/api_ast_benchmark.go:19-24` (`apiBenchmarkSymbol`), outside this shard. An empty Go string becomes a null symbol. The C++ API passes non-null `""` pointers: name `""` prints `"; \n"` and status `""` prints `(set-info :status )`. The latter is confirmed in `bench2.c` output. Go prints no name line and `(set-info :status unknown)`.
- Outside this shard: `((_ map and) a a)` with `a : (Array Int Int)` gives g3 `(error "... g3: AST source precondition")`, while z3 says `map expects the argument at position 0 to have the array range the same as the function` (`src/ast/array_decl_plugin.cpp:180-185`). Input: `$S/work/ast_07/mapmsg.smt2`.
- Outside this shard: `(set-option :interactive-mode true)` after an assertion. g3: `line 3 column 34: option value cannot be modified after initialization`. z3: `line 3 column 30: error setting ':produce-assertions', option value cannot be modified after initialization`. The column and the text both differ.
- `pkg/ast/ast_sort_size.go:57` (`SortSize.Size`) returns an error for non-finite sizes. The C++ `sort_size::size()` only SASSERTs and returns `m_size`, which is 0 for `mk_very_big`/`mk_infinite`. A release-build caller that reads `size()` without checking would continue in C++ and fail in Go. I did not audit callers (outside this shard).

**ast_08**

- `pkg/ast/util_psort_ast_bounds.go:573-596` (`atMostOneSmall`) vs `src/util/sorting_network.h:384` builds `not(result)`, then `not(xs[i])`, then `not(xs[j])` left to right. In `add_clause(ctx.mk_not(result), ctx.mk_not(xs[i]), ctx.mk_not(xs[j]))`, GCC (right-to-left argument evaluation, as assumed elsewhere in the port, e.g. `qe/nlqsat_division.go:366`) would create `not(xs[j])` first. When the negations are new, AST ids differ. A 7x6 pigeonhole `card2bv` + smt run and the goal printout were identical between the binaries, so no observable effect was found. Comparing AST ids in a trace build (for example with a tag that prints `get_id()`) would settle it. Other multi-`mk_not` call sites (`cmp_le`, `dsmerge` 3-literal clauses) reuse negations already created by earlier clauses, so they are unaffected.
- Outside this shard (rewriter): `pkg/ast/rewriter/pb2bv_rewriter.go:742-760`, `rewriteApp`, rewrites `at-least 1`/`pbge` with bound 1 directly into `(or ...)` and adds `keepCardinality`/`retainWeighted` paths. 4.7.1 `card2bv_rewriter::mk_app_core` (`src/ast/rewriter/pb2bv_rewriter.cpp`) has none of these, and they look like newer-Z3 features. A small at-least-1 `card2bv` input produced identical goals here, but the reviewer of the pb2bv shard should check it against the 4.7.1 source.
- `pkg/ast/ast_well_sorted.go:177-179` returns `ErrASTDomain` when a left- or right-only associative decl has more arguments than its arity. The C++ reads `decl->get_domain(i)` out of bounds (UB). The SMT2 parser left-folds `(- a b c)`, so no such app was produced; this only matters for API-built terms.

### Models (`pkg/model`)

**model_01**

- `pkg/model/model_evaluator.go:670-672,779-781` vs `src/model/model_evaluator.cpp:149-165,186-193`. Go returns `ErrModelEvaluatorTheory` for an equality over a sort family > 4 that no dispatcher handles, and for applications of any unhandled family > 4. The C++ falls through to `m_b_rw.mk_app_core` (equality), or to `evaluate`/`evaluate_partial_theory_func` and BR_FAILED. Any registered family without an evaluator rewriter (for example the datalog finite-domain `datalog_relation` sorts and ops) would make Go abort evaluation where z3 leaves the term. To settle it: evaluate a finite-domain equality from a `fp.engine=datalog` model.
- `pkg/model/model_evaluator.go:171` vs `src/model/model_evaluator.cpp:64`. The C++ builds `m_bv_rw(m)` without the evaluator params `p`, while Go passes `p` to `NewBVRewriter`. This only matters if a caller passes `rewriter.*` BV keys (hi_div0, blast_eq_value, …) in the evaluator's local params.
- `pkg/model/model_eval.go:269-285` vs `src/model/model.cpp:79-90`. `model::eval` catches `model_evaluator_exception` (rewriter_exception: max memory or cancellation) and returns false. `Model.Evaluate` returns the error. This is the same class as smtcore_14-F3. The callers that matter are `api/api_model_evaluate.go` (C++ `Z3_model_eval` returns TRUE with whatever result) and `qe/bool_project.go`.
- `pkg/model/model_copy.go:191-192` vs `src/smt/proto_model/proto_model.cpp:382`. `TransferFunctionInterpretations` clears `functionDeclarations` (`m_func_decls`), but the C++ only resets `m_finterp`. It matters only if the proto model is queried after `mk_model`.
- `pkg/model/fpa/bv2fpa_functions.go:122-213` vs `src/ast/fpa/bv2fpa_converter.cpp:279-311`. The C++ applies `m_th_rw` to every rebuilt argument, result and else. Go does not. This matters only when `rebuild_floats` rebuilds a non-value application, such as a datatype containing floats.
- `pkg/model/fpa/bv2fpa_functions.go:228-232`. The arity-0 array branch of `convert_uf2bvuf` (`convert_array_func_interp`) is skipped with a comment saying it is handled elsewhere. A quick `(check-sat-using (then fpa2bv smt))` over `(Array Int (_ FloatingPoint 3 3))` matched z3, so it is not confirmed as a bug.
- `pkg/model/model_implicant_minimize.go:251-284`. `markCone` (for `for_each_expr`) does not visit quantifier patterns or no-patterns, but `for_each_expr` does. Only reachable with quantified formulas in the implicant.

### Numerals (`pkg/util/numeral`: mpz, mpq, mpf, mpbq, mpn, rational, hwf)

**util_numeral_01**

- `pkg/util/numeral/hwf_numeral.go:197-200` (`HardwareFloatNumeralManager.Power`) vs `src/util/f2n.h:101-114` (`f2n::power`).
  - **Go:** for `exponent >= 2^31`, Go returns `arena.ErrBounds`.
  - **C++:** the `mask <<= 1` loop wraps `mask` to 0. Squaring `power` then either overflows, so `check` throws `f2n::exception`, or loops forever when |a| <= 1.
  - **Why it matters:** subpaving callers catch only `ErrHardwareFloatNonRegular` (for example `math/subpaving/hardware_context_propagate.go:117`). For |a| > 1, Go would propagate a hard error where C++ catches the exception and continues.
  - **Reachability:** it needs a monomial degree of at least 2^31, so it is practically unreachable. The deviation is commented next to the code.
  - **What would settle it:** mapping the |a| > 1 case to `ErrHardwareFloatNonRegular` would match C++ exactly.
- `pkg/util/numeral/inf_int_rational.go:277-283` (`infIntPublishSecond`) and `InfIntString` (INT_MIN branch) vs `src/util/inf_int_rational.h:154-175,231-234` and `inf_int_rational.cpp:26-39`.
  - **C++:** `int m_second` overflow is undefined behaviour, which GCC compiles as wrap-around.
  - **Go:** returns `ErrInfIntOverflow` instead.
  - **Reachability:** `OwnedInfIntRational` has no consumer outside `pkg/util/numeral`, so this is latent only.

**util_numeral_02**

- `pkg/util/numeral/mpf_numeral_arithmetic.go:6-81` + `mpf_numeral_raw_scope.go:3-11`, C++ `src/util/f2n.h:96-111`. When `Inv` or `Power` stops on a `check()` failure (the C++ throws `f2n::exception`), Go leaves `rawPending=true`. Every later `Inv`/`Power` on that wrapper then returns `ErrArbitraryFloatNumeralRawPending` until someone calls `CleanupRawLocal`, and no non-test code does. The C++ leaks the local, but later calls work, and `context_t::propagate` / `relevant_new_bound` catch the exception and continue (`subpaving_t_def.h:1313,1725`). An interval power whose endpoint is 0 or underflows would make every later monomial power propagation fail in Go. To settle it, drive an mpf subpaving context through a failing `Power` and then a valid one. The fix is probably for `beginRawLocal` to release (via `CleanupRawLocal`) a stale local from a previous failed call, or for callers to call `CleanupRawLocal` when they catch the error.
- `pkg/util/numeral/mpf_integer_query.go:100` (`finishIntegerQuerySource`) leaves `s.active = ... || MatchesCopyAllocationInvocation(&s.copy)` after a successful call. If that receipt keeps matching after a big-significand copy, the next `IsInt` returns `ErrNumericPending` (`IsInt` refuses while `integerQuery.active`). A unit test calling `IsInt` twice on a value with sbits ≥ 33 would settle it.
- `pkg/util/numeral/mpbq_select.go:563-588` (`refineWithReceipt`) and `mpbq_select.go:244-253` (`SelectSmallCore`) turn the C++ `SASSERT` preconditions (`l < q < u`, q not dyadic, `lower <= upper`) into returned errors. Release C++ would go on (and refine on a dyadic q still terminates). This only matters if a retained caller can pass a dyadic q. The upolynomial callers appear to exclude that.
- `pkg/util/numeral/mpf_extrema.go:41-48`: `max/min(+0,-0)` uses the Go `UnreachableSource` hook. Release C++ `UNREACHABLE()` exits the process. I did not check how the hook maps this. The fpa rewriter normally intercepts these inputs first.

**util_numeral_03**

- `pkg/util/numeral/mpf_remainder_object_trace.go:16-23` vs `src/util/mpf.cpp:1621-1633` (`to_string_hexfloat(mpf const&)`). The Go builds the high 32 bits of the printed word from `mpz::m_val`. In the GCC LP64 layout `mpz` is 8-byte aligned, so `significand` starts at offset 8, and bytes 4-7 of `mpf` are padding. `build_trace/z3 -tr:mpf_dbg_rem` printed `X = 1.9541015625 9=7CAD000C0008`; the high word `0x7CAD` is not the significand. The C++ value is indeterminate, so g3 cannot match it exactly. Printing only the low word, or zero for the high word, would be the closest deterministic choice. This is a debug trace only.
- Whatever F1's fix does to the histories in this shard, the root of the close-time O(n²) is in `pkg/ast` (`astScopedFloatVector.destroy` → `ArbitraryFloatValueCopyChain.Cleanup`) together with `mpf_value_copy_invocation.go`. Both are outside this shard, so whoever owns them should re-check them.

**util_numeral_04**

- `pkg/util/numeral/mpff_convert.go:128-132` vs `src/util/mpff.cpp:348-349` (`set_core` mpz). When the decomposed mpz's top word has its MSB set, `num_leading_zeros` is 0 and the C++ calls `shl(w_sz, w, 0, ...)`. `bit_util.cpp:214-222` then shifts by `comp_shift = 32`, which is UB; on x86 it ORs each lower word into the next. Go's `ffShift` with k=0 copies cleanly. The C++ release result for, say, `2^95 + 1` would differ in the low significand word. This is reachable only through the MPFF subpaving numeral (currently broken per KNOWN math_subpaving_04-F1). It is a C++ UB bug, so it probably belongs in `z3_bug_exclusions.txt` rather than being copied. A `build/z3` run of `(check-sat-using (using-params subpaving :numeral mpff))` on a problem with a 96-bit integer coefficient would settle it.
- `src/util/mpfx.cpp:485-506`. When `q_sz < m_total_sz` and rounding carries out of the low `q_sz` quotient words, the C++ `inc(m_total_sz, w_q)` writes the carry into a stale buffer word that is never copied, so the result collapses to zero/epsilon. Go's `roundMagnitude` keeps the carry. I believe the operands needed for this are very unlikely in practice; it is a C++ defect, not a porting bug.
- Out of shard (for re-dispatch to the subpaving reviewers): the same `sp1.smt2` mpfx_trace diff shows the 9-line `(1)/(20) ... (10)^10 ... (1)/(8192)` setup block emitted 3 times by C++ and 2 times by g3. It also shows extra Go `[mpfx] (1 < 9) == (1 == 1)` comparisons where the C++ has none, and a different later propagation order (`(4) * (53687091/2^30)`), which suggests a divergence in `math/subpaving` (fixed context bound normalization / propagation) or the subpaving tactic, not in `util/numeral`.

**util_numeral_05**

- `pkg/util/numeral/mpq_power.go:56-58` (`Power`) vs `src/util/mpq.cpp:287-292`: when `p >= 2^31`, the C++ `mask <<= 1` wraps to 0 and `while (mask <= p)` never ends. Go returns `PowerDomainError` at the wrap. This replaces a hang with an error and is documented in the function comment. It is only reachable with huge exponents. `bitwiseBinary`'s `BitwiseNonterminationError` does the same for negative operands, which violate the C++ `SASSERT(is_nonneg)`. I am not reporting either as a bug. I list them only so the owner can confirm both are recorded deviations.
- `pkg/util/numeral/mpz_div.go:40-42` and the related division entry points return `ErrDivideByZero` where the C++ small path divides by zero natively (SIGFPE) and the big path is undefined. This is an explicit-error-instead-of-crash policy. No observable difference on valid input.

**util_numeral_06**

- `pkg/util/numeral/mpz_power_shift.go:278-291` (`powerCoreWithPhysicalContext`) and `pkg/util/numeral/mpzzp.go:602-615` (`powerWithSourceContext`) vs `src/util/mpz.cpp:1497-1504` / `src/util/mpzzp.h:248-253`: when the exponent is >= 2^31, the C++ `mask <<= 1` wraps to 0 and `while (mask <= p)` never ends (a hang). The Go returns `PowerDomainError`. This is a deliberate guard on a nonterminating C++ path, so it is not reported. It only matters if some caller can pass such an exponent and expects the error to be handled.
- `pkg/util/numeral/mpzzp.go:144-155` (`Field`): the Go refuses with `ErrModularPrimeUninitialized` when the manager was built with `NewIntegerModularManagerWith{Modulus,Uint64}` and no later `SetZP`/`SetPSquare` happened. The C++ constructor leaves `m_p_prime` uninitialized, so this mirrors undefined behavior. Neither constructor has a non-test caller today (grep). If one is ever wired in, `Divides`/`Div` in finite mode would error where the C++ reads garbage.
- `pkg/util/numeral/mpz_root.go:42-44` (`rootDomain`): `n == 0` with a nonzero operand returns `RootDomainError` where the C++ divides by zero in `div_l`. This is a guard on a crash path, with no observable difference on defined inputs.

**util_numeral_07**

- `pkg/util/numeral/rational_service_small_rat.go:15-122` (`SetSmallRat`, `SetBigRat`, `BigRat`) are Go-only fast paths with no C++ counterpart. The ast and rewriter numeral constructors call them in place of the `mpq_manager::set(char const*)` / `to_string` round trip. I checked that they store the same normalized representation as `SetString`: a reduced numerator and denominator, a one-limb value through `SetInt64`, `-2^31` stored big on both paths, and a den of 1 stored small. They step aside when the `mpq_set`/`mpn_to_string` traces are on. No divergence found. The one residual question is cell capacity: a value set from limbs may get a different cell capacity than one built digit by digit. Capacity is not observable in the answer, statistics or traces unless memory accounting output is compared.
- `pkg/util/numeral/scoped_binary.go:337-356` (`macroCompare`, `compareRaw`) are reached only from `scoped_binary_test.go`. They model the `MPBQ_MK_COMPARISON` macros correctly, but they are dead on live paths.

### LP solver (`pkg/util/lp`)

**util_lp_01**

- `pkg/util/lp/driver_lu_check.go:37-46,67-97,131-158` versus `src/test/lp.cpp:2568-2620`:
  on a truncated `--checklu` file (EOF before `basis_end`), C++ `getline` yields `""`
  forever. `read_basis` then loops pushing `atoi("")==0` and never ends. Go returns
  `io.EOF`. This is a crash in the C++, so the Go is arguably better. Noted only for
  completeness.
- `pkg/util/lp/driver_file_list.go:18-44` versus `src/test/lp.cpp:2508-2527`: if the
  `--filelist` path is a directory, `std::ifstream` opens it on Linux, `getline`
  fails at once, and C++ returns an empty list. Go `os.Open` succeeds, then
  `ReadString` returns `EISDIR`, which Go propagates as an error. This only affects
  the test driver.
- `pkg/util/lp/driver_arguments.go:160-176`, `driver_lu_check.go:50-53`: strict
  `strconv` parsing replaces `atoi`/`atof`. The Go comment records this as a
  deliberate deviation. Malformed numbers produce errors instead of a prefix value
  or 0.
- In the float core (`core_base_float.go:205-226`, `core_iteration_float.go:140`,
  `core_values_float.go:23,59,115,167`), expressions such as `x*y+z` may be fused
  into FMA by the Go compiler on arm64/ppc64/s390x. On amd64 (default GOAMD64=v1)
  they are not fused, which matches GCC x86-64. This is not a finding for the
  reference platform.

**util_lp_02**

- `pkg/util/lp/dual_solver_float.go:190-210` (`FloatDualSimplex.GetCurrentCost`) and its sibling `primal_solver_float.go:84` sum `cost*value` over columns in ascending key order. C++ `lp_dual_simplex.hpp:377-384` iterates `std::unordered_map<var_index, column_info*>`, whose libstdc++ order is generally not ascending. For doubles a different summation order can change the last bits of the `cost = ` line in the float MPS drivers, and with it the `values_are_one_percent_close` decision only in extreme cases. Comparing printed `cost =` lines of `test-z3 lp --file X.mps` against a Go run on a model with many columns would settle it. The project's `StdUnorderedRationalMap` emulation shows how the libstdc++ order could be reproduced if needed. The rational instance sums exactly, so order does not matter there.
- `pkg/util/lp/driver_settings.go` relies on `DriverArguments.uintValue` (`driver_arguments.go:160`, outside this shard). It uses `strconv.ParseInt` and returns an error for inputs such as `--rep_frq 12abc` or `--max_iters ""`-style junk, while C++ `atoi` silently yields the numeric prefix (or 0). This only matters for malformed driver arguments.

**util_lp_03**

- `pkg/util/lp/lar_conflict_certificate.go:213` (`TheLeftSidesSumToZero`) prints the leftover `left side = ...` combination by ranging over a Go map. C++ (`lar_solver.h` `the_left_sides_sum_to_zero`) iterates a `std::unordered_map<var_index, mpq>`. This only runs inside a debug-only assertion that is failing, so the printed order is cosmetic. If it matters, use the same libstdc++ order emulation.

**util_lp_04**

- `pkg/util/lp/mps_reader_float.go:637-689` (`fillFloatSolver`) against `src/util/lp/mps_reader.h:707-727`. The C++ walks `m_rows` and `m_columns` in `std::unordered_map` order; Go uses insertion order. The source and the manifest both document this. `lp_solver` keys constraints and column info by index, so the solution should not depend on the order, and the test LP printed the same model. A larger LP whose `print_model` order or tie-breaking could depend on `m_names_to_columns` / `m_A_values` construction order would settle it.
- `pkg/util/lp/mps_reader_float.go:323-328` (`rowPairs`, range branch) against `src/util/lp/mps_reader.h:582`. The C++ evaluates `m_line.substr(14)` before `read_range_by_columns` checks `m_line.size() < 14`. On a RANGES line shorter than 14 bytes whose row is unknown, it therefore throws `std::out_of_range`, which is uncaught. Go prints `line is too short` instead. This is a z3 crash path; it could be listed in `z3_bug_exclusions.txt` rather than changed.
- `pkg/util/lp/mps_reader_float.go:311-315` (`rowPairs`). An empty token list returns `ErrBounds`, where the C++ loop bound `tokens.size()-1` wraps to `UINT_MAX` (undefined behavior). This needs an RHS line exactly 14 bytes long, or one whose data after column 14 is blank. It is an explicit error, not a silent divergence.

**util_lp_05**

- None in this shard beyond F1. Things I checked and did not report:
  - `RandomUpdater.Update` iterates a sorted snapshot of `vars`, which matches the ascending `std::set` order.
  - `GetCurrentCost` / `BoundsHold` (float) visit `unordered_map` keys in ascending order and say so in comments. Only the float sum order is affected, on the lp driver path, not SMT.
  - `NewFloatPrimalCoreSolverWithZeroLowBounds` leaves `EpsilonOfReducedCost` and the Bland threshold at zero. That is correct: the C++ second constructor leaves them uninitialized, and `init_run` sets epsilon.

**util_lp_06**

- `pkg/util/lp/solver_float.go:111-147` and `pkg/util/lp/solver_prepare_exact.go:8-56` (`MapExternalRowsToCoreSolverRows`, `MapExternalColumnsToCoreSolverColumns`, and the presolve/cleanup loops in `solver_presolve_float.go`/`solver_presolve_exact.go`) walk `AValues` in insdict insertion order. The C++ (`lp_solver.hpp:383-436`) walks `std::unordered_map<unsigned, std::unordered_map<unsigned,T>>` in libstdc++ order: with an identity hash, keys inserted ascending iterate descending until a rehash. Core row and column numbering, and therefore LU pivoting, can differ.
  - 600 random MPS LPs (2-15 rows, up to 20 columns, many tied optima) gave identical values and status, so I could not show an observable effect.
  - What would settle it: a degenerate LP whose optimal vertex depends on the basis order, or a debug comparison of `m_core_solver_columns_to_external_columns` between the two builds.
  - The comment at `solver_exact_model.go:22` says this is deliberate.
- `pkg/util/lp/static_matrix_float.go:287-322` (`MinAbsRow`, `MinAbsColumn`, and the maximum versions) use `math.Abs`. The C++ `lp::abs` (`lp_settings.h:349`) returns `-0.0` for `-0.0`, so `get_A_ratio` could produce `-Inf` where Go produces `+Inf` if a stored coefficient ever became `-0.0`. `Set` rejects zeros and IEEE `x + (-x)` gives `+0`, so I believe this is unreachable.

### Parameters (`pkg/util/params`)

**util_params_01**

- `pkg/util/params/util_param_descrs.go:655` (`ParamDescrs.Copy`) vs `src/util/params.cpp:200-206` (`param_descrs::imp::copy`). The C++ copies `other.m_info` in hash-table order, so the destination's `m_names` (what `get_param_name(i)` returns) gets hash order. Go copies in insertion order. `Copy` is only reached from `RegisterGlobal`/`registerModule` (global descriptors and modules registered twice: rewriter, nnf, sat, ackermannization). Those descriptor objects are not exposed through `Z3_param_descrs_get_name`/`to_string` (`api_params_object.go:212` only sees collector-built descriptors), so I found no observable effect. If gparams descriptors are ever exposed through the API, the same table emulation as in F1 is needed for `ParamDescrs.entries`.
- `pkg/util/params/util_param_descrs_stream.go:106-107` and `util_params_ref.go:1248-1249` (descriptor name display) vs `src/util/params.cpp:183-184`. For an uppercase letter, the C++ executes `out << (s[i] - 'A' + 'a')`, which inserts an `int` and prints the decimal code (for example `97`). Go prints the lowercase letter. No registered parameter name contains an uppercase letter (I checked all `.pyg` files and `insert(` call sites), so this is unreachable today.
- `pkg/util/params/util_gparams.go:380` (`GlobalParams.reset`) iterates a Go `map` (random order) to deallocate module cells. The C++ `imp::reset` (`gparams.cpp:116`) iterates `m_module_params` in table order. The only effect is the order of `dealloc` lines in debug (`g3debug`) `memory` traces.
- Front-end lead items 2–5 (`set-option` built-in kinds, the `:expand-definitions` `unsupported` path, the `produce-proofs` error text, error columns) do not originate in this shard. `GlobalParams.SetName`/`setValue` reproduce `gparams::set` exactly, including its message texts. Those divergences come from the caller in `pkg/parsers/smt2`/`pkg/cmd_context` routing built-in options to gparams; another shard needs to root-cause them. Item 9 (`-memory:`) is in `pkg/shell` and the memory runtime. `env_params::updt_params` (`util_env_params.go`) faithfully forwards `memory_max_size` through the saturating `megabytes_to_bytes`.

### Utilities (`pkg/util/*`)

**util_misc_01**

- `pkg/util/mincut/min_cut.go:113-209` (`validInitialGraph`) and `src/muz/spacer/spacer_unsat_core_plugin.cpp:633-700`. Go returns `ErrGraph` when a reached positive-capacity node cannot reach the sink. Go `Finalize` (`pkg/muz/spacer/unsat_core_plugin_min_cut.go:181`) then fails spacer where the C++ would loop. I could not find a spacer proof shape that produces such a node: every leaf pushed by `advance_to_lowest_partial_cut` is processed later and gets a sink edge. A spacer run with `minimize_unsat_core=true` on a proof with an already-closed B-pure leaf would settle it.
- `pkg/util/bitset/vector.go:105-129` and `src/util/bit_vector.cpp:37-79`. Go grows `words` to exactly `num_words`, while the C++ grows to `(num_words*3+1)>>1` (and to 2 or 1.5x in `push_back`). So the `bit_vector` TRACE line `capacity: N` prints different values. The manifest records this ("source word-capacity scheduling"), and `bitset.Vector` has no production caller (only `FixedManager` is used, by `muz/rel/tbv.go`), so it is not observable today.
- `pkg/util/backtrack/union_find.go:157-169` (`Dissolve`). The C++ `dissolve` resets only `v` because `v` never advances; Go dissolves the whole class. This is recorded in the manifest, and the C++ has no caller (grep finds none outside the header), so it is not observable.

**util_misc_02**

- `pkg/util/statistics/statistics.go:146` (`writeValue`) vs `src/util/statistics.cpp:131,152`. A double
  statistic that is infinite or NaN prints as `+Inf` / `NaN` in Go (strconv) and as `inf` / `nan` in C++
  (`std::fixed`). I confirmed the Go side with strconv. No in-shard producer of such values was found, and
  the one obvious producer (sls `moves/sec` with zero seconds) is guarded in Go. Mapping ±Inf/NaN to
  `inf`/`-inf`/`nan` (and `-nan` for a negative NaN) would make the outputs match.
- `pkg/util/statistics/statistics.go:246` (`DisplayInternal`) ports `statistics::display_internal`. In C++
  its only caller is `context::display_istatistics`, and nothing calls that (`g_display_istatistics` is set
  in `shell/main.cpp` but never read). The C++ loop never advances `key` (an infinite loop) and prints
  `'A'+…` as an int; the Go version is a "fixed" re-implementation with no counterpart. It is dead code with
  no Go caller, so this is policy only (dead C++ should not be ported).
- `pkg/util/prime/generator.go:12` (`ErrCapacity`): the text is `mpnum: prime generator capacity
  exceeded`, while the C++ exception message is `prime generator capacity exceeded`. It is only reachable
  after more than 2^20 primes during univariate factorization, which `m_max_p` bounds. If this error can
  ever reach an `(error "...")` line, the `mpnum: ` prefix would differ from the C++.

### Polynomials and algebraic numbers (`pkg/math/polynomial`)

**math_polynomial_01**

- Model divergence, probably not in this shard. With `qfnra-nlsat`, g3 prints a different (valid) model from z3 on:
  ```smt2
  (declare-const x Real) (declare-const y Real) (declare-const z Real)
  (assert (<= (+ (* 6 y y) (* -3 x x x y y z z z) (* 5 x x y z z z) (* -1 x x x y z)) 0))
  (assert (= (+ (* 6 x x z z) (* 2 x x y z) 4) 0))
  (check-sat-using qfnra-nlsat) (get-model)
  ```
  g3 gives `y=-214/5, x=1/8, z=10` (5 conflicts). z3 gives `y=7, x=-1, z=-2` (9 conflicts). In the `-tr:algebraic` traces, the first difference is that g3 calls `isolate_roots` on two extra x1-polynomials (`9 x1^5 + 40 x1^4 + 384 x1^3 - 9217 x1^2 - 393216` and `3 x1^2 + 128`), and there is no sort-order difference before that point. That points at nlsat explain/projection or the evaluator, not at this shard. Running nlsat traces of the two binaries side by side would settle it.
- Performance, probably not in this shard. g3 is 60 times slower or worse on some random nlsat inputs, with the same answers. One instance takes 17.4 s for g3 against 0.28 s for z3:
  ```smt2
  (declare-const x Real) (declare-const y Real) (declare-const z Real)
  (assert (= (+ (* 7 y y y z) (* -8 x z z) (* 6 x y y y) (* 9 x z)) 0))
  (assert (>= (+ (* -4 x x x y) (* -5 x x x y z) (* -9 y z)) 0))
  (assert (< (+ (* 1 x x y z) (* -4 x y y y z z)) 0))
  (assert (> (+ (* 4 x y z z) (* -7 x x y y) (* 1 y y z z)) 0))
  (check-sat-using qfnra-nlsat) (get-model)
  ```
  On another instance, z3 needs 2.45 s and g3 times out at 20 s. Counts of algebraic events (compare, isolate_roots) are within about 8% of z3, so the cost is likely in polynomial resultant or the receipt machinery rather than in the algorithm here. A CPU profile would settle it. Inputs are in `$S/work/math_polynomial_01/gen/t5.smt2` and `t11.smt2`.
- `display_decimal` (`algebraic_display_decimal.go`) refines a copy of the stored interval. Because of F1, the stored interval can differ from C++, so the last printed digit before `?` could in principle differ. Not observed.

**math_polynomial_02**

- These two points are outside this shard; they came up while testing it. `rlimit-count` under `-st` differs between g3 and z3 even on trivial input with no algebraic numbers. `(declare-const x Real)(assert (> x 0.0))(check-sat-using qfnra-nlsat)` gives z3 `:rlimit-count 45` and g3 `47`. `(assert (= (* x x) 2.0))` gives 105 vs 110. `(check-sat-using (then simplify nlsat))` and `(check-sat-using simplify)` agree (9/9 and 6/6). So the extra `m_limit.inc()` calls come from the `qfnra-nlsat` tactic composition (its preprocessing tactics), not from the algebraic or polynomial checkpoints. Owners of the qfnra tactic and preprocessing shards should look. Related recorded findings: smtcore_05-F8 and smtcore_14-F1.
- Performance, outside this shard. `work/math_polynomial_02/n3.smt2` (three chained irrational definitions, `qfnra-nlsat`) takes 1.17 s on z3 and about 51 s on g3, with the same answer and model. `perf` puts the time in `util/numeral.(*IntegerManager).Digit/writeDigit/multiplyCells` under `pseudoCore`, `mulAddWithReceipt` and `resultantWithReceipt`. That is a constant factor in the bignum layer, not an algorithmic blowup in this shard. Inputs like this hit the 20 s harness timeout under g3 only.
- `gparams_catalog_collectors.go:59-67` registers `factor_params::get_param_descrs` with explicit defaults `"4294967295"` and `"1"`. The C++ (`polynomial.cpp:58-62`) inserts these with no default (`def = nullptr`), and the shell never registers a `factor` module: `-pm:factor` gives `unknown module 'factor'` on both binaries. As far as I can tell this is not observable; it would matter only if some g3 path printed these descriptions.

**math_polynomial_03**

- None found. The algebraic resultant path that exercises `ComposeXMinusY`, `ComposeXPlusY` and `ComposeXDivY` (algebraic `+`, `*`, `/` in nlsat models) gives byte-identical output on `$S/bin/g3` and `build/z3` for a QF_NRA input with `sqrt(2)`, `cbrt(3)`, their sum, their product, and an `(eval (/ z (- x y)))` (input kept in `$S/work/math_polynomial_03/alg.smt2`).

**math_polynomial_04**

- `pkg/math/polynomial/polynomial_gcd_power_buffer.go:51` vs `polynomial.cpp:4253`: for more than 16 tied variables, both libstdc++ introsort and pdqsort permute ties, in different ways. F1's fix covers this too. The open question is whether nlsat inputs in the regression corpus reach `mod_gcd` with that many variables. Running `-tr:mgcd` on the largest nlsat vectors would settle it.
- `pkg/math/polynomial/polynomial_factor_univariate.go:143` vs `polynomial.cpp:6701`: when `upolynomial::factor_square_free` reports p irreducible (one factor, degree 1), both C++ and Go push `p` and ignore an `fs` constant of -1. They agree, but that looks like a latent C++ sign issue for primitive polynomials with a negative leading coefficient. It is not a porting bug; it would belong in `z3_bug_exclusions.txt` only if confirmed.

**math_polynomial_05**

- `pkg/math/polynomial/polynomial_monomial_table.go:22-27` and `polynomial_monomial_manager_trace.go:22` versus `polynomial.cpp:796-800,1284-1292`: the monomial table iterates in insertion order (insdict), but C++ `chashtable` iterates in bucket order. The source comment documents this. It only shows in the `~monomial_manager` "monomials leaked" trace and in the insertion order of the table rebuilt by `rename`. Neither changes results. It matters only if a leaked-monomial trace is ever compared against native output.
- `pkg/math/polynomial/polynomial_linear_rational.go:289`, `polynomial_linear_modular.go:309,368`: the pivot and row factor are held as value copies of `unumeral.Rational`/`unumeral.Int` handles, where the C++ holds references (`numeral & A_k_k`). The copies are not used after the cell they alias is overwritten (`setInto(rk,k,1)` / `setInto(ri,k,0)`), so this looks safe. A focused test with big (multi-limb) pivots in `RationalLinearSolver.Solve` would settle it.

**math_polynomial_06**

- `pkg/math/polynomial/polynomial_skeleton.go:84-95` vs `src/math/polynomial/polynomial.cpp:2985,680-686`: the skeleton sorts with Go `sort.Slice` instead of `std::sort(…, lex_lt2(x))`. `lex_compare2` only returns 0 for identical (hash-consed) monomials and looks like a strict total order, so the sorted result is the same. But `lex_lt2::operator()` emits `TRACE("lex_bug", …)` on every comparison, and the number and order of comparisons differ between introsort and pdqsort. So the `lex_bug` trace differs, though it is debug-only. This falls under the approved Go-sort substitution; record it only if lex_bug trace identity matters.
- `pkg/math/polynomial/polynomial_psc_cleanup.go:19-31` (`pscEnter`): at depth 0 it refuses with `ErrPolynomialPending` when an earlier PSC-owned record is still marked (`powerLocal.pscOwner`, `pseudoDivision.pscOwner`, `exactDivision.pscOwner`, `generatedPSC`, `pscReceipts.factory`). C++ has no such failure. Every success path I read clears these fields, and the nlsat differential run went through many psc_chain/normalize calls without error. A stale marker after an error in an earlier call (for example, a cancelled checkpoint inside pseudo-division) could make later PSC/normalize calls fail until `CleanupPSC`. To settle it, run a cancelled nlsat problem (`timeout=`/`rlimit=` hitting during explain) followed by another check-sat on the same manager.
- `polynomial_psc_chain1.go`, `polynomial_psc_chain2.go` and `polynomial_psc_classic*.go` port `psc_chain1`, `psc_chain2` and `psc_chain_classic`. These are dead in C++ (commented out in `psc_chain`, `polynomial.cpp:5897-5902`), and AGENTS.md says not to port dead C++ code. They are faithful ports, and in Go they are reachable only through the exported API/tests.

**math_polynomial_07**

- `pkg/math/polynomial/polynomial_subresultant_chain.go:130-168` vs `src/math/polynomial/polynomial.cpp:5527-5530`. The Go regular branch (`r == j`) leaves out C++'s `TRACE("psc", "j: ... sRes_j+1 ... sRes_j ... prem ...")`. In C++, `subresultant_chain` is reached only from `psc_chain1`, and `psc_chain` has that call commented out (polynomial.cpp:5898). So the whole Go function ports C++ code that is dead in this build. The effect would show only in a `-tr:psc` trace if a Go caller ever reaches it. A grep for callers of `SubresultantChain` / `psc_chain1` in pkg would settle whether it is live. If it is dead, project policy says to remove it rather than add the trace.
- `pkg/math/polynomial/polynomial_som_owner.go:516` (`PolynomialSOMBuffer.DisplayInto`) formats coefficients with `integer.String`. The sqrt trace path (`polynomial_sqrt_trace.go:67`) uses `modular.String`. C++ `som_buffer::display` uses `mpzzp_manager::to_string`, which carries the `SASSERT(is_p_normalized(a))`. The output text is identical; the only difference is that the debug-build assertion is skipped on the public DisplayInto path. This is cosmetic and debug-only.

**math_polynomial_08**

- `pkg/math/polynomial` (drs root isolation, outside this shard) vs `src/math/polynomial/upolynomial.cpp` `drs_isolate_roots`, `drs_isolate_0_1_roots` and `add_isolating_interval`: on `nl1.smt2` above, C++ `-tr:upolynomial` writes 3, 12 and 4 records at these functions and g3 writes none. On nl2, C++ writes 6 + 8 and g3 none. These are not in KNOWN.md (only translate_q is, as math_polynomial_11-F1). The shard that owns the drs isolation Go file should confirm.
- `upolynomial_division.go:203-244` (`divRemCoreSpanWithSourceContext`): if a `receipt` (Hensel) and a Berlekamp or remove-one-half-root context were ever passed together, `h.amConstructed` would be set but that receipt's `finishHenselAmSource` would never run. No such combined caller was found, so this is latent.

**math_polynomial_09**

- `pkg/math/polynomial/upolynomial_factor_field.go:795-798` (`FactorZP`) vs `src/math/polynomial/upolynomial_factorization.cpp:375-377`. The C++ calls `get_p_from_manager` only inside the `TRACE`. Go calls `m.factorPrime()` unconditionally before `beginFactorField`. `zp_square_free_factor` calls it unconditionally right after, so the "prime too big" exception is the same; only the point where it is raised moves ahead of the frame and trace. Probably not observable; settle it with a > 32-bit modulus through `FactorZP` with and without the trace tag.
- `pkg/math/polynomial/upolynomial_factor_scope.go` / `upolynomial_factor_field_scope.go:33-50`: `beginFactorField` takes frames from a fixed `m.factorFieldFrames` array and returns `ErrUPolynomialCleanupPending` when none is free. With `FactorZP` nesting `squareFreeFactorZP`, two frames are needed. If a frame is left active after an error path, later `FactorZP` calls on that manager fail where the C++ would not. Settle it by forcing an error inside `squareFreeFactorZP` (for example a cancelled checkpoint), then calling `FactorZP` again.

- `pkg/math/polynomial/upolynomial_gcd.go:297` (`subresultantGCD`) has no TRACE records (C++ `upolynomial.cpp:903,915,931`). The function is used only by `src/test/upolynomial.cpp` in C++, so it is dead in production. It is listed here only in case the Go API is reached by a live consumer later.

The `hensel_lift`, `hensel_lift_quadratic`, `check_hansel_lift`, `mignotte_bound`, prime-trial and recombination algorithms themselves are in out-of-shard files (`upolynomial_factor_hensel.go`, `upolynomial_factor_recombine.go`, ...). Their fidelity should be checked by whichever shard owns those files. The trace text in `upolynomial_hensel_pair_trace.go` (590/614/637/641/646/653/658/663/536) does match the C++ strings and tags.

- `pkg/math/polynomial` drs isolation (not in this shard) vs `src/math/polynomial/upolynomial.cpp:2151-2340`: on `tq.smt2`, the C++ trace has 16 `drs_isolate_0_1_roots` and 9 `drs_isolate_roots` `[upolynomial]` records. ### Real closure (`pkg/math/realclosure`)

**math_realclosure_01**

- `pkg/math/realclosure/root_coefficient_interval_any.go:15` vs `realclosure.cpp:1464-1540`. The Knuth bounds use a fresh initial-precision interval for rational coefficients (`rationalApproxInterval`). C++ `interval(a)` uses the value's cached interval, which may already have been refined. `magnitude_lb`/`magnitude_ub` can differ when an endpoint crosses a power of two. That would change the root bound N and therefore the isolating interval. To settle it, refine a rational coefficient just below a power of two (via a sign determination) and then isolate.
- `pkg/math/realclosure/interval_restore.go:46-90` vs `realclosure.cpp:659-710`. C++ `save_interval` keeps the value alive with `inc_ref`. Go stores only the `*BinaryInterval`. If a temporary value is refined past `max_precision` and then released inside the same API call, `restore()` calls `SetFrom` on a closed interval and the call returns an error.
- Cross-shard, from the differential runs:
  - `value_display_api.go` (`displayPolynomialValue`) prints `(-3)*x` and `(2)*x^2` where C++ prints `-3*x` and `2*x^2`.
  - `displayValue` prints any algebraic-main value as `r!k`, for example `r*pi` is shown as `[r!1; ...]`, and errors on `r+1`.
  - `sign_sturm_rational_refine.go:15` (`sturmIntervalMagnitude`) errors on unbounded intervals, where C++ `magnitude` returns INT_MAX. As a result `RCFDecimalString(1/eps)` errors instead of printing `?`.
  - `transcendental_interval.go:46` builds the first epsilon interval with `inf_precision`; C++ `mk_infinitesimal` uses `m_ini_precision`.
  - `api.GlobalParamSet("rcf.clean_denominators","false")` has no effect on g3's RCF manager: roots of x^2-1/2 still print `root((2)*x^2 + -1, ...)`, while C++ prints `root(x^2 + -1/2, ...)`. `rcf_params.go` itself reads `gparams::get_module("rcf")` correctly, so the plumbing in `pkg/api` (`realClosureValues`, `config.Globals`) is suspect.
- `display_collect_ranked.go:28` adds non-algebraic extensions to the collected list. C++ `collect_algebraic_refs::mark` keeps only algebraic ones. This is only reachable from the test-only `displayCompactRankedValue`.

**math_realclosure_01b**

- `pkg/math/realclosure/algebraic_sign_interval.go:11-47` (`restrictBinaryIntervalToSign`) against `realclosure.cpp:4538-4600` (`refine_until_sign_determined`, `expensive_algebraic_poly_interval`). This extends the existing math_realclosure_02 Needs-verification item on `value_sign_ranked.go:63-74`.
  - For an algebraic value that does not depend on infinitesimals, after a single-root Tarski query the C++ refines the coefficients and the extension until the value's interval is (l>0, u) or (l, u<0), with no zero endpoint. It uses `set_lower_zero`/`set_upper_zero` only when the value depends on infinitesimals or the extension has a sign_det.
  - Go always overwrites the near endpoint with an open 0, giving (0, u). Then 1/d gets the unbounded interval (1/u, +oo) where the C++ interval is bounded.
  - With d = sqrt2 - 7071/5000, I found no output difference: decimal, display, roots and inverse all matched (`$S/work/math_realclosure_01b/c/sg1.c`, `go2/`). Magnitude-based code on the unbounded interval (see math_realclosure_01's note on `sturmIntervalMagnitude`) is where a difference would appear.
- `pkg/math/realclosure/integer_exact_divide_value.go:11-25` against `realclosure.cpp:3427-3458` (`exact_div_z`). The C++ builds the quotient's numerator directly and sets its interval to interval(a)/b at `m_ini_precision`. Go uses the non-ranked `divideRetainedValues`, which rejects transcendental and infinitesimal values (the F3 family), plus `canonicalizeAnyRetainedResult`. The interval history therefore differs from the C++. Use `divideRankedRetainedValues`, or port `exact_div_z` directly.
- `pkg/math/realclosure/polynomial_evaluate_bound_any.go:31-56` (`signAnyPolynomialAtBinaryBound`). C++ `expensive_eval_sign_at` runs under `flet<bool> set(m_in_aux_values, true)`. The ranked counterpart `exactSignAtBinaryBound` sets `withAuxiliaryValues()`, but the live "any" one does not. With lazy algebraic normalization, this changes whether intermediate algebraic products are reduced modulo a non-monic defining polynomial. The sign is unaffected, but the work and the intermediate representations differ. It also uses non-ranked arithmetic (math_realclosure_01-F3).
- `pkg/math/realclosure/polynomial_scalar_ranked.go:24-32` (`makeRankedPolynomialMonic`). C++ `mk_monic` skips the work when the leading coefficient is rational one, and otherwise stores `one()` as the leading coefficient. Go divides every coefficient, including the leading coefficient by itself. A probe with transcendental leading coefficients ((pi*e+1)/(pi*e+2), (pi*e^2-pi)/(pi*e-pi)) matched the C++ exactly, so lc/lc canonicalizes to 1 today. This depends on math_realclosure_02-F4 not leaving a 1/1 rational-function value.

**math_realclosure_02**

- `pkg/math/realclosure/transcendental_refine.go:12-46` against `realclosure.cpp:1323-1330`. `refineTranscendentalRoot` performs one `refine_transcendental_interval(t)` step per call. The C++ `refine_transcendental_interval(t, prec)` loops until `check_precision(t->interval, prec)` and calls `save_interval_if_too_small` each time. `refineTranscendentalPolynomialValue` also divides at `workPrecision` instead of `inc_precision(prec, 2)`, and calls `Div` even when the numerator or denominator interval contains zero. `Div` fails with `ErrExtendedDomain` in that case, while `update_rf_interval` leaves the interval unchanged. Values agreed in my probes (`1/(pi-355/113)`, `1/(pi-3)^2`), but the interval history differs. Settle this by checking decimal output, or with a denominator whose interval stays ambiguous after one step.
- `pkg/math/realclosure/transcendental_interval.go:162-163` against `realclosure.cpp:1309-1320`. When `-m >= 1<<16`, `inc_precision` returns `-m`, but Go uses `initialPrecision`. The C++ also sets both endpoint open flags from the exactness of the upper endpoint, because the second `mpq_to_mpbqi` call overwrites them, while Go ORs the openness of the source and each endpoint. This only matters for open or closed exact endpoints.
- `pkg/math/realclosure/value_sign_ranked.go:63-74` against `realclosure.cpp:4767-4788`. For algebraic values, Go goes straight to a Tarski query and does not refine `refine_algebraic_interval` up to `max_precision` as `determine_algebraic_sign` does. The sign is the same, but the extension and value intervals differ from the C++, which can change later decimal output or the isolating-interval refinement history.
- `pkg/math/realclosure/sign_polynomial_algebraic_content.go:17-23` (`integerContentValue`) and `value_clean_denominators.go:23-31` (`hasCleanDenominator`) against `realclosure.cpp:3114-3122, 3350-3372`. The C++ returns false or "not clean" for a rational-function coefficient whose denominator is not one, but the Go recurses into the numerator only. `hasCleanDenominator` guards `isolateNonzeroCleanTowerRoots` (`root_isolate_clean_tower.go:12`), so an unclean transcendental-denominator coefficient would pass the check.
- `pkg/math/realclosure/sign_sturm_algebraic_refine.go:34-38`. `refineSturmAlgebraicInterval` gives up (returns `false, nil`) when the defining polynomial has non-rational coefficients, while the C++ `eval_sign_at` handles any coefficient. Its only caller is `refineValueInterval`, which has no API caller today.
- Outside this shard but seen while probing, and all confirmed with the binaries or library:
  - `IsolateRoots([1+eps, -(2+eps), 1])` fails in Go with `invalid or dead slot` at `algebraic_polynomial_value.go:14`, via `cleanAnyValueDenominator` → `publishAlgebraicPolynomialResult`. The C++ returns 2 sign-determined roots.
  - `IsolateRoots` of `(x-1)(x-1-2^-200)` (rational) fails in Go with `interval: undefined extended rational operation` from `makeRootBoundInterval` → `BinaryInterval.SetFinite`. The C++ returns 2 roots.
  - The isolating intervals that Go prints are upper-closed, `(39/2^5, 109/2^6]`, where the C++ prints `(39/2^5, 109/2^6)`.
  - `APIValues.Display` (`api_values.go:389`) dereferences `a.value` without a nil check, so displaying any zero result (for example `Sub(x, x)`) panics with a nil pointer.
  - `reduceRankedAlgebraicPolynomial` (`algebraic_polynomial_reduce_ranked.go`) always reduces modulo `p`. The C++ `normalize_algebraic` skips the reduction when lazy normalization is on, `m_in_aux_values` is set and `p` is not monic.

### Subpaving (`pkg/math/subpaving`)

**math_subpaving_01**

- `pkg/math/subpaving/arbitrary_refcount_trace.go:31-32` vs `src/math/subpaving/subpaving_t_def.h:796`: C++ `dec_ref` traces `a->display(tout, nm())` with the default `display_var_proc` (`x0`). Go `displayInequality` uses the installed variable display (user names). This is trace-only (`subpaving_ref_count`); compare a `-tr:subpaving_ref_count` run.
- `pkg/math/subpaving/fast_clause.go:155-175` and `fast_display.go` `DisplayConstraints` vs `subpaving_t_def.h:835-840,1150-1153`: C++ stores `lemma && !watch` clauses nowhere and displays only `m_clauses`. Go keeps lemmas in `c.clauses` and displays them. This looks unreachable (the tactic only adds non-lemma clauses).
- `pkg/math/subpaving/fast_display.go` `DisplayBounds`: with `c.root == nil`, Go returns `ErrInvalidSlot` (via `(*FastNode).open`). C++ prints nothing. This is probably unreachable, because the tactic always runs a search first.
- `arbitrary_context_propagate.go`/`fast_context_propagate.go`: when `PropagateQueued` returns early with an error, the queue is not reset, while C++ resets after the loop. That only matters on cancellation or error paths.

**math_subpaving_02**

- `pkg/math/subpaving/tactic/fixed_core_tactic.go:273` and `tactic/fast_core_tactic.go:271` call `DisplayConstraints(stream, true)`; C++ `display_constraints(std::cout)` defaults `use_star=false`. This is confirmed for mpfx: g3 prints `k!3 = x*y*w` where z3 prints `k!3 = x y w` (input `down_mpfx.smt2`, the F1 vector with `:print_nodes true`). Out of shard (math_subpaving_04).
- `(check-sat-using (using-params subpaving :numeral mpff))` fails in g3 with `(error "... arena: invalid configuration")` on every input tried, while z3 prints `unknown` and runs the search. This is confirmed. It most likely comes from the `ProcessOwner()` checks that return `arena.ErrConfig` in `tactic/fast_core_tactic.go:71-76,134` or `tactic/fast_engine.go:45`. Out of shard (math_subpaving_04). As a result the MPFF engine in this shard cannot be reached from SMT-LIB at all.
- `pkg/math/subpaving/fixed_refcount_trace.go:33` and `hardware_refcount_trace.go`: the C++ `dec_ref` trace calls `a->display(tout, nm())` with the DEFAULT `display_var_proc` (`x<k>` names).
